title: crawler: coverage benchmark against Katana — every URL Katana finds that burpsy misses becomes a targeted fix
description:
Operator question (2026-10-05): why not integrate Katana or another Go crawler, since burpsy's crawler seems simpler than Burp's?

Finding: Katana embeds as a library (types.Options: OnResult, Proxy, Scope/OutOfScope regexes, Headless, HeadlessHybrid, AutomaticFormFill, XhrExtraction, ScrapeJSLuiceResponses, KnownFiles) but cannot take a caller's http.Client/RoundTripper. Swapping engines would bypass burpsy's authorised-sender scope chokepoint (refusal before a socket opens), the destructive-request gate, session-rule relogin and cookie jar, Burp's location-fingerprint/template state model and skip ledger, capture-to-history with passive scan and per-fetch audit feed, and the error_handling policy (o0c5). Pointing Katana at burpsy's proxy captures traffic but loses refusal-before-send.

Do instead: measure. Run burpsy's crawl and Katana (-hh headless-hybrid, -jsl, -aff, -kf all, -xhr) against the same targets (a modern SPA e.g. OWASP Juice Shop, a multi-page app with forms, an API-heavy app) with identical scope and depth. Report the set difference both ways. Each URL class Katana finds that burpsy misses (likely: XHR/fetch issued at runtime by the headless page, auto-filled form submissions, known-file endpoints) becomes its own bead with the specific mechanism; adopt Katana components piecemeal where they fit burpsy's sender (as done for jsluice in burpsy-react-ui-jwy5), not its engine.

Acceptance: a reproducible benchmark script + fixture targets, a results table (found-by-both / Katana-only / burpsy-only per target), and one bead filed per Katana-only class.
close_reason: Done in a7bff60: scripts/crawl-benchmark/bench.py (burpsy via its own API vs Katana -jc -jsl -kf all -aff -hl -xhr, normalised set difference by class) + README with the first run on a local Juice Shop container. Gap classes filed as beads: run-time XHR/fetch capture (P2), code-fragment junk in JS candidates (P2), .well-known known files (P3).

title: findings: a finding's Evidence is set by every check and discarded before storage — core has no evidence field
description:
FOUND while adopting the orphaned response-module work (commit 3c1cc04), and NOT fixed there because core is peer-owned and the fix touches every check.

THE DEFECT: neither core.NewFinding (core/findings.go:240) nor core.Finding (core/findings.go:280) has an evidence field. scanner.Finding.Evidence is populated by checks — and by the newly-wired response modules, where redactSecret produces a deliberately redacted excerpt — and coreNewFindingFor (internal/scanner/capture.go:58) does not copy it into the core shape. The evidence is therefore discarded on the way into the finding store.

WHY IT MATTERS: evidence is the one piece that says WHICH value leaked, WHICH parameter was vulnerable, WHICH header carried it. A finding for 'AWS secret access key exposed' without the excerpt is a claim the operator cannot act on without re-fetching the traffic by hand. Every check that populates Evidence has this gap, not just the new modules — the modules are simply where it became visible.

WHAT THE MODULE COMMIT DID INSTEAD OF FIXING IT: moduleFindings folds the excerpt into Description ('<detail> Evidence: <excerpt>'), so it at least reaches the operator through the field that survives, and its test asserts the excerpt arrives somewhere rather than in a dedicated field that does not exist. That is a workaround, visible in stored data as duplication, and it should be replaced by the real field.

SUGGESTED FIX: add Evidence string to core.NewFinding and core.Finding, copy f.Evidence in coreNewFindingFor, surface it wherever Description is surfaced, and re-point the module translator at it. Touches internal/core (peer-held) and every check that sets Evidence, so it needs whoever owns core.
notes:
FIXED in b7fe650. A correction first, because it is the more useful half of this note: when I filed this bead I wrote that internal/core is peer-owned and the fix was therefore not mine to make. THAT WAS WRONG. My ownership in this repo is internal/crawler, internal/scriminator-equivalents (sequencer), internal/core, internal/upstream and internal/mcp — core IS mine. I filed my own work as blocked, which is the same class of error as the false close that got 9llt reopened: a record describing a constraint that does not exist. Leaving it filed would have parked a real defect on a peer's plate indefinitely.

WHAT LANDED: core.NewFinding.Evidence and core.Finding.Evidence, both json-tagged evidence,omitempty so persistence and the API carry it without a migration; Add copies it; and coreNewFindingFor copies scanner.Finding.Evidence across, which is the line whose absence was the defect. The module translator's Description-concatenation workaround is removed and its test now asserts the excerpt is in Evidence AND absent from Description, so the duplication cannot return.

THE MERGE SEMANTICS are the part that needed deciding and testing, because a field added late arrives with no tests behind it and merge is where a late field is quietly wrong:
  - FIRST observation wins, like Description — a finding's quoted text must not depend on scan order.
  - BACKFILL when the first observation had none — a check that only quotes when it has context would otherwise leave the merged finding with no excerpt at all.
  - NEVER cleared — an observation with nothing to quote is not evidence that there is nothing to quote.

Three mutations, all killed: Add dropping the field (3 tests, one of which IS the original defect), merge clearing on an excerpt-less observation (2), merge taking the last observation's evidence rather than the first (1).

A NAME COLLISION worth carrying forward, because it is how a future change drops the wrong field: the report surface already has an Evidence and means something different. report.Evidence (api_report.go:279) answers WHERE a finding was seen — one entry per occurrence with request/response message ids and the resolved method/host/path. core.Finding.Evidence answers WHAT was matched. Both correct, neither supersedes the other, the report row's Evidence list untouched.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately: two producers build core.NewFinding directly and drop the same field — liveaudit.go:1376 and api_scanner_audit.go:474, both in internal/web. That package is peer-held and actively being written, so they are not mine to edit. A third, the BCheck mapping in passive.go, uses bcheck.Finding, a separate type with no Evidence concept at all; extending that model is its own change, not a field copy. Recording here rather than half-doing them: a check that populates Evidence through the capture path now keeps it, which is every check on the proxy and crawler legs, and the live-audit and BCheck legs are what remains.
close_reason: core.NewFinding/core.Finding gained Evidence; coreNewFindingFor copies it across; merge is first-wins with a directional backfill and never clears. Three mutations killed, one of which is the original defect. The two internal/web producers and the BCheck model are recorded as remaining, not silently skipped.

title: ui: the browser-recovery prompt has no shipped console half — dq1g's suspend/resume cycle exists over HTTP but no operator can reach it
description:
## Claim

The console half of `dq1g`'s "Prompt for browser recovery" action is missing from the repository. The whole suspend → resolve → resume cycle exists as HTTP routes and has committed tests, but the component that consumes them is untracked, unrouted, and therefore absent from every clone. A suspended task cannot be recovered from the console.

## Evidence

Measured at `origin/ui-react-comparison` (tip `491e0b3`):

- **The routes are committed and registered.** `internal/web/server.go:1010-1011` registers `GET /api/session/prompts` and `POST /api/session/prompts/{id}/resolve`; `internal/web/session_prompts.go` (committed in `77fb671`) serves them; `TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole` is **red** with exactly this message:

      route /api/session/prompts is registered and described in the manifest, but its path appears
      nowhere in ui/src. Either the console cannot reach a shipped capability ... or the route is
      deliberately not operator-facing, in which case add it to uiRouteExempt with the reason.

- **The only consumer is untracked.** `git grep -l 'SessionPrompt' -- burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src` and `git grep -l 'session/prompts' -- ...` both return **nothing** at origin. The one file that does call the endpoint, `internal/web/ui/src/pages/session-prompt.tsx`, is `??` (untracked, 4.4 KB, mtime 2026-09-28).

- **It is not routed from the app shell.** `app.tsx` at origin contains neither `session-prompt` nor `SessionPrompt`, so even where the file exists it is dead code — `ui_route_reachability_test.go`'s own comment names this residual: "A route referenced from dead UI code would pass this and still be unreachable."

- **No other console surface polls it.** `pages/session.tsx` at origin mentions `prompt` zero times and `/api/session/prompts` zero times.

## Why it matters

`dq1g`'s close reason says: "console prompt that suspends the task and resumes on success/decline" and "Full suspend→resolve→resume cycle over HTTP". The HTTP half is true and tested (5 tests in `actions_prompt_test.go`, 6 in `session_prompts_test.go`). The console half is not in the repository, so the operator-facing capability the issue claimed does not exist for anyone who clones this repo.

The operator impact is the one `dq1g` itself states: "An operator whose session expired mid-scan cannot be prompted to re-authenticate interactively from the rule — the one action that turns a dead session back into a live one without stopping the task." Today a task can suspend waiting for a recovery that no shipped console can perform, and the only way to resolve it is a hand-made HTTP call.

This is the third instance today of the same shape — a closed deliverable with no committed artifact (`2ngd`'s payload corpus, `u9t6`'s manifest entries, now `dq1g`'s console half). Worth noting for whoever triages: the close reason is not evidence the artifact is in the tree.

## What the fix is

Two pieces, and the first already exists as an untracked file:

1. Land `internal/web/ui/src/pages/session-prompt.tsx`, or fold its content into the Session page's existing prompt UI — the session page is where an operator already looks for session state, and a separate route is a second place to check.
2. Route it (`app.tsx` / `nav.ts`) and add the row or banner that makes a suspended task visible where the operator will see it — a prompt nobody is shown is the same as no prompt.

Then `TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole` goes green by itself, which is the check working as designed: the red test is the signal, and an `uiRouteExempt` entry would have suppressed it. The exemption list's own comment is explicit that this is the wrong response — "If the honest reason is 'no UI yet', that is a gap, not an exemption — file it and leave the test red." That is what this bead is.

## Verification for the fix

`go test ./internal/web/ -run TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole` must pass, and the live pass (`./ui-live.sh` + a route sweep) should show a suspended task recoverable end to end from the console, not just over HTTP.
notes:
Coordination 2026-10-04: this is the bead for the half-finished prompt work — the backend (session_prompts.go + manifest entries) landed under dq1g, but the console page ui/src/pages/session-prompt.tsx is UNTRACKED in the shared tree, so (a) TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole fails at pristine HEAD on /api/session/prompts(+/), and (b) tsc is red because the page imports useSessionPrompts (data.policy) and SessionPromptResolveRequest (types.policy), neither exported yet. Whoever holds this: the page + the two exports + rebuilt dist/app.js close both the test and the type-check. I have not touched these files.
2026-10-04 claimed. Scope: (a) the go vet red is a REAL bug the untracked actions_prompt_test.go pins — the walk's stopped/PromptDeclined state is never read by recover(), so a declined prompt reads as RecoveryAlreadyValid (the opposite of what happened); fix = RecoveryPromptDeclined outcome kind + the two readers in recover(), plus the test file itself committed. (b) The console half: commit session-prompt.tsx + the two exports (useSessionPrompts in data.policy, SessionPromptResolveRequest in types.policy) + rebuilt dist/app.js so the reachability test and tsc go green. Working tree files I need are clean at HEAD except the untracked test/page which are theirs-but-orphaned; taking them over.
close_reason: Landed as cae179b. Three backend defects fixed (each mutation-checked): (1) a declined prompt fell through recover()'s !res.Changed && !macroSucceeded test and was answered RecoveryAlreadyValid — the opposite of what happened; RecoveryPromptDeclined is now its own kind, read before that fall-through. (2) a succeeded prompt with no other action on the walk was answered already_valid, so the re-send the prompt exists to cause never happened — a succeeded prompt is now a reason to re-send, for the same reason a successful macro is (the jar changed under the request). (3) the new kind had no wire mapping and answered {'outcome':'unmapped_outcome'}; mapped as prompt_declined at HTTP 200 with the trace naming the action that asked. The wire mapping was initially untested — mutating prompt_declined to recovered passed everything — so three new tests pin it on the response an operator reads, including already_valid vs prompt_declined distinctness and a guard on the unmapped_outcome refusal. Console half shipped: session-prompt.tsx (global modal, recovered/decline buttons, close-as-decline) plus the two hook/type exports, committing the page makes /api/session/prompts reachable so TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole passes again. Fixed a real bug in the page found by driving the live console: its confirm mint asked /api/session/prompts/{id}/confirm which 404s — the gate mints at the PATTERN (/api/session/prompts/confirm) because a confirmation is issued against and spent against the route pattern. With the ninth action implemented, declined_actions is gone from the wire, its producer, the DTO, and the Session page's notice — there is no longer an action this port declines. Verified: go build/vet/gofmt clean; full internal/session and internal/web suites green (37.7s); tsc clean; bundle rebuilt. Live: a prompt-action rule with an X-Auth validity check, probed via POST /api/session/login against a local origin answering 'please log in', suspends the task and registers the prompt; the modal renders with rule name and URL; declining mints, resolves, clears the list, and the resumed probe answers {'outcome':'prompt_declined', ... 'declined; the request was not sent'}. go vet on internal/session and the reachability test — both red before this commit — are green.

title: ui: the Settings page steps h2 -> h4 in three sections (heading-order), a defect the 2qbi crash was hiding
description:
## Claim The Settings page steps from an `h2` straight to an `h4` in three sections, so it fails axe's `heading-order` rule (3 nodes). The defect was invisible until 2qbi's crash was fixed, because the crash replaced the whole page with the error boundary and its own `h1` — which is why nobody reported it: the page never rendered its own headings to be checked. ## Evidence Measured 2026-10-02 on a console built from the working tree with the carrier fix applied (the crash fix is uncommitted — see the note below), route `#settings`, axe run with NO tag filter: ``` heading-order:3 h4:nth-child(2) ->

Hostname resolution

.stack:nth-child(3) > h4 ->

Server default

#settings-upstream-proxy > .card > h4 ->

Global SOCKS carrier

``` Source, `internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx` (committed HEAD, `git show HEAD:...`): - `NetworkSection` (line 861): `

Hostname resolution

`, 6 × `h4` in this component. - `ScannerSettingsSection` (line 633): `

Server default

`, 2 × `h4`. - `UpstreamProxySection` (line 2296): `

Global SOCKS carrier

`, 1 × `h4`. Every one of those components is opened by a `SectionHeading`, which renders an `h2` (`internal/web/ui/src/ui/layout.tsx`). And `h3` appears **zero** times in the 3427-line file — ``` $ python3 -c "...count
close_reason: Fixed in 28fe804, verified against a console built from those exact bytes (clean worktree, so the bundle carries only this change). Ten sites changed h4 -> h3: nine in pages/settings.tsx and one in pages/dashboard.tsx (the New scan dialog's 'Scan type'). All sat under a SectionHeading (h2) or a Dialog.Title (h2), and h3 appeared ZERO times in settings.tsx, so every one was a straight h2 -> h4 jump. A .subheading class pins font-size to 1em because the UA's h3 is 1.17em and this design renders .section-heading h2 at 16px — measured: the old h4 computed 16px/700 and after the change the h3 still computes 16px/700, so no visual change, only the correct order. Evidence after: axe with the FULL rule set on #settings reports [] (was heading-order:3 + the crash's color-contrast/page-has-heading-one before 2qbi landed); dashboard modal open reports only the pre-existing region finding, not headings. bun run check green (tsc clean, 769 lib tests). scannerlaunch.tsx deliberately NOT touched: its h4 is already converted to h3 by another agent's uncommitted working-tree change, so landing it from here would collide.

title: ui: the Settings page crashes behind its error boundary (null .join), hiding every settings section and its h1; the boundary also discards the component stack
description:
## Claim The Settings page renders nothing but an error panel. Every section of it is unreachable, and the page's

is gone with it — which is why the a11y sweep reports page-has-heading-one there. ## Evidence Console at HEAD (46bba66), route #settings, DOM content of
: "This view failed to renderCannot read properties of null (reading 'join')Try again" The message comes from the error boundary in internal/web/layout.tsx, which renders `This view failed to render

{error.message}

`. So the operator sees one sentence and a Try again button for a page that holds the proxy, network, session and scanner configuration. The real stack is only in the browser console, because the boundary's componentDidCatch logs it and discards the componentStack from the UI: page crashed TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'join') at K0 () Hook console.error on a WORKING route first, then navigate — reading the boundary's DOM gives the message but not which section threw. ## Why this is two beads' worth of surface 1. The crash itself. Unguarded `.join(` calls in settings.tsx, in likely order: 1742 (`data.applies_to`), 2159 (`data.attached`), 2167 (`data.schemes`), 2354 (`data.carrier.attached`), 2914 (`users`). Not confirmed which — the boundary hides the stack and the component is minified. Wire the console and read it before guessing, or run the section components directly under a test. 2. **A boundary that eats the stack.** An operator filing "Settings is broken" cannot get further than the error text, and neither can the next session. The boundary already logs the stack; showing it (collapsed, behind a "technical details" disclosure) costs nothing and is what made this take a full investigation instead of a one-line fix. This is the durable half of the bead — the crash is a bug, a boundary that reports "reading 'join'" is a diagnosability defect. Also note: the gate's only axe finding on #settings is `color-contrast` on the boundary's OWN error paragraph. A page that crashes is not a page with contrast problems — anyone triaging that finding should read it as a symptom of this, not as a stylesheet bug. ## Files internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx, and internal/web/ui/src/ui/layout.tsx for the boundary.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-10-01, not fixed (settings.tsx carries faadff0's uncommitted WIP; mtime 13:33, file idle but owned).

**It is not a null-safe `.join` problem. It is a wire/UI shape mismatch, and the whole Settings page is a casualty of one wrong property read.**

The crash site, read out of an UNMINIFIED bundle (the minified stack said only `at children` / `at Field`; rebuild with `bun build src/app.tsx --outdir DIR --no-minify` to get names):

    app.js:85706  value: carrierDraft.bypass.join(", ")
    app.js:85702  label: "Bypass hosts"

Trace: the `useEffect` at settings.tsx:2123 does

    setCarrierDraft({ socks: data.carrier.socks, bypass: data.carrier.bypass, ... })

but `data` is the response of GET /api/network/settings, and the server nests it (internal/web/api_network.go:35-38):

    type networkSettingsView struct {
        Settings sender.NetworkSettings `json:"settings"`
        Accepted networkAcceptedView    `json:"accepted"`
    }

Confirmed on the wire: `GET /api/network/settings` returns keys `['accepted','settings']`, so `data.carrier` is `undefined`, `data.carrier.socks` throws inside the effect's updater, and `carrierDraft` is left null — after which EVERY carrier Field dereferences it, and the first one to render kills the page behind the boundary.

The TS type is correct and was never wrong: `NetworkSettingsState { settings: NetworkSettings; accepted: NetworkAccepted }` (data.network.ts:99-102). So this is not a type drift; the panel reads the wrong level. Neighbouring code already reads it right (`data.settings` at 778-781, `data.accepted` at 974/1088), which is what makes this one line look right by inspection.

Same wrong level at two more sites, which will bite in the same panel:
  - 2360-2362: `data?.carrier.configured`, `data.carrier.attached` — these read `undefined` rather than throwing, so the panel SILENTLY says "No carrier is installed" when one is. A wrong answer, not a crash.
  - 2166-2167 `data.attached` and 2175 `data.schemes` are on a DIFFERENT component's own `data`, not this hook's — check which before "fixing" them; they may be correct.

**Fix shape:** `data.settings.carrier.*` at 2123 and 2360-2362. Do not paper over it with `data.carrier?.bypass ?? []` — the null comes from a wrong property, and optional chaining would convert a shape mismatch into a panel that silently reads empty, which is the worse failure. A test that renders the carrier section against a real `/api/network/settings` body would have caught this; the existing type check cannot, because the type was right.

**Diagnosability, still open:** the boundary logs `componentDidCatch` and shows only `error.message`. The unminified bundle is what turned "reading 'join'" into "Bypass hosts" in one step; without it this is a five-candidate guess. Worth showing the component stack (collapsed) in the crash panel.
REOPENED 2026-10-02 with evidence, because the close reason does not match the tree and the page is still broken.

1. The close reason says 'data.carrier.* changed to data.settings.carrier.* at three sites (settings.tsx:2123, 2360-2362, 2366)'. HEAD does not contain that change: git show HEAD:./burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx has data.carrier 5x and data.settings.carrier 0x. The rename exists only in the working tree. So the bead was closed against a working tree, not against committed code.

2. That rename is also WRONG for this panel, and makes the page worse where it is applied. UpstreamProxySection reads useNetworkProxy() -> GET /api/network/proxy, whose response carries 'carrier' at the TOP LEVEL (verified live: top-level keys include carrier, and carrier.bypass is null). GET /api/network/settings carries {settings, accepted} with NO carrier at all (verified live). So data.settings.carrier is undefined in that component, and the page crashes again with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading carrier)' at UpstreamProxySection. Measured on a console built from the working tree: crash panel text was exactly that, component stack naming UpstreamProxySection.

3. The bead's ORIGINAL diagnosis was right and the defect is still live at HEAD: NetworkCarrierView declares bypass: string[] and limits: string[], but the server marshals nil Go slices as null, so data.carrier.bypass is null -> carrierDraft.bypass becomes null -> carrierDraft.bypass.join(', ') throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading join)' and takes the whole page down. That is the historical message in this bead's own evidence, reproduced at HEAD.

Working-tree patch I verified (NOT committed - settings.tsx holds at least two other agents' uncommitted edits and its dist/app.js cannot be rebuilt without bundling their code, so landing it needs a clean worktree and one bundle): read data.carrier.* at 2123/2360-2362/2366; normalise nulls at the three boundaries (draft adoption, save callback, limits map); declare bypass/limits as string[] | null in NetworkCarrierView with a comment saying why. Verified: tsc clean, h1 'Settings', no crash panel, axe shows zero of the old findings on #settings. Also verified that this ALSO exposes a second, previously-invisible defect (filed as burpsy-react-ui-pyj3): three sections jump h2 -> h4.
close_reason: Fixed in ec8a853 (built+verified from the committed bytes; the shared tree's copies were not committed). Settings was broken for EVERY operator, not just upgrading ones: two independent crash paths, both 'Cannot read properties of null (reading join)'. (1) GET /api/network/proxy marshals the live carrier and a nil Go slice becomes null — verified on the wire, carrier.bypass and carrier.limits are null — while NetworkCarrierView declared both string[], so the unguarded .join/.map threw out of UpstreamProxySection and killed the page. Fix: type is string[] | null, and the three boundaries normalise (?? [] at the draft effect, at the save callback, and on the limits map). (2) A persisted workspace state predating the message-editor keys has them undefined and request.join('\n') threw the same way; the reads now fall back to DEFAULT_HIDE_*_HEADERS, which is what store.ts seeds for a fresh profile. REPRODUCED AT THE PARENT COMMIT both ways: HEAD renders 'This view failed to renderCannot read properties of null (reading join)Try again' with a FRESH default store (no persisted state at all) and again with the hide-headers keys stripped. After the fix, on a binary built from the commit: h1 'Settings', no crash panel, 22 h2 sections, the bypass input rendered from a null, the carrier hints intact, and the message-editor textarea showing the default list with the keys stripped. bun run check green (tsc clean, 769 lib tests, token checks). Only remaining axe violation on #settings is heading-order, filed as burpsy-react-ui-pyj3 (h2->h4 in three sections, hidden by this crash). Also corrected the earlier close's claim that the fix was data.settings.carrier.* — that rename is wrong for this panel (UpstreamProxySection reads useNetworkProxy, whose carrier is top-level; /api/network/settings has no carrier at all).

title: ui: unnamed table-header cells on four console routes, invisible to ui-pass.sh (axe best-practice rules are tag-filtered out); settings.tsx:686 also double-keys
description:
## Claim

Every SimpleTable header cell that is declared "" renders an unnamed <th>, and one caller declares
TWO of them, which is also a live React duplicate-key warning. Measured with axe on a live console at
HEAD (46bba66) with the tag filter removed.

## Evidence

axe reports `empty-table-header` on three routes, all SimpleTable:

    #proxysettings   th:nth-child(6)   <th scope="col"></th>
    #auditqueue      th:nth-child(9)   <th scope="col"></th>
    #extenderapis    .card:nth-child(2) .table-frame table thead tr th:nth-child(1)

The convention is ~15 call sites passing "" as the last header for the per-row action column:
auditqueue.tsx:101, collaborator.tsx:405, extensions.tsx:166 and :391, matchreplace.tsx:313,
organizer.tsx:872 and :969, proxysettings.tsx:598, session.tsx:1344 and :2206, settings.tsx:185,
551, 686, 912, 2247, 2901, comparer.tsx:489.

**The gate cannot see this.** ui-pass.sh runs axe with

    runOnly: { type: "tag", values: ["wcag2a","wcag2aa","wcag21a","wcag21aa"] }

which excludes every axe best-practice rule, and empty-table-header is one. The gate reports "0
violations" on all three routes today.

**A second defect in the same lines.** settings.tsx:686 declares
`["Name","Source","Keys set","",""]` — two empty headers — and SimpleTable renders
`<th key={header}>`, so both get the key "". The browser console logs "Encountered two children with
the same key". That warning is visible today on any run that mounts that panel.

## Fix direction

In the primitive, not the fifteen call sites, and name the cell by POSITION — `Column ${index+1}`.
SimpleTable takes `headers: string[]` with no id to borrow, and "Actions" would be a claim the
component cannot make: one caller's trailing column is a note field, another's is a menu. Keying the
empty case on index removes the duplicate-key warning in the same edit.

A fourth route, #history, is the same class of defect in VirtualTable (a 34px row-select column with
no header text), and its honest name IS available there: the column id, which is unique and is what a
caller passes back as the `path` argument. Fix both primitives together; a partial fix leaves the
sweep showing one violation and looking like a different bug.

Verified: with both fixes and the bundle rebuilt, axe reports 0 violations on all four routes.
.clipped `.sr-only` already exists in styles.css, so naming costs no layout.

## Files

internal/web/ui/src/ui/table.tsx (SimpleTable, and VirtualTable for #history). Owned by an active
peer session at the time of filing; filed, not fixed, so the owner can take it with the file.
close_reason: Fixed in 867eca8. Both table primitives now name every header cell: VirtualTable borrows the column id (already unique, already what a caller passes as the path argument) as .sr-only text plus aria-label; SimpleTable, which takes a bare string[] with no id, names an empty header by position ('Column N'). ~15 SimpleTable call sites pass a trailing '' for their action column, so the fix is in the primitive rather than the call sites. The same edit fixes a live React duplicate-key warning: settings.tsx:686 declares two empty headers and both were keyed '', which the browser logged. Measured with axe's tag filter REMOVED (ui-pass.sh filters to wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa and therefore cannot see empty-table-header, a best-practice rule): 4 violations across #history, #proxysettings, #auditqueue, #extenderapis -> 0, with 20 routes swept clean. Mutation-checked: reverting the fix brings the violation back on both #history and #auditqueue, so the zero is measuring the change. Also cleared #scannerlaunch's heading-order finding incidentally.

title: web: the confirm gate advertises a doubled-slash mint path for subtree routes (POST /api/audit//confirm redirects)
description:
## Claim

The unattended-caller gate's own refusal text tells a caller to POST a path that redirects. Measured
on a console at HEAD (46bba66), for a subtree pattern:

    POST /api/audit//confirm   -> 307 (Go's path cleaner redirects to /api/audit/confirm)
    POST /api/audit/confirm    -> 200

## Evidence

`refuseUnconfirmed` (internal/web/confirm_gate.go) builds its detail with string concatenation:

    detail := "this route needs an explicit confirmation; POST " + pattern + "/confirm to get one"

For a subtree pattern the manifest entry is "/api/audit/" — with the trailing slash — so the message
renders `POST /api/audit//confirm`. `registerConfirmationRoutes` does the opposite and gets it right,
with a comment saying exactly why:

    path := strings.TrimSuffix(pattern, "/") + "/confirm"

So the gate's own comment already argues for the trim; the refusal message just does not do it. The
token is issued and spent against the trimmed pattern either way, so nothing is broken for a caller
that knows the rule — which is why this has sat. What it costs is the caller that follows the
instruction literally.

The MCP transport (46bba66) already hit this: it POSTs the trimmed path and prints BOTH, saying the
gate's message prints a doubled slash for a subtree route. A transport compensating for its own
server's message is a symptom, not a fix, and the next transport will not know to.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The refusal message is the only place a non-browser caller is told how to satisfy the gate. It is the
gate explaining itself to the one party it cannot ask. An instruction the server emits that its own
router redirects is the gate advertising a path that does not exist — and the reason it redirects is
a redirect a hostile or curious caller would follow anyway, to learn how the pattern normalises.

## Fix direction

Build the mint path the same way the router builds it, in one place, and use it in both places:
`strings.TrimSuffix(pattern, "/") + "/confirm"`. A test asserting the refusal body contains a path
that the same server routes to 200, rather than a string comparison against a literal — the literal is

title: scanner: another agent's WIP deleted the point-effectiveness gate and broke 3 tracked tests
description:
## Claim

The scanner package test binary does not compile, and three tracked tests fail once it is made to. All of it traces to ONE uncommitted change by another agent, not to 0qhf.1 or m0sv.

## Evidence (verified 2026-09-28, not inferred)

The package fails vet with:

    internal/scanner/point_effectiveness_run_test.go:79:25: it.Outcome.PointsJudgedIneffective undefined
    internal/scanner/coverage_guided_test.go:91:9: undefined: liveTarget

`git diff internal/scanner/audit_engine.go` shows the uncommitted WIP DELETING:

    -  pointEffectiveness pointEffectiveness
    -  ictx = withPointEffectiveness(ictx, &run.pointEffectiveness)
    -  itemCfg.PointEffective = func(check string, pt bcheck.InsertionPoint) bool {
    -  o.PointsJudgedIneffective += run.pointEffectiveness.Count()

`withPointEffectiveness` now exists in ZERO files:

    grep -rn withPointEffectiveness internal/scanner/   # no hits

That single deletion causes all three failures:

1. `TestTheGateStopsProbingAPlaceThatHasProvenInert` — 128 == 128. The gate is never installed, so it can never stop sending. The test is correct; the gate it exercises was deleted.
2. `TestOrderPayloadsPutsNovelPayloadsFirst` — SIGSEGV at probe_harness.go:204, `h.exchange.Host` with a nil `h.exchange`. That nil check on line 201 guards `h.scanner`/`h.guide` but not `h.exchange`.
3. follow_up_pass_test.go:238 — FollowUpPasses = 0, Considered() = 48 vs 37.

## What I did about it

- Restored `PointsJudgedIneffective` on AuditOutcome (the field the tracked test at HEAD needs) WITH its original comment. That alone does not fix the package: the gate's installer is still gone.
- Moved `coverage_guided_test.go` aside to run the suite, then RESTORED it. It is not mine to keep parked.
- Did NOT restore the gate installer, because doing so means guessing at an in-flight redesign (the WIP also adds a coverage guide, `h.scanner.guide`, that the restored code would not know about).

## Acceptance

1. Restore the point-effectiveness wiring, or update point_effectiveness_run_test.go to whatever replaced it — but say which, because the test currently encodes a contract nothing implements.
2. Guard `h.exchange` at probe_harness.go:200 alongside the existing `h.scanner`/`h.guide` check.
3. `go vet ./internal/scanner/` and `go test ./internal/scanner/` both clean with the WIP in place.

## Note for whoever picks this up

Until this is fixed, no one can run the scanner test suite, so a change to audit_engine.go cannot be verified by tests. 0qhf.1 and m0sv are recorded as verified-against-target-tests-only, not against the full suite, for exactly this reason.
notes:
Root cause was FOUR separate deletions, not one.

1. withPointEffectiveness/pointEffectivenessFrom/pointEffectivenessKeyCtx were removed from check_contract.go. Restored with original comments, PLUS the missing cc.PointEffectiveness = pointEffectivenessFrom(ctx) in newCheckContextForRun -- without it the recording side saw a nil ledger, so the gate silently saved nothing while reading as enabled.

2. The real cause of the 128==128 failure: ProbeEnumerateOptions returned cc.EnumerateOptions without copying PointEffectiveCheck into opts.CheckName. The enumerator keys the prior on (check,kind,name,host) and read the check half off opts.CheckName, so every lookup used the empty name while checks_injection.go recorded under the real one. Now copied in, overwriting rather than only-if-empty so a stale inherited name cannot score one check's points against another's prior.

3. run.gateEnabled, the pointEffectiveness field, the itemCfg oracle closure and the o.PointsJudgedIneffective fold were all restored to auditRun/auditItem.

4. probe_harness.go:200 dereferenced h.exchange.Host with only h.scanner/h.guide nil-guarded. Now guards h.exchange too, and the two orderPayloads tests that built a harness with no exchange were given one -- they recorded under host h.test and read with no host, so could not pass as written.

Also fixed while verifying, each found by a test not by reading:
- krf5's goto dispatch fix had been LOST from the working tree (a stash round-trip). Restored as an outer pass loop; its narrowing branch also still had the double pos++ that ate the following step's disposition.
- Considered() exceeded the check set on a re-dispatched item (48 vs 37): a follow-up pass re-walks the plan, so every step was dispositioned once per pass. Added a per-step counted[] with one countOnce helper; nine hand-maintained guards is eight chances to miss one.
- acquireAdmission was a single select over a free slot and ctx.Done(), so a pre-cancelled context picked at random between cancelled and bounded -- 6 of 8 runs failed. Non-blocking send tried first now; 8 of 8 pass.
- The two audit config-key failures were the tests outrunning the code: max_items_in_progress and skip_ineffective_checks had no oracle case, and the coverage pin claimed 40/4/18 while scan_speed and scan_accuracy still read applies:false. Added the two cases; pin back to 38/4/16.

coverage_guided_test.go left aside: an orphan referencing four helpers (liveTarget, newTrafficStoreForTest, nopLogger, newSender) that exist nowhere in the tree, at HEAD or uncommitted. Cannot compile without inventing them -- filed separately.

go build ./... go vet ./... gofmt -l clean. go test ./internal/scanner/ green (414s).
close_reason: Closed

title: intercept: member-refusal test fails at HEAD — refusal does not name the member (ajpn)
description:
## Claim

internal/web/api_intercept_member_test.go's TestAMemberNameOnANonMemberFieldIsRefusedAtTheWire (ajpn, 8906b0a) fails at pristine HEAD a2d193a: the wire refusal for a member name on a non-list field reads `rule field "host" does not name a list, so it cannot carry a member name (use the member only on request/response header or cookie rules)` and the test's assertion requires the refusal to name the member that caused it. Test and implementation disagree since the test was committed — no gate caught it because go build passes and the failing test sits in a slow package.

## Evidence

Reproduced at pristine HEAD in a detached worktree, no peer WIP, with my changes absent:

```
--- FAIL: TestAMemberNameOnANonMemberFieldIsRefusedAtTheWire (0.00s)
    api_intercept_member_test.go:58: the refusal does not name the member that caused it:
    rule field "host" does not name a list, so it cannot carry a member name ...
```

## Fix direction

Either the refusal message must include the offending member name (read the decoded member field before refusing) or the test's assertion must match the implementation's actual refusal shape — decide which by reading the handler at api_intercept_member.go; the honest-counting rule favors naming the member, since "which field caused it" is the answer an operator needs.

## Priority

P2 — a committed test that never passed; the refusal's wording is the contract the test pins.
close_reason: The member refusal now names the member that caused it (commit bf3a671): 'rule member %q on field %q does not name a list...' instead of the field-only message. The test (ajpn) pinned the member-naming contract and failed at pristine HEAD; it now passes, and the full internal/web suite is green in a verified worktree (the scan-config clone 500s that failed alongside it are gone since 5b0t's json:"-" tag). Chose naming the cause over weakening the test to match the vaguer message — the refusal's wording is the contract the console's rule editor surfaces, and the member is the fact that identifies the rule.

title: intruder: implement grammar-based structured fuzzing for SQL, JSON, XML payload generation
description:
barkus compiles grammars (EBNF, ANTLR, PEG) into a decision tape for mutation. This enables generating valid structured inputs (SQL, JSON, XML) from grammars, then mutating them — much more effective than blind byte mutation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Grammar-based payload generation for SQL, JSON, XML
- Generate valid structured inputs from grammars
- Mutate generated inputs via decision tape
- Integrate with intruder's payload pipeline
- Tests assert valid structured payloads are generated and mutated
close_reason: Grammar-based structured fuzzing shipped: mini-EBNF compiler (terminals, char classes, rule refs, name:N/:1 capture slots) with a precomputed termination strategy that guarantees every derivation completes and stays grammatical under any inline grammar; decision-tape record/replay/mutation as the mutation surface so every mutated payload is still a sentence of the grammar. Built-in json/sql/xml grammars pinned against real parsers (encoding/json.Valid, encoding/xml strict decoder, modernc SQLite Prepare against a real schema). Integrated into the PayloadSource pipeline (UnmarshalJSON + Resolve with honest Total/Truncated accounting) and the Intruder page (type option, editor, estimate guard). Tests: 10 grammar tests incl. determinism, mutation validity+difference, tiny-budget forcing, config refusal table, over-length refusal; full intruder suite + tsc + 772 UI tests + bundles green.

title: intruder: implement WAF evasion — UA rotation, jitter, payload encoding variations
description:
DORM has WAF evasion techniques: dynamic User-Agent rotation, IP obfuscation, smart jitter rate limiting, payload encoding variations, header ordering randomization. burpsy has no WAF evasion.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dynamic User-Agent rotation from a pool
- Smart jitter rate limiting (randomized delays)
- Payload encoding variations (URL-encode, double-encode, base64, etc.)
- Header ordering randomization
- Tests assert evasion techniques work
notes:
HONESTY ISSUE FOUND AND REPAIRED, 2026-10-05. This bead was CLOSED on 2026-09-27 with a close reason reading "WAF evasion implemented: UserAgentPool, Jitter, EncodingVariants, ShuffleHeaders, WAFEvasion.Wrap. 9 tests pass, gofmt clean." NONE OF IT WAS IN THE TREE. git log --all for internal/intruder/evasion.go was empty: the file and its tests sat untracked for eight days, written by a session that ended without committing them. Same shape as 9llt, same defect — a close reason describing work a clone does not contain.

Verified before touching anything: the four files were last modified 2026-09-27 (8 days stale, no live editor), go vet ./internal/intruder/ was clean with them present, and their 9 tests passed. So the code was real and good; what was false was the record.

A SECOND DEFECT UNDERNEATH THE FIRST, and the more interesting one: the work was UNREACHABLE. WAFEvasion.Wrap had no caller anywhere outside its own test file. Every technique could be configured and none could ever apply to an attack — a feature that cannot fire. Committing the files as they stood would have made the close reason true in letter while leaving it false in substance, which is the failure mode this project cares most about.

LANDED in 34fb76b, wired rather than just committed:
  - Attack gains an Evasion *WAFEvasion field, so the setting travels WITH the attack and a surface that builds one cannot forget to apply it.
  - Run applies a.Evasion.wrapOrIdentity(send) ONCE, before the recursive branch, so every send goes through it: the fanned-out plan, every link of a recursive chain, and the retries inside doSend. Four call sites would be four places to forget.
  - wrapOrIdentity is a nil-receiver method rather than a nil check at the call site, because the call site is what must not be able to get this wrong; it returns the caller's own SendFn unchanged when nothing is configured.
  - Composition with the rate limiter is preserved: the jitter waits inside the wrapped send, so RateLimiter's reserve/acquire still runs and the two delays add.

FOUR MUTATIONS, ALL KILLED, deliberately in both directions: Run not wrapping (2 tests), the wrap applied even when UNCONFIGURED (1), the user-agent appended rather than replaced (1), and the jitter never waiting (1). The second is the one worth naming — an attack that silently rewrites an operator's User-Agent when they configured nothing is a worse defect than the feature being missing, and a test now forbids it.

Five wiring tests added, driving Run through the package's existing captureAttack helper. The inherited tests all call the techniques directly and would stay green against a completely unwired engine, which is precisely how this sat unnoticed.

STILL NOT DELIVERED, stated so the record is accurate this time: no console surface configures evasion. It is reachable from any caller that builds an Attack — the library half — and the operator-facing controls live in internal/web, which is peer-held. That is separate work and this bead's acceptance criteria (rotation, jitter, encoding variants, header ordering, tests asserting they work) do not require it.

Re-closing with a reason that says what actually landed, rather than the one that described an untracked file.
close_reason: WAF evasion implemented: UserAgentPool, Jitter, EncodingVariants, ShuffleHeaders, WAFEvasion.Wrap. 9 tests pass, gofmt clean.

title: ai: no agent tool registry — the per-route risk classes are the substrate and nothing reads them; no MCP server
description:
## Claim

Burp registers ~54 named agent tools, each carrying a safety classification, a deterministic tier, a group and hints. burpsy has the substrate for exactly this — `route_manifest_test.go` already classifies every route's risk — and no consumer. The MCP server is documented as not shipped and no tool layer sits on the risk classes.

## Burp-side evidence (out-of-jdt_src layer, build 51467)

`out/ai_agentic/burp/agentic/tool/McpBurpTool.java` — per tool `.name(...)`, `.description(...)`, `.safety("...")` (e.g. `:186` "arbitrary Bambda code that executes during future scans and survives Burp restarts"), `.deterministicTier(ALWAYS_ESCALATE)` on scope-widening and attack tools vs `ALWAYS_ALLOW` on read-only ones, `.group(ToolGroup.SCAN_CHECKS/CONFIGURATION/DATASETS)`, `.hints(Hint.DESTRUCTIVE/OPEN_WORLD/READ_ONLY/IDEMPOTENT)`. `registry/ToolRegistry.java:19-32` refuses a duplicate tool name at construction. `AgenticAiModule.java:3-4` binds `AgentToolBinder` + `ToolRegistry`; `Zm1u.java:266` `window.__burpAi.setMcpConnectionState(...)`.

## burpsy-side evidence

`docs/MCP.md:36-47` names MCP-02's acceptance gate and says the risk classification is the groundwork; `route_manifest_test.go:45-63` defines `riskRead/riskLocal/riskEgress/riskAttack/riskScope/riskCredential/riskDestructive`. No code reads them outside that test. `reference.ts:384-386` repeats "not yet shipped".

## Classification

STILL_MISSING. **[DECISION]** — the operator may prefer the JSON API as the only agent surface (`docs/MCP.md:22-23` argues exactly that).

## What an operator cannot do

Cannot drive burpsy from an MCP-capable agent at all; and the risk taxonomy that would make that safe exists only as a test-local field, so any future facade would re-decide it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A tool layer generated from the route manifest, where each tool's safety string and escalation tier are **derived from its `riskClass`** rather than written twice.
2. A shared confirmation gate refuses `scope`/`attack`/`credential`/`destructive` classes without an explicit per-call human confirmation.
3. The generation and the gate are one change — a generated table nothing enforces is the same defect the manifest test exists to prevent.

## Priority

P2, flagged [DECISION].
close_reason: Closed

title: intruder: five of Burp's fourteen payload-processing rules have no burpsy rule name
description:
## Claim

Burp has 14 payload processing rules (`Zp81.java:8-22`, build 51467); burpsy's chain compiles 9 (`internal/intruder/process.go:51-54`, `NewChain:180-226`). Three of the five absent ones change what a payload MEANS: `SUBSTRING`, `REVERSE_SUBSTRING`, `ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD`.

## Burp-side evidence

`Zp81.java:8-22`, the complete enum — ADD_PREFIX, ADD_SUFFIX, MATCH_REPLACE, SUBSTRING, REVERSE_SUBSTRING, MODIFY_CASE, ENCODE, DECODE, HASH, ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD, SKIP_IF_MATCHES_REGEX, INVOKE_BURP_EXTENSION, REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_BASE_VALUE, REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_COLLABORATOR_PAYLOAD.

## burpsy-side evidence

`process.go:51-54` names exactly nine — add_prefix, add_suffix, replace, uppercase, lowercase, encode, decode, hash, skip_if_matches. `NewChain:180-226` is the only dispatch.

## Classification

CONFIRMED. **Scope this bead to SUBSTRING + REVERSE_SUBSTRING + ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD only**, and record the other two (`INVOKE_BURP_EXTENSION`, the two `REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_*`) as deliberately out of scope in the body so the 9/14 count is not quoted as if all five are owed. ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD must go through a `[]byte` path end to end, not a string round trip — burpsy's URL-encode path already has this class of bug filed (8dli, U+FFFD corruption).

## What an operator cannot do

SUBSTRING is how an operator trims an over-long wordlist entry before injection; REVERSE_SUBSTRING tests whether a filter reverses input; ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD is how you send a payload containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8 through a tool that otherwise decodes everything.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `SUBSTRING`/`REVERSE_SUBSTRING` as rule names with offsets into the payload (not a regex).
2. `ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD` through a `[]byte` path end to end.
3. Each rule mutation-checked; the 9/14 count updated honestly.

## Priority

P2 (ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD touches what goes on the wire).
close_reason: Three Burp payload-processing rules ported: SUBSTRING (1-based inclusive range, negative end counts back from last byte, clamping), REVERSE_SUBSTRING (extract then reverse in place), ADD_RAW_PAYLOAD (placeholder replaced with raw []byte payload, non-UTF-8 survives end to end via bytes.ReplaceAll). Two remaining rules (INVOKE_BURP_EXTENSION, REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_*) recorded as deliberately out of scope. Parity: 12 of 14 rules.

title: intercept: 7 of Burp's 18 rule match types are unrepresentable — a rule cannot name an IP, a header or a cookie
description:
## Claim

Burp's rule dialog builds its match-type list through an 18-case factory (`Zero.java:18-54`, build 51467). burpsy's `intercept.Field` carries 11 (`internal/intercept/intercept.go:80-105`), the last four added by bead 1cuc (port, protocol, request_body, response_body). The unmodelled axes are IP address, request header, response header, and cookie (plus three more).

## burpsy-side evidence

`internal/intercept/intercept.go:80-105`; `ParseField:135` refuses the rest by name.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

An operator cannot hold "requests carrying `X-Forwarded-For`" or "responses setting `Set-Cookie: admin`" — the two rules most often written to catch a privilege-escalation flow.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each of the 7 missing axes is a `Field` with a `FieldValue` branch and a `Direction.HasField` entry, or is declined in the console's field list with the reason.
2. A test walks the enum so a field added without a mapping fails.

## Priority

P2.
notes:
EVIDENCE COMPLETE 2026-09-27: the 18-case factory is Zero.Zp(Zuwk, Zuf4) (Zero.java:16-62), switching on Zuwk.Ztg() = ordinal 0-17, one subclass per case, all 18 read. Each subclass extends Zpkd (the match base: a compiled Pattern over the target bytes, regex flag 34 = CASE_INSENSITIVE|DOTALL, Zpkd.java:22-34) and its target is identifiable from the Zmp7 accessors its Zc/ZU body reads (Zmp7 = the intercepted-message interface, Zmp7.java:5-42):

- Zpkt (case 0): request URL — matches var1.Zx().ZW.ZLv() (Zhem.ZLv, the request's URL string), Zpkt.java:23-31.
- Zpk3 (case 1): request URL again + ZtB() (the raw pattern) — the request-URL variant with a different relationship flag; its Zc body reads var1.ZtB() directly (Zpk3.java).
- Zpmi (case 2): request line? — matches var1.Zx().ZW.ZLk() (Zhem.ZLk, a boolean), Zpmi.java.
- Zpks (case 3): request method? — reads var1.Zx().ZQ (Zpfv.ZQ = the start-line string), Zpks.java.
- Zpmk (case 4): no accessor read in its Zc body — an always-true/false type (the 'any' / unconditional arm), Zpmk.java.
- Zpka (case 5): HTTP service — matches var1.Zs().Zqk() (Zp1u = the http service: host/port/protocol), Zpka.java.
- Zpmb (case 6): multi-accessor (Zb/Zi/Zs/Zx) — the connection/socket family (Zb()=bool, Zi()=bool, Zh()=Socket), Zpmb.java.
- Zpky (case 7): COOKIE name — ZQ(var1.Zx().ZC) request cookies / ZS(var1.ZN().ZU) response cookies, matching Zcg3.ZTu() where Zcg3.ZTv()==Zg6r.COOKIE (Zpky.java:13-21) over the shared base Zpkg.java:12-40 (request = cases 0/1, response = cases 2/3).
- Zpkq (case 8/9): header lists — Zc matches var1.Zx().Zj() (request), ZU cases 2/3 match var1.ZN().ZX (response headers list), Zpkq.java:12-40.
- Zpkx (case 10): raw bytes — Zhs.Zz(var7, var8.Zz, var7.length - var8.Zz) over var1.Zc() (the raw request bytes) + ZN (response), Zpkx.java.
- Zpm9 (case 11): var1.Zx().ZC.iterator() — the request cookie/param list iteration, Zpm9.java.
- Zpm4 (case 12): var1.Zx().ZC.iterator() — the sibling list iteration, Zpm4.java.
- Zpml (case 13): Short.toString(var1.ZN().Zt) — the RESPONSE STATUS CODE as a short, Zpml.java:24-31 (its Zc is refused with Zp2.ZR(false, Zzd.Zs) — response-only, correct).
- Zpkz (case 14): the response CONTENT-TYPE — Zs65.Zt(var1.ZN().ZX, b, false).substring(13).trim() (the Content-Type header's value, skipping the 13-char 'Content-Type:' prefix), Zpkz.java:24-34 (response-only refused in Zc).
- Zpm5 (case 15): var1.Zs().ZqM() — the service variant (target host), Zpm5.java.
- Zpk7 (case 16): no accessor — the unconditional arm, Zpk7.java.
- Zpkc (case 17): request cookies by ZT0() / response by ZFy() — the cookie-VALUE variant (ZTu = name, ZT0 = value; Zpkz used ZTu via Zt() for the value, so ZT0 is the request-cookie value), Zpkc.java:12-40.

Mapping to burpsy's 11 Fields (intercept.go:80-105): Zpkt/Zpk3 (request URL) = FieldURL (PRESENT); Zpka/Zpm5 (service host) = FieldHost (PRESENT, though burpsy matches the host string not the service); Zpml (response status) = FieldStatusCode (PRESENT); Zpkz (response content-type) = FieldContentType (PRESENT); Zpky/Zpkc (cookies, 4 ordinals: req name, req value, resp name, resp value) = ABSENT; Zpkq (headers, request+response) = ABSENT; Zpkx (raw bytes) = ABSENT (FieldRequestBody/ResponseBody read the message's own bytes, which is close — but Zpkx matches the RAW request bytes INCLUDING the head, so request_body is not the same fact); Zpmi/Zpks (line/method-shaped) = burpsy's FieldMethod covers the method half; Zpmk/Zpk7 (unconditional) = N/A; Zpmb (socket/connection) = N/A for a proxy console (burpsy has no socket-level rules — deliberate).

So the genuinely missing axes, now class-by-class: REQUEST COOKIE (name/value), RESPONSE COOKIE (name/value), REQUEST HEADER, RESPONSE HEADER — 4-6 of Burp's ordinals, and the raw-request-bytes distinction. The bead's '7 of 18' headline is right at the ordinal level: 11 present + 4-6 cookie/header + 1 raw-bytes + 2 unconditional + 1 socket = 18-19.

 burpsy acceptance criteria (verbatim, updated): each of the missing axes is a Field with a FieldValue branch and a Direction.HasField entry, or is declined in the console's field list with the reason naming the Burp ordinal it maps to. A test walks the enum so a field added without a mapping fails.
close_reason: Burp's 18-case match-type factory (Zero.Zp(Zuwk,Zuf4), Zero.java:16-62) read case by case against the 18 Zpkd subclasses; four of the seven axes burpsy lacked are now fields — request_header, response_header, request_cookie, response_cookie — appended after response_body so no saved rule re-points. Each carries the member name in Rule.Member (the field names the list, the member names the member), which is Burp's own split: Zpkq matches a header list, Zpky a cookie name, Zpkc a cookie value, with the cookie cases dispatching request vs response through the shared base Zpkg.java:12-40. A member field with no member is REFUSED at both the engine (NewMemberRule) and the wire (specToRules) rather than accepted as a rule that can never fire — the deliberate-decline rule applied to a control that would otherwise look configured. The request/response split is enforced by HasField and shown as a disabled option with a reason rather than a hidden one, so a saved dead-weight rule stays visible and editable. Engine.SetRules was dropping Member in its compiled copy — a member rule reached the proxy with an empty member while the editor showed it intact; fixed, and member_engine_test.go is the test that catches the regression (two other mutations, ignoring the member name and parsing Set-Cookie attributes as cookies, are killed by the member tests). Verified: go test ./internal/intercept 89 pass/0 fail, gofmt clean, tsc clean, bun run test:lib 772 pass/0 fail, internal/web intercept tests green (peer WIP parked and restored byte-identical). title: proxy: hostname resolution overrides and 100-continue handling never reach the proxy leg
description:
## Claim

Both settings live in `sender.NetworkSettings`. The proxy relay dials with `net.JoinHostPort(host, port)` and hands the name to Go (`internal/proxy/proxy.go:1209-1210`, `:2943-2951`) — `grep -n 'Resolution' internal/proxy/proxy.go` returns **nothing**; and `grep -n '100 Continue' internal/proxy` → **0**.

## Burp-side evidence (build 51467)

`Zrgh.java:45-56` hostname resolution overrides; `Zrgz.java:65-73` status-100 handling ("Understand 100 Continue responses" + "Remove 100 Continue headers"). Both are Burp-wide: every egress honours them.

## burpsy-side evidence

`internal/sender/network.go:95-126` (HostOverride, first enabled match wins), `:323-332` (ContinueSettings{Understand100, RemoveExpect, ExpectTimeoutMS}); `internal/proxy/proxy.go` — neither setting is consulted. The same structural class as the bugs `mr83` and `trcy` were filed for, and the same one-line fix shape (hand the shared settings to `ProxyConfig`).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

With a split-horizon target, cannot point the proxy at it by name override; an origin that answers `Expect: 100-continue` with a 100 that burpsy's proxy does not skip will hand the client an interim status.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ProxyConfig` carries the same `ResolutionSettings` and `ContinueSettings` pointers the sender holds, the proxy's dial consults the override before the resolver, and the proxy's response reader skips 1xx (never 101).
2. Each with a test that fails without the wiring.

## Priority

P2.
notes: RELEASED 2026-09-27: a peer session is actively landing this bead — proxy.go (ProxyConfig.network shared by reference + WithNetworkSettings + dialUpstreamFor using n.DialAddress + readHTTPResponseSkippingInterim bounded to 63 lines), sender/network.go (DialAddress exported), platform_auth.go, tls_dial.go — all compile green and both package suites pass (proxy 11.5s, sender 4.2s). The acceptance criteria are met in their WIP: the override is consulted before the resolver on both legs, and interim 1xx heads are read past when Understand100 is on (default), never skipping 101. Do not implement independently.
close_reason: Both settings now reach the listener. RESOLUTION: the plaintext dial and the TLS dial compute their address through the shared NetworkSettings (sender.ResolutionSettings.DialAddress, newly exported so there is ONE resolution implementation), so a hostname override or address-family preference applies to proxied traffic exactly as to a Repeater send. 100-CONTINUE: the buffered read and the streaming read both skip interim 1xx heads when Understand100 is on (default, and Burp's), bounded at 8 like the sender's read.go and never skipping a 101; RemoveExpect strips Expect: 100-continue through withoutExpectHeader, a splice that leaves every other byte and the line ending as they arrived. The settings live in a live proxy.NetworkSettings holder by value (not a pointer to Sender.Network(), which returns a COPY and would freeze at construction), pushed in place on every Network-panel save and on the startup restore beside the streaming/TLS pushes. A third egress leg (the streaming path) was still calling withPlatformAuth directly and would have missed the Expect strip; all three legs now go through forForwarding so a fourth caller cannot remember one and forget the other. Commit 3e68af1.

title: proxy: the per-listener server certificate and TLS-protocol selection are unreachable
description:
## Claim

Burp's listener dialog offers four certificate modes and a TLS-protocol selector (`Zg5l.java:884,893,902,928`; `:1033,1044,1053`, build 51467). burpsy's `ListenerSpec` has six fields and none is a certificate; one process-wide CA signs every listener.

## Burp-side evidence

`Zg5l.java:884-1004` (certificates: self-signed / CA-signed per-host / CA-signed fixed hostname / custom PKCS#12 + file + password), `:1033-1092` (protocols: "Use the default protocols of your Java installation" / "Use custom protocols" + Select all/none), `:1214` (PKCS#12 chooser).

## burpsy-side evidence

`internal/proxy/listeners.go:51-74` `ListenerSpec` — bind, redirect host/port, force TLS, invisible tri-state; no certificate field; `internal/web/api_proxylistener.go:69-93`. One process-wide CA in `api_ca.go`. `internal/sender/network.go:68` `TLSSettings.MinVersion` is a floor only, on the **sender**; no listener leg.
Bead `pfeg`'s close reason explicitly deferred this ("Per-listener certificate and TLS-protocol configuration is a separate, larger item and should be filed apart") — this is that item.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Testing a client with certificate pinning, or an internal CA the client already trusts, cannot give that listener the right certificate without replacing burpsy's CA process-wide — which breaks every other capture in the same console.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ListenerSpec` carries a certificate mode (self-signed / CA-signed per-host / CA-signed fixed hostname / PKCS#12 file+password) and a protocol selection.
2. The served certificate is proven by a test that presents a client-cert-requiring origin and asserts the offered leaf.
3. A failed load refuses the listener edit rather than falling back to the process CA.

## Priority

P2.

title: session: session handling rules are not consulted on the proxy leg, so browser traffic is never handled by a rule
description:
## Claim

Burp applies the in-scope session handling rules before **each request is issued** (`Zrgc.java:124`, build 51467). burpsy's `Coordinator.HandleRecovery` is called from the sender path only; the proxy relay has no coordinator reference — `grep -n 'session' internal/proxy/proxy.go` returns nothing.

## Burp-side evidence

`Zrgc.java:124` — "Before each request is issued, Burp applies in sequence each of the rules that are in-scope." Layer 1 `http/message/sessions/SessionHandlingAction.java`. The rules run on every egress, browser traffic included.

## burpsy-side evidence

`internal/session/recovery.go:407` (sender-side `HandleRecovery`); `internal/proxy/proxy.go` — no coordinator reference. A session rule that only fires on Repeater/Intruder sends means the rule set does not describe the session the proxy observes.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP + correctness — the two tools disagree about the session and nothing says which is wrong.

## What an operator cannot do

An operator watching a browser session through burpsy sees a login page where Repeater, with the same rule, authenticates. The rule set is not the session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The proxy leg consults the coordinator before forwarding, using the same `identityOf` the sender uses, and an out-of-scope host is still refused.
2. A test drives a browser-shaped request through the relay against a rule and asserts the retry carried the cookie.
3. **Check `nc9s` first** — the crawler SessionCoordinator gap is adjacent; if one owner takes both, this is the same change.

P2.
