title: organizer: no in-scope, status or MIME filter
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. organizer.tsx's table is headers ['#','Exchange','Title','Highlight','Note',''] (line 174) with no filter controls at all: zero references to in-scope, status or MIME. Burp's Organizer has organiserShowOnlyInScopeCheckbox plus status and MIME-type filters.

This one is real, unlike most of the batch it arrived in — the page genuinely has no filtering, and an organizer that only grows is unusable once it holds more than a screenful.

Scope note: the exchanges are already stored with status and MIME available (the Exchange column resolves them), so this is a UI filter over data that is present, not a new query path.
acceptance_criteria: Organizer offers in-scope-only, status-class and MIME filters; they compose; the empty result of a filter is distinguishable from an empty organizer.
close_reason: Done in 69ce17b. Backend: api_organizer_view.go resolves each saved item against the traffic store and the scope (server-side, because that is where both live). Frontend: in-scope-only checkbox, status class select including a 'No response' option, and a MIME select whose options are derived from what is actually saved rather than a fixed vocabulary. The design decision worth reading: an item whose exchange has been EVICTED cannot be judged, so resolved=false, every derived field is ABSENT rather than zero, and such rows are exempt from every filter rather than failing it — dropping them would hide a note the operator wrote at exactly the moment they are searching, and defaulting to status 0 / mime '' / in_scope false would make the row answer questions it cannot. The row says 'exchange no longer retained' and the toolbar reports 'N shown unjudged' next to the count. Also carried: status is optional because a request that never came back is not a status of zero, and has_response separates 'no response' from 'a response that named no usable Content-Type' (core.Exchange.Mime is '' for both, and the store's own doc says not to render them identically). Split OrganizerEdit from OrganizerItem so a save cannot claim to know a derived field. Seven tests; the three honesty cases were mutation-tested (default the fields / drop the row / hardcode has_response) and each mutation fails the test written for it. Full suite: exit 0, 37 packages, 0 failures. bun run test:lib 79 pass. dist/app.js deliberately not rebuilt while another agent holds three UI files.

title: site map: no crawl-paths view and no passive-scan branch controls
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. sitemap.tsx is a URL tree plus a table in a SplitPane; it contains no 'view' switch of any kind (zero matches for 'view' in 22KB — confirmed not grep-invisibility: the file has no NUL bytes and a positive control on the same file matches 'import' 16 times).

Missing, both real:
1. Crawl paths view — Burp toggles between URL view and Crawl paths view, the latter showing how the crawler reached each node rather than where it sits in the path hierarchy. burpsy has crawl data (internal/crawler) but never presents it as reachability.
2. Passive-scan branch controls — Burp's 'Passively scan this branch' / 'Passively scan selected branches'. burpsy has no per-branch scan action.

Note the tree already carries out-of-scope marking and subtree finding counts (lines 127, 159, 168), so the per-node action surface exists to hang these off.
acceptance_criteria: The site map can switch between URL and crawl-paths presentations; a branch can be sent for passive scanning and reports what it queued.
close_reason: Crawl-paths half done in 565c6c7; passive-scan half re-filed as a decision. The view existed nowhere because the DATA existed nowhere: frontierItem.foundAt was documented 'reporting only' and populated on every REFUSAL, so the graph the crawler declined to walk was reconstructible and the graph it actually walked was not. Fetch now carries FoundAt and LinkText off the frontier item that already had them; Report.Fetches was already on the wire, so no new endpoint. Depth said how far from a seed, this says which way — two pages at depth 2 can have entirely different parents, which is what a depth-only rendering cannot express and what a test now pins. THREE STATES THE VIEW REFUSES TO FLATTEN: a seed has no found_at and absent means seed, not unknown; an ORPHAN (parent refused, dropped at a limit, or retention-excluded) is shown under a heading saying so, because dropping it understates coverage — the request was made — and re-parenting it to a seed asserts a path nobody walked; a duplicate has no children by design, which is not the same as being a leaf. Three empty states, not one, because an empty view during a running crawl is the case most likely to be misread as a result. The tree builder is pure, exported and tested as structure, with an iterative sort walk and a visited set because the input describes a target's link graph and a found_at cycle must not spin the render. Mutation-tested: removing the edge fails all four crawler tests (the original bug reproduced), and drop-orphans and re-parent-orphans each fail three UI tests. Full suite exit 0, 37 packages, 0 failures; bun run test:lib 99 pass.

title: proxy settings: TLS pass-through and resource pools are absent
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. Two Burp proxy-settings sections have no counterpart.

1. TLS pass-through — Burp's configPanelProxyTlsPassThrough / proxy.ssl_pass_through: a host-pattern list whose matches are relayed without MITM. Absent. The single grep hit in proxysettings.tsx:74 is unrelated prose ('as they pass through the proxy'), not a feature.

2. Resource pools — Burp's configPanelResourcePoolsEditBtn: named pools with concurrency and delay, assignable per tool. Zero references in proxysettings.tsx. Note that Intruder already has its own per-attack resource-pool controls (intruder.tsx:1024), so the gap is the shared, named, cross-tool pool rather than the concept.

Check before building: TLS pass-through needs a decision about what happens to a host that is both in scope and pass-through, and pass-through traffic cannot appear in history at all — that is the point of it, and it must be visible in the UI that this is why the host is missing.
acceptance_criteria: TLS pass-through host patterns can be added and removed and are honoured by the proxy; a named resource pool can be created and assigned; a pass-through host's absence from history is explained on screen.
close_reason: FALSE ON BOTH COUNTS, and the error was mine — I wrote the verified body for this issue and I verified it wrong. TLS PASS-THROUGH EXISTS, fully: route GET/POST/DELETE /api/proxy/passthrough (internal/web/api_tlspolicy.go, in the route manifest at route_manifest_test.go:446), typed hooks usePassthrough/useAddPassthrough/useRemovePassthrough in lib/data.policy.ts, and a functional panel at pages/settings.tsx:407 with add, remove, live-apply and an explanatory notice stating that a matched connection is relayed untouched and never appears in history. RESOURCE POOLS EXIST: /api/pools and /api/pools/ with lib/data.pools.ts and a named-pool panel in settings.tsx (~line 1999) including the support table that shows which tools name each pool. Both live on the SETTINGS page rather than Proxy settings — which is also where Burp puts TLS pass-through (Settings → TLS), so it is not even a placement divergence. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: the issue's framing was 'not in Proxy settings page', and I grepped proxysettings.tsx alone and reported the absence as verified. That is the identical failure I had just diagnosed in the original audit — reasoning about where a feature ought to live instead of searching for whether it exists — committed while explicitly claiming to have avoided it. The single grep hit I dismissed as 'unrelated prose' was unrelated prose; the feature was in another file I never looked at. Nothing to build. Reopen only if someone wants these surfaced on the Proxy settings page as well, which is a placement question and not a capability gap.

title: WS compressed frames (RSV bits) not supported
description:
## What's missing
wsHoldable() refuses any frame with RSV bits set (permessage-deflate). Burp inflates compressed frames.

## Evidence
- internal/proxy/ws.go:421-425 — wsHoldable() refuses compressed frames
- stripWsHandshake() removes Sec-WebSocket-Extensions by default, so this only arises when operator disables stripping

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inflate DEFLATE-compressed payloads
- [ ] Hold/re-edit/re-compress on forward
- [ ] Only when operator has disabled extension stripping

Found by: BlueBison (code grep ws.go:421)
close_reason: Decided and partially built in ecdd831. DECODING: compressed messages are inflated for the operator's view where the handshake agreed no_context_takeover for that direction (core/websocket_deflate.go). EDITING compressed messages is deliberately REFUSED, not omitted: RFC 7692 s7.1.1 lets the LZ77 window carry across messages, so re-compressing only the edited ones corrupts every LATER message on the connection. Where decoding is not provably correct the message stays compressed and the note names the missing parameter, because a fresh window yields convincing WRONG plaintext on a surface read as evidence. Reopen if editing compressed frames is actually wanted; that is a whole-direction recompress, not a patch.

title: crawl: Burp's shipped defaults for parse_api_definitions, parse_soap_wsdls and perform_graphql_introspection are not recorded — burpsy's no-config crawl has them off
description:
Follow-up from PR #341 (tyso), which wired the switches but left defaults unchanged.

## Evidence
The tree does not record Burp's shipped default for these three crawl switches; a crawl with no named configuration runs with all three off.

## Task
Establish Burp's defaults (from its shipped configuration library) and decide whether burpsy's no-config crawl should match them, recording the decision in gaps.md.
close_reason: MERGED via integrator (b57953a4). Burp's shipped defaults established from the current community JAR (build 47134, parsed over HTTP ranges, never executed; cross-build confidence via 7 sibling values byte-identical to the 2026.7.1 tree): parse_api_definitions, parse_soap_wsdls, perform_graphql_introspection all ON, guess_hidden_graphql_endpoints OFF. No-config crawl now matches Burp on the two READ-ONLY readers (their only traffic is ordinary GETs through admit()). GraphQL introspection deliberately stays OFF without a named configuration - the one switch that makes a crawl originate a POST of its own initiative, against the no-config-crawl-does-not-write rule (SubmitForms carries the same rule as 'a requirement rather than a default'). Named configurations still decide all five. Caveat recorded in gaps.md (integrator re-application 1cc9a3b4): named configs REPLACE not overlay, so a saved config omitting the keys runs readers off where Burp runs them on - closing that needs the o0c5 pointer-family treatment, filed as follow-up scope.

title: sitemap: four node-identity leftovers from u6f8 — query-with-slash placement, item delete leaves query variants, hidden items count toward the cap, unrequested items render depth 0
description:
Found next to u6f8 in PR #334 (to file).

## Evidence
1. A grey (unrequested) item whose query contains "/" is placed in the tree by its raw path instead of sitemap.NodePath.
2. Deleting an item on a clean path leaves its query variants visible until Sync.
3. Hidden unrequested items still count toward the 20000 unrequested-item cap.
4. Unrequested and inserted items render with depth:0.

## Consequence
The tree misplaces or keeps showing items the operator removed, and the cap can be reached by items the operator never sees.

title: editor: editable-editor selection actions (in-place convert, copy selection, palette transforms) flatten CRLF to LF across a line break — a converted or copied selection loses its CR bytes
description:

## Evidence
Editable editors write the document back with LF line endings, so in-place Convert selection, copy-selection and the command palette's selection transforms see \n where the message has \r\n.

## Consequence
A selection spanning a line break is transformed or copied without its CR bytes, altering the request.

Undoing a conversion still restores LF from CodeMirror history (filed separately).

title: extscan: nuclei hits parsed before a timeout are reported as a completed run — a cut-short scan reads as a clean finish
description:
Reported as still open in PR #339 (which made a killed tool an error and flagged incomplete captured output at the same call sites).

## Evidence
When nuclei times out, the hits parsed so far are returned as the result of a completed run.

## Consequence

title: scanner: the tool-runner timeout does not bound a call whose tool starts a child process — TestExecToolRunnerTimesOut sets 50ms and takes 5s every run
description:
Found while profiling the test suite for PR #331.

## Evidence
- TestExecToolRunnerTimesOut sets a 50ms timeout, yet the test takes about 5s on every run.
- ExecToolRunner's timeout kills the direct process, but a child process it spawned keeps the stdout/stderr pipes open, so the call returns only when that child exits.

## Consequence
The timeout does not bound a tool call whose tool starts a child process, so a hung child stalls the scan for as long as it lives.

## Fix direction
Run the tool in its own process group (Setpgid, then kill -pgid on timeout), or set WaitDelay on the exec.Cmd. Add a test asserting the call returns within a small multiple of the timeout.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #339 (merge 9cc6f3d): new internal/procgroup Contain(cmd): on unix the tool leads its own process group and timeout/cancel kills the group (pid-reuse safe), WaitDelay=1s everywhere; applied to the scanner tool runner, extscan and tlsprobe. TestExecToolRunnerTimesOut went from ~5.0s to 0.05-0.12s and asserts the child is dead.

title: sitemap: an unrequested link with a query (/search?q=1) stays a grey unrequested item after that exact URL is requested — the dedupe strips the query from the item but stored keys keep it
description:

## Evidence
- The merged site-map dedupe matches unrequested items against requested ones by a key with the query stripped on the item side, while the stored (requested) keys keep the query.
- So /search?q=1 learned from a proxied page stays grey after the browser requests /search?q=1.

## Consequence
The site map shows a link as never requested when it was, for every URL with a query string.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #334 (merge 3f09aa0): one node identity, sitemap.NodePath (path without query, leading slash, no trailing slash), applied when a link is recorded and when the read merges items in; a request for /search?q=1 also clears an unrequested /search?q=2 (one requested /search node).

title: discovery: data races in the content-discovery session — handleDiscoveryGet writes the *discoveryRun outside d.mu while discoveryRuns.finish mutates it, so go test -race fails the discovery tests
description:

## Evidence
- handleDiscoveryGet writes fields of the *discoveryRun without holding d.mu, while discoveryRuns.finish mutates the same run under its own path.
- go test -race over the internal/web discovery tests reports about 45 races.

A polled session can read a torn run (status/counters) while it finishes, and the -race gate cannot be turned on for internal/web.

title: tests: TestTheCollaboratorBatchMintAgainstThePublicPool says it skips when interactsh-client, the network or the registration is unavailable, but it only skips in -short mode — on a machine without the binary it fails the whole internal/web package
description:
Evidence: internal/web/api_collaborator_batch_test.go:22-24 comment: 'The test is skipped automatically when the binary, the network, or the registration is not available — the honest-failure contract this project runs on.' The code (:26-28) skips only on testing.Short(); mintPayload then t.Fatalf's on the 503. Seen on PR 305's gate run 37655456827: the only failure in the whole suite, '503: "interactsh-client" not found on PATH'.

The internal/oob package keeps its live tests behind the oob_live build tag (internal/oob/live_test.go:4); this test reaches the public interactsh pool from the default go test run with no tag.

CI now installs interactsh-client v1.3.1 (PR 305), so the gate is not blocked by this. The defect is the disagreement between the documented contract and the code, and that every contributor without the binary gets a red internal/web.

Fix direction (decide one): (a) implement the documented skip — recordSkip/t.Skip when exec.LookPath("interactsh-client") fails or registration times out, with the skip line visible; or (b) move the test behind the oob_live build tag like the oob package, and run that tag in CI. Do not weaken the assertions on a successful registration.
notes: 2026-10-09: PR #328 (merge 00847c9) completed the fix: the live Collaborator batch test now also skips, with that reason, when interactsh-client is not on PATH (PR #308 only covered a 503 from the pool). CI installs the binary, so the test still runs there.

title: Reporting and engagement tools
description:
USER STORY
As a penetration tester wrapping up an engagement, I want to hand the client a report with my own title, organisation, detail level and message length. I want an XML export their Burp-ingesting tooling accepts, and a CSRF PoC that works for JSON and XML endpoints. I also want a clickjacking PoC I can record and replay, plus a Target analyzer and a content-discovery run with built-in lists, recursion and backup-file variants, so I can size the engagement at the start. The outcome is that every deliverable and early-engagement step Burp's Engagement tools provide is produced from burpsy's own data without hand-editing.

---

Deliverables and the Engagement tools menu. Burp-XML export (m7dk) and report settings (a9qy) shape what a client receives. CSRF PoC techniques for JSON and XML bodies (0z10), content discovery lists and recursion (dgbi), Target analyzer (dnvi) and Clickbandit (g67w) fill the remaining engagement tools.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-m7dk, burpsy-react-ui-a9qy, burpsy-react-ui-0z10, burpsy-react-ui-dgbi, burpsy-react-ui-dnvi, burpsy-react-ui-g67w (6).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none. All 6 children are open and unclaimed.
Phase 1 — Report settings and Burp-XML export (closes burpsy-react-ui-a9qy, burpsy-react-ui-m7dk)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/report/report.go`: a `Settings{Title, OrganiseBy, TOCDepth, Sections, MessageMode, MaxMessageLen}`; `HTML(rows, settings)`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/report/burpxml.go` with the DTD embedded.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_report.go`: `reportFilter` gains the settings, `case "xml"`, and evidence messages loaded only for xml and full-message HTML.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/scanner.tsx`, or the report launcher, gains a report-settings dialog.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/report/AGENTS.md`.
  Design:
  - Message mode `relevant` gives an extract around the evidence spans, `full` gives the whole messages, and either is truncated at `MaxMessageLen` with an explicit "truncated" marker.
  - The bulk exports still carry no messages by default (the existing `FindingReport` rule). XML and full-message HTML opt in, bounded by the length.
  - `type` is the advisory `TypeIndex` (for example `HexIndex()`). A finding with no catalogue entry is given `type` 0x08000000 ("extension generated") and flagged in a comment, not invented.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/report/burpxml_test.go`: validates against the embedded DTD; base64 round-trips byte-exact including binary; ampersands and CDATA terminators are escaped.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/report/report_settings_test.go`: by type, severity and URL ordering; TOC depth; truncation marker.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_report_settings_test.go`: through `/api/report`, including a 400 naming bad parameters.
  - E2E `report-settings.spec.ts`.
Phase 2 — CSRF PoC techniques (closes burpsy-react-ui-0z10)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_csrf.go`: `technique=auto|form|multipart|plain|xhr`, `auto_submit`, and a `test_url`.
  - A new ephemeral PoC host (`burpsy-go/internal/web/poc_host.go`): a separate listener or port serving one-shot PoCs with no cookies or credentials for the console.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts` and the CSRF dialog.
  - `route_manifest.go`, `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.ts`.
  Design:
  - `auto` follows Burp's documented choice: urlencoded gives a form; multipart gives a multipart form; JSON or XML gives a plain-text form when the body can be split at `=`, otherwise a cross-domain XHR that is honestly labelled "requires CORS".
  - Notes state what the browser will actually send, for example a changed Content-Type.
  - "Test in browser" opens the PoC from the separate origin, never under `/api` on the console origin.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_csrf_test.go` (extended): each technique for each body type gives the expected HTML; a JSON body with no `=` gives XHR with the note; the auto-submit script appears only when asked; params and notes are `[]`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/poc_host_test.go`: the PoC host never serves from the console origin, and tokens are single-use.
  - E2E `csrf-poc.spec.ts`.
Phase 3 — Target analyzer (closes burpsy-react-ui-dnvi)
  Files:
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_target_analyzer.go`, reading the site map and the store.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/server.go`, `route_manifest.go`, `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.ts`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/targetanalyzer.tsx`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/engagement-menu.ts`: the row at about :193-200 is enabled.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/engagement-menu.test.ts`.
  Design:
  - For each host or prefix, it reports dynamic URLs (query or body parameters, or a non-GET method), static URLs, the parameter total, and unique parameter names, using the request-parameter spans the store already computes.
  - "Save report" exports HTML or CSV with formula-guarded cells.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/target_analyzer_test.go`: a seeded store gives exact counts; an empty host gives zeros with `[]` lists.
  - `engagement-menu.test.ts`: the row is enabled.
  - E2E `target-analyzer.spec.ts`.
Phase 4 — Content discovery: built-in lists, recursion, observed names and variants (closes burpsy-react-ui-dgbi)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/extscan/ffuf.go`: `Options.Wordlist` may be a burpsy-generated temp file.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_discovery.go`: `lists:["builtin-short-files",…]`, `recurse_depth`, `observed_names`, `derivations`, `variant_extensions`; the run becomes a tree of levels.
  - The built-in lists already ship in `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/wordlists` (`burp-directories-short/long.txt`, `burp-filenames-*.txt`, `burp-extensions-*.txt`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/contentdiscovery.tsx`.
  Design:
  - Recursion runs as successive bounded ffuf runs, one per discovered directory up to the depth, and each directory is checked against `scope.MayContain…` before it is launched.
  - Observed names come from the site map's paths on that host.
  - Derivations are a stated, deterministic rule set recorded in gaps.md: numeric suffix, `_old`, `.bak`, case variants.
  - The variant-extension pass runs over discovered files.
  - Every level reports discovered, out-of-scope and skipped counts.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_discovery_test.go` (extended, with a fake ffuf on PATH recording its argv and a local listener): depth 2 issues exactly the expected runs; an out-of-scope subdirectory is counted, not run; the merged wordlist contains the built-in plus observed names; levels are `[]` with no hits.
  - E2E `content-discovery.spec.ts`.
Phase 5 — Clickbandit (closes burpsy-react-ui-g67w)
  Files:
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/clickbandit/clickbandit.ts`, bun-built to `ui/dist/clickbandit.js` and embedded by `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/package.json` (`build:clickbandit`).
  - An engagement-menu row "Copy Clickbandit to clipboard".
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/clickbandit.tsx`: instructions and a PoC preview from a downloaded file.
  Design:
  - Follows Burp's model: the operator pastes the script into the target page's devtools console, so it runs same-origin. It wraps the page in a same-origin iframe, records clicks (Start / Finish), offers a review mode with opacity and offset controls, and Save downloads the standalone PoC HTML.
  - burpsy never hosts or frames the target itself.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/clickbandit/clickbandit.test.ts`: the recorder state machine and PoC HTML generation, with recorded coordinates escaped.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui_route_reachability_test.go` (extended): the script asset is served with the right type.
  - E2E `clickbandit.spec.ts` against an e2e origin page.
Risks / open decisions:
- How to give the PoC host a separate origin: a second listener port, or a magic host through the proxy listener the way Burp does it. Note that `/api/exchange/in-browser/` already serves target HTML on the console origin. That is out of scope here, but worth a separate security bead.
- Unmapped `type` values in the Burp XML: decide whether to emit 0x08000000 or omit the issue.
- Derivation rules are burpsy's own. Burp's derivation algorithm is not in the evidence, so the divergence is recorded.
- Clickbandit is a self-contained JS artefact with its own build step, and the largest piece of new code here. If review size becomes a problem, it is the natural piece to cut.
QUESTION FOR THE USER: none.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- None of this epic's children hard-depend on another epic.
- If the user wants one Burp-XML writer, i9ti's pznm (Save entire history) can reuse `internal/report/burpxml.go` from Phase 1. That makes i9ti Phase 2 land after td8g Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration tests use the real routes:
  - `GET /api/report?format=html` with every new settings parameter, and `format=xml`, validated against Burp's DTD with base64 messages decoded byte-identical.
  - The CSRF route with each technique (form/urlencoded, multipart, plain-text form, cross-domain XHR) for urlencoded, JSON and XML exchanges.
  - The Target analyzer route against a seeded site map.
  - The discovery route with built-in lists, recursion depth 2 and extension variants against a local listener.
  - The Clickbandit asset route.
- Marshalled JSON: new arrays are `[]`, not `null`. That covers analyzer URL and parameter lists, discovery levels, and CSRF notes and params. Asserted by marshal tests.
- E2E specs perform the actions:
  - `report-settings.spec.ts`: open report settings, choose by-URL and a max length, and download.
  - `csrf-poc.spec.ts`: generate an XHR PoC from a JSON exchange and toggle auto-submit.
  - `target-analyzer.spec.ts`: open it from the engagement menu after seeding, with counts rendered.
  - `content-discovery.spec.ts`: start a run with the built-in short list and recursion, and the results tree shows a second level.
  - `clickbandit.spec.ts`: load the script on an e2e origin page, record two clicks, Finish, Save, and the downloaded HTML contains the overlay.
- Generated PoCs (CSRF "Test in browser", Clickbandit) never run on the console's origin. They are served from a separate origin or port, or downloaded. A test confirms that no new route returns target HTML under the console origin without `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`.
- The XML export carries Burp's `serialNumber`, `type` (from `advisory.Definition.TypeIndex`), `name`, `host`, `path`, `location`, `severity` and `confidence`, plus base64 `requestresponse`, and respects the max message length from a9qy.
- Content-discovery recursion is driven by burpsy, one bounded ffuf run per discovered directory, and each run is judged against scope before it starts. ffuf's own `-recursion` is not used, so egress stays scope-checked per directory. Out-of-scope directories are counted, not fetched.
- Every new route is in `route_manifest.go` and `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.ts` is regenerated, and `route_manifest_test.go` passes. `engagement-menu.test.ts` is updated now that Target analyzer is enabled. Divergences from Burp are in `gaps.md`.
- At the end of the epic, a live drive runs against the combined rebuild (`./ui-live.sh` with agent-browser, UI-VERIFICATION part c): report, CSRF, analyzer, discovery, Clickbandit.
- Gate is green:
  - `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./...`, build, vet, `go test ./...`, `../e2e-go.sh`.
  - UI `tsc` plus `bun run check`.
  - `./ui-pass.sh` on the touched routes with 0 axe violations.
  - The GitHub gate on the epic PR.

title: Utility tools: Logger, Comparer, Collaborator, Sequencer, Decoder
description:
USER STORY
As a penetration tester using burpsy's smaller tools mid-engagement, I want my Collaborator payloads to stay polled across a burpsy restart. I want to export OOB interactions as CSV for the report, and to recompute a JWT HS256 signature or an NTLM/SHA-3/BLAKE2 digest in the console. I also want to narrow a noisy Logger by scope, MIME, extension, response and parameters, with extractor columns, and to diff a response saved on disk against a live one with line wrap. I want the per-bit-position FIPS results Burp's Sequencer gives. The outcome is that a late blind-SSRF callback is never lost to a restart, and token and hash checks never leave the tool.

---

Per-tool residue in the smaller tools. Collaborator client persistence across restarts (d657) loses real callbacks and comes first; health check (8e3n) is in progress elsewhere. Logger view filters and custom columns (uvpb, n3sy), Comparer load-from-file and line wrap (ppqw, 2vuk), Collaborator CSV (aw2y), hash HMAC and the wider digest set (wi55, 7tgt), and per-position FIPS (c0k3). tni8 and qpfy are closed fixes kept here for history.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-d657, burpsy-react-ui-8e3n, burpsy-react-ui-uvpb, burpsy-react-ui-n3sy, burpsy-react-ui-ppqw, burpsy-react-ui-2vuk, burpsy-react-ui-aw2y, burpsy-react-ui-wi55, burpsy-react-ui-7tgt, burpsy-react-ui-c0k3, burpsy-react-ui-tni8, burpsy-react-ui-qpfy (12).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed:
- burpsy-react-ui-qpfy: closed, decoded gzip/deflate rendering.
- burpsy-react-ui-tni8: closed, Organizer column alignment.
- burpsy-react-ui-8e3n: in progress in another session (Collaborator health check and unset). It is not planned here, but d657 and aw2y are sequenced after it.
Phase 1 — Hash: HMAC, output encodings and the wider digest set (closes burpsy-react-ui-wi55, burpsy-react-ui-7tgt)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/tools/codec.go` (`Hasher`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_toolkit.go` (`handleToolsHash` at about :1943).
  - `burpsy-go/go.mod`: `golang.org/x/crypto` goes from an indirect to a direct dependency.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.workbench.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.workbench.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/decoder.tsx`.
  - `burpsy-go/gaps.md`.
  Design:
  - Request: `{input, input_encoding: utf8|hex|base64, algorithm, key?, key_encoding: utf8|hex|base64, output: hex|base64|base64url}`.
  - HMAC-{MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512} come from the standard library.
  - Digests: SHA-224, SHA-384, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 from the standard library; MD4, RIPEMD-160, SHA3-224/256/384/512, Keccak-256/512 (legacy), BLAKE2b-256/384/512 and BLAKE2s-256 from x/crypto.
  - BLAKE3, Whirlpool, SM3 and GOST need new third-party dependencies. They are refused by name, listed in gaps.md, and need the user's decision before anything is added.
  - `base64url` is unpadded, which is the JWT encoding.
  - The algorithm list lives in one Go table. A test compares it with the TS constant (the `ui_source_bytes_test.go` pattern), so no new route is needed.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/tools/codec_hash_test.go`: a known-answer vector for every algorithm, RFC 4231 cases 1–4, and RFC 7515 A.1.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/toolkit_hash_api_test.go`: through the route; an unknown or unsupported algorithm gives 400 naming the supported set; a bad key encoding gives 400.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/hash_algorithms_ui_sync_test.go`.
  - E2E `decoder-hmac.spec.ts`.
Phase 2 — Comparer: load from file and line wrap (closes burpsy-react-ui-ppqw, burpsy-react-ui-2vuk)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_toolkit.go`: `handleToolsCompare` gains optional `a_base64` / `b_base64`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (`ComparerItem.bodyBase64`, persisted size cap), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/comparer.tsx` (Load button with a file input; "Enable line wrapping" toggle, remembered).
  Design:
  - The request carries a file's bytes as base64, so a binary file is not mangled through a JSON string.
  - Files over a cap (proposed 2 MiB, inside the 16 MiB request bound) are refused with the size.
  - Line wrap is CSS on the diff panes. Hunk next/previous navigation still scrolls correctly with wrap on.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/comparer_base64_test.go`: a non-UTF-8 file diffs byte-exact, and `a`/`a_base64` together gives 400.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/comparer-items.test.ts`: the cap.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/comparer.test.ts`: the wrap state.
  - E2E `comparer-file.spec.ts`.
Phase 3 — Logger view filter axes and extractor columns (closes burpsy-react-ui-uvpb, burpsy-react-ui-n3sy)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_dashboard.go`: `toolLogEntryView` adds `mime`, which exists on `toollog.Entry` but is not projected today, and `has_params`. `toolLogMatches` gains `scope_only`, `mime`, `ext`, `has_response` and `parameterized`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_toolkit.go` (`toolLogGet` query parameters).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.ts` and the `toolLogToCSV` area of `lib/api.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/logger.tsx` (filter panel; `ExtractorManager`/`ExtractorCell` from `ui/extractor-manager.tsx` fed through `/api/history/extract {ids}` with the row's `exchange`).
  Design:
  - The filters are view-side and reversible, judged at query time against the current scope. They are kept separate from the destructive capture filter, matching the `Zfp2` two-axis model documented in `toollog.go`.
  - `has_response` means `ResponseLen != nil`.
  - `parameterized` means a query string or body parameters, read from the linked exchange only when that filter is on.
  - Extractor columns reuse the History extractor set rather than defining a second model. Rows with no exchange show "no stored message".
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/toollog_view_filter_test.go`: each axis through `GET /api/tools/log`; a scope change re-judges rows; `mime` null versus "" round-trips.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_history_extractors_test.go` (extended): Logger exchange ids.
  - `csv-guard.test.ts` (extended).
  - E2E `logger-filters.spec.ts`.
Phase 4 — Collaborator: persisted client identity and CSV export (closes burpsy-react-ui-d657, burpsy-react-ui-aw2y)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/oob/client.go`: `Options.SessionFile` adds `-sf <path>` (the flag is confirmed in the installed interactsh-client), and `-o` moves to a stable per-project path.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/persist/persist.go`: a minted-payload table, including xixe's attribution field.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_collaborator.go`: `collaboratorHub.minted` is restored at start, plus `?include_raw=1` on interactions.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_backup.go` / `api_backup_config.go`: session file excluded.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/api.ts` (`collaboratorToCSV` using `csvCell`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/collaborator.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.collab.ts`.
  - E2E fixture: `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/harness/fake-interactsh.mjs`, shared with xixe Phase 5.
  Design:
  - Burp's `restoreClient(SecretKey)` corresponds to interactsh's session file. Minted payloads are persisted with the project, so attribution survives too.
  - The CSV follows Burp: type, time, client IP, payload, and base64 raw request and response, with every cell formula-guarded.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/oob/client_session_test.go`: the fake binary records argv, so `-sf` is passed and the file mode is 0600.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/collaborator_restart_test.go`: mint, rebuild the `Server` on the same persistence, append a callback, and the interaction is attributed to the payload minted before the restart.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_collaborator_raw_test.go`: `include_raw` gives base64, and rows are `[]` with no interactions.
  - `collaborator.test.ts`: CSV columns and guard.
  - E2E `collaborator-export.spec.ts`.
Phase 5 — Sequencer per-position FIPS (closes burpsy-react-ui-c0k3)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sequencer/fips.go`; new `burpsy-go/internal/sequencer/fips_position.go`, reusing `perTokenBits` from `advanced.go`, the binomial code in `effective.go` and `chiSquareUpperTail` in `chi.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sequencer/report.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go` (`handleSequencerAnalyse`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx`: a significance chart per bit position with the "FIPS pass level" line. Burp's `Zhwj.java:15` draws it at `6 + log10(threshold)`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sequencer/AGENTS.md`, `burpsy-go/gaps.md`.
  Design:
  - For each bit position, the bit sequence across tokens gets the four tests.
  - Pass and fail follow Burp's `Zpu3.ZF`/`Zd`/`ZC`.
  - The significance values come from Burp's lookup tables, interpolated across a sample-size grid in `Zc6a.ZH`, which uses `Zsge.Ze`, `Zw_0` and `Zcmb`. The per-position driver is in `Zpix.java` at bytecode offsets 0bc8 to 10d0.
  - The first step is to recover those tables. If they cannot be recovered, the fallback is exact computation: binomial for monobit, chi-square for poker (as `Zp2s.ZK`), and an exact dynamic program for the runs and long-run distributions. The method used is stated in the output.
  - The deferral notice from 3f3 under the FIPS heading is removed only when this lands.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sequencer/fips_position_test.go`: at N=20000 the exact interval edges (9725/10275, 2315..2685, …, run under 26) pass and fail; at other N the threshold edges hold; a stuck bit position fails monobit; long run under 12 always passes.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/sequencer_api_test.go` (extended): per-position arrays are `[]` below the minimum sample.
  - E2E: the existing `sequencer-extended-battery.spec.ts` gains a per-position chart assertion after running an analysis.
Risks / open decisions:
- d657 and aw2y edit the same files as 8e3n, which is in progress, and the live worktree has uncommitted changes in `oob/client.go`, `api_collaborator.go`, `collaborator.tsx` and `data.collab.ts`. Phase 4 must start only after 8e3n merges.
- The hash dependencies need a decision: add third-party packages for BLAKE3, Whirlpool, SM3 and GOST, or record them as gaps.
- c0k3 depends on recovering Burp's significance tables from `Zc6a`, `Zw_0`, `Zcmb` and `Zsge` (some are bytecode-only). The exact-computation fallback is a documented divergence.
- `parameterized` reads the request body of each candidate row. Bound the cost, for example by evaluating only after the cheap axes have filtered.
QUESTION FOR THE USER: none.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- 8e3n (this epic, in progress elsewhere) must merge before Phase 4 (d657, aw2y).

title: UI shell and cross-tool UX
description:
USER STORY
As a penetration tester who has used Burp for years, I want burpsy's console to take my muscle memory and my table habits. That means Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+Space working where the browser allows, selecting 30 history rows and sending them to Comparer or scope in one action, and jumping to "entry 1843" from a ticket. I want a new finding or a listener error to show up in a dock while I am in Repeater, saved filters, my own tab order, and a documentation link at the bottom of every menu. Opening a client's project cold, with tasks paused and a different config, should be a step, not a surprise.

---

Conventions that span every tool. The hotkey catalogue (2czi, with Burp's 47 default chords recovered in its notes) and multi-row table selection (fe16) are the structural gaps. Then the shell: bottom dock (08wx), Help menu (n2un), tab drag-order (sk29), per-tool settings cog (zpka), restore defaults (9x9x) and the project-open step (xaxw). Table conventions: Hide column (bae7), zebra striping (69p0), saved filters (mntt), go-to-entry (vfu2), expand/collapse all (txnw), Add to scope from history (pahd). Consistency: native dialogs (bea3) and documentation menu entries (u9zz). lxqq is closed.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-2czi, burpsy-react-ui-fe16, burpsy-react-ui-08wx, burpsy-react-ui-n2un, burpsy-react-ui-sk29, burpsy-react-ui-zpka, burpsy-react-ui-9x9x, burpsy-react-ui-xaxw, burpsy-react-ui-bae7, burpsy-react-ui-69p0, burpsy-react-ui-mntt, burpsy-react-ui-vfu2, burpsy-react-ui-txnw, burpsy-react-ui-pahd, burpsy-react-ui-bea3, burpsy-react-ui-u9zz, burpsy-react-ui-lxqq (17).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: lxqq (closed). No child is in_progress.

**Phase 1 — Hotkey catalogue and go-to-entry (closes 2czi, vfu2)**

Files:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/shortcuts.ts` (rows gain `burp: {action, chord}`, `disposition`, `reason`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/burp-hotkeys.ts` (new: the 50 shipped rows as data)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/keymap.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/palette-commands.ts`
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/app.tsx` (390–445, 800–812), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/nav.ts`
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx` (`burpEditorKeys` 416–450, `basicSetup` 1614)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:439`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intercept.tsx:1085`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx`
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx` (`HotkeysSection` 1593), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/runtime.ts` (desktop detection)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/table.tsx` (`scrollToId`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/history.tsx`

Design: how each of the 50 rows is handled, grouped by tier.

- **Bound to Burp's own chord** (preventDefault where the browser has a default):
  - Ctrl+R / I / O (already bound)
  - Ctrl+F forward (already bound on Intercept)
  - Ctrl+K (already bound)
  - Ctrl+S / U / Shift+U / H / Shift+H / B / Shift+B (already in the editor keymap)
  - Ctrl+Space issue_repeater_request: a literal `ctrl+space` on every platform, because `mod` would be Cmd+Space, which is Spotlight; mod+enter stays as a second binding
  - Ctrl+Shift+D / P / R / O switch_to_*
  - Ctrl+Shift+L switch_to_logger. This collides with today's `view.toggleTheme` (`mod+shift+l`). Theme moves to unbound plus the palette, because Burp ships no theme chord.
  - Ctrl+Alt+C copy prettified (new)
  - Ctrl+Comma / Ctrl+Period: previous / next search match (CodeMirror `findPrevious` / `findNext`)
- **Native in CodeMirror; confirm per platform and document:**
  - Ctrl+X / C / V / Z / Y / A
  - Ctrl+Backspace / Delete
  - Ctrl+Left / Right / Home / End, each with Shift
- **New commands:** Ctrl+Up / Down paragraph moves (blank-line boundaries), each with Shift.
- **Ctrl+D delete line.** Bound only while the editor is focused, at `Prec.high` with preventDefault. That displaces CodeMirror's Mod-d `selectNextOccurrence` (installed by `searchKeymap: true`), and Chrome's bookmark shortcut when focus is in the editor. Outside the editor it is left to the browser, which is documented.
- **Unclaimable in Chromium; documented alternative:**
  - Ctrl+T toggle interception: keeps alt+T
  - Ctrl+Shift+T switch_to_target: keeps the alt+digit binding
- **Uncertain; settle with the live probe before deciding:**
  - Ctrl+Shift+I switch_to_intruder: DevTools in both browsers
  - Ctrl+Shift+P: Firefox private window
  - Ctrl+Minus / Ctrl+Equals prev/next tab: browser zoom. Claiming them also takes away WCAG 1.4.4 text resize, so the recommendation is a documented alternative (keep mod+alt+←/→) with an opt-in rebind.
- **Declined:** the three Burp AI rows (Ctrl+E, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G), because burpsy has no Burp AI or account (see 4ep5/9g5y).
- **Desktop shell.** Under the Wails desktop shell (`onDesktopEvent`) there are no browser reservations, so every row uses Burp's exact chord.
- **Go to entry (vfu2).** A palette and toolbar action (Burp's TABLE_GO_TO_ENTRY, which has no default chord) opens a small themed dialog and calls `VirtualTable.scrollToId`. TABLE_GO_TO_TOP and TABLE_GO_TO_BOTTOM map to the existing Home/End listbox keys.

Tests:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/burp-hotkeys.test.ts`: 50 rows, exactly one disposition each, every reason non-empty, no two rows on the same chord, and the alternative chord passes `validateChord`.
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/hotkeys.test.ts` (extend): registry ids are unique; every rebindable id is installed (keymap-installed pattern).
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/palette-commands.test.ts`: each catalogue action is in the palette.
- Live drive: keydown probe page in Chromium and Firefox; the tiers are recorded in the hotkey table's reasons.

**Phase 2 — Multi-row selection and table conventions (closes fe16, bae7, 69p0, mntt)**

Files:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/table.tsx`: props 171–240; header `ContextMenu` 561–566; row click, double-click and context menu 650–657
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/table-selection.ts` (new)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts` (new `menuMany(exchanges)` beside `menu` 702)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/history.tsx` (the `checkedRows` tick-box column merged into the selection), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/logger.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/organizer.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/sitemap.tsx`
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/column-visibility-menu.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (`tableStripes`)

Design:
- **Selection.** `selectedId` stays as the primary/focus row that drives the detail pane. A separate `selection: Set<id>` with an anchor is added. `menuGroups(row, selected[])` builds the multi-row menu when `selected.length > 1`.
- **Hide column.** `enableColumnVisibility` defaults to true wherever a table persists column state, and "Hide column" is added to the header menu.
- **Zebra striping.** Burp's default is `zebra_striping: true`. The recommendation is to follow it, re-baselining the screenshots and checking stripe contrast in both themes.
- **Filter presets.** A versioned JSON schema, saved to localStorage as named presets and to a downloaded file (Burp's Save/Load settings), plus "Restore defaults".

Tests:

**Phase 4 — Shell: dock, tab order, Help, settings cog (closes 08wx, sk29, n2un, zpka)**

Files:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/dock.tsx` (new), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/event-log.tsx` (extracted from `pages/dashboard.tsx`), and the issue list extracted from the dashboard and scanner

- `burpsy-go/cmd/desktop/` (`buildMenu` Help items)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/settings-cog.tsx` (new), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/settings-sections.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx` (export the section components)

Design:
- **Dock.** It reads queries the shell already keeps warm, with no new poll (the `app.tsx` attention comment explains why). It is a labelled region landmark. Detach uses the same `window.open` route pattern as tab detach.
- **Tab order.** Stored the way Burp's `WorkspaceDefaults.json` stores `suite.components`: one ordered list with a hidden flag per tool. It migrates `burpsy.tooltabs.hidden`.
  - Keyboard alternatives for reordering: "Move left/right" on the tab's context menu, and Alt+Shift+←/→ on the focused tab.
  - Cycling follows the displayed order. The alt+digit bindings stay tied to each tool, not its position.
- **Help.** Documentation and Getting started go to Discover; Diagnostics goes to `settings#diagnostics`; About shows the build. License and Check for updates point at the 4ep5 decline text instead of being dead items.
- **Settings cog.** Opens a Modal hosting the tool's own settings section.

Tests:

- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/settings-sections.test.ts` (extend): every cog target id exists.

**Phase 5 — Settings reset and project open (closes 9x9x, xaxw)**

Files:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_config.go` (a new `handleConfigReset` that imports a defaults bundle through the existing import path), `burpsy-go/internal/web/server.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/route_manifest.go`, `burpsy-go/docs/JSON-API.md`
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/user-settings.ts` (new: a registry of the `burpsy.*` localStorage keys for the "user" scope)
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_project_open.go` (request struct 161; pause/resume 202–259), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/project-switcher.tsx`

Design:
- **Reset.** One importer handles both import and reset, and the coverage block lists what was not reset. Risk class riskDestructive behind the confirm gate.
- **Project open.** The request gains `config`: project (the default) | defaults | file, plus `config_file`, `pause_tasks` and `disable_extensions`. `pause_tasks` defaults to Burp's `pause_tasks_at_startup_default: true`. "Default to the above in future" is a per-browser preference.

Tests:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_config_reset_test.go`: through the route, a PATCHed network setting reads back at its default; marshalled `applied` and `not_reset`; 428 without confirm.
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_project_open_test.go` (extend): `pause_tasks:true` leaves `tasks.Paused()` true and the JSON says `tasks_paused: true`; `config:"defaults"` ignores the project's stored settings.
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/user-settings.test.ts`.

Risks / open decisions:
- **Hotkey tiers need evidence.** The three tiers rest on a live probe, not memory. If Ctrl+Shift+I or Ctrl+Minus/Equals turn out to be claimable, the remaining decision is policy (DevTools access, zoom accessibility), not feasibility.
- **Burp's go_to_previous/next_tab.** It isn't confirmed whether Burp's Ctrl+Minus/Equals cycles top-level tools or sub-tabs such as Repeater's. Check Zipf usage before mapping it to `nav.nextTool`.
- **fe16 touches every table.** Merging History's tick-box column into the selection changes how Delete and Audit work there today. Recommendation: keep the tick box as a mirror for one release.
- **Zebra default ON** follows Burp but changes every table screenshot and needs the stripe colour checked for contrast in both themes.
- **Reset coverage.** 9x9x can only reset what the config bundle covers. Any rj3h setting missing from coverage silently survives a reset.

- **PR A, "Keyboard, tables, menus":** Phases 1–3, closing 2czi, vfu2, fe16, bae7, 69p0, mntt, u9zz, pahd, bea3 and txnw. UI only.
- **PR B, "Shell and project lifecycle":** Phases 4–5, closing 08wx, sk29, n2un, zpka, 9x9x and xaxw. Includes the Go routes.

Approve the split, or keep one PR with five checkpoints?

acceptance_criteria:

Inspector, the site-map tree and the crawl-paths tree offer Expand/Collapse all or branch.

title: Proxy, network, session and scope settings
description:
USER STORY
As a penetration tester setting up a phone or a second laptop, I want to point it at a burpsy listener, browse to http://burpsuite to get the CA, and have the proxy behave the way Burp's settings say it will. That covers HTTP/1.0 for legacy origins, per-listener HTTP/2, quiet failures, cookies the browser already holds reaching the jar, and redirect, keep-alive and logging policy across the project. With several clients sharing one listener I need to see which device sent each request. I need to set a separate drop scope and a macro that refreshes only the token it should, so traffic captured on a long engagement stays inside the rules of engagement and can be audited later.

---

Settings Burp exposes that burpsy has no control for. The proxy in-browser interface for CA download (beof) matters most for mobile work. Allowed redirect types (z9zi) and cookie-jar absorption from request headers (sm1k) change tool behaviour. The rest are panels and switches: per-listener HTTP/2 (34rd), HTTP/1.0 and error suppression (0q9d), the out-of-scope logging prompt (z80e), client source IP (3bkn), platform-auth prompt (3xnt), server TLS certificates (t75m), project-wide HTTP defaults (ry5n), custom drop scope (47ed), macro parameter scope (8gk8) and file logging (nvfl). ga5e and wtm2 are closed fixes kept here for history.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-beof, burpsy-react-ui-z9zi, burpsy-react-ui-sm1k, burpsy-react-ui-34rd, burpsy-react-ui-0q9d, burpsy-react-ui-z80e, burpsy-react-ui-3bkn, burpsy-react-ui-3xnt, burpsy-react-ui-t75m, burpsy-react-ui-ry5n, burpsy-react-ui-47ed, burpsy-react-ui-8gk8, burpsy-react-ui-nvfl, burpsy-react-ui-ga5e, burpsy-react-ui-wtm2 (15).

Design (beof):
- **Where it runs.** The interface is served inside `internal/proxy`, before the listener redirect, Match & Replace, intercept, the scope/egress check, the upstream proxy and record. It never touches `internal/web`. The console's same-origin gate (`internal/web/api_sameorigin.go`, which closed s19k) protects only the console port, and the obvious way to make it serve `Host: burpsuite` would be an allowlist that weakens it.
- **Triggers:**
  - absolute-form host `burpsuite`, case-insensitive
  - an origin-form request whose Host is the listener's own bound address (any local interface IP for a 0.0.0.0 bind)
- **Inert by construction.**
  - GET and HEAD only, 405 otherwise.
  - Fixed routes: `/` for the welcome page and `/cert` for the DER CA; `.pem` is optional.
  - Constant bodies, so no reflection of the request.
  - Headers: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `nosniff`, no Set-Cookie, `Connection: close`.
  - Never the CA key, project name, hosts or history.
  - With no engine (interception off), `/cert` is a 404 that says interception is off, mirroring `/ca.crt` in `api_ca.go`.
- **Disable switch.** `OptDisableWebInterface` (`disable_web_interface`, default false, per Burp) turns the magic host into an ordinary host. The self-address guard stays unconditional (400, never self-dial). It also fixes a latent loop: `invisible_proxy` is seeded ON, so today `GET /` with `Host: 127.0.0.1:8080` appears to dial the listener itself. A test pins this.
- **Troubleshooting.** A browser that never reaches the proxy can't be shown a page by it. The troubleshooting copy therefore lives in the console's Proxy listeners section ("Can't reach http://burpsuite?").

Design (0q9d):
- Three keys with Burp's names, all default false: `use_http_10_in_requests_to_server`, `use_http_10_in_responses_to_client`, `suppress_burp_error_messages_in_browser`.
- **Correction to the bead.** On master an upstream failure mostly sends nothing: `stream_response.go:376` logs and returns, and the TLS loop returns at 1464/1666. The error page has to be built before it can be suppressed.
- **New error page.** `error_page.go` emits a 502/504 with a constant short body naming the failure class. It is written only when no byte has gone to the client yet.
- **What "suppress" covers:** the new upstream-failure pages, the tunnel 502 (`proxy.go:1969`), the 400 for an unattributable request (2083), and the intercept-drop 403 (2169). The scope-drop 403 (3092) is engagement-policy evidence and stays (open decision below). Suppressing means closing without bytes.
- **HTTP/1.0 to the server.** Rewritten in `applyRequestRules`, so history equals the wire. A chunked body is converted with the existing `rewriteChunkedToLength`, and the upstream connection is closed after the response.
- **HTTP/1.0 to the client.** The status line is rewritten. A buffered response has chunked framing converted to Content-Length. A streaming response is sent close-delimited, and the client connection closes afterwards.
- The h2 relay is unaffected; gaps.md records this.

Design (34rd):
- `ListenerSpec.DisableHTTP2` (zero value means h2 allowed, matching Burp's default `enable_http2: true`), exposed on the wire as `support_http2`.
- `AlpnOffer` filters h2 when interception is on OR the listener disallows it.
- `DowngradeNote` names the listener as the reason.

- **Client IP** is taken from `clientConn.RemoteAddr()` at accept time and threaded the way `ListenerPort` already is.
- **Persistence decision.** `ServerIP` and `ListenerPort` are not persisted today (no hits in `internal/persist`). `client_ip` is persisted. The other two are filed as a follow-up bead rather than fixed here.
- **Request cookies** are absorbed by `AbsorbRequestCookies(SourceProxy, host, port, tls, reqStages.original)`.
  - It reads the client's original bytes, not `x.Request`, which already carries Match & Replace edits and jar/session-injected cookies and would feed the jar back into itself.

Design (8gk8):

Design (z9zi):
- Five booleans named as in Burp, `understand_*`, with ProjectDefaults values.
- Refresh header and `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` are parsed from at most the first 64 KiB.
- **JavaScript-driven redirects are partial.** burpsy has no JS engine, so this arm is static pattern detection (`location=`, `.href=`, `.replace()`, `.assign()`), off by default. gaps.md says it is partial.
- Every redirect that is not a 3xx becomes a bodiless GET. The existing `visitKey`/`max_hops` bound covers Refresh-to-self loops.

Design (ry5n):
- `http.enable_http2` (default true) and `http.enable_keep_alive` (default false, per the docs and ProjectDefaults).
- The pool key is scheme, host, port, SNI, resolved address, client certificate and upstream proxy, with Burp's documented 5 s idle close.
- Repeater's per-tab reuse still overrides the project setting. `pipeline.go`'s smuggling and desync probes keep private sockets.

Design (3xnt):
- `prompt_on_authentication_failure` (default false).
- A 401 for Basic, Digest or NTLM from a host with no credential queues one de-duplicated prompt (host + scheme + realm) in an id-keyed, timeout-bounded registry shaped like `session_prompts.go`.
- **Non-blocking, with no automatic retry.** This matches the lockout reasoning at `stream_response.go:405`; the credential applies from the next request. It differs from Burp and is recorded in gaps.md.

Design (t75m):
- `alpn.Dialer` is the TLS chokepoint for both the proxy's upstream leg and the sender. `servercerts.Log` is bounded, de-duplicated by leaf SHA-256, and records hosts, first/last seen and whether the chain verified.
- The `http.Transport` at `sender.go:289` gets a `VerifyConnection` hook, or gaps.md records why it can't.

- `burpsy-go/internal/toollog/toollog.go` (a fan-out sink beside the single-slot `SetPersistenceSink` 698)

Design:
- Burp's exact shape: `requests` and `responses` maps of tool to file path (`all_tools`, `proxy`, `scanner`, `repeater`, `intruder`, `sequencer`, `extender`), where an empty string means off, as in ProjectDefaults. burpsy-only tools fall under `all_tools`.
- Writes go through an async bounded channel, and dropped entries are counted in the GET. Bytes are resolved from the traffic store by exchange id, off the `toollog` lock.
- Files are opened `O_APPEND|O_CREATE`, mode 0600, after an `Lstat` that refuses symlinks and non-regular files.
- **Risk class.** The route writes to a path the operator supplies, so it is riskDestructive behind the confirm gate. An imported config bundle that carries logging paths shows them and needs that confirm before any file opens.
- The file format follows Burp's log format. Open question: the exact separator and header lines need confirming against the decompiled writer before they are implemented.

Tests:
- `burpsy-go/internal/filelog/filelog_test.go`: format, symlink refusal, drop count.
- `burpsy-go/internal/proxy/filelog_proxy_test.go`: a real socket exchange; the file contains byte-for-byte the stored request and response.
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_filelog_test.go`: marshalled JSON; 428 without confirm; files closed on project switch.

Risks / open decisions:
- **`CONNECT burpsuite:443`.** Burp serves https://burpsuite with a leaf from its own CA, but before the CA is trusted that page shows a warning. Recommendation: support it only when the engine exists, otherwise refuse cleanly.
- **Fingerprinting.** Any page in the operator's browser can fetch http://burpsuite/cert and learn that a burpsy CA is in use. Burp has the same property. The mitigation is `disable_web_interface`, and gaps.md documents this.
- **Scope-drop 403 under "Suppress error messages".** Recommendation: never suppress it, because it is the engagement-rules evidence. This differs from Burp.
- **Pre-handshake TLS failure.** An upstream dial failure inside `interceptTLS` (1464) happens after `200 Connection Established` but before the client's TLS handshake. Sending a page there means reordering the handshake. Recommendation: keep closing the connection and document it.
- **8gk8 alternative.** Instead of building the full model, decline only/except in gaps.md and map "update with jar cookies" to the existing `ActionAddCookiesFromJar`. Cheaper, but it leaves the parity gap open.
- **Keep-alive pool.** It is a new reuse surface on the authorised send path. A pooled connection must not outlive a scope, upstream-proxy or client-certificate change; invalidate the pool on any settings PATCH.
- **Server-cert log persistence.** In-memory is recommended; persisting it is optional.
- **Size.** 13 children, mostly proxy-core and sender behaviour, make this PR heavy to review. See the question below.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: Should rj3h stay one PR, as the one-PR-per-epic rule says? The alternative is two PRs: (A) proxy core, Phases 1–2 (beof, 0q9d, 34rd, 3bkn, sm1k), and (B) settings and policy, Phases 3–5 (47ed, z80e, 8gk8, z9zi, ry5n, 3xnt, t75m, nvfl). The plan above assumes one PR, with the phases as review checkpoints.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- **z80e and ga7i/bea3.** z80e's prompt uses the themed Modal. bea3 removes `window.confirm`/`window.prompt`, so the two must not reintroduce native dialogs between them.

- **New settings and ga7i/9x9x.** Every setting added here (proxy misc keys, listener `support_http2`, drop scope, redirect types, HTTP defaults, auth prompt, logging) must appear in the config bundle's coverage, so that 9x9x's "Restore default settings" resets it.
- **Hotkey intercept rows and ga7i/2czi.** The intercept-response and Forward all / Drop all rows (palette-only) touch `intercept.tsx`, which Phase 2 also edits for the client-IP line.
- **3xnt.** Its prompt modal is installed at the shell level and must not collide with ga7i/08wx's bottom dock or the existing session prompt.
acceptance_criteria:
- **http://burpsuite works and is inert.** A client using a listener (loopback, and a listener bound to 0.0.0.0) gets the welcome page and `/cert`. The `/cert` bytes are the DER of `TlsEngine.CertPEM()`. The request is never dialled, never recorded (store and tool-log counts unchanged), never reaches `internal/web`, answers POST with 405, and stops being served once `disable_web_interface` is on. An origin-form request to the listener's own address never connects back to the listener. All of this is proven over a real socket and parsed with `http.ReadResponse` + `io.ReadAll`.
- **Proxy relay tests use a real proxy and a strict client.** Each test runs a real proxy, a real origin and a strict client, never line reads. They cover:
  - HTTP/1.0 to the server, with a chunked request rewritten to Content-Length
  - HTTP/1.0 to the client, buffered and on the streaming path (close-delimited)
  - the error page and its suppression for upstream dial, TLS and read failures
  - per-listener "Support HTTP/2", checked as the ALPN a real `tls.Client` actually negotiates
- **Client IP is recorded.** Every proxy capture site (HTTP/1 plain, the TLS loop, the h2 relay, the WebSocket handshake, the completeResponse path) and the intercept hold record the client IP. The marshalled `/api/history` and intercept JSON carry `client_ip`.
- **The jar learns from request cookies.** A `Cookie:` the browser sends with no Set-Cookie ever lands in the jar, read from the client's original bytes. A cookie added by Match & Replace or a session rule is not absorbed, and no Set-Cookie attribute is overwritten. Checked against the marshalled `/api/session/cookies` JSON.
- **New settings use Burp's names and defaults.** Every new setting uses Burp's key names and the defaults in `Preferences/ProjectDefaults.json` / `UserDefaults.json` (tree build 51467). For example: redirect types 3xx, Refresh and meta on, JavaScript and any-status off; `enable_http2` true; `enable_keep_alive` false; `prompt_on_authentication_failure` false; drop `scope_option` "suite"; history logging action "prompt". Each setting:
  - round-trips through its HTTP route, checked against the marshalled JSON
  - round-trips through config export/import, including the bundle's coverage block
  - survives a restart where Burp scopes it to the project
- **Network behaviour is measured on the wire.**
  - The redirect follower, driven through the Repeater send route, reports each hop's `kind`.
  - The keep-alive on/off connection count is measured at a real origin.
  - The certificate a real TLS origin presents, reached both through the proxy and through Repeater, appears exactly once in `/api/network/server-certs` with a matching SHA-256.
- **Macro and drop scope behave as configured.**
  - A macro set to "update only csrf" changes only `csrf` in the bytes the origin receives.
  - The custom drop scope forwards and drops by its own rules, not the suite scope's, checked through the proxy.
- **File logging writes what was recorded.** Each tool and direction writes the exact recorded bytes to its configured file. The writer refuses symlinks and non-regular files, does no file IO under the tool-log lock, and closes its files on a project switch.
- **Routes are classified.** Every new route has a `route_manifest.go` risk class, `bun run check:gated-routes` is clean, and `docs/JSON-API.md` is regenerated.
- **Epic-end live drive.** Drive the console against the combined rebuild after a fresh browser load: new profile or hard reload, with the bundle hash checked against the built `dist/app.js`. A second client (curl, or a mobile emulator) fetches http://burpsuite. axe reports zero violations in light and dark on Proxy settings, Network settings, Scope, Session and the add-to-scope modal.
- **Gate is green.**
  - `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./...` leaves no diff.
  - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `../e2e-go.sh` pass.
  - UI `tsc --noEmit` and `bun run check` pass.
  - The GitHub gate is green on the epic PR.
