  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/message-sections.tsx`.
  Design:
  - In an editable context, every optional view (Query params, Body params, Cookies) is offered with an empty state and Add. Read-only editors keep "only what the message can fill".
  - Reordering moves whole raw header lines, keeping repeated names and their original spelling. The Inspector is a writer over the same text, so the raw view stays the source of truth.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/message.test.ts`: `moveHeader` is byte-identical apart from order, keeps duplicate names, and leaves CRLF and the body untouched.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/editor-tabs.test.ts`: editable with no cookies offers Cookies; read-only does not.
  - E2E `inspector-reorder.spec.ts`: reorder in Repeater, send, and the stored request's header order matches.
  - `inspector-codepoint.spec.ts` still passes.
Phase 2 — Repeater tab workflow: notes, tab search, history export, response change-highlighting (closes burpsy-react-ui-jva5, burpsy-react-ui-qqcn, burpsy-react-ui-pznm, burpsy-react-ui-b4gt)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (`RepeaterTab.note`, persisted), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` (Notes panel, tab-search box, Save entire history, Highlight changes toggle).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/repeater-tabs.ts` (`filterTabs`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/palette-commands.ts` and `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/keymap.ts` ("Open tab search").
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts`: notes go with send-to Organizer and Intruder.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_history_export.go`, registered in `burpsy-go/internal/web/server.go`, plus `route_manifest.go`, `route-risk.ts` and `gated-routes.ts`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/response-diff.ts`.
  Design:
  - Notes are per tab and persisted, and travel as the Organizer note when a request is sent on.
  - Tab search is a filter over tab names and targets, also reachable from the palette.
  - Save entire history: `POST /api/repeater/history-export {entries:[{request_msg_id,response_msg_id,sent_at,…}]}` returns one file with base64 messages. History is component-local `useState` (`repeater.tsx:142`), so the export uses ids, never text.
  - Change highlighting diffs the new response against the previous entry in the same tab through the existing `/api/tools/compare` (granularity `words`). Byte offsets are mapped to UTF-16 indices for CodeMirror in `response-diff.ts`.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_history_export_test.go`: a binary body round-trips byte-identical, a missing response is counted, and entries are `[]` when empty.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/response-diff.test.ts`: multibyte (é, emoji) offsets map correctly.
  - `repeater-tabs.test.ts`: filter cases.
  - The e2e `repeater-workflow.spec.ts` covering two sends, the note, search and export.
Phase 3 — Per-tab connection and TLS overrides (closes burpsy-react-ui-adkx, burpsy-react-ui-k011, burpsy-react-ui-of0z)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sendopts.go` (from xixe Phase 1): `SNIOverride`, `StreamingTimeout`, `H2Reuse`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sender.go` (`dialTLS` already takes `serverName` separately from `addr`; see the comment at `network.go:88-94`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/redirect.go`: the cross-domain hop keeps the selected `ProtocolPreference`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/repeater_h2_sessions.go`: per-tab h2 connections with an idle TTL.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/repeater_options.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go` (`sendOneRepeaterRequest`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` (target dialog: Override SNI; override menu: Streaming response timeout, Unpack compressed responses, HTTP/2 connection reuse, Enforce protocol on cross-domain redirects).
  Design:
  - Every new field is a per-send option, never a global one.
  - SNI override changes only the ClientHello server name, while Host and the dialled address stay as they are.
  - The streaming timeout forces the streaming read for this send with its own cutoff.
  - Unpack chooses whether the tab shows MessageView `decoded`, which exists since qpfy, or the raw compressed bytes. It changes display only, and the stored bytes are untouched.
  - H2 reuse keeps one h2 connection per (tab, authority). It is off by default because today every send dials fresh; Burp's default is on, so this goes in gaps.md.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sni_override_test.go`: a TLS listener's `ClientHelloInfo.ServerName` equals the override while Host keeps the original name.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/repeater_h2_reuse_test.go`: two sends with reuse on give one accept, and with reuse off give two.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_redirects_test.go` (extended): the cross-domain hop keeps h1 when forced.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/streaming_policy_test.go` (extended): a per-send cutoff on an SSE listener.
  - `api_repeater_options_test.go`: unpack on and off changes only the decoded field.
Phase 4 — GraphQL context actions (closes burpsy-react-ui-7v1e)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx` and `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts`: a GraphQL submenu.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/graphql-introspection.ts`: the full standard query and the legacy variant.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_graphql_sitemap.go`, using `burpsy-go/pkg/graphqlmap` to turn the schema into operations and the existing site-map insert path, plus `route_manifest.go`, `route-risk.ts` and `gated-routes.ts`.
  Design:
  - "Set introspection query" replaces the body with the full standard query. The crawler's query at `internal/crawler/graphql.go:52` is deliberately cut down and is not reused.
  - The legacy variant drops the newer fields for old servers.
  - "Save GraphQL queries to site map" posts the selected response's message id. The server parses the schema, generates one query per operation (capped by `crawler.MaxGraphQLOperations`), and inserts them as site-map items without sending them.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_graphql_sitemap_test.go`: a fixture introspection answer gives N site-map nodes, a non-GraphQL body gives 400 with a reason, and `operations` is `[]` for an empty schema.
  - `graphql-introspection.test.ts`.
  - E2E `repeater-graphql.spec.ts`.
Phase 5 — HTTP/2 kettled requests and Inspector CRLF injection (closes burpsy-react-ui-jae5, burpsy-react-ui-ln2a)
  Files:
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/http2/kettle.go`: `KettleReasons`, built on the refusal kinds in `authorise.go`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_http2_kettle.go`, plus manifest and risk updates.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go`: `repeaterSendSpec.H2Headers`, sent through the existing frame-program path behind `/api/http2/program` (`AuthorisedSender.SendFrameProgramForcingHTTP2`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (`RepeaterTab.h2Headers`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/inspector.tsx` (context menu Copy name / Copy value; Shift+Return inserts `\r\n`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ui/editor.tsx` (kettled note).
  Design:
  - A tab becomes kettled when an Inspector edit makes something HTTP/1 text cannot carry (CRLF in a value, an uppercase name, pseudo-header order). The structured list is then the send's source.
  - Any edit to the raw text clears the list at the store's `updateRepeaterTab` chokepoint, following the shadow-copy data-loss lesson. The tab returns to the text path and the note disappears.
  - On an HTTP/1 tab, Shift+Return is refused with "would split the header; only HTTP/2 can carry this".
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/http2/kettle_test.go`: each reason.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/repeater_kettled_send_test.go`: an h2 TLS listener decodes one header whose value contains CRLF; refused on an h1-only target; reasons are `[]` when not kettled.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/repeater-tabs.test.ts`: editing the raw text clears `h2Headers`.
  - The e2e step in `inspector-reorder.spec.ts` for Copy value plus Shift+Return showing the kettled note.
Phase 6 — WebSocket attach, clone and reconnect (closes burpsy-react-ui-wuwf)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/proxy/ws.go`: a registry of live connections in `relayWebsocket`, and one locked writer per side shared by the relay goroutines and injection.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/proxy/ws_inject.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/wsclient/wsclient.go`: a new `Session` with a read loop, a bounded inbox, and Reconnect.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_ws.go`, which today handles a one-shot send and refuses to-client at :141.
  - Routes: `GET /api/ws/live`, `POST /api/repeater/ws/sessions`, `POST|GET|DELETE /api/repeater/ws/sessions/{id}…`, `POST /api/ws/live/{id}/send`, plus manifest and risk updates.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` and `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (a WS tab gains `session` / `attachedConnection`, and the handshake request becomes editable).
  - The e2e origin in `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/harness/server.ts` gains a WS echo endpoint.
  Design:
  - Attach means injecting frames on a live relayed connection: client-to-server frames are masked, server-to-client frames are not.
  - Injected frames bypass the interception queue and are recorded with `injected:true`, so the capture never pretends the peer sent them.
  - Clone opens a new Repeater session from the captured handshake, which the operator can edit. The session is authorised through `AuthorisedSender` at the handshake and kept open.
  - Reconnect re-dials using the same handshake.
  - Change frames reuse `changeWS`.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/proxy/ws_inject_test.go`, under `-race`: relay bytes are intact in both directions while frames are injected, with interception on and off, and injection into a closed connection returns a named error.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_ws_session_test.go`: open, send, read the echo, close, reconnect, and messages `[]` when empty.
  - E2E `repeater-ws-attach.spec.ts`.
Risks / open decisions:
- Size: 13 children, including two risky subsystems (WS injection into a live relay, and structured h2 sends). See the question below.
- Phase 5 assumes the frame-program path can carry a HEADERS block that is not normalised. If `h2program.go` cannot, Phase 5 needs a new sender primitive, which should be confirmed before Phase 5 starts.
- H2 reuse default (off versus Burp's on) and unpack being display-only both need sign-off and gaps.md entries.
- The Save entire history file format (a JSON bundle versus Burp's items XML) is undecided, because Burp's exact format is not in the evidence.
- Phase 3 depends on xixe Phase 1's `SendOptions` and Repeater override menu. Expect rebase conflicts in `repeater.tsx`.
QUESTION FOR THE USER: This epic is probably too large for one review. May I move Phase 6 (wuwf, WebSocket attach/clone/reconnect, which touches the live proxy relay) into its own follow-up PR, and possibly Phase 5 (jae5 + ln2a, structured h2 sends) as well? If you say no, all six phases ship as one PR with review checkpoints.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- Phase 3 extends the `sender.SendOptions` struct and the Repeater override menu that xixe Phase 1 introduces with mmca. xixe Phase 1 must merge first, or this PR rebases onto it.
- jva5 notes travelling to Intruder need a note field on xixe's attack tab (9bv2). The second PR to land adds it.
- pznm's export format could share a base64 "items" XML encoder with td8g's m7dk, if the user wants one Burp-XML writer. Otherwise they stay independent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each backend feature is covered by an `httptest` integration test through its real entry point:
  - `POST /api/repeater/send` with the new options (SNI, h2 reuse, streaming timeout, unpack, structured h2 headers);
  - the GraphQL site-map route, the history-export route, and the WS attach and session routes;
  - for WS attach, through a real relayed connection in `internal/proxy`.

  Each test asserts what the listener received: the SNI it saw, the header order and CRLF bytes, and the frames it got.
- Every new wire array is `[]`, not `null`, in marshalled JSON. That covers WS session messages, the live connection list, kettle reasons, and GraphQL operations saved. Asserted by a `*_wire_arrays_test.go` in `internal/web` for each new route.
- E2E specs perform the actions that reveal each view:
  - `repeater-workflow.spec.ts`: send twice with a changed payload and the diff highlight appears; type a note; tab search finds a tab; Save entire history downloads a file.
  - `inspector-reorder.spec.ts`: move a header up and the sent request's order matches.
  - `repeater-ws-attach.spec.ts`: proxy a WebSocket through the e2e origin, attach from Repeater, send to server and to client, and both frames show in the WebSocket history.
  - `repeater-graphql.spec.ts`: set the introspection query, send it, and save to the site map.
- A Repeater request with no Cookie header shows an empty Cookies view in Repeater, and adding a cookie there writes a `Cookie:` header. A read-only History editor still hides empty views.
- Reordering in the Inspector and saving entire history are byte-faithful:
  - Reordering moves whole header lines, including duplicates, with no normalisation.
  - The export is built from message ids (`/api/message/{id}` base64), not from displayed text.
  - Both use binary and multibyte fixtures.
- Kettled requests:
  - Typing CRLF into an h2 header value through Inspector Shift+Return marks the tab kettled, and the editor shows "This request is kettled because: …" with the reasons from `internal/http2`.
  - The send puts the header on the wire as one h2 header containing CRLF.
  - On an HTTP/1 tab, the same edit is refused with an explanation.
  - Editing the raw text afterwards invalidates the structured header copy (the shadow-copy lesson).
- WS attach injects frames without corrupting the relayed byte stream in either direction. A `-race` test proves this, with interception both on and off.
- Every new route is classified in `route_manifest.go` and `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.ts` is regenerated, and `route_manifest_test.go` passes. Divergences from Burp are in `gaps.md`.
- At the end of the epic, a live drive runs against the combined rebuild (`./ui-live.sh` with agent-browser, UI-VERIFICATION part c) covering each child's behaviour.
- Gate is green:
  - `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./...` with `gofmt -l .` empty; build, vet, `go test ./...`, `../e2e-go.sh`.
  - UI `tsc` plus `bun run check`.
  - `./ui-pass.sh --route repeater` with 0 axe violations.
  - The GitHub gate on the epic PR.
notes:
Split approved by the user on 2026-10-07: this epic ships as 3 PRs, one per sub-epic — burpsy-react-ui-i9ti.1 = Repeater A: editor views, tab workflow, per-tab overrides, GraphQL actions (PR 1 of 3); burpsy-react-ui-i9ti.2 = Repeater B: HTTP/2 kettled requests and Inspector CRLF injection (PR 2 of 3); burpsy-react-ui-i9ti.3 = Repeater C: WebSocket attach, clone and reconnect (PR 3 of 3). The QUESTION FOR THE USER in the design is answered by this split. Children now sit under the sub-epics; the plan's phases map to them as stated in each sub-epic's scope.
2026-10-09: i9ti.1 (PR #321) and i9ti.2 (PR #327) are closed; i9ti.3 (WebSocket attach, clone and reconnect) remains open.

title: Intruder: attack management and result analysis
description:
USER STORY
As a penetration tester running Intruder against a login form or an API parameter, I want to keep several attacks open in their own tabs and re-request only the attempts that failed on a network error. I also want each OOB hit tied to the payload that caused it and the results ranked by how much each response differs from the rest. Finally, I want to control how the attack uses the network: connection reuse, the HTTP version, a per-send response timeout, and keeping the Host header in step with the target. The outcome is that a 50,000-request attack that ends with a few dropped requests and one strange response can be finished and triaged where it is, without rerunning it or rebuilding it in a second tool.

---

Intruder's engine is at parity on attack and payload types; the residue is how attacks are managed and read. Attack tabs (9bv2) and Request item again (2rw7) are the workflow gaps. Collaborator interactions per result (nib6) and connection reuse with an HTTP-version override (xhqr) affect findings and speed. The rest are settings and result tooling: grep-payloads options (7qc3), capture filter (ip2b), Host-header sync (ety8), extract-from-highlight (df8r), append placement (1krs), storage switches (nqww), anomaly ranking (pglp) and per-send timeout (mmca, shared with Repeater).

Children: burpsy-react-ui-9bv2, burpsy-react-ui-2rw7, burpsy-react-ui-nib6, burpsy-react-ui-xhqr, burpsy-react-ui-7qc3, burpsy-react-ui-ip2b, burpsy-react-ui-ety8, burpsy-react-ui-df8r, burpsy-react-ui-1krs, burpsy-react-ui-nqww, burpsy-react-ui-pglp, burpsy-react-ui-mmca (12).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none. All 12 children are open and unclaimed.
Phase 1 — Send-path foundation: per-send options, connection reuse, HTTP version, Host sync (closes burpsy-react-ui-mmca, burpsy-react-ui-xhqr, burpsy-react-ui-ety8)
  Files:
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_send.go`, extracted from `handleIntruderRun` in `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go`, which currently runs from about :828 to :1426.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go` (new fields on `intruderRunReq`).
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sendopts.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sender.go` (`setDeadline`, `sendHTTP1Plain`).
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/sender/connpool.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/authorised.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/sender/pipeline.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/sender/h2.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/repeater_options.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.ts` (`RepeaterSendOptions`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` (override menu: Response timeout).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx` (Settings: Response timeout, HTTP/1 connection reuse, HTTP version, Update Host header to match target), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts` (`IntruderConfig`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/AGENTS.md`, `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/AGENTS.md`, `burpsy-go/gaps.md`.
  Design:
  - The send closure, which today holds the jar, redirects, timeout and authorising sender, becomes `buildIntruderSendPlan(req) (*intruderSendPlan, error)`, so every later phase changes one function. Phase 5 reuses it for requeue.
  - `sender.SendOptions{ResponseTimeout, …}` travels on the `ctx` (`sender.WithSendOptions`). `setDeadline` and the h2/pipeline read paths prefer it over `Network().readTimeout(host)`, so a per-send read bound never touches `NetworkSettings`.
  - Today's `timeout_ms` is a total per-attempt deadline. It exists in `api_tools.go:591` and `:1115`, but no UI sends it. It stays as is, and `response_timeout_ms` is added beside it as Burp's read timeout (`RequestOptions.withResponseTimeout`).
  - Repeater gets the same field on `repeaterSendOptions`. i9ti Phase 3 later adds its own fields to this same struct (see cross-epic dependencies).
  - xhqr connection reuse:
    - `sender.ConnPool` is keyed by authority and capped at `max_in_flight`.
    - A connection goes back to the pool only when the response was delimited cleanly and no `Connection: close` was sent or received. Otherwise it is closed.
    - `AuthorisedSender.SendReusing` still authorises every raw request. `SendKeepAlive` is a serial batch and not reusable here.
    - `http1_connection_reuse` together with `set_connection_close` gives 400, naming both settings.
    - `http_version` (`""|"http1"|"http2"`) goes through the existing `AuthorisedSender.SendAs(ctx, raw, pref)`.
  - ety8 Host sync:
    - `update_host_header` rewrites Host to the target authority after the splice, at the same point as `applyJarCookies`, so span offsets stay valid.
    - It is skipped when a selected position overlaps the Host header, the same rule as `exemptCookieNames`.
    - The report carries `host_header_updated`.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/sendopts_test.go`: a context-carried read timeout fires on a silent listener while a sibling send with no override completes, and `Network()` is unchanged.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/sender/connpool_test.go`, run with `-race`: N sends at `max_in_flight` k open at most k sockets; a `Connection: close` response is never reused; an unframed body is never reused.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_send_options_test.go`, through `/api/intruder/run`:
    - With reuse on, the listener counts fewer accepts than requests, and `connections_reused` is greater than 0.
    - `http_version:"http1"` against an h2-capable TLS listener negotiates h1.
    - Retargeting rewrites Host on the wire, and a Host position stays untouched.
    - The reuse plus Connection: close combination returns 400.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_repeater_options_test.go` (extended): `response_timeout_ms` bounds one Repeater send.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-state.test.ts`: the new config fields reach the request body.
Phase 2 — Payload placement and grep options (closes burpsy-react-ui-1krs, burpsy-react-ui-7qc3, burpsy-react-ui-df8r)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/points.go` (`PointConfig.Placement`), `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/engine.go` (`doSend` reflection, `Attempt`/`ResultBucket` fields), `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/process.go` (`URLEncodeSet` keeps the pre-encoding items), `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/payload.go` (`PayloadSet.Unencoded`).
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go`: both `handleIntruderPoints` and `/run` take `payload_placement` and `grep_payloads`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.tools.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-extract.ts`: builds the extract rule from a selection.
  Design:
  - 1krs append placement:
    - Append is a zero-length span at the end of the value.
    - `/points` (the display) and `/run` (execution) must take the same placement. If they don't, the UI shows append markers while the attack replaces values.
    - The manual-versus-discovered overlap check at `api_tools.go:897` misses zero-length spans, so it is fixed to treat an equal offset as an overlap.
  - 7qc3 grep-payloads options:
    - Options: `{enabled, case_sensitive, exclude_headers, match_pre_url_encoded}`.
    - `reflected` stays the bucket key and is computed with the configured options. Changing the options can therefore change the bucket count, which is stated in gaps.md.
    - The per-set `reflected_counts []int` is reported per attempt and per bucket, not added to the key.
    - For pre-URL-encoded matching, `URLEncodeSet` keeps the original items before rewriting them in place.
  - df8r is UI only. "Define extract grep from response" on a result row opens the stored response, and the operator highlights text. `intruder-extract.ts` builds a regex from escaped prefix and suffix anchors with a lazy capture, writes it into `grepExtract`, and previews the match against that response before saving.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/points_append_test.go`: the append span is zero-length at the end of the value, and the splice gives `base+payload`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_placement_test.go`: `/points` and `/run` agree, and a zero-length manual span at a discovered span's offset is refused.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/engine_grep_payloads_test.go`: a case-folded match, a header-only reflection excluded, and an encoded payload matched only when `match_pre_url_encoded` is set.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_wire_arrays_test.go` (extended): `reflected_counts` is `[]`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-extract.test.ts`: regex metacharacters are escaped, and a multi-line selection works.
  - The e2e highlight-to-extract step in `intruder-attack.spec.ts`.
Phase 3 — Capture filter and storage switches (closes burpsy-react-ui-ip2b, burpsy-react-ui-nqww)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/engine.go` (`collector`, `RecordRequest`/`RequestFn`, `record`), `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.tools.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-export.ts`.
  Design:
  - `capture_filter{discard_no_response, term, regex, case_sensitive, negate, statuses}` runs in the collector before the `Attempts` append and before the exemplar record.
  - `Sent`, `Failed` and the bucket counts never shrink, and a new `discarded` counter is reported.
  - `store_requests` and `store_responses` (defaults on) skip `RequestFn` and `record` respectively. The ids then go out as `null`, and the UI shows "not stored (attack setting)", never an empty message.
  - The capture filter is distinct from the existing client-side view filter at `intruder.tsx:91-119`, and the UI labels it as destructive.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/capture_filter_test.go`: `discarded` plus kept equals sent, and buckets still count discarded attempts.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_storage_switch_test.go`: with `store_responses:false`, the traffic store does not grow by one exemplar per bucket, and the marshalled JSON has `"example_response_id":null`.
  - `intruder_wire_arrays_test.go`: arrays are `[]` when every row is discarded.
  - `intruder-export.test.ts`: the CSV is correct with null ids.
Phase 4 — Attack tabs (closes burpsy-react-ui-9bv2)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/store.ts`: `intruder`, `intruderRun` and `intruderTab` become `intruderTabs[]`, `activeIntruderTab` and `closedIntruderTabs`, with persist `version` and `migrate`.
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-tabs.ts`, mirroring `repeater-tabs.ts`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/app.tsx` (menubar `intruderCommand` and `intruderStatus` are aimed at the active tab), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/palette-commands.ts`.
  Design:
  - A send-to opens a new tab instead of replacing one. That changes the semantics of `intruderSeed`, so the effect at `intruder.tsx:1362` changes.
  - There are Close, Close others, Reopen closed tab and Rename actions, and the tab cap follows the Repeater pattern.
  - The run mutation and `myTaskId` are keyed by tab id. `/run` stays synchronous, so a running attack lives in its tab's mutation and survives a tab switch.
  - The `intruderLaunchBlocker` check runs per tab.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/intruder-tabs.test.ts`: a v-old persisted blob becomes one tab with an identical config; open, close and reopen; the cap.
  - `intruder-menu-bridge.test.ts` (updated).
  - The two-tab e2e step in `intruder-attack.spec.ts`, including launching in tab 1, switching to tab 2 and back, with the results present.
Phase 5 — Retained attacks: Request item again and Collaborator interactions (closes burpsy-react-ui-2rw7, burpsy-react-ui-nib6)
  Files:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_intruder_control.go`: `attackRegistry` keeps a bounded LRU of finished replay contexts.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_send.go`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_collaborator.go`: `mintedPayload` gains `Attack *mintAttribution{task_id, set, item}`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/server.go`: routes `POST /api/intruder/attacks/{id}/requeue` and `GET /api/intruder/attacks/{id}/interactions`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/route_manifest.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/route-risk.ts`, `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/gated-routes.ts`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx` (row menu, Interactions column, interaction detail pane), `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.attack.ts`.
  - E2E fixture: a new `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/harness/fake-interactsh.mjs`, plus `server.ts`, which points `/api/collaborator/server` `client_path` at it. The origin script appends a JSONL interaction whenever a request carries a minted domain.
  Design:
  - The replay context holds the base request, the selected points, the resolved sets (including minted addresses and `ChainPayloads`), the plan, the grep settings, a snapshot of the cookie jar (so requeued rows compare with their bucket), and the send plan from Phase 1.
  - Requeue answers with fresh `Attempt` rows that keep their ordinal and carry `requeued:true`. An evicted context gives 410.
  - Before implementing, confirm whether `RequestFn` stores bytes from before or after the jar is applied.
  - Interactions are reached through attribution, not by holding the attack open. The endpoint returns `{rows:[{ordinal,address,count,interaction_ids}], unattributed}`, and the UI polls it while the tab is visible.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_requeue_test.go`: a listener that fails ordinal 3 once; requeue `[3]` sends the identical payload bytes; 410 after eviction; a recursive-grep ordinal resolves.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_collaborator_test.go` (extended, with the fake channel): an interaction on minted item k is attributed to its ordinal, and the marshalled `rows` is `[]` with no hits.
  - `route_manifest_test.go`.
  - The e2e Collaborator step in `intruder-attack.spec.ts`.
Phase 6 — Response variations and anomaly ranking (closes burpsy-react-ui-pglp)
  Files:
  - New `burpsy-go/internal/analysis/variations.go`, `burpsy-go/internal/analysis/rank.go` and `burpsy-go/internal/analysis/AGENTS.md`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tools.go`: rank the kept attempts after `Run`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/engine.go`: `Attempt.AnomalyRank *int`.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx`: an "Anomaly rank" column, sortable.
  - `burpsy-go/gaps.md`.
  Design:
  - Port the attribute set from `/root/burp-re/in/extract/burp/api/montoya/http/message/responses/analysis/AttributeType.java`. That enum has 32 values, while the bead says 33; reconcile this before coding.
  - Port the ranking from `/root/burp-re/out/clean/compilable/burp/RankingUtilsHelper001.java`. It uses an attribute subset (`Zq`), a rank of -1 when there is no response, and scoring in Z_f, Zs00 and Zuy3, which still need reading.
  - Ranking runs over the stored exemplar and attempt responses within `DetailLimit`. When responses are not stored (Phase 3), the rank is `null` and the reason is given.
  - Moving `scanner/infra_authdiff.go` to this attribute set is optional and gated on no change in finding counts. Otherwise a follow-up bead is filed.
  Tests:
  - `burpsy-go/internal/analysis/variations_test.go`: per-attribute golden cases, such as tag names, word count and cookie names.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/analysis/rank_test.go`: the one outlier among N identical responses ranks first, and a missing response gives -1.
  - `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_anomaly_test.go`: the real `/run` against a listener that returns one different body puts that ordinal at rank 1, and the field is `null` with `store_responses:false`.
Risks / open decisions:
- Size: 12 children across sender, engine, API, a rework of the page's state, and a new analysis package. See the question below.
- The default for `update_host_header`. Burp's is on; burpsy treats an absent field as "behave as before". Proposal: the UI sends true, and an API nil means false. This needs sign-off and a gaps.md entry.
- The anomaly-ranking scoring classes (Z_f, Zs00, Zuy3) have not been read yet. If they cannot be recovered, the fallback is a documented rarity score labelled as such, not "Burp's algorithm".
- Rebase hazard: the live worktree has uncommitted changes from another session in `pages/intruder.tsx`, `pages/comparer.tsx`, `oob/client.go` and `api_collaborator.go`. Branch from master and expect conflicts in `intruder.tsx`.
- Phase 5 changes `mintedPayload` while 8e3n (in progress) also edits `api_collaborator.go`. Land Phase 5 after 8e3n merges.
- The LRU bound for retained replay contexts (count and bytes) needs choosing. Resolved sets can be large, so they should be capped by bytes, not only by count.
QUESTION FOR THE USER: This epic is probably too large for one review, about six phases spanning sender, engine, API and a state migration. May I split it into two PRs?
- PR-A covers Phases 1–3: mmca, xhqr, ety8, 1krs, 7qc3, df8r, ip2b, nqww.
- PR-B covers Phases 4–6: 9bv2, 2rw7, nib6, pglp.

If you say no, it ships as one PR with six review checkpoints.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- mmca closes here, both halves: the sender-level `SendOptions`, Intruder `response_timeout_ms`, and Repeater `repeaterSendOptions.response_timeout_ms` plus its override control in `repeater.tsx`. i9ti Phase 3 (of0z, adkx, k011) adds fields to the same `SendOptions` struct and the same override menu, so it lands after xixe Phase 1 or rebases onto it.
- nib6 (Phase 5) depends on 8e3n (odvj, in progress) merging first, and must not collide with odvj's d657. Both edit `mintedPayload` and `api_collaborator.go`. d657 also persists minted payloads, so its schema must include the `Attack` attribution field.
- 9bv2 attack tabs: i9ti's jva5 says notes travel with a request sent to another tool, so send-to-Intruder carrying a note needs a field on the Intruder tab. Whichever PR lands second adds that field.
- The `internal/analysis` package (pglp) could later back i9ti's b4gt response highlighting, but b4gt does not depend on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every request each child adds goes through the real `POST /api/intruder/run` in an `httptest` integration test against a real local listener (pattern: `engine_net_test.go`, `intruder_wire_arrays_test.go`). That covers capture filter, storage switches, append placement, grep-payload options, Host sync, HTTP version, connection reuse, and the per-send timeout. Each test asserts what reached the listener, not only the report.
- Every array the UI reads is `[]` and never `null` in the marshalled JSON of a clean run. This is asserted by extending `burpsy-go/internal/web/intruder_wire_arrays_test.go` to cover the new fields: `reflected_counts`, `discarded` rows, the requeue rows, the interactions rows, and the anomaly fields. Fields that are null on purpose (`example_response_id` when responses are not stored, `anomaly_rank` with no response) are declared nullable in `types.tools.ts`. A Go test confirms that the TS declaration matches the wire.
- An e2e spec actually launches attacks and drives the results: `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/specs/intruder-attack.spec.ts`. It sends two exchanges to Intruder and checks that two tabs exist. It runs an attack and checks that the Results tab renders rows with no "This view failed to render". It right-clicks a row, chooses Request item again, and checks that the row updates. It runs a Collaborator-payload attack against the fake OOB client and checks that the Interactions column shows a count of at least 1. It also defines an extract grep by highlighting a response.
- Every setting proves on the wire that it did something:
  - `connections_opened` and `connections_reused` (reuse), `protocol` (version override).
  - `discarded` (capture filter), `requeued` (Request item again), `host_header_updated` (Host sync).
  - A setting with no observable effect fails its test.
- Request item again re-sends exactly the resolved payload combination for that ordinal, through the same authorising sender. An evicted attack gives 410, and a recursive-grep ordinal uses `ChainPayloads`. Both cases are tested.
- A Collaborator interaction is attributed to its attack, payload set and item. Attempts beyond `DetailLimit` are reported as an `unattributed` count, not silently left out.
- The per-send response timeout applies to Intruder (`response_timeout_ms`) and to Repeater's per-tab override. Two concurrent sends with different timeouts each honour their own, and the global network settings are unchanged. Asserted in `sender` and `web` tests.
- Moving persisted state to attack tabs preserves an existing single-config localStorage blob as one tab (a zustand `version` + `migrate` test). Switching tabs does not abort a running attack.
- Every new route is in `route_manifest.go` and `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.ts` is regenerated, and `route_manifest_test.go` passes.
- Every divergence from Burp is recorded in `burpsy-go/gaps.md`. That includes the reuse plus Connection: close refusal, the anomaly-ranking algorithm source, and the default for Host sync. `internal/intruder/AGENTS.md` and `internal/sender/AGENTS.md` document the send-plan builder and per-send `SendOptions`.
- At the end of the epic, a live drive runs against the combined rebuild (`./ui-live.sh` with agent-browser, `docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md` part c): attack tabs, run, requeue, OOB interactions, anomaly sort.
- Gate is green:
  - `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./...` with `gofmt -l .` empty; `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `../e2e-go.sh`.
  - UI `tsc` plus `bun run check`.
  - `./ui-pass.sh --route intruder --route repeater` with 0 axe violations.
  - The GitHub gate on the epic PR.
notes: Split approved by the user on 2026-10-07: this epic ships as 2 PRs, one per sub-epic — burpsy-react-ui-xixe.1 = Intruder A: send settings, payload placement, grep and capture (PR 1 of 2); burpsy-react-ui-xixe.2 = Intruder B: attack tabs, Request item again, Collaborator interactions, anomaly ranking (PR 2 of 2). The QUESTION FOR THE USER in the design is answered by this split. Children now sit under the sub-epics; the plan's phases map to them as stated in each sub-epic's scope.
close_reason: All child epics closed (xixe.1 by PR #310, xixe.2 by PR #318).

title: MCP tool surface
description:
USER STORY
As a pentester driving burpsy from an AI assistant, I want a short list of capability-grouped MCP tools with typed arguments, paged and windowed reads, structured request edits, and task handles that report progress and completion, so that the model can drive a long engagement without guessing wire shapes or blocking on an audit. As an operator, I want each confirmation bound to the exact call it previews, and per-tool and per-project policy with a floor I cannot lower by accident, so that approving an agent's step means approving exactly what will run.

---

Burp's 54-tool agent registry has 42 burpsy equivalents, 30 of them full. This epic closes the shape gaps that make burpsy harder for a model to drive. Start with typed input schemas (3zw0) and capability-grouped tools (cvzq), because every other item lands on that surface. Then task handles and progress push (wdza), paged datasets (co88), windowed message reads (yahm) and structured send edits (vuxy). Policy follows: call-bound confirmations with previews (e0yq) and per-tool policy (2jig). Small API additions: collaborator long-poll (myr2), site map add by message id (4bfp), and an in-scope query (z5z3). Skills (ulsy) last.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-3zw0, burpsy-react-ui-cvzq, burpsy-react-ui-wdza, burpsy-react-ui-co88, burpsy-react-ui-yahm, burpsy-react-ui-vuxy, burpsy-react-ui-e0yq, burpsy-react-ui-2jig, burpsy-react-ui-myr2, burpsy-react-ui-4bfp, burpsy-react-ui-z5z3, burpsy-react-ui-ulsy (12).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none — all 12 children open. Context: q31t (MCP transport), ejp5 (confirm gate) and acdv (tool registry) are closed and are the base.

Phase 1 — Typed schemas and capability-grouped tools (closes 3zw0, cvzq)
  Files: internal/web/route_manifest.go (route gains a request type and query params); new internal/web/route_schema.go (reflect → JSON Schema from json/desc tags); handlers' anonymous request structs hoisted to named types (api_capture.go historyDelete, api_scanner_audit.go, api_tools.go — repeaterSendReq already named — and others); internal/web/mcp_export.go (MCPRouteInfo.InputSchema); new internal/mcp/groups.go; internal/mcp/tools.go; cmd/burpsy-mcp/main.go (-surface grouped|routes, default grouped); docs/MCP.md.
  Design: the handler's own type is the single source; 3zw0's "second source nothing checks" objection is answered by a checker — a shared decodeBody[T] with DisallowUnknownFields plus a test sweep. Groups are a curated table (short description, group name); the risk class is always read from the manifest. -surface routes keeps today's generator for debugging.
  Tests: web/route_schema_test.go (every body-taking mutating route declares a type; generated example accepted; unknown field → 400); mcp_test.go (grouped list JSON with typed properties and no assets; coverage test; existing binding and gate tests).

Phase 2 — Reads that scale and small API additions (closes co88, yahm, z5z3, 4bfp, myr2)
  Files: internal/web/api_capture.go handleMessage window params byte_offset, max_bytes ≤ 65536, pattern with context (returns total_bytes, next_offset, matches); new internal/web/api_datasets.go route /api/datasets/ GET riskRead (sources history, issues, sitemap, tool-log, ws-history, intruder/{id}; params q, regex, columns, sort, offset, limit, facets, wait_seconds ≤ 60, since); new /api/scope/check GET ?url= / POST {urls} riskRead (in_scope + matched rule); new /api/sitemap/record POST {exchange_id} riskLocal (following /api/issues/record — adding by id destroys nothing, so not behind riskDestructive /api/sitemap); internal/web/api_collaborator.go poll body payload_id, wait_seconds ≤ 60, min_interactions; internal/mcp groups.
  Design: the dataset envelope is a new route, so the UI's /api/history shape is untouched; long-polls are bounded below the MCP -timeout.
  Tests: web/datasets_api_test.go (page to the last row; facets; long-poll wakes on a new row; marshalled envelope); web/message_window_test.go (3 MiB body read fully in windows; pattern anchor); web/scope_check_test.go (same answer as the capture matcher for include, exclude, port); web/sitemap_record_test.go; web/collaborator_poll_wait_test.go (returns early on an interaction and at the deadline with none); mcp_test.go windowed read via tools/call past maxResultBytes.

Phase 3 — Structured send edits (closes vuxy)
  Files: new internal/reqedit/ (ops set/add/remove_header, set/remove_query_param, set_form_fields, set_json_field, set/remove_cookie, set_method, set_path, set_body, raw_replace); internal/web/api_tools.go (repeaterSendReq gains from_message, edits, http_version "1.1"|"2" via the existing force-h2 path, dry_run).
  Design: ops work on raw bytes and touch only the addressed span; Content-Length fixed; dry_run returns the edited bytes without sending — reused by e0yq previews and riw8 2z3c. The route stays riskEgress.
  Tests: reqedit/reqedit_test.go (each op byte-exact elsewhere; duplicate headers; invalid ops refused); web/repeater_edits_test.go (the httptest target received exactly the dry-run bytes; HTTP/2 forced).

Phase 4 — Task handles and progress push (closes wdza)
  Files: internal/web/api_scanner_audit.go (async:true → dash task, 202 {task_id}); route_manifest.go (/api/tasks/ gains GET {id}); internal/mcp/mcp.go (bounded concurrent dispatch with a mutex-serialised encoder; logging capability; notifications/cancelled; 15s sync window then a handle plus burpsy_task_status; notifications/progress when the client sent a progressToken; a transport-owned SSE subscription to /api/events pushing notifications/message for task completion and High findings).
  Design: the handle lives server-side (dash.Registry) so it survives an MCP restart; cancel is the existing riskLocal /api/tasks/{id}/cancel.
  Tests: mcp_test.go with a shortened window (handle returned; ping answered while a call is pending; completion notification carries the task id; progress only with a token; cancellation stops the dash task); -race.

Phase 5 — Call-bound confirmations with preview (closes e0yq)
  Files: internal/web/confirm_gate.go (mint body {method, path, query, body}; canonical digest; per-route previewer and driftIgnore fields in the manifest; bounded body buffering at spend); internal/mcp/tools.go (burpsy_confirm takes the full call, returns preview + token); ui src/lib/api.ts and its test; docs/MCP.md.
  Design: route-only tokens are removed so no weaker path remains. Send preview = reqedit dry-run + scope verdict; audit preview = the exchange + a config summary.
  Tests: confirm_gate_test.go (drift → 428 and token burned; same body → 200; another path on the same route refused; preview JSON); mcp_test.go (confirm-then-call with mutated args refused); bun test src/lib (mint helper).

Phase 6 — Per-tool policy and autonomy mode (closes 2jig)
  Files: persist settings key agent_policy; new /api/settings/agent-policy GET/PUT riskScope, not exposed to agents; internal/web/confirm_gate.go (applied to requests with X-Burpsy-Agent, which the transport always sets); internal/mcp (hide disabled tools; refuse the policy route); ui pages/settings.tsx.
  Design: per tool Ask / Act / Disabled. Modes: Manual — every non-read call needs a token; Smart — today's set; Autonomous — only the floor. The floor is needsConfirmation membership and cannot be lowered; "always approve" exists only above the floor.
  Tests: web/agent_policy_test.go (disabled → 403 for agent-marked calls; Manual gates a riskLocal call; Autonomous cannot relax a floor class; the PUT itself needs a token); mcp_test.go (tools/list omits disabled tools; policy route unreachable).

Phase 7 — Skills library (closes ulsy)
  Files: cmd/burpsy/cli.go (-skills dir, named by the operator at start; no route takes a path); new internal/skills/ (manifest: name, description, prompt, tools, optional script); /api/skills GET riskRead; internal/mcp/mcp.go (prompts capability: prompts/list, prompts/get with a banner listing the tools a skill calls); Phase 6 policy store for per-project disable; settings.tsx.
  Design: prompt-only skills ship in this PR; script-bearing skills run via wiwh /api/scripts/run (gated) and are listed as unavailable with the reason until wiwh lands.
  Tests: skills/skills_test.go (malformed manifest refused and counted); mcp_test.go (prompts/list and prompts/get JSON; a disabled skill is absent).

Risks / open decisions:
- X-Burpsy-Agent is spoofable: policy prevents accidents, not an adversary, until console auth (s19k) lands — the same limit ejp5 already states for self-minted tokens.
- Hoisting handler request types touches many api_*.go files and conflicts easily with in-flight branches.
- Concurrent MCP dispatch changes a strictly sequential transport; -race coverage is mandatory.
- Buffering bodies at the gate for the digest needs a size bound; large gated bodies such as HAR import need a stated limit.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: 2jrr is borderline for one PR — 7 phases that change the MCP transport model, the confirm-gate contract and the UI's mint path. Keep it as one PR, or make the policy half (e0yq, 2jig) its own PR?

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- wiwh 6c8f consumes co88, wdza, 3zw0 and e0yq; landing 2jrr Phases 1-5 before wiwh Phase 4 avoids interim shapes.
- 2jig's floor must include wiwh's new riskScript class; defining the floor by needsConfirmation makes this automatic.
- z5z3 and yahm helpers are reused by wiwh Phase 5 (scope.check, store.message).
- vuxy's reqedit and e0yq's previews are prerequisites for riw8 2z3c.
- wdza's cancel path and notification stream are reused by riw8 h83q (Stop interrupts in-flight calls) once x40l exists.
- ulsy's script skills depend on wiwh Phases 1 and 4.
acceptance_criteria:
- The default tools/list is the grouped surface: no asset routes, no _subtree spellings; each tool binds exactly one (pattern, verb) and never spans two risk classes. A test asserts every non-asset manifest route-verb is reachable from exactly one grouped tool or sits on an explicit not-exposed list with a reason. TestAToolCannotReachARouteItDoesNotName still passes.
- Every grouped tool's inputSchema is derived from the handler's own request type and proven against the handler: an example valid against the schema is accepted by the real handler; an unknown field is refused with 400. The dangling "See /api/apidoc" reference (a route that does not exist) is gone from tools.go and docs/MCP.md.
- A body over the 1 MiB result cap can be read to its last byte through windowed reads, and a long history paged to its last row through the dataset route — both tested through MCP tools/call, not only the HTTP handler.
- A confirmation is bound to a digest of method, path, query and canonical body: the same token on a drifted body → 428 with a drift reason and the token burned; burpsy_confirm returns the preview the token authorises (for a send: the edited raw bytes and the scope verdict). The UI moves to call-bound minting (src/lib/api.ts) in the same PR.
- An audit started asynchronously returns a task handle within the sync window; the MCP session keeps answering ping and other calls meanwhile; completion and high-severity findings arrive as notifications; notifications/cancelled stops the task — tested over the real stdio transport against a real gated server.
- Policy only tightens below the floor: a tool disabled by policy is refused server-side for agent-marked calls; an always-require class cannot be relaxed by any policy; the policy route is riskScope, gated, and refused by the MCP transport.
- Every new route has a manifest entry and risk class; the confirmation-worthy test list, gated-routes.ts, route-risk.ts and MCP tool counts are updated.
- Marshalled JSON asserted for the dataset envelope (rows [] when empty, facets null unless requested), message windows (matches []), scope check, collaborator poll, preview, task handles and notifications.
- Live drive: a real MCP client over stdio against the combined rebuild — initialize; grouped typed tools/list; a windowed read past the cap; an edited send with preview → confirm → drift refusal; an async audit with its completion notification; a collaborator long-poll.
- Gate green: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./..., build, vet, go test ./..., go test -race ./internal/mcp/..., UI tsc + bun run check, ../e2e-go.sh, GitHub gate on the epic PR.
notes: Split approved by the user on 2026-10-07: this epic ships as 2 PRs, one per sub-epic — burpsy-react-ui-2jrr.1 = MCP surface: typed grouped tools, scalable reads, structured sends, task handles, skills (PR 1 of 2); burpsy-react-ui-2jrr.2 = MCP confirmation and policy: call-bound confirmations, per-tool policy (PR 2 of 2). The QUESTION FOR THE USER in the design is answered by this split. Children now sit under the sub-epics; the plan's phases map to them as stated in each sub-epic's scope.

title: Plugin protocol and script runtime
description:
USER STORY
As an extension author, I want my JSON-RPC plugin to read the traffic store, keep state, send in-scope requests, hook proxy and tool traffic, and contribute Intruder payloads and scan checks, so that an auth signer, a verifier or a custom detection can be written in any language without a JVM. As an operator, I want short sandboxed scripts in Match & Replace rules, Repeater custom actions and an agent-callable script runner, all on one runtime behind the same scope and confirmation controls as the rest of the console, so that I can automate a computed rewrite or a bulk check without ever handing a model or a plugin an ungated way to run code or send traffic.

---

burpsy's JSON-RPC plugin protocol covers UI registration points only. The Montoya capabilities extension authors rely on are absent: originate requests (p81m), traffic hooks (tvv5), scan checks and insertion points (9r77), payload generators (0qwh), persistence (97dk), store read access (ieg3), event-log events (rvq2), hotkey selection (gqvg) and AI prompts (xpuh). FIRST STEP, shared by 80wl, 1944 and 6c8f: decide whether the sandboxed script runtime from ydmj backs a general script runner. Match & Replace script rules, Repeater custom actions and the MCP script family all depend on that one call.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-p81m, burpsy-react-ui-tvv5, burpsy-react-ui-9r77, burpsy-react-ui-0qwh, burpsy-react-ui-97dk, burpsy-react-ui-ieg3, burpsy-react-ui-rvq2, burpsy-react-ui-gqvg, burpsy-react-ui-xpuh, burpsy-react-ui-80wl, burpsy-react-ui-1944, burpsy-react-ui-6c8f (12).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none — all 12 children open. Context: ydmj (the pre-request run_script session action) is closed and is the sandbox being generalised.

Phase 1 — Script runtime and code-execution risk-class decision (closes none; every script phase and the risk half of plugin phases 5-8 depend on it)
  Files: internal/jsexec/request_script.go; new internal/jsexec/script.go; new internal/scriptrun/ (runner importing jsexec + sender + store); internal/web/route_manifest.go, agent_tools.go, agent_tools_test.go, route_manifest_test.go; ui src/lib/route-manifest.ts, gated-routes.ts, route-risk.ts; internal/jsexec/AGENTS.md; gaps.md.
  Design: options — (A) generalise the ydmj goja sandbox into one capability-scoped runtime shared by 80wl, 1944, 6c8f; (B) scripts are plugins (child processes); (C) one runtime per feature; (D) Bambda/Java compatibility. RECOMMEND A: B puts a process round trip on the proxy hot path per M&R rule and cannot serve agent-authored code without a path-taking route (forbidden by the allowlist rule); C means three sandboxes to audit that will drift; D is declined by ROADMAP. Shape: jsexec stays a leaf with no host bindings; scripts return send intents (burpsy.send / burpsy.sendAll only record them); internal/scriptrun dispatches intents through AuthorisedSender with pacing, a per-run cap and the scope check on final bytes, then calls an optional onResponses(results) exactly once. Messages become raw bytes plus ordered [][]string header pairs (matching extension.SessionRequest) — ydmj's map[string]string loses order and duplicates; request.headers stays as a compatibility view. Programs compile once at install (*goja.Program), fresh VM per run. Budgets: pre-request 500ms / 64KB source; M&R 50ms per rule per message, oversize bodies skipped and counted; Repeater 2s; MCP run up to 120s with the send cap in the confirmed args. Risk: add riskScript ("runs operator- or agent-authored script source") to needsConfirmation with safety/tier/group/hints entries; riskExecute stays outside the set (its reason — the operator allowlisted the binary — does not cover agent-authored source). Plugin grants are the plugin-side analogue: a command-line decision, never a request field.
  Tests: jsexec/script_test.go (duplicate-header ordered request round-trips byte-identically; intents returned, not executed; each budget interrupts while(true){}); scriptrun/runner_test.go against httptest (out-of-scope intent refused and counted; cap enforced; onResponses once; a throw leaves no partial result); agent_tools_test.go (riskScript in the set, safety string derived); bun run check accepts the new class.

Phase 2 — Match & Replace script rules (closes 80wl)
  Files: internal/matchreplace/matchreplace.go (TargetRequestScript/TargetResponseScript before TargetCount, Rule.Script, ScriptFailed() counter); internal/persist/persist.go (script column migration); internal/web/api_toolkit.go; route_manifest.go (new /api/tools/rules/scripts GET/PUT riskScript); ui pages/matchreplace.tsx.
  Design: script rules install only through their own gated route; /api/tools/rules (riskLocal) and /api/tools/rules/test (riskRead) answer 400 for a script target and name the gated route — otherwise a riskRead route would execute code. The script receives the raw message and returns a replacement or null; applied in rule order inside RuleSet.Apply, honouring InScopeOnly and Content-Length fixing; a failure passes bytes through and counts.
  Tests: matchreplace_script_test.go (enum walk covers the targets; unchanged → byte-identical; throw/timeout → unchanged + counter); web/matchreplace_script_api_test.go (gated sequence; marshalled rule list with script only on script targets, empty list pinned; riskLocal route refuses a script target); proxy integration: a request through the real listener rewritten by a script rule.

Phase 3 — Repeater custom actions (closes 1944)
  Files: new internal/web/api_repeater_actions.go; persist repeater_actions table; route_manifest.go /api/repeater/actions GET/PUT riskScript and /api/repeater/actions/run POST riskScript; ui pages/repeater.tsx, lib/data.ts.
  Design: an action is a stored script run over a tab's request and last response, returning text, extracted variables and optionally capped send intents via scriptrun. "Auto-run on response" is per-tab UI state — the operator's standing consent; the UI mints a token per run; an MCP caller cannot set it. Output and log lists are bounded.
  Tests: web/repeater_actions_api_test.go (gated sequence; marshalled result JSON; out-of-scope intent refused); UI lib test for auto-run minting; live: an auto-run action fires on a real response.

Phase 4 — MCP script execution family (closes 6c8f)
  Files: new internal/web/api_scripts.go; persist scripts table (id, name, source, param schema); route_manifest.go /api/scripts GET/POST riskScript (update keeps the id; a compile error stores nothing and returns line-numbered errors), /api/scripts/run POST riskScript (inline or stored; typed params: message id, exchange id, a dataset as an internal/query filter resolved host-side with a row cap), /api/scripts/results/ GET riskRead; internal/dash (task kind script/bulk-send); internal/toollog (ToolScript); internal/mcp grouped entries; docs/MCP.md.
  Design: Burp mapping — run → /api/scripts/run; update → POST /api/scripts; inspect-result → /api/scripts/results/{id}; bulk-send → a run returning sendAll (a dash task, results as a paged dataset); cancel-bulk-send → the existing /api/tasks/{id}/cancel (in-flight sends finish, partial rows stay readable). The bulk cap is part of the confirmed body, covered by the e0yq digest once 2jrr lands.
  Tests: web/scripts_api_test.go (compile error stores nothing; id preserved on update; bulk send creates a dash task, cancel stops scheduling, partial rows remain; marshalled result/dataset JSON); internal/mcp/mcp_test.go (tools/call without confirm → isError carrying the 428 body; with token → result).

Phase 5 — Plugin host services, grants and read/local methods (closes ieg3, 97dk, rvq2, gqvg)
  Files: internal/extension/protocol.go (MethodSpecs rows, Manifest.Capabilities, ungranted-method error code); session.go (inbound entries); host.go (Config.Plugins[...].Grants; a HostServices interface defined here so the package stays a leaf); new internal/web/extension_services.go (adapter modelled on extension_session_action.go); cmd/burpsy/cli.go (-plugin-grants name=read+storage+events,...); persist extension_data table; internal/dash/events.go (extension source); ui lib/plugin-hotkeys.ts, pages/extensions.tsx.
  Design: methods store.history (query DSL, offset/limit ≤ 500), store.message (windowed, reusing yahm's helper), store.sitemap, store.issues, store.organizer, scope.check (the z5z3 matcher), storage.get/set/delete/list (project-scoped, bounded per plugin; preferences in a user-level file that survives reload), events.raise (debug/info/error/critical, rate-limited, drops counted); hotkey.invoke gains an optional selection {exchanges, message, raw} filled by the console (its "no selection" Why text is corrected). Each method is refused unless granted; refused grant requests appear in PluginView.
  Tests: extension/host_services_test.go with helper-plugin behaviours (ungranted → error code; granted → rows; storage survives unload/load and a persist reopen; events.raise appears in /api/dashboard JSON); hotkey_test.go (selection passed through); protocol_test.go green; marshalled PluginView JSON.

Phase 6 — Plugin-originated requests and AI prompt (closes p81m, xpuh)
  Files: internal/extension/protocol.go (remove the p81m UnsupportedCapabilities row; update AGENTS.md); internal/web/extension_services.go; new internal/llm/ (OpenAI-compatible client extracted from internal/scanner/triage.go, triage switched to it); internal/toollog (ToolExtension).
  Design: http.send / http.sendMany (bounded concurrency and per-call total) build an AuthorisedSender per call with pacing and session-rule tool scope "extensions", returning status, raw response and tool-log id; a refusal is reported as a refusal, never an empty response. ai.prompt runs host-side under the operator's endpoint config with the two-gate rule (configured AND enabled); the API key never crosses to the plugin. Grants send and ai are separate (ai is third-party egress).
  Tests: extension/http_send_test.go (helper plugin vs httptest: in-scope sent and logged as extension:<name>; out-of-scope refused with reason; no grant → refused); extension/ai_prompt_test.go (fake chat endpoint; bytes on the plugin's stdin never contain the key; unconfigured → refusal); scanner/triage_test.go green after the extraction.

Phase 7 — Traffic hooks (closes tvv5)
  Files: internal/extension/protocol.go (kinds http-handler, proxy-request-handler, proxy-response-handler, ws-handler, one method each); internal/proxy/options.go (hook seam beside ApplyRequest/ApplyResponse); internal/sender/authorised.go (pre-bind hook seam); new internal/web/extension_traffic_hooks.go; internal/wsclient.
  Design: hooks run BEFORE the scope check on final bytes; a hook that moves the authority out of scope is refused and counted. Budget 2s per hook (well below DefaultCallTimeout); timeout/error/crash → original passes and counts. In-scope traffic only by default; "all" is an explicit grant option. Proxy hook answers: continue, modify, intercept, doNotIntercept, drop. Order documented and tested: M&R → plugin hook → intercept. Grant: hooks.
  Tests: proxy/plugin_hook_test.go (real listener + helper plugin: header injected; timeout and crash → pass-through + counter; out-of-scope authority swap refused); sender hook test via /api/repeater/send; WS message hook test; run with -race.

Phase 8 — Payload generators/processors and scan checks (closes 0qwh, 9r77)
  Files: internal/extension/protocol.go (intruder.generate/intruder.process, scan.passive/scan.active, scan.insertionPoints, notification audit.issue); internal/intruder/payload.go, process.go (kind extension); internal/scanner/check_contract.go (ImplementationExtension), check_registry.go; internal/web adapters; docs/SCANNER-COVERAGE.md.
  Design: a generator is stateful per attack; an unloaded or crashed plugin fails the attack visibly, never yields zero payloads as success. Plugin checks become CheckDescriptors that run only inside an audit started through the existing riskAttack-gated routes; active checks probe via http.send (needs Phase 6's grant). Returned issues are validated against the severity/confidence enums and labelled with the extension; coverage docs do not count them as native coverage.
  Tests: intruder/extension_payload_test.go (attack payloads equal the plugin's; unload mid-attack ends the attack in a counted error state); scanner/extension_check_test.go (a passive plugin finding appears in /api/issues JSON with its implementation); audit.issue notification delivered.

Risks / open decisions:
- goja has no heap limit; vm.Interrupt bounds time only. Agent-authored 6c8f scripts with a 120s budget could exhaust memory. Mitigations: input/row/output caps, SetMaxCallStackSize. Open alternative: run 6c8f in a re-exec'd burpsy worker child with RLIMIT_AS via the extension host's process machinery. Decide in Phase 1 review.
- Phase 1 changes ydmj's header shape; existing run_script rules must keep working through the compatibility view.
- Plugin→host methods never cross an HTTP route, so the manifest and gate do not see them; the grant flag is the only control. Console auth (s19k) is still what stops a local caller minting its own confirmations.
- The M&R script budget sits on the proxy hot path; a per-message aggregate budget may be needed if many script rules stack.
- Hooks on all tools' traffic give a plugin every in-scope credential — intended under the hooks grant, and the Extensions UI must say so.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: wiwh is too large for one reviewable PR (12 children across a new code-execution risk class, the proxy hot path, the sender, Intruder, the scanner registry and persistence). One PR anyway, or split into (a) the script runtime — Phases 1-4: 80wl, 1944, 6c8f — and (b) the plugin protocol — Phases 5-8?

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- 6c8f (Phase 4) consumes 2jrr co88 (paged dataset results), wdza (task handle and completion push), 3zw0 (typed params schema) and e0yq (preview and digest covering the bulk cap); until those land 6c8f uses /api/scripts/results/ paging and plain route tools.
- Phase 5's scope.check and store.message reuse the matcher and windowing helper from 2jrr z5z3 and yahm — whichever lands first owns them.
- Phase 6 extracts internal/llm, which riw8 hiq7 and 2z3c also need — whichever epic merges first does the extraction.
- The riskScript class from Phase 1 must sit inside 2jrr 2jig's always-require floor; defining the floor by needsConfirmation membership makes the order irrelevant.
- 2jrr ulsy's script-bearing skills run through Phase 4's /api/scripts/run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase 1's decision (which runtime backs which surface, which risk class guards it, what is refused) is written into internal/jsexec/AGENTS.md, internal/extension/AGENTS.md and gaps.md before any script phase merges. The ROADMAP importBambda decline stays: these scripts are JavaScript over a burpsy binding, not Bambda/Java.
- No HTTP route that installs or runs script source is reachable without confirmation, tested through the real gated chain (mutating call without token → 428, mint → 200, replay → 428) for M&R script rules, Repeater actions and /api/scripts/*. A script originates traffic only through sender.AuthorisedSender; an out-of-scope send intent is refused and counted in the result, never silently dropped.
- Every new plugin→host method needs a per-plugin grant on the operator's command line (-plugin-grants); without it the method answers a distinct JSON-RPC error. Tested against a real child process via the plugin_helper_test.go re-exec. UnsupportedCapabilities and MethodSpecs agree with the dispatched set (Test_the_documented_method_set_is_the_dispatched_method_set and the kind↔method test stay green).
- Integration tests through the real entry point for each surface: a request through the real proxy listener rewritten by a script rule and by a plugin hook; an Intruder attack whose payloads come from a plugin; an audit started via the gated route reporting a plugin check's finding; an MCP tools/call of the script runner.
- Marshalled JSON (not Go structs) for every new wire shape — script rule lists, script results (log, rows), plugin view (grants, refused_capabilities, per-method call counts), hotkey selection params — with each nil-able list decided as null or [] and pinned (PolicyView.Registry: null is the precedent).
- A hook, script or plugin that times out, throws or crashes never blocks or half-applies a request: the original bytes go through, a counter increments, and the console or trace says why.
- A script rule or hook that changes nothing re-serialises the message byte-identically, including duplicate headers and header order (byte-exact test).
- Every new route has a manifest entry and risk class, appears in Test_the_confirmation_worthy_routes_are_the_ones_we_think_they_are when gated, is in the regenerated src/lib/gated-routes.ts and route-risk.ts, and is counted in the MCP tools/list tests.
- New sends are attributed in the tool log (toollog.ToolScript; toollog.ToolExtension with the plugin name), covered by the ToolAll enum walk test.
- Live drive against the combined rebuild: load a real example plugin with grants; see a hook rewrite browser traffic; run a Repeater action; drive the script runner from a real MCP stdio session (initialize → tools/call → 428 → burpsy_confirm → run).
- Gate green: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./... (gofmt -l empty), go build, go vet, go test ./..., go test -race ./internal/extension/... ./internal/jsexec/..., UI tsc + bun run check, ../e2e-go.sh, GitHub gate on the epic PR.
notes: Split approved by the user on 2026-10-07: this epic ships as 2 PRs, one per sub-epic — burpsy-react-ui-wiwh.1 = Script runtime: M&R script rules, Repeater actions, MCP script runner (PR 1 of 2); burpsy-react-ui-wiwh.2 = Plugin protocol: host services, requests, hooks, payloads, scan checks (PR 2 of 2). The QUESTION FOR THE USER in the design is answered by this split. Children now sit under the sub-epics; the plan's phases map to them as stated in each sub-epic's scope.

title: Scan launch, API scans and task control
description:
USER STORY
As a scan operator starting an API engagement, I want to launch a scan bounded to /myapp/ rather than the whole host, from the client's Postman collection or WSDL, after reviewing the endpoint list — dropping destructive endpoints, pinning parameter values, adding Basic or Bearer auth. Once it runs, I want to pause or reconfigure that one task without stopping the whole suite. Today the Postman export is refused, a scan of /myapp/ walks every app on the host, and my only lever on a noisy task is "Pause all" or cancel.

---

What an operator decides before and during a scan. Per-scan scope (501u) and Postman/WSDL loading (r39r) unblock the common API-engagement start; the API-details review step (vuw7) builds on r39r. Per-task pause/resume (g0ba) and per-task live-audit configuration (chct) give each running task its own controls. Isolated scans (13uw) and the HTTP/HTTPS seed option (in8j) round it out.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-501u, burpsy-react-ui-r39r, burpsy-react-ui-vuw7, burpsy-react-ui-g0ba, burpsy-react-ui-chct, burpsy-react-ui-13uw, burpsy-react-ui-in8j (7).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none — all 7 children are open.

Phase 1 — Per-scan scope and protocol expansion (closes 501u, in8j)
  Files: internal/web/api_crawl.go (crawlStartReq :219-352 gains scope and protocols; startCrawl :614; crawlConfig :1299; header :33-36); internal/crawler/crawler.go (Scope interface :209-212, a narrowing wrapper); internal/core/scope.go (reuse rule types for prefixes); internal/web/api_apiscan.go (same wrapper); ui lib/parse-seeds.ts, pages/scannerlaunch.tsx.
  Design: narrowScope{engagement, perScan} is used for Contains only (the frontier pre-filter); AuthoriseRaw stays the engagement scope, so a per-scan rule can never widen what goes on the wire. Default per-scan scope = each seed's final directory, matching Burp. protocols "both"|"specified" expands schemeless seeds server-side; the UI mirrors it for preview only.
  Tests: crawl_scope_per_scan_test.go through POST /api/crawl (/other/ skipped as out of scope; a per-scan rule naming an out-of-engagement host is still refused); parse-seeds.test.ts and a server seed-expansion test; JSON of the run record's scope.

Phase 2 — Postman and WSDL on the API-only path (closes r39r)
  Files: internal/apidoc/apidoc.go (detectFormat :275, Parse :178, new postman.go and wsdl.go); internal/crawler/apidoc.go (parseWSDL :277 shared with apidoc so crawl and API-only use one parser); internal/web/api_apiscan.go (prepareAPIScan :270); api_apiscan_test.go.
  Design: Postman v2.1 items and folders become operations; {{vars}} resolve from collection variables and anything unresolved is counted in the existing PlaceholderValues. WSDL: each operation gets a SOAP envelope from its message parts, placeholders counted, SOAPAction set. The crawler imports apidoc, not the reverse (apidoc stays a leaf).
  Tests: apidoc tests for Postman and WSDL fixtures; api_apiscan_test.go flips the :258 refusal and adds an end-to-end POST /api/apiscan with a Postman body that sends N requests to a test target; dry-run JSON has operations: [] when empty.

Phase 3 — API-details review step (closes vuw7; needs Phase 2)
  Files: internal/web/api_apiscan.go (apiScanReq :91-125 gains exclude, parameters, auth, definition_url, definition_auth); internal/apidoc (stable operation ids, parameter override hook); route_manifest.go; ui scannerlaunch.tsx (endpoints table with delete, parameters Fixed/Dynamic, auth table); lib/data.ts.
  Design: dry run and launch share prepareAPIScan, so the reviewed table equals what is sent. The URL fetch goes through an AuthorisedSender, never an http.Client. OAuth2 on "Add Auth" is DECLINED in this PR with a gaps.md entry; Basic, Bearer and raw header are implemented.
  Tests: api_apiscan_review_test.go (an excluded endpoint is not sent; a pinned value is on the wire; Bearer is on every request; an out-of-scope definition URL is refused); marshalled JSON of the operations and parameters tables.

Phase 4 — Per-task control (closes g0ba, chct)
  Files: internal/dash/tasks.go (Handle gains its own paused flag; per-task GateCheck beside the suite gate PauseAll :586, GateCheck :626); internal/web/api_tasks_cancel.go ({id}/pause|resume behind the POST-only guard :108-133); internal/crawler (WithSuiteGate takes a combined gate); api_crawl.go (crawl feed); api_apiscan.go; liveaudit.go (:1401 cfg := s.scanner.AuditConfig() replaced by a resolved named config via resolveAuditConfig, api_scanner_configs.go:351, and a pool via the registry); project_state.go; route_manifest.go; ui dashboard.tsx (row pause/resume; live task's Scan configuration and Resource pool tabs).
  Design: a task is paused if the suite OR the task is paused, and the row says which. The live-audit config is resolved once per change, not per tick; an unknown config or pool name is a 400. Changing the config mid-run resets the sweep's re-walk ledger (m9e0) and says so.
  Tests: tasks_pause_test.go additions (pausing one crawl stops its fetches while another continues, through the HTTP route and a real crawl; GET refused); liveaudit_config_test.go (a named config's narrowed check set is what the sweep dispatches; the pool rate is honoured); task-list JSON.

Phase 5 — Isolated scans (closes 13uw)
  Files: internal/web/api_crawl.go, api_apiscan.go, api_scanner_audit.go (isolated flag); internal/scanner/capture.go (TaskID :114-118 already stamped); a registry of isolated task ids in internal/web; site map and issues handlers; liveaudit.go sweep exclusion; ui scannerlaunch.tsx, dashboard.tsx (task-scoped results).
  Design: the existing per-exchange and per-finding TaskID is the seam; the site map tree, All issues and the live sweep exclude isolated task ids; the task detail shows its own exchanges and findings; consolidation and dedup never merge an isolated finding into a live one.
  Tests: isolated_scan_test.go through POST /api/crawl with isolated:true — /api/sitemap tree, issues list and live-sweep admission count unchanged; task results JSON holds the findings.

Risks / open decisions:
- Per-scan scope must never authorise: if narrowScope ever reaches AuthorisedSender it is an SSRF widening. A test pins that AuthoriseRaw is the engagement scope.
- Isolation by view filtering is cheap but leaky: every surface that lists exchanges or findings (search, organizer, report export, MCP) must also filter. List them in the PR and test each or record it as a known gap.
- WSDL envelope synthesis from XSD types can over-promise; placeholder counting must cover every invented element.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: none

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- vuw7 needs r39r (Phase 2 before Phase 3).
- chct needs saq3/o2p3's per-run AuditConfig override plumbing (Scanner Phase 4) before a live task's connect_timeout / follow_redirections can apply; until then those keys stay "not applied" on the live task too.
- The crawl+audit feed (api_crawl.go:1041-1046) has the same global-config gap as chct and should adopt the same per-task mechanism; saq3/ftk2's priority ordering lands in that feed.
- 501u's narrowed scope must be the one re16's soft-404 probe (s92h), subresource fetch (4ocj) and fragment routing (wbqx) use for their pre-filter.
- 13uw must also exclude isolated tasks from re16/t3zk's unrequested site-map nodes.
- vuw7's auth step overlaps re16/uzil's login credentials — share one credential model if uzil lands first.
acceptance_criteria:
- A crawl seeded with https://h/myapp/ stays inside /myapp/ by default; a "detailed scope" override accepts prefixes and rules. The per-scan scope is always the INTERSECTION with the engagement scope, never wider, and the sender chokepoint still authorises against the engagement scope. An integration test through POST /api/crawl asserts a sibling path is skipped as out of scope.
- A schemeless seed can be expanded to both http and https ("Scan using HTTP & HTTPS") or used as typed; server and ui/src/lib/parse-seeds.ts agree, with a test on each side.
- POST /api/apiscan accepts Postman Collection v2.1 and SOAP WSDL; the Postman refusal pinned at api_apiscan_test.go:258 is flipped; apidoc's header comment (:12-24) and refusal (:304) are updated.
- The dry run returns an endpoints table and a parameters table (Fixed or Dynamic per value); the launch accepts excluded endpoint ids, pinned values and auth methods (Basic, Bearer, Authorization header). "Upload from URL" fetches the definition through internal/sender (scope-checked), with optional Add Auth.
- Any crawl, audit or API-scan task can be paused and resumed on its own via POST /api/tasks/{id}/pause|resume, behind the same POST-only and same-origin guard as cancel; suite-wide pause still works.
- The live-audit task can be given a named scan configuration and a resource pool, applied in the sweep and persisted with the project.
- An isolated scan's exchanges and findings stay out of the site map, All issues and the live-audit sweep, and appear only in that task's results; a test asserts each surface.
- Every Go slice reaching the UI is asserted on the marshalled JSON: operations, parameters, auth, the excluded-endpoint list, the task list's per-task state.
- Live drive of the console against the combined rebuild at epic end: a /myapp/-scoped crawl; upload a Postman collection, prune endpoints, add Bearer, launch; pause and resume that task alone; give live audit a config and pool; run an isolated scan and confirm the site map and All issues are untouched.
- Gate green: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./..., go build, go vet, go test ./..., ../e2e-go.sh, UI tsc and bun run check, GitHub gate on the epic PR; every new route has a route_manifest risk class (route_manifest_test.go, ui_route_reachability_test.go).
