title: crawler: a JSON response's own url/href/next members are never read, so a documented API reachable from the crawled HTML contributes no locations
description:
## Claim
Burp reads non-HTML documents for locations — `Zb8w.API` and `Zb8w.DISCOVERED_CONTENT` (`Zb8w.java:18,20`), with a `parse_api_definitions` gate (`map_root.tsv:6175`). burpsy's `isHTML` gate admits four content types (`crawler.go:2098-2111`) and everything else is `SkipNotHTML` (`crawler.go:1332`), so a JSON payload listing its own endpoints yields nothing.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zb8w.java:18,20`, `map_root.tsv:6175`.
- burpsy: `crawler.go:2098-2111` (`isHTML`, four types), `crawler.go:1332` (`SkipNotHTML`).

## Fix direction
Add a bounded JSON/XML location extractor: walk the document for string values that parse as same-origin URLs or paths under a size cap, and enqueue them with a distinct action reason. Bound it hard (depth, count, document size) and record the count so the branch's yield is measurable; refuse rather than guess on ambiguous strings.

## Why it matters
Modern apps hand their API surface to the client as JSON. Burp enumerates it; burpsy stops at the HTML shell, which is why API-heavy targets come back thin.
close_reason:
Implemented and verified. New file internal/crawler/jsonloc.go (LooksLikeJSON, ParseJSONLocations, locationFromString) + a branch in the fetch path beside the sitemap sibling + SkipJSONUnparsed + two report counters (JSONDocumentsRead, JSONLocationsFound). Commit 9936196.

THE DESIGN DECISION, which is the substance of the bead: JSON has no link vocabulary — unlike HTML's href/src/action — so the document shape must be inferred from VALUES, and the honest rule is the tight one. A location is an absolute http/https URL, a slash-rooted path, or a relative reference ONLY under a key that names a link (next/href/self/endpoint/...). A bare word is NOT a path. `{"name": "users"}` is data, and reading it as /users is how a crawler invents URLs nobody observed. Template syntax (`/api/{id}`, `/api/${x}`) is refused for the same reason: it names a shape, and fetching it 404s on a URL the server never published. These three refusals are the feature, not its limits.

A SIBLING of the HTML gate, not a relaxation: the HTML gate exists for the link walk, form submit and base-href resolution, and admitting JSON through it would hand the markup extractor a document with no tags. A PDF still records SkipNotHTML unchanged, asserted by test.

Every location goes through the existing admit(), so destructiveness, scope, the crawl-scope query, depth, dedup and capacity apply without this feature re-implementing any of them. A JSON body naming /logout is refused as destructive, asserted by test.

Also ended a small dishonesty: a JSON response that names nothing used to record SkipNotHTML, which told an operator nothing true — the response WAS read and had no locations in it. It now counts as read with no skip; a body that claimed to be JSON and failed to parse gets SkipJSONUnparsed, whose remedy differs.

BOUNDS are hard and reported: 2 MiB document, depth 32, 20k strings, 500 locations, keys walked in sorted order so the caps truncate identically every run (a test asserts the same document yields the same order).

MUTATION-CHECKED, three ways, each caught by a test carrying its own claim message: removing the branch fails 5 tests (fetch, counter, the not-HTML honesty, the unparseable reason, the destructiveness gate); dropping the bare-word refusal fails 2 and prints the fabricated locations it invented; dropping the template refusal fails 1.

TWO TEST-SIDE CORRECTIONS I had to make, recorded because the first versions were wrong rather than the code: (1) I asserted `{"docs": "docs/index.html"}` yields a location, but "docs" is not a link key so it is data — the assertion over-claimed and was changed to use a link key; (2) I wrote a scope-refusal test, but this package's harness leaves Config.Scope nil so everything is in scope and SkipOutOfScope cannot fire — a fixture that cannot fail. Replaced with a test asserting the location reaches the normal admission path, and the destructiveness test (which the harness DOES exercise) carries the structural claim instead.

Gate: gofmt clean, go build ./... clean, go vet clean, internal/crawler green.

title: crawler: button/input[formaction], math[href] and object/embed are never read, so a JS-driven app whose only action is a styled button contributes no links
description:
## Claim
Burp's extraction surface includes `formaction` on buttons and inputs, `math[href]`, and `object[data]`/`embed` (`Zueq.java:124-142`, `Zpio.java:60-78`, `Zb5z.java:61-63` for `onclick`). burpsy's `discover.go:190-223` reads `a`, `area`, `iframe`, `frame` and `form` only.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zueq.java:124-142`, `Zpio.java:60-78`, `Zb5z.java:61-63`.
- burpsy: `discover.go:190-223` (five element kinds).

## Fix direction
Extend the extraction walk to the missing element/attribute pairs, each with a skip reason when refused (the destructive/scope gates must apply to the new shapes exactly as to anchors). Do NOT add `onclick` string parsing without a stated rule — Burp's handling of inline handlers is not fully recoverable here, and a guessed URL parser would invent locations.

## Why it matters
`<button formaction="/api/x">` and SVG/embedded content are common in modern apps; a crawler that only follows anchors reports such an app as a dead end.
close_reason:
Implemented and verified, commit b2e0b21. internal/crawler/discover.go reads three more shapes, and internal/crawler/extraction_test.go pins both the additions and the deliberate non-additions.

ADDED: button[formaction] and input[formaction] (read as navigation targets in their own right, because formaction OVERRIDES the enclosing form's action for that control — folding it into the form signature would make the form's identity disagree with where its button submits); math[href] (MathML's link element, which the HTML walk never visited); object[data] and embed[src] (embedded documents the crawl never fetched).

NOT ADDED, each documented in the source where the next pass will read it:
- Inline handlers (`onclick` etc). Burp's handling is not recoverable from this evidence base, and a guessed JavaScript URL parser invents locations — `onclick="doThing()"` is not a URL while `onclick="location='/x'"` is. Reading some and not others on an uncitable heuristic is exactly the fabrication the refusal-first design prevents. A handler-delivered link is what the rendered pass (nx7b) finds by executing the page.
- meta refresh: redirect handling here is explicit and understand_meta_refresh_tag is unimplemented, so following it would make the crawl's fetch list disagree with the redirect policy the rest of the tree enforces.
- classid/archive/codebase: plugin binaries and Java archives, not web locations.

VERIFICATION: mutation-checked. Removing the new cases fails exactly the four addition tests, each with its own claim message, while the two control tests (inline handler not scraped, meta refresh not followed) still PASS — which is the shape that proves the controls test the refusal rather than the absence of an implementation. gofmt clean, go build ./... clean, go vet clean, internal/crawler green.

SCOPE NOTE, stated because it bounds the fix: this closes the STATIC extraction surface. A link that only exists after script runs still needs the rendered pass, and the non-addition list above is where that boundary is recorded rather than left implicit.

title: crawler: max_locations, max_links_per_page, max_template_visits and max_capture_bytes have no wire field, so four CrawlStops are unreachable from a UI
description:
## Claim
`internal/crawler/limits.go` defines 11 bounds and 12 named stops, but only three bounds are settable over the wire (`api_crawl.go:187-226` has 13 request fields, 3 of them bounds; `api_crawl.go:401-410` applies them with `if > 0`). Four stops are therefore reachable only via a Go test or a default, not by an operator.

## Evidence
- burpsy: `api_crawl.go:187-226` (request fields), `api_crawl.go:401-410` (the three `if > 0` applications), `limits.go` (11 fields / 12 stops).
- Burp: `Zmst.java:27-30` ships three crawl limits in a config — Burp exposes its bounds as configuration, which is the parity point.

## Fix direction
Add the missing bounds to the wire request and the crawl launcher UI, with the same refuse-rather-than-clamp discipline the scanner keys use (a max of 0 must mean "no locations", not "unlimited" — the iueb precedent). Report every applied bound on the run record so a truncated crawl says which bound stopped it.

## Why it matters
The limits module's whole value is that a stopped crawl names its stop. With four bounds unreachable, the honest stopping vocabulary exists but the operator cannot use most of it — and a bound that fires with no control behind it is indistinguishable from a bug.
close_reason: The eight bounds the crawler had but the wire did not are now settable, and the 0-means-unlimited defect is fixed. TWO defects, and the second would have survived a naive fix: eight bounds had no wire field at all, AND every bound was applied with 'if n > 0' so a bound of 0 meant 'unset' and silently ran the DEFAULT. Zero is a real answer for all eleven (zero locations, zero links per page, zero re-logins) and reading it as unset means an operator who asked for a bounded-nothing crawl gets five hundred requests and a report naming a stop they never chose. The eight new fields are therefore POINTERS applied on presence, not on positivity - the iueb shape the audit path's OptUint32 already refuses to flatten. The three pre-existing fields keep their plain-int 0-means-default rule; that asymmetry is deliberate and documented, since converting them is a wire break for a field the UI has always sent. A NEGATIVE bound is refused with a 400 naming every bad bound in the request rather than clamped, because clamping to the default is the worst of the three available answers (the crawl runs, stops on the default, and reports a stop nobody chose) and a refused request leaves no task row. The run now publishes its effective bounds, and that took a fix of its own: crawler.Limits has no json tags, so publishing it directly emitted 'MaxLocations' and 'MaxDuration': 300000000000 while the rest of the endpoint was snake_case and seconds - found by reading a LIVE run, not by a test, with every value correct and the console reading all of them as undefined. Now published through crawlLimitsView, with a test asserting against the raw body because a decoder accepting 'MaxLocations' for 'max_locations' would hide exactly this. The console's DEFAULTS now come from the server (GET /api/crawl publishes default_limits from crawler.DefaultLimits) rather than a second hard-coded table, which had MaxRelogins as 10 against the engine's 5 and so showed an operator a bound they never set as one they had - a live run caught that too. UI: eight fields under 'Bounds the engine would otherwise choose', each with a 'default' placeholder, going through crawlBound which is lifted into src/lib precisely so 'bun test src/lib' can reach it. crawlBound omits a blank field entirely and sends a typed 0 as 0, which '|| undefined' cannot express. Mutation check: six mutations all caught (M1 bound not applied, M2 pointer-presence replaced by >0, M3 run publishes defaults, M4 negative clamped, M5 json tag dropped, M6 duration in nanoseconds). M3 is the one that changed the code - a defensive copy of limits looked obviously right and removing it changed nothing, so it is gone with the reason recorded, because an untestable defence is not a defence. VERIFIED LIVE: on the real console 'max_locations: 0' and 'max_links_per_page: 13' reached the wire while 'max_frontier' was absent entirely, and the run row read 'requests 200 - locations 0 - links/page 13' with nothing invented. Gate: gofmt/build/vet clean, web 37.951s ok, crawler 0.571s ok, tsc clean, 766 lib tests pass, e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: crawler: every crawl starts with an empty identity table and cannot be seeded from the site map, so a second crawl re-walks what the first already found
description:
## Claim
Burp pre-seeds a crawl's dedup from every prior location (`Zrbx.java:91-93`) and publishes each action's HTTP chain to the site map (`Zplt.java:59-61`). burpsy's crawl state is per-instance (`crawler.go:677-689` — `queued`/`locations`/`templates` fresh each run) and the only cross-run seed is `TakeLiveSeenURLs()` (`api_crawl.go:370-394`), which is the live-audit set rather than the site map.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zrbx.java:91-93`, `Zplt.java:59-61`, `Zb8w.SITEMAP`.
- burpsy: `crawler.go:677-689` (per-instance state), `api_crawl.go:370-394` (seeds ∪ live-seen only); the site map store exists and is not consulted for seeding.

## Fix direction
Seed a new crawl's location and template tables from the site map for the target's origins (the site map already records every observed URL and its action), and record how many locations were seeded so the saving is measurable rather than assumed. Keep it scoped to the same origins and honour scope rules on the way in.

## Why it matters
This is the "reuse what we already know" half of application-aware crawling: on a large target the second crawl currently repeats the first crawl's entire discovery cost, and the site map — burpsy's own record of that work — is not consulted.
notes: 2026-10-05: wired. POST /api/crawl gains seed_from_site_map (OPT-IN: a seeded request is not fetched so its links are not extracted — free crawl-to-crawl, but a page only browsed via proxy may hide unvisited links). FIXED A DEFECT in the landed engine half: SeedFromSiteMap seeded the crawl's own seed URLs, and seeds go through the same enqueue dedup, so a seeded crawl whose start page was in the site map (almost always) fetched NOTHING. Seeds/seed requests are now exempt (engine test TestSeedingNeverMarksTheCrawlsOwnSeedAsAlreadyQueued, failing before the fix). API test TestSeedFromSiteMapSkipsKnownRequestsButNeverTheSeed (both modes). Report.sitemap_seeded carries the count. UI checkbox queued to frontend agent.
close_reason: Done: seed_from_site_map (opt-in) wired into crawl start; engine defect fixed (the crawl's own seeds were pre-marked, so a seeded crawl fetched nothing); sitemap_seeded reported. Crawl dialog 'Reuse the site map'; live: seeded re-crawl fetched 1, reused 3. UI completed and driven live 2026-10-05 by the frontend-ux agent (tsc clean, bun test src/lib 802 pass, build ok, Go reachability tests ok). Full Go module build+vet+tests green. NOT committed.

title: crawler: a crawl's task row reads 0% until the instant it finishes, and there is no action-kind or phase vocabulary on the run record
description:
## Claim
Burp's crawl supervisor drives nine named phases over 23 action kinds (`Zc16.java:159-174`, `Zb8w.java:7-30`) and computes a real percentage (`Zbcc.java:75-77` `/8` and `:71-73` `(100+n*7)/8`). burpsy calls `task.Advance` once after `Run` returns (`api_crawl.go:489`) and its discovery tag is a free string (`discover.go:68`) with no phase type — so an operator watching a crawl sees 0% and then 100%.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zc16.java:159-174`, `Zb8w.java:7-30`, `Zbcc.java:75-77`, `:71-73`.
- burpsy: `api_crawl.go:489` (single Advance), `discover.go:68` (free-string tag), no phase type in `internal/crawler`.

## Fix direction
Add a small phase enum to the crawl report (seeds, robots/sitemap, frontier walk, rendered pass, audit feed — the five burpsy actually has) with per-phase visited counts, and advance the task row per batch instead of once at the end. Do not invent Burp's 23 action kinds; name the actions burpsy really takes and say how many of each.

## Why it matters
A long crawl is indistinguishable from a hung one, and the run record cannot answer "did it ever get to the rendered pass?" — which is the question an operator asks when coverage looks wrong.
notes:
PARTIAL in a775042. Criterion 2 met: CrawlPhase is a closed vocabulary of the twelve stages this crawler performs, PhaseOfTag maps every discovery tag to one, and Report.Phases counts them — so the 'did this crawl ever reach the rendered pass' question has an answer on the record. Counted BEFORE any gate can refuse, so the tally is of DISCOVERIES not egress; an unrecognised tag lands in a PhaseNone bucket that is counted rather than folded into a real phase, so the phases sum to what was discovered. Every phase present at zero. 8 tests, 2 mutations killed (legend not pre-filled; unknown tag folded into frontier-walk).

Twelve phases rather than Burp's twenty-three action kinds (Zb8w.java:7-30), deliberately: inventing 23 values burpsy never produces is a table of absences, and an operator reading '0 API actions' cannot tell 'this build does not do that' from 'the crawl did not need to'.

Not done, criterion 1: no per-batch task progress. The task row still advances once (api_crawl.go:489), which needs internal/web/api_crawl.go — a peer's working set — and batch boundaries inside Run. The bead says 'Do not invent Burp's 23 action kinds', which this change follows.
close_reason: Criterion 1 done 2026-10-05 (criterion 2 phases landed earlier in a775042): the crawl task row now advances per fetch during the crawl via the crawler's OnFetch hook (internal/web/crawl_progress.go), composed with the audit feed; settle() credits only the remainder so final Done == report Fetched. Test internal/web/crawl_progress_test.go TestACrawlsTaskRowAdvancesWhileTheCrawlIsStillRunning holds the origin mid-flight and asserts done>=2 while running (fails on the old once-after-Run advance); green under -race. NOT committed.

title: crawler: location identity is an exact hash with no tolerance band, so a page that changes one link is a new location
description:
## Claim
Burp's location identity is tolerant: `Zgjj.java:146-152` (7 per-feature unmatched tolerances) plus `:140-142` (3 fingerprinting thresholds) over its `Zmqs` strategy bundle. burpsy's is an exact 4-component hash (`discover.go:288-300`) with the false-split bias deliberately documented (`fingerprint.go:36-46`) — and no tolerance axis, so a page whose links rotate (a nonce, a timestamp, a session id) is a brand-new location on every visit and the crawl re-walks it.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zgjj.java:146-152`, `:140-142`, `map_root.tsv:7347-7351,7391-7393`.
- burpsy: `discover.go:288-300`, `fingerprint.go:36-46`.
- Related decline: `gaps.md` "Decline 4" declines the full `crawl_optimization.*` tolerance family — that decline covered the CONFIG family; this bead is the narrower in-code tolerance band that stops the duplicate explosion.

## Fix direction
Add one bounded tolerance to the location key: when a candidate's fingerprint differs from a known location by at most N of M components (start with links), treat it as the same location and record the near-duplicate rather than enqueueing. Report the near-duplicate count so the tolerance's effect is visible, and document the bias honestly rather than claiming exactness.

## Why it matters
On a dynamically-rendered target the exact hash produces a frontier of near-identical pages, which costs requests and buries the genuinely distinct locations. The current bias is documented, but it is still a coverage tax on exactly the apps Burp's tolerances were built for.
close_reason:
Implemented a bounded tolerance band on location identity, burpsy-react-ui-9x67.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A page differing only by a rotating link value folds into its known location
   instead of counting as new. TestARotatingLinkValueFoldsIntoTheKnownLocationAndIsReported
   (end to end: two renders of /view, one link's ?v= value moves, the report shows
   exactly 1 fold and 7 locations for 7 genuinely distinct pages).
   TestAFoldedPageIsADuplicateAndIsCountedAsAFold pins the same decision at the
   admission path.

2. A page differing STRUCTURALLY is still a new location, at any band width.
   TestAStructurallyDifferentPageIsNeverFolded,
   TestAShapeIndexKeepsDifferentlyShapedPagesInDifferentBuckets (the index is what
   refuses it — the comparison alone would have folded these), and
   TestABandOfAnyWidthNeverFoldsADifferentLinkPath (a differing link PATH is never
   tolerated, checked at bands 2, 10 and 1000).

3. The fold is visible on the report. Report.LocationFolds (json location_folds),
   always a subset of DuplicateLocations, named in Report.Summary() when non-zero,
   plus a new skip reason SkipLocationFolded wired through all four tables
   (const, SkipAll 38 -> 39, slot 38, String, Explanation) and CategoryDuplicate.
   Asserted in three tests.

The band's width is 2, from burp.Zmqs.NORMAL's shipped
totalUnmatchedActionDescriptorTolerance and unmatchedAnchorTolerance = 2
(deobf_merged/burp/Zmqs.java:243; keys at Zeuc.java:17-18, read at
Zgjj.java:145-147). Burp's MORE_COMPLETE and MOST_COMPLETE set both to 0, so it is
a per-strategy setting; 2 is the value that ships. Pinned by
TestTheBandWidthIsTheBeadsNumber.

The band covers query VALUES only. Path differences, link-count differences and
structural differences are all refused. A session id in the path is therefore NOT
folded — named as the price of not merging detail pages.

Mutation log (each killed by the test named):
  M1 band 2 -> 6: TestTheBandWidthIsTheBeadsNumber
  M2 key-set equality deleted: TestABandOfAnyWidthNeverFoldsADifferentLinkPath,
     TestTheBandFoldsAtItsEdgeAndNoFurther, plus 5 pre-existing crawler tests
  M3 shape index ignored (full map scan): TestAShapeIndexKeepsDifferentlyShapedPagesInDifferentBuckets,
     TestAStructurallyDifferentPageIsNeverFolded
  M4 LocationFolds++ deleted: TestAFoldedPageIsADuplicateAndIsCountedAsAFold,
     TestARotatingLinkValueFoldsIntoTheKnownLocationAndIsReported
  M5 empty-shape refusal deleted: TestAPageWithNoStructureIsNeverFolded

M1, M3 and M5 each exposed a test that passed for the wrong reason or a gap nothing
covered. Those tests were rewritten or added rather than the limitation being noted:
the empty-shape test now plants a location under the empty key (on an empty crawler
it could not fail), the edge test sizes its fixture to the band (a widened band used
to panic the suite), and the band width is pinned directly because no fixture moves
more than two values.

Verification: gofmt clean, go build ./internal/crawler/ clean, go vet clean,
go test ./internal/crawler/ -count=1 green. Commit 78b66a5, not pushed.

Not done, deliberately: the band is not applied to the non-HTML path
(rawBodyFingerprint responses carry no link set, so there is nothing to compare and
the band is not offered the chance to guess), and the tolerance family of Burp
crawl_optimization KEYS is still unrepresented — this bead is the narrower in-code
band, and the config projection was declined as gaps.md "Decline 4" covers.
gaps.md is another agent's file and was not touched; the two sentences above are
what that file would want to say about this change.

title: scanner: JWT weak-HMAC findings merge by target like every other row, not by the fingerprint Burp's merger compares
description:
## Claim
Burp's issue merger has a per-issue-type merge rule and JWT weak-HMAC uses a fingerprint comparison (`Zbvp.java:53-56`, `Zu` / `Zxi().ZZ()`). burpsy has exactly one keying rule for all findings (`core/findings.go:432-442`) and `jwt_weak.go:546-549` uses a third, different rule — so the same issue reported from two requests either over-merges or under-merges relative to Burp.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zbvp.java:53-56` (the merge gate), `:62-64` (a third exemption whose constant is ZKM-stripped — unrecoverable, and honestly so).
- burpsy: `core/findings.go:432-442` (one keying rule), `jwt_weak.go:546-549` (a different one), `dedup_policy.go:33-36` (documents the stripped constant).

## Fix direction
Give `core.Finding` an optional fingerprint field and let a check supply a merge key, with the default remaining today's target keying; express JWT weak-HMAC's rule in that field so it merges by fingerprint as Burp does. The stripped third exemption stays documented as unrecoverable rather than guessed.

## Why it matters
Duplicate findings on one hand and silently swallowed distinct findings on the other are both report-quality defects, and JWT-weak-HMAC across many requests is exactly the shape that triggers them.
close_reason: A JWT weak-HMAC finding now states its own dedup identity: core.NewFinding.MergeKey, set to the secret the check recovered. Burp's merger compares a fingerprint for exactly this row (Zbvp.java:53-56, Zu / Zxi().ZZ()); burpsy had one keying rule for every row, so one weak key proven on three endpoints became three High findings for one fact - the shape a long crawl produces. Three decisions, each a place the obvious version is wrong: the merge key REPLACES the target rather than adding to it (folding it in alongside origin+path leaves every duplicate in place); it is the secret and not the signing input (two tokens signed with different keys can carry byte-identical claims, so claims do not identify which key is weak); and it is still scoped by host (two hosts can each ship a JWT signed with 'secret', which is two findings - the weakness is only actionable on the application that issued the token). Empty is every other row's behaviour so path- and host-scoped keying are untouched, and a new keying input cannot bypass the rows that can never merge. THE PART THAT NEEDED A REFACTOR: the conversion from scanner Finding to core.NewFinding was inlined in Capture.ScanExchange, and the first version of this fix was completely inert while every test passed - the check set MergeKey, core's store honoured it, and nothing in between carried it. Deleting the single 'MergeKey: f.MergeKey' line (M1) passed both the check-level and the store-level tests, because each half is correct on its own and no test asked the two together. Fixed by naming the conversion coreNewFindingFor, so the seam is observable and the test calls the same function the store keys on rather than writing its own copy of the struct literal (which could not fail either). Mutation check: 3 mutations, all caught - M1 slipped at first and is the reason the commit includes the refactor, M2 (signing input instead of secret) and M3 (key folded into the target rather than replacing it) both caught immediately. Burp's third exemption clause, a fingerprint against a string constant at Zbvp.java:62 that the obfuscator stripped, stays documented as unrecoverable rather than guessed at. No wire field: TimesSeen is len(Occurrences), so a key seen on 40 pages already reports as one finding seen 40 times. Gate: gofmt/build/vet clean, core 0.102s ok, scanner 378.039s ok, web 42.126s ok, e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: scanner: a skipped insertion point is reported as "Skipped" with no kind, and XML/multipart parameter kinds do not exist
description:
## Claim
Burp's item status vocabulary names the insertion-point kind a status refers to (`Zq5.java:48-85`, a 16-row `Zd`/`Zs` table), so a row can say *which* kind was skipped and why. burpsy's status labels (`audit_items.go:245-271`) cannot name a kind, and `insertion.go:76-108`'s 17 kinds omit XML and multipart parameter bodies that Burp enumerates.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zq5.java:48-85` (16 status/kinds), `Zs` table.
- burpsy: `audit_items.go:245-271` (labels with no kind), `insertion.go:76-108` (17 `IpKind`s; XML and multipart bodies are handled as whole-body/JSON-adjacent points rather than their own parameter kinds).

## Fix direction
Split in two: (a) let a skipped-point status carry its `IpKind` (a small change in `AuditItemPointStatus` plus the reason text); (b) add the missing XML/multipart parameter kinds to the enumerator, with the multipart case mindful of bead cmyx's finding that a form codec emptied a raw-safe part.

## Why it matters
"Skipped" with no kind is unactionable: an operator cannot tell a skip they chose from a point the enumerator refused, and a multipart API's fields are currently invisible to insertion-point selection.
close_reason: Landed in a647c0d. Both halves: (a) a skipped point's row now names its kind — LabelFor composes status+kind on the row, which is the one place both are in hand, and ONLY the bare 'Skipped' is elaborated since the other statuses already name their own cause (tested); (b) IpXML and IpMultipartAttr exist, so XML values and multipart name/filename attributes stop reporting as body parameters. The multipart split is deliberate: attributes become the new kind, a part's CONTENT stays IpBody because it is the parameter's value and a body byte range like any other — both directions tested. Four existing tests pinned the old body: strings and moved with the behaviour. 6 mutations, all killed; the multipart one only died after the test was tightened from 'at least one attribute' to 'both'.

title: scanner: the audit queue has no URL-level disposition, so AUDITABLE and NETWORK_ERROR cannot appear on a row
description:
## Claim
Burp's queue carries per-URL dispositions — `Zeze.java:10-17` (the 10 values) applied at `Zwee.java:76-78,102-107` — so a URL that is auditable, that failed at the network, or that is not worth auditing are three distinguishable queue states. burpsy has nine `Disposition` values at `audit.go:260-284` and every one is *check-level*; the queue row itself carries no URL-level state.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zeze.java:10-17`, `Zwee.java:76-78,102-107`.
- burpsy: `audit.go:260-284` (9 check-level dispositions); `audit_items.go` item record has no URL disposition field. `LOW_VALUE` is separately declined on the record (`gaps.md:1270-1276`) because its prerequisite is crawler action metadata — that decline stays valid; what is missing is the *other* dispositions and the field itself.

## Fix direction
Add a URL-level disposition to the audit item (AUDITABLE when admitted; NETWORK_ERROR when the send failed below HTTP; keep LOW_VALUE out until the crawler half lands), set it in the dispatch loop, and show it on the queue row.

## Why it matters
A row that cannot say "never reachable" versus "audited and clean" makes an audit's outcome unreadable exactly when it matters — a run where a third of the queued URLs never answered looks identical to a clean one.
close_reason: AuditItem.URLDisposition set at Resolve: AUDITABLE (Ran>0), NETWORK_ERROR (SendFailures>0 && Ran==0), else empty; rendered on the queue row. LOW_VALUE kept out (crawler metadata). Table-tested; scanner suite green.

title: scanner: an audit records nothing about which phases ran, so a re-pass, a skip and a not-applicable are indistinguishable
description:
## Claim
Burp tracks audit *phase* state per item: `Zekf.java:85-98` packs a 4-bit state per phase and `Zbef.java:5-11,53-55` defines the 7 phase values with their applicability predicate. burpsy's `check_contract.go:28-33` is a 6-value *label* enum with no state at all, so an item's record cannot say "phase 2 ran twice", "phase 3 was not applicable", or "phase 4 never ran".

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zekf.java:85-98` (packed per-phase state), `Zbef.java:5-11,53-55` (the 7 phases + applicability).
- burpsy: `check_contract.go:28-33` (label only); `audit_items.go` item record has no per-phase field.

## Fix direction
Add a per-item per-phase state (not-run / running / done / not-applicable / repeated) recorded by the dispatch loop, and surface the counts on the audit item. This is the prerequisite for the follow-up-pass gap below (a follow-up pass has to know which phases are worth re-running) and for an honest per-phase progress reading.

## Why it matters
Two structural consequences today: every audit is single-pass by construction, and an operator reading an item cannot tell "nothing found" from "this phase never ran here".
notes: 2026-09-27 review of the uncommitted 0qhf diff: ByPhase does not partition the flat counters for bounded, failed, paused or undispatchable items. Filed as child 0qhf.1, which is blocked by krf5 (the follow-up-pass goto bug from 5efx, which inflates ItemFailed). Do not close 0qhf while 0qhf.1 is open. The audit_phase_test.go compile error (scan.WithStore, SessionRefused) the review also found was already fixed in the working tree by 10:44.
close_reason: Session sweep: cleared open P3/P4 parity beads per operator request. Gaps remain documented in gaps.md and can be re-filed when scheduled.

title: scanner: an audit has no manual insertion points, so a hand-marked request is re-guessed by the enumerator
description:
## Claim
Burp can audit operator-marked positions: `Zuq.java:178-197` builds a `MANUAL_INSERTION_POINT` (`Zbg8`) and `:68-71` short-circuits the whole heuristic enumeration when manual points exist — the marked request is audited exactly where the operator marked it. burpsy's `IpKind` list (`internal/bcheck/insertion.go:76-108`) has 17 members and no manual one, and Intruder's §-markers (bead mun, landed) are Intruder-only: nothing carries a marked span into an audit.

## Evidence
- Burp: `Zuq.java:178-197`, `:68-71`, `Zbg8.MANUAL_INSERTION_POINT`.
- burpsy: `insertion.go:76-108` (kind enum), no manual member; `internal/intruder/points.go` has the markers but the audit path never consults them.

## Fix direction
Add a manual insertion-point kind fed from the request's marked spans (the Intruder marker model already stores `{start,end}` per request), and make the enumerator prefer marked points over its heuristics for such a request — the same precedence Burp gives them. Test: an audit of a marked request probes the marked span and nothing else.

## Why it matters
Burp's audit-where-I-say is how an operator confirms a suspected injection point the enumerator does not model (a custom body format, a header the parser skips). Without it burpsy re-guesses and silently ignores the operator's intent.
notes: BACKEND LANDED (commit on ui-react-comparison): IpManual kind + locManualRaw raw-span Apply + EnumerateOptions.ManualSpans short-circuit (bcheck); AuditConfig.ManualSpans on the shared enumerateOptions() path; POST /api/audit/{id} accepts insertion_spans. Tested end-to-end at the audit layer (harness enumerates exactly the marked span; unmarked finds several). The acceptance BEHAVIOUR (audit probes the marked span and nothing else) is met and API-reachable. REMAINING: the editor gesture to mark a span and launch the audit — filed as its own ready bead. Keeping open until an operator can click it.
close_reason: Backend landed in 234072c (IpManual + locManualRaw + EnumerateOptions.ManualSpans + AuditConfig wiring + /api/audit insertion_spans); the operator-facing mark-a-span gesture landed in ec47393 (bead c6oq) and is live-verified to audit exactly the marked span. User story complete.

title: scanner: DOM clobbering has no row anywhere — not in the catalog, not in the checks, no declined-with-reason entry
description:
## Claim (QA round, Burp-re comparison, 2026-09-25)

Burp detects DOM clobbering, and burpsy has nothing at all: no catalog row, no check, no declined entry saying why not. The comparison was made against the whole evidence base:

- The catalog (internal/scanner/catalog_data.go) has no clobbering row — grep 'clobber' returns nothing across internal/scanner.
- The declined registry (check_registry_declined.go) has no entry, so the absence is not a stated decision the way other browser-only rows are.
- Burp's own placement, verified from the evidence base: DOM clobbering appears ONLY in the DOM Invader browser-extension docs (tools/dom-invader/dom-clobbering.html: "DOM Invader can automatically test for DOM clobbering vulnerabilities on your behalf") and the Web Security Academy manual-testing guide. It is NOT a scanner catalog issue in the binary (zero 'clobber' strings in map_root.tsv) and has no issue-descriptions page. So Burp's shape is: browser-extension detection, not an HTTP-pass scanner row.

## Why this is still a gap worth a row

burpsy's scanner DOES do browser-tier confirmation already (domexec, the DOM check families, the two-tier prototype pollution confirm). The DOM check family covers DOM XSS, web messages, storage, prototype pollution (checks_dom_extra.go, with the honest note that Burp defers gadget discovery to DOM Invader) — clobbering is the one DOM Invader attack type (dom-invader/settings/attack-types.html) with no burpsy counterpart, not even a declined-with-reason.

## Honest shape, decided by where Burp puts it

Because Burp detects it in the browser, the parity shape is NOT an HTTP-pass check (that would be a row Burp itself does not have). The two honest options: (a) a domexec-tier check in the DOM families alongside prototype pollution — inject HTML into rendered pages and observe a clobbered DOM property being read by script — or (b) a declined entry with the reason. What cannot stand is silence: the DOM check family's own docs enumerate Burp's attack types, and one is missing without a word.

## Evidence
tools/dom-invader/dom-clobbering.html; tools/dom-invader/settings/attack-types.html; the web-security guide's DOM clobbering topic; absence verified by grep across internal/scanner (catalog_data.go, check_registry_declined.go, checks_dom*.go).
close_reason: Closed as a stated disposition, not a detection. The QA finding's three options collapse once Burp's placement is measured: clobbering has no Burp catalog row (zero strings in the binary, no issue-descriptions page), so burpsy's 183-row catalog has nothing to decline, and inventing a row to decline it would misstate Burp's own scanner set. Option (a) - a domexec-tier detection - is structurally out of reach at this tier: the observable is a NAMED property read (window.someId resolving to an injected element), which is DOM identifier resolution the ES engine cannot model (named access is a DOM behaviour, and goja has no DOM) and is not among domexec's instrumented sources/sinks; that would take a property-read instrumentation layer, a domexec subsystem out of scope until a bead asks for it by name. So the fix is the third thing the bead said cannot stand: silence. SCANNER-COVERAGE.md gains 'Outside the catalog: DOM Invader's detections' naming clobbering, citing Burp's placement, spelling out the structural reason, and fencing the page's coverage numbers off from being read as covering it; checks_dom.go's header (the enumeration the bead called out) carries the same note at the family list. Registry invariants green (ValidateRegistry/TestDeclinedCatalog/EveryCatalogRow), gofmt/vet/build clean. Commit 6997d6b.

title: build: check:tokens is red on the branch head — 19 raw CSS literals from the editor/comparer work
description:
## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-25 in a detached worktree at ab97520 (no WIP, git status empty), burpsy-go/internal/web/ui:

    bun run check:tokens
    → Closed token set check failed: 19 raw literal(s) found outside the token files.

All 19 are in src/styles.css, in two clusters introduced by the recent editor/comparer work:

- 4469 (.enc-span[data-encoding], from 6fq): border-bottom: 2px solid var(--enc-tint)
- 4877-4961: .editor-tabs-settings-panel / -row, .editor-plugin-tab .notice, .comparer-item — gap/padding/font-size literals, some already inside a var() fallback (e.g. gap: var(--s1, 4px)) which the checker counts because the fallback is itself a raw literal

The sibling 2px at :4345 (from an earlier commit) was the ONE violation bead vtij closed, so this is the same class of failure recurring with 19 more. Not tracked: searched beads for token/check:tokens/closed token; vtij is closed and fixed a single earlier literal, and no open bead covers these lines.

## Why it matters

The token gate is one of the four gates bun run check runs. A permanently-red gate is the exact failure dp8p was filed for on the Go side: an agent working in this tree cannot tell a NEW formatting defect from the known ones, so it either ignores the gate or reformats an unrelated file mid-task.

## Fix

Replace each literal with its token, or add a trailing /* token-exempt: <reason> */ comment on the lines where the literal is deliberate (the var() fallbacks are deliberate: they are what lets a component render before the token sheet loads). Same shape as vtij.
close_reason: The UI gate is green: bun run check passes in full (tsc, gen-tokens --check, check:tokens, transit+fetch, test:lib 711/0) for the first time on this branch. The 19 literals break down as: 15 were FALLBACK literals in var() calls (var(--s1, 4px) etc.) — the token was referenced and the fallback was dead weight, since the tokens live in the generated layer verified into the same build; fix is dropping the fallbacks. --editor-font-size was the one fallback with a real job (the runtime font picker, 7bd) and now has a :root definition instead. The two 2px strokes take --border-focus, the same token debff3c chose for the tab marker, and the tracer's var(--line, var(--border)) also lost its --border fallback, a token defined nowhere in the set. Two 2px half-step values keep targeted token-exempt comments naming their specific reason (below the 4px --s1 step of the fluid scale; a token below the grid would exist only to silence the check) — the peer coordination's principle: real tokens everywhere, exemptions rare and individually argued, which is how these two differ from the blanket-exempt anti-pattern the fix was warned against. Bundle + minified style.css rebuilt and verified carrying the token references. Commit 7146d7d.

title: session: 'Request in browser' — re-issue a stored request in the original vs the current browser session, showing both
description:
## Claim

Burp's context menu offers "Request in browser — In original session / In current browser session": it re-issues the selected request in the operator's own browser, once with the exact Cookie header the stored request carried, once with whatever the session jar holds now. burpsy has no such action.

## Why it is its own bead now

Recorded from the a09g epic's comment (2026-09-11): js5y closed with only its response-viewer half, and this re-issue half was parked there so it was not lost with the closed issue. The epic itself is now closed complete (11/11), so the follow-up needs its own row rather than living in a dead umbrella's comments.

## What it needs

The session re-issue machinery the session epic owns: take a stored exchange's request, replay it with (a) the original Cookie header verbatim and (b) the coordinator's current jar, and show both outcomes side by side. The browser half (opening the operator's own browser rather than burpsy's sender) is the part with real design surface — a URL-into-browser handoff — and is worth scoping before implementing.

## Evidence

From a09g's close reason and its comment thread; the a09g epic closed 2026-09-25 with the note written 2026-09-11 by burpsy.
close_reason: Landed as the server half, honestly scoped against the Burp evidence (repeatRequestInBrowserDialog + renderUrlTxtField: a URL the operator copies and pastes). POST /api/repeater/browser-reissue mints TWO one-shot URLs for a stored exchange; GET /reissue/{token} spends one, re-sends under its variant, records the exchange with a variant-naming note so the comparison survives the dialog, and answers with a static script-free page. 'original' re-sends the stored bytes verbatim; 'current' substitutes the coordinator's jar via a header-splice that touches nothing else. Security: one-shot 16-byte random tokens, 5-minute expiry, swept on mint, spent-on-first-use (410 with the reason, never a silent re-send); BOTH scope gates (host-level at mint + AuthoriseRaw on the bytes); the answer page runs no script. Honest limits stated in code: a console with no recorded -web bind refuses to mint rather than render a broken URL; the mint is not yet wired to an SPA context menu and the reachability-test exemption says so in those words, the UI half being the follow-up. Three position-is-the-id traps caught by failing runs: *uint64 for the exchange field (absent != first), msg id 0 is a real request (the 'has no stored request' check deleted), and a fixture port hardcoded to 80. Six tests; three mutations checked (jar substitution dropped fails variant 2; spend-not-one-shot fails one-shot; both scope gates removed together fail the 403 - removing either alone leaves the other, which is the defense in depth working, and the test's comment documents why it cannot distinguish the word-identical refusals). Full internal/web green 41s; both new routes in the sorted manifest. Commit 466390d.

title: web: internal/web has real data races under -race across crawl and API scan
description:
## Claim

The `internal/web` package has genuine data races that `-race` reports, in the crawl and API-scan paths as well as live audit.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-22 at committed HEAD (`9ac6186`) in a detached worktree with empty `git status --porcelain`:

```
go test -race ./internal/web/
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c00063c2b8 by goroutine 43:
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIScanSendsTheRequestsTheDefinitionDescribes (0.47s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0004af4b8 by goroutine 74:
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIScanThatIsCappedSaysHowManyEndpointsWereNeverSent (0.29s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0004d9460 by goroutine 165:
--- FAIL: TestACrawlFetchesItsSeedAndTheLinksItFinds (0.38s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c000471ee0 by goroutine 177:
--- FAIL: TestACrawlSeedOutsideTheScopeIsRefusedNotFetched (0.19s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0003e6970 by goroutine 189:
```

Every failure is a data race, not an assertion failure. The affected tests span API scan, crawl, and (per an earlier report) live audit — so this is not one subsystem's bug.

## Scope note — what this is NOT

This is **not** the project gate. The gate is `go build && go vet && gofmt -l && go test ./...`, all of which pass at HEAD apart from the separately-filed `dp8p` (gofmt) and `lgxe` (stored-XSS row). `-race` is not run by CI.

That is exactly why it is worth a bead rather than a drive-by fix: the races are real, they are invisible to every gate the project runs, and each one is a latent nondeterminism in a concurrent capture/audit path. A production burpsy running under load has the same races; nothing in the repo would report them.

## What was falsified along the way

An earlier agent report claimed `TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried` was "flaky, worse on my branch". Measured directly at the committed state: `go test ./internal/web/ -run 'LiveAudit|Skipped|Stall|Retry' -count=3` returns **ok in 4.27s**. The flake claim does not reproduce; do not trust it. The `-race` failures above are the real finding.

## Fix direction

Run `go test -race ./internal/web/` and fix each race at its source. Do not add a `-race` exclusion list — that would make the project's own gate blind to the same class of bug it is already blind to. If a race is genuinely in a test helper rather than production code, say so explicitly in the fix and keep the production assertion.

## Do not

Do NOT close this as "-race is not the gate". That is the premise the bead rejects: a real race is a real defect whether or not CI happens to run the detector.
close_reason: crawlRuns.get/list handed out the live *crawlRun after releasing c.mu, so State/Report/Finished/Definition were read unsynchronised while finish()/setDefinition() wrote them under the lock. Reproduced at HEAD with 4 DATA RACE stacks under go test -race; fixed by returning a crawlRun snapshot copied under the lock (new crawlRun.snapshot, get returns a value, list returns []crawlRun, both launch handlers take the ok). Post-fix the same command is ok with 0 races.

title: gofmt: internal/web/liveaudit.go is not gofmt-clean at HEAD, so the burpsy-go gate can never be green
description:
## Claim

`gofmt -l .` inside `burpsy-go/` fails at HEAD with `internal/web/liveaudit.go`. This is committed state, not working-tree WIP.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-22 against HEAD 629740a, twice, in two independent trees:

1. Detached worktree `/tmp/verify-7suo` created with `git worktree add --detach /tmp/verify-7suo HEAD`. Its `git status --porcelain` was EMPTY. `gofmt -l .` printed `internal/web/liveaudit.go`.
2. Detached worktree `/tmp/verify-s9ma` at 9cd2424 — also clean porcelain — failed the same way on the same file.
3. Direct check against the committed blob: `git show HEAD:burpsy-go/internal/web/liveaudit.go | gofmt -l` prints `<standard input>`.
4. Control: `git show HEAD:burpsy-go/internal/vulnapp/vulnapp_stored.go | gofmt -l` prints nothing, so the check itself is sound.

## Why it matters

The AGENTS.md gate for the Go tree is `go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./...`, all clean. A permanently-red gofmt means the gate cannot distinguish a NEW formatting defect from this known one, so every agent working in `burpsy-go/` either ignores the gate or reformats an unrelated file mid-task. That is the failure mode this bead exists to end.

## Blast radius

Bounded: exactly one file, and `go vet`/`go build`/`go test` are all unaffected by it. No behavior change.

## Fix

`gofmt -w burpsy-go/internal/web/liveaudit.go`, then confirm `git diff` touches only whitespace/alignment and no tokens. Land it on its own, not bundled with a feature change, so the diff is readable as pure formatting.
close_reason: gofmt-only fix, landed alone per the bead. HEAD printed internal/web/liveaudit.go for gofmt -l (verified against the committed blob directly), so the AGENTS.md gate could never be green. The fix is 4 alignment lines, verified whitespace-only (git diff -w empty): two composite-literal field alignments and one tab in a var group. Measured in a detached worktree at HEAD with only this file changed: go build ./internal/web/ OK, go vet ./internal/web/ OK, gofmt -l . CLEAN across the whole tree. go test ./internal/web/ on the same tree failed only TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried 'pending retry slot is empty' — measured 5/12 runs at PRISTINE HEAD vs 1/12 on the formatted tree, i.e. a pre-existing test-harness race (the test reads a slot the next 5ms tick is entitled to clear; takePendingRetry clears it whether or not the response landed, iyqg's once-only contract), not a regression from whitespace. That flake is filed as burpsy-react-ui-a4ng. Working-tree note: the peer's iosv WIP in the same file was stashed, the fix cherry-picked, the WIP restored on top and verified intact and still gofmt-clean. Commit 905d1f5.

title: live-audit: no per-source traffic control — scope gate is engagement scope + query only
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G8): liveAuditAdmits (liveaudit.go:378-402) gates on engagement scope first (:378-379) then the DSL-03 query (:401); there is no per-source toggle. Burp offers a scope source choice ('Proxy' / 'Everything', Zhwl :1606-1607). Smallest honest shape: an enum on the sweep config (proxy-only | everything-in-scope) that decides whether an exchange is admitted, with the refused count per source surfaced. Small, directly evidenced; the gate already exists, this adds the source dimension.
close_reason: Burp's scope source choice (Zhwl :1606-1607) is live: LiveAuditTrafficSource proxy|everything on the sweep. Default PROXY — only core.SourceProxy captures, the fact the capture seam already records — because a sweep that audited the crawler's and its own requests by default would be the feedback loop the choice exists to prevent (pinned directly: SourceScanner captures are refused under the default, with the refusal counted). 'everything' admits any tool's in-scope captures so a crawl with the sweep on gets its discoveries audited as they land. Unknown wire value REFUSED at the door (a typo must not silently widen). The gate sits in liveAuditAdmits after scope, before the query — Burp's scope dialog's own order — and refusals are COUNTED: refused_source on the state/view + a 'N not this source' pane badge, because an in-scope exchange the gate skipped is a floor on coverage with its own reason, not a silent gap. The change made the test fixtures honest: completeExchange mints unattributed exchanges and core.Source's contract says unattributed is NOT proxy — so every fixture meaning 'the operator's own capture' now says so via a proxiedCompleteExchange helper (the attribution-histogram test, whose point IS the unattributed count, keeps the neutral helper). Tests: liveaudit_source_gate_test.go 4/4 — default refuses crawler captures with the view stating proxy and the refusal counted; everything admits them and round-trips; unknown value is a 400 that changes nothing; the sweep's own probe traffic refused under default. Mutations: gate inverted FAILs 2, typo-widens FAILs, silent refusal FAILs 2 — all killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web suite green 36.4s; tsc clean; bun test green; bundle rebuilt with traffic_source present; e2e-go.sh 24/24.
