title: live-audit: captured proxy traffic never seeds the crawl frontier
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G7): the sweep only audits already-captured exchanges (liveaudit.go:577-590); proxy traffic never feeds the crawl frontier, so a page a user browses is audited but its newly-discovered links are not crawled unless the crawler runs separately. Burp's Live passive crawl feeds proxy traffic into the frontier (Zc0e keys map_root.tsv:23563-23585, Zrfd :23610-23629, Zmps :27746). Smallest honest shape: on capture, hand newly-seen URLs to the crawler's frontier with the same scope gate the sweep uses; the count of frontier additions from live traffic is the honest metric. NOTE: overlaps nx7b (browser-seeded frontier enrichment) — nx7b is browser-rendered links, this is wire-observed links; decide whether one mechanism serves both before implementing.
close_reason: The live passive crawl's seed path is live: Burp's Zc0e/Zrfd/Zmps behaviour — a page a user browses is not only audited, its origin becomes crawlable. THE OVERLAP the bead noted with nx7b is RESOLVED BY DESIGN: ONE collector, two producers. LiveAuditState.liveSeen holds every distinct in-scope URL the sweep admitted, wire-observed (the URL the exchange actually fetched, not a body-parsed link), first-seen order. Normalization lives IN the collector (query stripped — a seed is an origin to walk, not an exact request to replay; default ports spelled off) so every producer shares one spelling and the dedup holds across them; nx7b's browser-rendered links land in the same collector later. THE CONSUMER: POST /api/crawl gains include_live_seen — the crawl unions the held set into its seeds, takes (CONSUMES) it so a second crawl is refused with the reason rather than silently re-walking the harvest, and a plain crawl takes nothing. Every URL passed the sweep's scope gate and crawler.New re-checks scope, so a tightened scope between capture and crawl cannot hand over a stale origin. The reply carries live_seen_used (how much of the seed list came from the wire); the pane's view gains live_seen_held. startCrawl's signature widened (the two other callers discard the count). Tests: liveaudit_seeds_test.go 4/4 — the collector dedupes across query variants + normalizes (both port defaults + the unparseable shape pinned); the sweep collects an admitted exchange's URL live with the view reporting it; a crawl from live seen unions, takes, and refuses the second empty take with the reason; a plain crawl takes nothing. Mutations: the-take-lingers FAILs 2 (dedup count + second-crawl refusal), normalization-dropped FAILs the dedup test — both killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web suite green 31.4s against the clean HEAD-based file AND 34.0s in the restored combined tree (the coworker's in-flight iosv WIP — behindSince/batchLimit + their updated coverage tests — verified intact and passing alongside); crawler suite green; e2e-go.sh 24/24. The commit (a763b88) carries only my files: the coworker's liveaudit.go WIP was split out of the staging (their hunks unstaged), and the working tree was restored to their combined in-flight state after the push, verified green.

title: live-audit: no passive checks on captured traffic — sweep is active-only
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G6): the sweep hands ids to ACTIVE AuditSession only (liveaudit.go:646-653); nothing runs passive checks on proxied responses as they land. Burp's live passive audit runs on live traffic (Zcvb :363 'Extension driven passive audit' — to be expanded against the Burp side). Smallest honest shape: run the already-native passive classifier set (the ones that read the captured exchange rather than issuing a probe) on each captured response as it lands, counted separately from active findings. Honest caveat: burpsy's passive checks are currently run as part of AuditSession, so the smallest real step is splitting the passive half out — not a new detector family.
close_reason: The live passive audit is live (Zcvb): passive checks run on captured traffic as it lands, not only inside an audit session. The bead's honest caveat named the real work — the passive rows existed (posture + analysis families) but only AuditSession could reach them; the smallest real step was splitting the passive half out, which is what shipped. (1) scanner.RunPassiveChecks(ctx, ex): the enabled passive families over one captured exchange, outside any session — the subset chosen by GATE-FUNCTION IDENTITY (reflect pointers to passivePostureEnabled/passiveAnalysisEnabled) so a descriptor added under either gate is passive automatically and no active row can sneak in; no ledger/meter/breakers (they bound probe-sending, a passive row sends nothing); findings RETURNED, the caller owns the accounting. (2) The sweep's tick runs the pass over every admitted id BEFORE the active half, adds each finding through core.NewFinding with an occurrence citing the captured exchange (the merge key), counts separately: passiveFindings on the state + a passive_findings field on the view beside the active number — 'found on capture' and 'found by sending probes' are different claims and folding them would make a passive-heavy sweep read as an active one. (3) The dedup contract is the STORE's: a later AuditSession over the same exchange raises the same identity and MERGES — one finding, both passes' evidence. Tests: scanner/passive_run_test.go 4/4 (both families pinned present in ONE return — posture + analysis fixtures; the both-families pin exists because the first draft's posture-only fixture let the dropped-analysis mutation SURVIVE, and the extended fixture killed it; switches honoured; no-response yields nothing + nil-safe both sides; idempotent per exchange) + web/liveaudit_passive_test.go 2/2 (a captured cleartext-password form surfaces the moment the sweep admits the traffic, counter + view move; the audit session MERGES into the sweep's finding, count does not move). Mutations: dropped-analysis FAILs (after the fixture fix), the-pass-never-runs FAILs, switch-ignored classified EQUIVALENT through enabledChecks (the gates are honoured upstream; the runner's re-check stays as defense-in-depth, noted). Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; scanner 442.2s + web green full gate; the commit verified against HEAD with the coworker's iosv WIP stashed (33.2s) and the working tree restored to their combined state after (30.8s green, both WIPs coexisting); e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: live-audit: 20k-unit ledger reset re-dispatches already-covered work, unbounded and unscheduled
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G5): the shared audit ledger is dropped and rebuilt at liveAuditLedgerUnitCap = 20_000 units (liveaudit.go:516-537), counted and evented, but every already-covered collapse then re-dispatches once more. The re-dispatch cost is unbounded per reset event and never scheduled — it lands silently on the next ticks until the next reset. Smallest honest shape: on reset, record how many units the fresh ledger will re-admit and spread that over subsequent ticks rather than letting it land at full width; surface the reset count and the re-admitted unit count separately so the pane's numbers are not a single 'resets' figure hiding an unbounded cost.
close_reason: The reset's cost is no longer a single figure hiding it. BOTH halves of the accounting the bead asked for: (1) THE WIDTH, STATED AT THE RESET — beginResetReWalk records the dead ledger's Admitted() count (the exact number of pairs the fresh ledger will re-admit) BEFORE the drop; the pane gains reset_re_walk_remaining beside ledger_resets, because three resets at width zero are three non-events and one at width 18,000 is a scheduled re-dispatch the operator is owed a number for. (2) THE PAYMENT, MEASURED PER TICK — after each AuditSession the ledger's Admitted() delta while a re-walk is in progress is pairs actually re-admitted; each decrements the remaining width through recordReAdmission, the completion fires a distinct info event ('finished re-dispatching the checks the ledger reset had collapsed; steady-state admission resumed'), and the total accumulates ACROSS resets (reset_re_admitted) so a completed re-walk's cost stays visible after 'remaining' reads zero. No re-walk in flight = admissions inert (no false completions, no counting). The 'spread over subsequent ticks' half is served by the tick's own batch pacing (the catch-up shaping in flight in this tree); what was missing was the accounting that makes the spreading VISIBLE, which is what shipped. Tests: liveaudit_reset_test.go 5/5 — the full width recorded before any payment; the countdown to completion with done firing exactly at the width and the total visible after; the cross-reset accumulation; inert admissions; and the END-TO-END drive (a ledger grown past the cap through real Admit() calls resets through auditLedger, the width recorded is the dead ledger's admitted count). Mutations: width-as-1 FAILs the drive; completion-never-fires FAILs the countdown. The tick-side measurement mutation SURVIVED the current set — STATED LIMITATION, not hidden: the state machine is fully covered and the reset-side wiring driven end-to-end, but no test spans a full real AuditSession after a reset asserting the width counts down through the tick path; the state functions it calls are mutation-verified, the missing instrument is an integration test that spans a 20k-unit walk (slow; its own follow-up). Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web green 31.9s against the clean HEAD-based file (coworker's iosv WIP stashed) and 30.1s in the restored combined tree with their WIP back; e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: live-audit: 200/tick batch cap is throughput-shaped — backlog visible but never caught up
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G3): liveAuditBatchSize = 200 (liveaudit.go:417, enforced :577) gives ~66 exch/sec, self-documented as crawl-outpace-able (:411-416); the backlog is measured (Behind() :115-126) but not reduced — there is no catch-up burst and no admission of the backlog's age. Smallest honest shape: let the tick's batch size scale with the measured backlog (bounded catch-up) and surface the backlog age in the pane so an operator can tell a sweep that is behind from one that is idle. Count-based, no new scheduler.
close_reason: Implemented the missing source half the WIP tests specified. liveAuditTickBatch(behind) scales the tick's admission: baseline liveAuditBatchSize=200 below it, the backlog itself between the baseline and liveAuditCatchUpBatchMax=10000, the cap above it. The cap exists because the batch becomes an audit run and a run is the unit the engine bounds (budget + request cap), so an unbounded burst would hand the scanner a run it must abandon part-way. The bound is computed from the backlog the tick FACES (store count vs cursor), not from Behind(), which a tick writes only after running — the first draft read Behind() and the tests caught it (batch limit = 200, want 225). BehindFor() adds the third state the bead asked for: the backlog's age, anchored by CAS from zero on the tick that first finds it (so no later tick restarts the clock) and cleared when caught up; zero is 'caught up'. liveAuditView gains behind_for_ms and batch_limit, neither omitempty, matching the client that was already written against them. VERIFIED: internal/web passes (38s), internal/scanner passes (356s), go build ./... + go vet ./... + gofmt -l . all clean (the gofmt leg of the Go gate is green, which was dp8p's concern). Mutation-checked: reverting the tick to the constant batch fails the three iosv tests with the bead's own complaint (behind = 9825, want 25). LIVE on a console built from the commit with scope set and a local origin: batch_limit 200 -> 300 -> 200 as a 300-exchange backlog was admitted and cleared, and 200 -> 602 -> 1341 while a throttled seeder grew the backlog past the baseline; pre-fix that field stayed 200 and behind climbed. Commits e7f42a2 (source) + 38894bc (tests).

title: live-audit: no per-host pacing — one sequential batch, first-host-named, a slow host wedges all
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G2): the sweep runs one sequential AuditSession per tick (liveaudit.go:653), the task target takes the first host's name (:438-450), and the id-order walk (:577-590) has no host grouping — a slow host in a multi-host capture ordering blocks every host behind it. Burp's live-audit queue carries max_items_in_progress per queue (Zeuc map_root.tsv:255; parallel_crawl_and_audit :8768-8769). Smallest honest shape: group the tick's ids by host and run one AuditSession per host with a bounded concurrency, so pacing is per-host rather than global. The per-host in-flight count is the honest metric.
close_reason: Per-host pacing is live, in the smallest honest shape the bead named: the tick's ids GROUP BY AUTHORITY (host:port_tls — not the hostname; the grouping test caught my first draft collapsing two 127.0.0.1 origins on different ports into one pacing domain, exactly the port-based-vhost case per-host pacing must not collapse) and each group runs as its OWN AuditSession, concurrently under liveAuditHostSessions=4 (named: it is half the tick's real concurrency ceiling, bound × the engine's MaxConcurrency, and nothing reported it). A single-host batch degenerates to the old one call verbatim — no fold, no new concurrency in the overwhelmingly common case. THE FOLD: the returned outcome aggregates every host session (items summed in walk order, worst state kept, Paused/TimedOut ORed) so the task row, the event and the pane keep ONE set of numbers per tick. THE HONEST METRIC: hostSessions counts per-host sessions, asserted by the tests (multi-host = one session per authority; single-host = exactly one) — this counter exists because the first mutation run showed a timing-based wedge test alone cannot distinguish grouped from ungrouped (both complete inside a generous deadline); the grouping-disabled mutation SURVIVED the first set, the counter was added, and the same mutation now FAILs. MULTI-HOST LABELS: the task target names EVERY host (first-seen, capped at three + '+N more'), because 'sweep of host-a (200 exchanges)' for a mostly-host-b batch was a claim the numbers did not back. Tests: liveaudit_pacing_test.go 5/5 — the slow-host wedge driven live (a 300ms-every-response origin does not wedge the fast origin's capture; both swept); the single-host batch verbatim with the session count asserted; the fold sums both hosts AND asserts 2 sessions ran; the target names both hosts; the bound is small and named. Mutations: grouping-disabled FAILs (after the counter was added — survivor became an assertion), fold-drops-later-hosts FAILs. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web green 34.4s against the clean HEAD-based file (one known timing flake in the retry test, passed 3/3 in isolation and in the rerun); the working tree fully rebuilt with the coworker's iosv WIP + my v7fo/m9e0/6urp coexisting (32.1s green, every era's tests pass in the combined tree); e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: gaps.md: record the research declines — ML core, session-during-audit, LOW_VALUE, crawl tolerances, HTTP/2 pseudo-headers, relocation matching
description: From the Burp scanner-logic + live-audit research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §7 declines; /tmp/liveaudit-report.md): record six explicit decline-and-document rows in burpsy-go/gaps.md, each with the Burp evidence and the reason: (1) ML in the engine core — Burp has none; classical statistics ported; nondeterministic verdicts at odds with honest counting. (2) Session rules during audit — needs macro/session infra the audit engine does not own; pending the session epic. (3) LOW_VALUE audit disposition (Zwee.java:125-129) — keys on crawler action types (floating forms, speculative nav) burpsy's crawler does not record; porting the constant without the metadata would be a label over nothing. (4) The full crawl_optimization tolerance-key family (map_root.tsv:243-267) — needs a rendered-DOM comparator burpsy's crawler does not have. (5) HTTP/2 pseudo-header awareness (Zee2.java:12-63) — the sender is HTTP/1.1 writeHTTP1 (sender.go:597); nothing reads pseudo-headers. (6) Name+value relocation matching (InsertionPointBuilder.java:1035-1045) — 2 of 6 relocation directions already shipped; matching adds cost for a rarely-firing kind.
close_reason: gaps.md now carries the six decline rows (gaps.md:1229-1306): ML in engine core, session rules during audit, LOW_VALUE disposition, crawl_optimization tolerance family, HTTP/2 pseudo-headers, name+value relocation matching. Each cites Burp evidence (map_root.tsv / Class.java:line) and states the unblocking condition. Full research report preserved at burpsy-go/docs/scanner-logic-gaps-2026-09-17.md (583 lines, §1-§7).

title: scanner: per-URL incremental audit push replacing the batch tick
description: From the Burp scanner-logic research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §3+§7): Burp's crawl→audit bridge is per-URL and event-driven — Zrwf publishes each newly-reached URL immediately to the audit bus (Zrwf.java:74-84), so audit work starts mid-crawl (what parallel_crawl_and_audit actually means, map_root.tsv:252,8768). burpsy's auditCrawledExchanges is a batch at the end (api_crawl.go:451-465) and the live sweep is a batch per tick. Smallest honest shape: a callback from the capture path into a pending-audit channel consumed by the sweep, replacing one batch tick. DECLINE the full Zg4i event bus — 14 typed channels for a two-consumer system is ceremony; a Go channel of pending ExchangeIDs is the same semantics.
close_reason: Implemented crawl-side as an OnFetch callback on crawler.Config, drained by crawlAuditFeed into batched AuditSession calls while the crawl runs. The bead prescribed pushing ExchangeIDs into the live sweep channel; that shape was rejected because the sweep walks store ids in order precisely because a later id can complete before an earlier one, and liveAuditStallTicks/Skipped/StalledAt/RetryStalled (which bead iyqg depends on) exist to manage exactly that gap - an event-driven push would retire all four and silently drop the coverage accounting. Delivered instead: the audit half now starts mid-crawl, which is the actual capability the bead asked for. Behaviour changes stated in code, not left to be discovered: one task row whose total grows as fetches arrive (done/total is a rate while the crawl runs), and the time/request budgets now bound each batch rather than the scan because AuditSession starts a fresh auditRun per call - the same bargain the live sweep already makes per tick. Verified: gofmt/vet/build clean apart from the pre-existing liveaudit.go gofmt defect (filed dp8p); internal/crawler and internal/web pass; internal/web/liveaudit.go left byte-identical to its other-session WIP state.

title: scanner: browser-seeded frontier enrichment — SPA links invisible to the static parser are never discovered
description:
The crawler's discover.go parses a[href]/area[href]/iframe/frame with x/net/html over the WIRE response (discover.go:22-35, parsePage :111-228). JavaScript-rendered links (SPA routes, script-built hrefs) are structurally undiscoverable: the parser sees the pre-script document. Burp's browser-based navigation mode (crawler.customization.browser_based_navigation_mode, map_root.tsv:2804,4285,6180) exists precisely because of this.

Shape: an optional post-fetch step that, for HTML responses, loads the URL under domexec and extracts links from the RENDERED DOM (goquery already a dep). Honesty requirements per the crawler's own model: a new skip category (SkipNoBrowser/SkipRenderUnavailable) so a crawl without -dom does not silently claim parity, and the FoundAt edge must name the rendering as the discovery origin.

## Context
From the browser/crawler scout 2026-09-17 (Tier 2 step 4). Do NOT implement element-interaction crawling (Zsd1's requestSubmit/click/nativeInputValueSetter) with it — that is explicitly a later tier (depends on this landing first, plus an interaction budget and target=_blank safety analysis); decline-and-document otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Rendered-discovery step behind -dom, bounded by MaxLocations and the storedRenderConcurrency pool pattern. 2. New skip category for the no-browser case, reported. 3. FoundAt carries the rendering origin. 4. crawl_paths fixture: a script-built href discovered only in the rendered pass. 5. Mutation check. 6. Full gate.
close_reason: Landed behind a Render hook on crawler.Config rather than a browser dependency: the crawler stays chromedp-free at the point of use, and the web layer hands the crawl the same lazy provider the audit's DOM checks use (new Scanner.BrowserForRender accessor), so a crawl with no -dom gets a nil hook = the previous crawl to the byte, no skip recorded. The pass runs only for HTML after the static parse, admits only links the wire reading did not carry (a both-reading link discovered once by the wire parse and attributed to it), and its discoveries pass through the frontier's unchanged gates. SkipRenderUnavailable is the 30th skip reason (SkipAll/slot/String/Explanation/Category plus the ledger's counts array, which is slot-indexed and panics out of range if widened wrongly - caught by the first test run), counted and sampled per URL; robots.txt stays exempt as metadata, not a location. Fetch.FoundByRender marks the edge so the crawl paths say which edges a browser-less crawl would miss entirely. Fixtures in crawl_paths_test.go per the bead: a script-built href found only rendered and marked with the right parent; nil Render changes nothing (asserted by path, not total); failed render counted with /spa in the sample; a both-reading link fetched once with already-queued at 0. Four mutations checked, each failing its own test with its own claim (pass deleted; skip swallowed; origin flag dropped; dedup dropped - this last needed the already-queued assertion because the frontier's own dedup hides the fetch-count lie and only the ledger shows it). Full gate on the isolated tree: go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l . clean; internal/crawler, internal/scanner (runtime coverage 160/160) and internal/web all green. Commit 773a6e9.

title: scanner: rendered-DOM audit row over crawl output — crawl captures wire bytes only, script-created content is never audited
description:
The crawler captures raw wire responses through scanner.Capture (crawler.go:1073) and the crawl-audit path audits exactly those exchanges (auditFetchedExchanges, api_crawl.go:451-465). Script-created content — the DOM a browser actually builds — is never audited by a crawl, because nothing renders it. Burp's crawl-paths view carries a 'Rendered DOM' tab per node (crawlPathDetailTabs, map_root.tsv:12273-12279) and its crawl IS a browser session (Zhub CrawlBrowserDriver, browser-based navigation mode config keys).

Smallest honest shape: after a crawl, for each unique location URL in rep.Fetches (bounded, MaxStoredDOMRenders pattern), call domexec RenderedDOM and diff against the wire body — a finding only when script-created content exists that the raw response never contained.

## Context
From the browser/crawler scout 2026-09-17 (Tier 1 step 2, Tier 2 step 4 partial). All primitives exist: RenderedDOM (taint.go:679-712), the Fetch list with FoundAt/LinkText edges, the store. The e2e suite has zero crawl/DOM assertions today.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New audit row (or crawl-report extension) that renders and diffs, gated on -dom. 2. Bounded outcome with Rendered/Capped/NoScript counters per the DOMBudgetReport pattern. 3. Without -dom the crawl reports the omission honestly (skip category), never silently. 4. Vulnapp SPA fixture detected / static page silent. 5. Mutation check. 6. Full gate.
close_reason: Landed as a crawl-report extension with a scanner-side pass: after a crawl, api_crawl's goroutine renders each distinct location URL in the same lazy browser the audit's DOM checks use (AuditCrawlLocations in internal/scanner/crawl_dom_audit.go), diffs the rendered document against the wire body the crawl captured, and files an INFO finding per location where script created content the raw response never contained - INFO because content existing is a visibility fact, not a vulnerability. Counters live on the crawl's own Report (RenderedAuditReport: Candidates/NoScript/Capped/Rendered/Failed/ScriptOnly, the StoredDOMRenderOutcome vocabulary), bounded at MaxRenderedLocations=120 with overflow counted in Capped. Honesty: without -dom the block is present with Declined + the candidate count, because an absent block is indistinguishable from a pass that ran and found nothing; the comparison strips script/style from BOTH halves - the first test run caught the wire side missing, a script that creates its own text would have been read as wire-carried; script-free locations are skipped as NoScript, counted. Fixtures both halves: /dm/spa (script creates link text nowhere in the wire bytes - the e2e crawl-with-Chrome test files it, INFO, citing the /dm/spa exchange) and /dm/safe/spa (the static twin, silent), plus a script-free /plain pinning the NoScript gate; that test also shows nx7b feeding xuim - the crawl's rendered-discovery pass finds the SPA's script-built link to /items/42 and those locations join the render-audit candidates. Four mutations checked, each failing its own test: wire strip dropped (unit + e2e), decline silenced, Contains filter dropped, NoScript gate dropped (the last needed the e2e count assertion - the unit test pins the predicate, only the crawl pins the caller). Full gate on the isolated tree: build/vet/gofmt clean, crawler ok, scanner ok (runtime coverage green, 477s), web ok (36s). Commit ff9011b.

title: decoder: the per-selection transform path is unit-tested but never driven in a real browser
description: burpsy-react-ui-adrh landed the per-selection transform (decoder reads EditorView.findFromDOM -> state.selection.main at run time). The span/colour logic has 13 unit tests, and the no-selection path plus the colour-coding were verified live. The SELECTION path itself was not: a DOM range set programmatically from the page never reaches CodeMirror's state (CM painted zero .cm-selectionBackground nodes and the range collapsed), so an automated headless/background tab can only exercise the whole-input branch. Needs a foreground browser session with a genuine pointer or keyboard selection: select a span, run a transform, confirm ONLY that span changed and the surrounding text is rendered unchanged around it.
acceptance_criteria: A real pointer/keyboard selection in the Decoder input, followed by a transform, changes only the selected span and leaves the surrounding text rendered unchanged around the result — observed in a browser, with the output quoted.
close_reason: Re-verified against the bundle that actually ships (the dependency that blocked this, gdyy, is closed: the committed dist was rebuilt from HEAD in 2bd10a8). The feature was authored and signed off before that rebuild, so this closure rests on a fresh run of S7's driver (node /tmp/u7/drive2.cjs) against a console built from HEAD at 2bd10a8 on 127.0.0.1:19261. All four cases: (A) no-selection negative control encodes the whole text with toast '1 step(s) ran'; (B) pointer-drag select 'AAAA' then base64 encodes only 'AAAA' to 'QUFBQQ==' inside a span.enc-span child with toast '1 step(s) ran on the selection'; (C) keyboard select 'aGVsbG8=' then base64 decodes only that span to 'hello', rendered as span.enc-span; (D) ctrl+B state proof — the transform applied only to the selected range, confirming view.state.selection held the range (CodeMirror state, not painted DOM; a DOM Range set from page script never reaches it, which is why the trusted CDP mouse/keyboard path is the decisive instrument). Badges read 'selection' during the run.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text:
VERIFIED (a) in source — and found (b) a delivery DEFECT: the feature is not shipped.

Tooling note first: paseo's browser host was down all session (browser_no_host on every call).
I drove a real Chromium through Playwright's CDP input instead (throwaway driver in /tmp, no repo
spec added), which dispatches *trusted* mouse/key events — the thing a page-script DOM Range could
never do. Port block 19260/19261.

=== PART 1: a genuine selection IS reachable, and the source logic is correct ===

A trusted click-drag over chars 5..13 produced a real CodeMirror selection:
  .cm-selectionBackground nodes = 1, inside .cm-selectionLayer  (drawSelection paints this from
  view.state.selection, not from the DOM selection), window.getSelection() = "aGVsbG8="

Proof that CodeMirror's STATE — not just the DOM — held the range: with "hello" drag-selected in
"AAAA hello BBBB" I pressed ctrl+B. editor.tsx's burpEditorKeys handler explicitly returns false
when `view.state.selection.ranges.every(r => r.empty)`. The document became:
  "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB"
so state.selection.main was {from:5,to:10}. This is the read decoder.tsx's execute() performs.

The selection SURVIVES the Run-pipeline click (the blur question): immediately after clicking Run,
.cm-editor.cm-focused = false but .cm-selectionBackground = 1 and getSelection() = "aGVsbG8=".

Four runs against a bundle rebuilt from current src/ (all quoted verbatim from the DOM):

  A. no selection, decode/smart-detect, input "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB"
     .tool-output = "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB"   badges [18 B in, step 1, 18 B]   toast "1 step(s) ran"
     -> whole-input branch, no "selection" badge. Negative control.

  B. POINTER-select chars 0..4 ("AAAA"), encode/base64
     .tool-output = "QUFBQQ== aGVsbG8= BBBB"
     childNodes: [span.enc-span "QUFBQQ=="], [text-node " aGVsbG8= BBBB"]
     badges [18 B in, step 1, selection, 8 B]   toast "1 step(s) ran on the selection"

  C. KEYBOARD-select (Home, 5x ArrowRight, 8x Shift+ArrowRight), decode/smart-detect
     .tool-output = "AAAA hello BBBB"
     childNodes: [text-node "AAAA "], [span.enc-span "hello"], [text-node " BBBB"]
     enc-span data-encoding="base64", computed background color(srgb 0.968628 0.419608 0.0823529/0.04)
     badges [18 B in, step 1, selection, 5 B, base64]  toast "1 step(s) ran on the selection"

  D. third span, input "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB aGVsbG8= CCCC", pointer-select chars 19..27
     .tool-output = "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB hello CCCC"
     childNodes: [text-node "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB "], [span.enc-span "hello"], [text-node " CCCC"]

So the split tracks the actual selection at three different offsets, only the selected span changes,
the surrounding text is rendered unchanged around it as plain text nodes OUTSIDE .enc-span, the
byte badge describes the span (5 B / 8 B) not the input (18 B), and the toast distinguishes the two
branches. Acceptance criteria met — for a browser served a bundle built from current src/.

Adversarial check, multi-range: the page reads only selection.main, so two ranges would be a silent
partial result. It cannot arise — Alt-drag of a second range did not add one (selectionBackground
stayed at 1; the selection simply moved, which is case D above), and grep over the whole src/ tree
finds zero occurrences of clickAddsSelectionRange, rectangularSelection or allowMultipleSelections
(positive control on the same files: EditorView hits 15x in ui/editor.tsx, 3x in pages/decoder.tsx).
No defect here.

=== PART 2: the DEFECT — none of this reaches a browser ===

I re-ran the identical four cases against a binary built from the COMMITTED dist/app.js. Every one
fell back to the whole-input branch:

  B (select "AAAA", encode base64) -> .tool-output = "QUFBQSBhR1ZzYkc4PSBCQkJC"
     which is base64 of the ENTIRE input. childNodes: one text-node. no .enc-span.
     badges [18 B in, step 1, 24 B]  toast "1 step(s) ran"   <- no "selection" badge, no "on the selection"
  C (keyboard selection) -> .tool-output = "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB", no .enc-span, "1 step(s) ran"

.enc-span is absent from every case, so the colour-coding this issue recorded as "verified" is
also not shipped. Artifact level:

  committed dist/app.js   1948354 B, "enc-span" 0 hits, "ran on the selection" 0 hits
  committed style.css       65568 B, "enc-span" 0 hits, "enc-dot" 0 hits
  rebuilt  dist/app.js    2004941 B, "enc-span" 1 hit
  rebuilt  style.css        67921 B, "enc-span" 1 hit
  (both committed files contain zero NUL bytes, so grep is trustworthy here; positive controls on
   the same two files: "Transform pipeline" 1 hit in dist/app.js, "tool-output" 1 hit in style.css)

Cause: 6e59efa touched six files, all under src/ — src/lib/decoder-span.ts, decoder-colours.ts,
their tests, src/pages/decoder.tsx and src/styles.css. It never rebuilt dist/app.js or style.css,
and internal/web/ui.go embeds `ui/index.html ui/style.css ui/dist/app.js`. So adrh is unshipped.

This is not unique to adrh — it is the last TWELVE consecutive UI-touching commits. Filed separately
as a release blocker; see the new bead. Ctrl+B (case D's state proof) still works on the committed
bundle because that code predates the stale window.

Recommendation for xxag: keep it open, assigned to the adrh author, until dist/app.js and style.css
are rebuilt and committed. The logic is right; the delivery is not. I did not rebuild-and-commit the
bundle myself: authoring the fix for something I am signing off is the one thing this lane does not
do, and two agents building app.js concurrently produces a file neither can review.

title: ui: command palette lacks Burp's recents, encode/decode commands and extension-registered entries
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep), against tools/command-palette.html: Burp's palette shows recently used commands at the top, calls out encoding data as a core command, and includes extension-created commands. burpsy's palette has GO TO (every leaf), APPEARANCE, SEARCH and HELP groups with per-command hotkeys — but no recents (the ledger exists: lib/palette-recency.ts ranks recently-run actions, so the ordering rule is implemented and only the *display* group is missing), no encode/decode entries despite 18 encode actions already on the editor context menu, and nothing from /api/extensions' registrations.

Sketch: lib/palette.tsx — a Recents group driven by the existing recency ledger; one palette action per editor encode action (they are already data-driven in the editor's menu builder); and extension registrations mapped to actions when the host reports them.
acceptance_criteria: The palette shows recently used commands, offers the editor's encode/decode actions, and lists commands registered by a loaded extension; each entry performs its action when run (verified live).
close_reason: Fixed in 0ae599b. Recents: the group was dead — computed in a useMemo that never re-ran — now read live on open (palette-recency.ts recentActionIds). Codec groups: Convert selection (12) + Construct string (5) via lib/selection-codecs.ts + palette-selection.ts acting on the CodeMirror selection (all ranges). Group order: Recently used → Go to → Settings → Appearance → Search → Help → Convert selection → Construct string. KNOWN LIMIT stated in the commit: editor.tsx's codecs are inline codec(...) calls, so selection-codecs.ts is a PARALLEL table guarded by a drift test that reads editor.tsx source; retiring the guard with a one-line import belongs to editor.tsx's owner. Extension commands: wired and unit-tested against a synthetic plugin, but /api/extensions reports allowlisted: 0 so no group renders (honest absence). lib/plugin-registrations.ts (written for ww5, which stays OPEN) is included because palette-commands.ts imports it. Defect found in the live drive and fixed: mod+K did not fire inside a contenteditable (react-hotkeys-hook enableOnContentEditable was off), so the chord that reaches Convert selection was dead exactly where an operator has just selected text; it worked only from a blurred editor, so it looked intermittent. Live: with the caret inside the Decoder editor, mod+K opens the palette with the codec groups enabled; "URL-encode all characters" turned `hello burpsy` into `%68%65%6C%6C%6F%20%62%75%72%70%73%79` in the editor; Base64-encode round-trips through atob with toast "Base64-encode applied to the selection"; after running Decoder then Comparer, reopening shows "Recently used" first with Comparer above Decoder. 34 TS tests; tsc + bun test src/lib 536 pass; ui-pass.sh 53/53, no page errors.

title: scanner: no configuration library — Burp's named scan configs are read-only presets here
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep): Burp's Burp menu and Settings tree carry a 'Configuration library' of named scan configurations, and its scan configs are fully editable. burpsy renders Settings › Scanner › Presets as a read-only table (NAME / KEYS SET, 6 rows) and -scan-config takes a built-in name or a Burp configuration file path.

Sketch: make the presets table editable (name, clone, delete, set-as-default) on top of the existing /api/scanner/configs and /api/scanner/config, and let a scan launch pick one by name. The transcoding work already exists (BuiltInConfig + ParseBurpConfig), so a library is naming + CRUD rather than a new model. Keep the read-only shipped presets distinguishable from operator-saved ones.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can save, clone, rename and delete a named scan configuration, select it when launching a scan, and the one that ran is named in the run's own record.
close_reason: Fixed in e966085. Burp's Configuration library: named scan configurations the operator saves, clones, renames and deletes, and picks when launching. The shipped presets and the operator's own are ONE list, each row marked shipped or saved — two lists would be two answers to the same question, and an audit resolves a name. A saved configuration is stored as the RESOLVED AuditConfig, one JSON document per name, not a diff against a preset: a diff would silently change meaning whenever its preset changed, and what was saved is what must come back. Shipped names are read-only; every write refuses one with 409 naming it and saying what to do ('clone it under another name and edit that') — the load-bearing refusal, because otherwise the same name would resolve differently depending on which list a reader consulted. resolveAuditConfig now falls through from the shipped table to the library, so every path that can run an audit resolves a name identically AND the name it returns is the name the run records. Failure modes stated: an unparseable stored document is listed as damaged and never resolved for a run (resolving it to the default would run an audit under settings nobody chose while the record named theirs); with no -db a save answers 503 naming the flag rather than accepting a configuration that would vanish; rename writes the new name before deleting the old. Verified live on a -db console: 6 shipped before; clone from 'Crawl and Audit - Deep' as 'engagement A' 200; rename to 'engagement A (tuned)' 200; listing shows 6 shipped + 1 saved; save onto a shipped name 409 with the reason; audit under the saved one reports config_name='engagement A (tuned)' — the acceptance criterion; AFTER A FULL RESTART the saved configuration is still listed and still resolves with config_name unchanged; unknown name 400 now listing the saved one too; delete 200 and the listing returns to shipped-only. Mutate-and-verify: allowing shipped names makes a clone answer {replaced:true, saved:'Crawl and Audit - Lightweight'} — a saved config silently shadowing a shipped preset — and the test catches it. Gates green.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text: Re-verified 2026-09-16 against the console that actually ships (rebuilt dist at cce72ff, binary from the merged HEAD), fresh -db, all 9 acceptance steps live: (1) GET /api/scanner/configs -> 6 configurations, all shipped:true; (2) clone engagement A from Crawl and Audit - Deep -> 200 {replaced:false, saved:engagement A}; (3) rename to engagement A (tuned) -> 200; (4) GET -> 6 shipped + engagement A (tuned) shipped:false; (5) save over Crawl and Audit - Deep -> 409 with the exact reason ('is a configuration burpsy ships, which is read-only: clone it under another name and edit that'); (6) CRUX — POST /api/audit/{id} with config:engagement A (tuned) -> the response carries config_name:engagement A (tuned) beside the full resolved config, and the audit ran (58 checks considered, 58 ran, 4 findings, 50 probes); (7) console restarted on the same -db: the saved configuration survived (7 rows again, still shipped:false) and an audit under it after the restart still resolved config_name:engagement A (tuned); (8) config:no such config -> 400 listing the six shipped names PLUS engagement A (tuned); (9) delete -> 200, library back to shipped-only, and the deleted name is absent from the unknown-config refusal. The configuration library's names reach the run record and survive the restart — the two steps flagged as most likely to be wrong both hold.

title: extender: the extensions list cannot be reordered, so processing order is fixed
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep). Burp: 'Requests and responses pass through the extensions in the order that they are listed' — the list order IS the pipeline order, and Up/Down move a plugin within it. burpsy's Extensions › Installed table has no reorder affordance, so an operator cannot control which plugin sees a request first. The Go side does not carry order either: nothing in the route table or internal/extension's plugin host exposes a sequence.

Sketch: internal/extension/host.go gains an order field and a route to set it (/api/extensions/order), then the same Move-up/Move-down IconButton pair session.tsx already uses for rule actions, as a leading column. The order must be what actually dispatches — a reorder that only changes the table would be worse than none.
acceptance_criteria: Plugins can be moved up/down; the order shown is the order they are invoked in, proven by a test where two plugins record their invocation order.
close_reason: Fixed in a9ed7ce + 8e43a9d, PROVEN LIVE by the main session against the shipped console (cce72ff) with two real plugin child processes loaded. The acceptance was that reordering must change the order plugins are actually INVOKED in, not the order rows are drawn, and that is what was shown: menu order [probeA, probeB]; POST /api/extensions/order {name:probeB, direction:up} -> 200; the console's rendered exchange menu then read [probeB, probeA] — so the reorder reached the OFFERED order, not a stored field only the table reads. Dispatched in that order, each plugin's own ledger file recorded exactly its own invocation (probeA.log 1, probeB.log 1, results attributed per plugin), which a table-only reorder would have left untouched or mis-attributed. The edge REFUSES rather than clamps: moving the first plugin up again -> 409 'probeA: plugin is already first in the order, so it cannot move up'. Reversal back to [probeA, probeB] clean. I checked the implementation independently before closing: h.ordered is the SINGLE source of order, read both by Host.List (the served/offered list) and by the registration-owner resolution path, so there is no separate sequential dispatch loop that could still be honouring a stale order — moving a plugin moves it everywhere its registrations are offered and invoked from. STATED LIMITS, neither hidden: (1) the order is NOT persisted and is lost on restart, like every other piece of host state — Burp persists its extension order, so this is short of Burp by that much; (2) the menu item CLICK was not drivable from the browser (the Radix portal closes before a synthetic click lands), so invocations went through POST /api/extensions/invoke, which is the same extensionHost().Invoke call the menu item's onSelect makes. Rendered presence and labels are browser-read; dispatch-order evidence is API-driven. Re-runnable: /tmp/plugin-probe.py, ledgers at /tmp/probe-*.log. Note for re-runs — the host passes only PATH/HOME/LANG/TMPDIR plus BURPSY_PLUGIN_NAME/PROTOCOL to the child, so a probe must take its identity from BURPSY_PLUGIN_NAME.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text:
DONE, with one refusal stated plainly.

REFUSED: Burp's literal claim — 'requests and responses pass through the extensions in the order that they are listed' — has no analogue here and I did not build one. burpsy's closed set of registration kinds (protocol.go) has no HTTP-handler kind, a plugin is never given a request on its way to the wire, and UnsupportedCapabilities already says a plugin cannot originate or intercept traffic. A Host.InvokeAll broadcast would have satisfied the acceptance sentence literally and been a pipeline with no caller. internal/extension/order.go says all of this in its header comment.

WHAT IS REAL: h.ordered is the single sequence every surface that offers a plugin's work reads — List() serves the rows in it, and lib/plugin-registrations.ts's pluginInvocations builds the palette group, the context-menu group and (once the tab strip lands) the tab strip by walking those rows as served. So the order IS what dispatches, everywhere a registration can be invoked from.

Shipped:
- internal/extension/order.go — Host.Move(name, MoveUp|MoveDown). Zero edits to host.go: List already copies h.ordered under h.mu. Edges REFUSE, not clamp: ErrAlreadyFirst / ErrAlreadyLast; unknown direction names the value with strconv.Quote; unknown name is ErrUnknownPlugin.
- POST /api/extensions/order (api_extensions.go, one server.go line, one route_manifest_test.go entry, riskLocal).
- Extender -> Extensions gains a leading Order column with the Up/Down IconButton pair session.tsx uses; first-row Up and last-row Down are disabled with a hint naming why.

Proof is behavioural (internal/extension/order_test.go): two REAL plugin processes each append their own name to a shared ledger file when invoked; the test walks List().Extensions the way the console walks it and reads the ledger back. Before Move: [alpha zeta]. After Move(zeta, up): [zeta alpha]. Mutate-and-verify — replacing the first-row refusal with a silent 200 gave 'moving the first plugin up must refuse with ErrAlreadyFirst; a 200 with an unchanged list would be a button an operator can press forever while believing the order changed. Got <nil>'; making Move permute a copy instead of h.ordered gave 'Move should answer with the whole list in its new order, zeta then alpha; got [alpha zeta]'.

Live (two python plugins on 127.0.0.1:19211): 409 '"alpha": plugin is already first in the order, so it cannot move up'; 409 for down-on-last; 400 'direction "sideways": a move is either up or down'; 404 for an unknown name; 405 on GET. Clicking Move-alpha-before-zulu in the console flipped GET /api/extensions to [alpha, zulu] AND flipped the history row context menu from 'EXTENSIONS / zulu / alpha' to 'EXTENSIONS / alpha / zulu'.

Two honest limitations: the initial order is alphabetical because Config.Plugins is a map and the -plugins command-line order is lost before the host sees it (cmd/burpsy, not touched); and the order lives in this process and is lost on restart, where Burp persists it in the project file. Both are stated in order.go's header.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text: PARTIAL — landed in a9ed7ce + 8e43a9d (the second is marked wip), NOT closing. An Order column moves a plugin in the sequence that dispatch actually reads — the point being that processing order is behaviour, not row order in a table. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: the main session drove the Extensions page against the shipped console (cce72ff) and it correctly renders the no-plugin state, so the Order column could not be exercised — /api/extensions reports allowlisted: 0 on stock builds. So this currently rests on the package tests plus the UI-build gate, not on a live drive. To close: load a synthetic plugin (internal/extension/plugin_helper_test.go shows how), reorder it, and show the INVOCATION order changed — not merely the rendered order. Until that is done the control is unproven where it matters.

title: intruder: resource pool has no delay jitter or increment (Burp's random variations)
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (tool-pages sweep). Burp's resource pool offers 'With random variations' and throttleIncrementMillis, so an attack can jitter or ramp its delay — the standard way to stay under a lockout or rate-limit threshold. burpsy has a single flat 'Requests per second': grep -ain 'random|increment' intruder.tsx returns nothing, and internal/intruder/limit.go has no jitter field (its AutoThrottle is reactive backoff on 429/503, a different thing).

Sketch: engine-side first — RateLimit in internal/intruder/limit.go gains an optional jitter fraction and a per-request increment, with the sampling seeded so a run is reproducible; then two inputs beside 'Requests per second' on the Resource pool tab. The backend serves none of this today, so the UI must not grow the controls before the engine can honour them.
acceptance_criteria: A run can be given a jittered or incrementing delay; the engine's actual inter-request timing (not the requested numbers) proves it, and a run with neither setting behaves exactly as today.
close_reason: Fixed in 57badba. intruder.DelayVariation{Jitter, IncrementMS, Seed} via RateLimit.WithVariation (unexported field so NewRateLimiter trusts it); k-th gap = (1/rps + k·inc)·(1+Jitter·u_k), u_k PCG-seeded; a variation REPLACES the bucket spacing (documented). Wire: delay_jitter_percent / delay_increment_ms / delay_seed on intruderRunReq. Refusals verified live (400 naming the value): jitter 100 and -5 ("must be at least 0 and below 100 …"), increment -1 and 600001 ("between 0 and 600000"), and a variation with neither jitter nor increment ("nothing to vary"). UI: two fields in Burp's words on the Resource pool tab beside REQUESTS PER SECOND — "With random variations (± %)" and "Increase delay between requests (ms)". Live timing from real attacks' per-attempt time_of_day (rps=5): flat [201,201,199,200,199]; inc 100 [200,301,401,501,600]; jitter 50% seed 7 [107,294,177,205,226]; same seed replay [107,294,177,206,226]; seed 99 [237,152,287,169,239]; jitter 25%+inc 150 [157,433,471,658,851]. 11 Go tests limit_variation_test.go + intruder_variation_api_test.go; tsc + bun test clean.

title: logger: capture filter cannot filter by MIME type
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (tool-pages sweep). Burp: 'Capture by MIME type' with per-type toggles (logger.capture_filter.by_mime_type.capture_other_binary), so a long engagement does not fill the log with images and fonts. burpsy's Filter settings panel has per-tool toggles, Status, search with Regex/Case sensitive/Negative, In-scope only and a row cap — but grep -ain 'mime' logger.tsx returns nothing.

Sketch: Organizer already has a working MIME TYPE filter, so the classification exists in the codebase; reuse it in logger.tsx's capture-filter panel and add the field to the capture-filter payload. Check first whether the tool-log record carries a content type — if it does not, this needs a capture-side field and should be re-scoped rather than faked.
acceptance_criteria: The logger capture filter can include/exclude by MIME type, the choice survives a reload, and a captured row's type is what the filter matched on (proven by a test that fails without the filter).
close_reason: Fixed in 3b4c089. The bead's first check mattered: the tool-log record did NOT carry a content type, so a filter matching on something reconstructed would have lied. The fact is now recorded rather than inferred — Entry.Mime holds core.MimeEssence of the response (the same one-line answer Exchange.Mime uses, so a Logger row and a history row can never disagree) supplied by the proxy path, which is where a long engagement's rows come from. NOTE: when I picked this up the filter arm existed but NO caller supplied a MIME, so it could never fire — a decorative control. Wiring the proxy record path is what made it real. Two kinds of 'no type' kept apart: nil = the caller never measured one (never judged), "" = a response that declared none (a measured fact matching no pattern); Record passes nil, RecordMime is for callers that know. EXCLUSION list, not inclusion: burpsy's vocabulary is the open set of essences MimeEssence produces, so an inclusion list would silently refuse every type nobody thought to add. Patterns are type/subtype or type/*; anything else refused with the reason. Verified live proxying a real image/png and text/html origin: no filter -> both captured; mime [image/png] -> /c.png RELAYED http=200 but NOT captured while /d.html captured, filtered_total 1; mime [image/*] -> /f.png not captured, /g.html captured, filtered_total 3; GET returns filter.mime so the choice survives a reload; mime [image] -> 400 'invalid MIME pattern "image": want type/subtype or type/*'. The relayed 200 on refused rows is the point: this is a CAPTURE filter, not a block. Mutate-and-verify: disabling the arm fails with 'a row whose response was image/png was captured, so the exclusion did nothing and the log still fills with images'. Gates green.

title: comparer: no word-level compare — Text/Hex are view toggles, the diff is byte-granular
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (tool-pages sweep). Burp has 'Word compare' (2 string hits) and 'Byte compare' (1) as distinct compare modes; word-level is what makes two HTML responses readable side by side. burpsy's Comparer buttons are Text / Hex — a *view* toggle, not granularity — and internal/web/diff.go is byte-granularity Myers throughout; the file's own header comment acknowledges the page 'compared bytes rather than words', which is a statement about granularity.

Sketch: diff.go already isolates the diff behind a token sequence (prefix/suffix trim, then Myers), so tokenising on word boundaries for a granularity=word request is contained to one file; then a Words/Bytes toggle in comparer.tsx. The output must say which granularity produced it, and a word-level diff of two byte-identical inputs must still be identical.
acceptance_criteria: Comparer offers Burp's two granularities; a word-level comparison of two HTML responses is demonstrably different from the byte-level one on the same inputs, and the rendered result names the granularity it used.
close_reason: Fixed in d5b37c2, together with burpsy-react-ui-mwq (the 2026-08-27 audit's earlier filing of the same gap; this issue's live sweep evidence confirmed it). Word compare is a real compare mode, not a view toggle: the server diffs tokens (diffWords) and the counters count tokens. Wire: granularity "bytes" (default) | "words", unknown → 400 naming the value; response echoes the applied granularity and the badge reads the echo. See mwq's close for the full evidence list.

title: ui shell: View menu is a theme menu, not Burp's tab-visibility list
description: Duplicate guard: if this title already exists, ignore this. title: ui: no Engagement tools submenu (Burp's eight-entry group)
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep): Burp's context menu carries an Engagement tools submenu — Find references, Discover content, Schedule task, Target analyzer, Generate CSRF PoC, Manual simulator (tools/engagement-tools/index.html), plus Find comments and Find scripts on the site map (tools/search.html). burpsy has one member flat on the row menu (Generate CSRF PoC) and the pages for several others (Target › Content discovery, Settings › Scheduled tasks, /api/search) with no context-menu route to them.

Sketch: pages/history.tsx row menu — add a 'sub' group holding Find references (/api/search scoped to responses linking the row's URL), Find comments / Find scripts (canned regexes per search.html), Discover content (navigate to #contentdiscovery seeded with the row's host+path), Schedule task (Settings › Scheduled tasks seeded), and keep Generate CSRF PoC. Only ship the entries whose action really runs; name any member that stays out.

close_reason: Fixed in 3e1803e + 6e4f9d9 + 005573a. Burp's Engagement tools group, built as data with its dispositions pinned, routed into the site map's menus and seeded from the origin actually captured. Follows the rule burpsy-react-ui-yinb established for the Intruder menu: an item either does its job or is disabled WITH its reason in the title, never a no-op. The history row menu carries 28 items. ui-pass.sh 53/53 with zero page errors against that console. title: repeater: no Send to… on the message editor's context menu
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep): both Repeater panes' context menus are encode/convert/find only; the sole send action on the page is a 'To Intruder' toolbar button. In Burp, Send to… is on every message editor (Send to Repeater/Intruder/Comparer/Sequencer/Decoder).

Merged clean with --no-ff (894e7e7): the only overlapping file, pages/repeater.tsx, took both sides — bg7j's send-on control plus HEAD's usePluginExchangeActions swap. tsc --noEmit clean and bun test green on the merged tree; bundle rebuilt and committed (eacfed5). The slice's own acceptance (an unsent Repeater draft can send itself on) shipped as committed.

title: ui shell: no tool-tab context menu (Burp's detach/reattach/hide)
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep): right-clicking a tool tab returns 0 menu items, with a positive control on a history row in the same evaluate returning 28. Burp has exactly three: suiteTabBarMenuDetach, suiteTabBarMenuReattach, suiteTabBarMenuHide.

description:

title: scope: no rule library — Burp's 'Save to library' has no equivalent
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (parity sweep). Burp keeps 'Save to library' in the scope panel class (burp.Zhw_ -13442, the same class as -13456 'Use advanced scope control'), so a rule set can be named and reloaded across projects. burpsy's scope page has no such control: grep -n -iE 'library' internal/web/ui/src/pages/scope.tsx returns nothing, and the page's only persistence is the live rule list. Burp's "Save to library" for scope: library_save / library_load / library_delete actions on the existing /api/scope (replace-not-merge on load — merging would make a load a widening whose result depends on what was already there). title: scanner: three Burp scan-config keys have a mechanism behind them but no configuration path
description:
Carved out of jvyw's close: the full classification of Burp's 55 scanner-side keys is now in builtInConfigKeys (25 honoured, 30 reported with a reason), and three of the 30 are cases where the engine already has the mechanism and only the wiring is missing:

Needed: an AuditConfig field, CheckContext plumbing, the harness passing it, and the caveats view reading the run's value instead of the constant.
2. scanner/misc_insertion_point_options/use_nested_insertion_points — nested expansion is unconditional in bcheck.EnumerateWithLimit; turning it off needs a flag on that entry point (and its callers: the probe harness, the audit-item ledger, and Intruder's uncapped body enumeration, which wants it on).
3. scanner/ignored_insertion_points/skip_all_tests_for_parameters and skip_server_side_injection_for_parameters — the enumerator has no parameter-name exclusion list; the second key additionally needs per-check exclusion, which the dispatch model does not have.

close_reason: Fixed in 315c4d1 + 556f464 + e2caa5b + e9d2232, with the bead's own framing corrected rather than accepted. The bead said THREE keys had a mechanism but no configuration path. Only TWO actually did, and saying so is the deliverable: max_insertion_points_per_base_request and use_nested_insertion_points are now read and applied through the row like every other key, each with a test that FAILS if the key is accepted and then ignored. The rest stay reported, with reasons that now name the missing mechanism instead of gesturing at it. The honoured-key table moves 25/30 to 27/28. Refuse-not-clamp held where it mattered: a max of 0 enumerates nothing, so the run probes nothing and reports a COMPLETED audit — clamping it to 1 would run a configuration nobody wrote, so 0 is refused with a new min of 1 on the row struct. Also reaches the operator through the configuration library the same session landed (uxcs) rather than a parallel surface, so a saved configuration carries these keys and the run records the name it ran under. INTEGRATION NOTE: this work tripped Test_a_configs_reported_keys_are_exactly_what_apply_overlays, the oracle that refuses to let a key reporting Applies=true go unchecked — I added both cases in 4afcce4, checking the VALUE not a presence bit, since 0 on use_nested_insertion_points is the meaningful setting and an unset cap must leave the base alone. go test ./internal/scanner green (476s) in the merged tree; uxcs itself live-verified end to end by the main session against the shipped console.

title: ws: an operator's edit to a frame is nowhere reported
description:
burpsy-react-ui-sd0d fixed the history Edited column by making it a fact recorded where the hold resolves. A WebSocket frame has no row of its own — this package's only rows for a socket are the handshake's (proxy.go/ws.go) — so an operator edit to a frame (intercept.tsx forwards edited payloads; ws.go's relay encodes them) is relayed correctly and reported nowhere: the handshake row's UserEdited comes from the request hold, not from any frame edit.

Not a misreport, a gap: nothing claims the edit did not happen. Closing it means deciding whether frames get their own rows in history (they already have a frames view attached to the handshake) or whether the handshake row's flag should be raised by any child frame edit — the second would put a request-hold fact and a frame fact in one bit, so the first is probably right, and it is a data-model decision rather than a patch.

The sites are named in ws.go's forwardHeld path (the Wait call discards the flag with a comment) so this does not have to be rediscovered.
close_reason: Fixed in 0a157fc. A WebSocket frame the operator edited in the hold was relayed correctly and reported nowhere. Resolved the data-model question the bead framed by giving the FRAME the fact (core.WsMessage.UserEdited) rather than raising the handshake row's flag: folding a frame fact into the handshake bit would put two different questions ('the upgrade request was edited' / 'some frame among these was') in one bit and lose which happened. The fact is CARRIED from intercept.Held.Wait (the site ws.go's comment named as discarding it), never recomputed from bytes — deriving it from 'recorded bytes differ' would report the tool's own Match & Replace rewrites as the operator's, the bug sd0d fixed on the HTTP path. MarkLastMessageUserEdited stamps AFTER the Feed so an interrupt flush of a stale partial cannot claim the flag. Wire sends "edited":false rather than omitting the key. Verified: 4 relay tests (client edit, server edit, untouched forward, M&R rewrite that must NOT read as a user edit) + the marshalled API row + the wshistory Edited column. Mutate-and-verify: stamping unconditionally fails exactly two with 'a frame the operator forwarded untouched was recorded as edited' and 'a Match & Replace rewrite was recorded as the operator's own edit'; restoring passes. gofmt/build/vet clean; go test ./internal/core ./internal/proxy ./internal/web green; tsc + bun test clean.

title: dashboard: 'Audit selected items' is Burp's third scan kind and has no launch — auditing is one exchange at a time
description:
Burp's New-scan dialog has four options (Zhw0, 2026.7.1 teardown) and this is the third: "Audit selected items" — "Identifies vulnerabilities in the selected items". The card now renders disabled in the New scan dialog with that reason on it, where before the dialog listed only three types, so the missing one was invisible.

What Burp does: the operator selects items in the target/site-map table (or holds a set from any tool) and launches an active scan over exactly that selection, as one task.

What burpsy has instead: POST /api/audit/{id} and the legacy /api/scanner/audit, both one exchange per call, driven from the Scanner queue (api_scanner_audit_items.go is the queue). There is no way to hand N exchanges to one run — the nearest thing is the live sweep, which decides for itself which traffic to audit.

The work is mostly a launch surface: accept a list of exchange ids (or a site-map selection), register a dash.KindAuditSession task, and hand them to scanner.AuditSession — which is exactly what auditCrawledExchanges now does for the audit half of crawl-and-audit. The difference is where the id list comes from (a selection rather than a crawl report) and the UI to make one.
close_reason: Implemented in 26e0bbe: POST /api/audit/selected (202 + task id, dedupes and reports what it ran) with the bulk-audit body now shared with the crawl-and-audit phase; launched from HTTP history's tick column and from the now-enabled 'Audit selected items' card in the New scan dialog, both reading the one selection in the store.

title: e2e-ui: behaviour.spec.ts's in-scope-only test hard-codes 5 history rows, so it fails in a full-file run (13 rows) and passes in isolation
description:
behaviour.spec.ts:729 asserts `toHaveCount(5)` on `tr.data-row` after seeding. Earlier tests in the same file proxy their own traffic (five proxyGet calls, plus whatever the browser sends), so by the time this test runs the history holds 13 rows.

Verified at HEAD (04e1860) with the working tree stashed: identical failure, Expected 5 / Received 13. So it is not a regression from a specific change — the number was correct when the file was smaller and nobody noticed it drift.

Also worth noting: the number cannot be repaired by bumping it to 13, because it is a count of *everything else in the file* — it will drift again on the next proxy-using test. The assertion wants to be about the delta this test causes (rows before vs after the scope rule), or the seeds want to be filtered to a host the earlier tests never touch.

Discovered while running the dashboard specs for the crawl-and-audit scan kind.
close_reason: Fixed in 9949bda: both count assertions now state what the test causes (a delta), not the file's history. behaviour.spec.ts 41 passed full file.

title: intruder: TestAutoPauseHaltsWhenTheExpressionAppears is load-sensitive — it fails under a full-suite run and passes 3/3 in isolation
description:
Found while landing burpsy-react-ui-d2g, in a package that commit does not touch.

## Symptom

`go test ./...` (the whole tree, packages in parallel) fails:

    --- FAIL: TestAutoPauseHaltsWhenTheExpressionAppears (0.08s)
        autopause_test.go:78: the attack started sends 3 -> 4 while paused; the hold did not hold
    FAIL	github.com/burpsy-go/burpsy/internal/intruder

The same test passes on three consecutive `-count=1` runs in isolation (`go test ./internal/intruder/ -run TestAutoPauseHaltsWhenTheExpressionAppears`), and the immediately following full-suite run passed too.

## Why it is filed rather than noted

The assertion is about a hold, so a red result is indistinguishable from a real auto-pause regression: 'the attack sent while paused' is exactly what a broken gate looks like. A test that only fails under load trains people to re-run the suite until it is green, which is the failure mode the repo's no-retries UI suite explicitly rejects. Either the test needs a deterministic gate (a channel/wait for the pause to be observed rather than a burst of sends) or the production code has a real ordering hole worth finding.

## Evidence it is load, not the change

Untouched by d2g: `git status --short -- burpsy-go/internal/intruder/` is empty, and the failure appeared only in the full-suite run.
close_reason: Fixed in e8047f7 — and the bead's premise was wrong in the most valuable way. TestAutoPauseHaltsWhenTheExpressionAppears was NOT a load-sensitive test. It was intermittently telling the truth about a real ordering hole in the attack driver, and it usually looked green because it lost the race to observe the fault. The hole: the plan loop gated, THEN queued for an in-flight permit — 'if !a.Control.gate() { break }' passes ordinal n+1 while ordinal n is still on the wire; ordinal n's response trips the auto-pause expression ('ACCOUNT LOCKED'); Pause() is set; ordinal n releases its permit; ordinal n+1, already past the gate, takes it and SENDS. One request escaped every halt in the engine. That is a safety defect, not a test defect: an operator halting an attack because accounts are locking had one more request go out anyway, after the halt. Fixed in the engine rather than papered over in the assertion — no added sleep, no retry. Verified: the test is now deterministic under -count and under load; go test ./internal/intruder green in the merged tree; the full combined batch (build/vet/gofmt/tsc/596 bun tests/seven Go packages) green at integ-batch5, merged to cce72ff.

title: ui e2e: the spec suite's own typecheck script is unwired and red at HEAD
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by this session (2026-09-12).

ui/e2e/package.json declares "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p .", and nothing runs it: e2e-ui.sh goes straight to 'npx playwright test' (e2e-ui.sh:100), and verify.sh/grep finds no reference to it anywhere.

It is red right now, on files nobody touched:

  specs/behaviour.spec.ts(849,87): error TS6133: 'consoleErrors' is declared but its value is never read.
  specs/behaviour.spec.ts(1044,93): error TS6133: 'consoleErrors' is declared but its value is never read.

Both tests destructure the consoleErrors fixture and never assert on it.

## Why it matters

Every other gate in this tree is a gate. The UI lib tests, the bundle build, the token checks, gofmt and vet are all wired into something that fails when they fail — so a spec written today is typechecked only if the author happened to run 'npx tsc --noEmit -p .' by hand. A Playwright spec with a type error still runs (Playwright transpiles without typechecking), so the failure mode is a spec that silently asserts nothing about a typo'd fixture field.

## Fix shape

Two halves, and the second is the one that matters:

1. Assert on consoleErrors in those two tests (or drop the fixture from the destructure if the route legitimately logs), so the existing suite is green.
2. Wire 'npm run typecheck' into e2e-ui.sh next to the browser-presence checks, so the check fails the suite rather than a human remembering. Note e2e-ui.sh's existing refusal shape (message + exit) for the 'typecheck failed' branch, and that it needs node_modules present — the same precondition line 46 already refuses on.
close_reason: Fixed in e61c5d2: e2e-ui.sh runs ui/e2e's typecheck and the two unread consoleErrors fixtures are asserted. Red at the 23ne tree, green after.

title: ui: the token gate is red on the branch head — one unexempted 2px spacing literal
description:
The UI gate `bun run check` fails at HEAD (bf97110, and still after 6dt/7nh2): check-closed-tokens.mjs reports "1 raw literal(s) found outside the token files" at src/styles.css:1419 — `.layout-switch { gap: 2px; }`.

The other three identical 2px gaps in the same file (lines 3410, 3547, 3912) each carry `/* token-exempt: sub-grid optical nudge, smaller than --s1; not part of the fluid spacing scale */`, and so does the 2px gap at line 1033. This one lost its comment, so the gate has been failing quietly — which is worse than a failing gate, because the gate is what stops the next real violation from landing.

Fix: add the same exemption the six sibling sites carry. The value is deliberate (a 2px optical nudge below --s1, exactly the case the exemption text describes), so the exemption is the honest fix rather than substituting a token that would change the layout.
close_reason: Fixed: added the token-exempt comment the four sibling 2px gaps already carry. bun run check is green again (tsc, gen-tokens, check:tokens, test:scripts, 305 lib tests).

title: intruder: insertion points fall back to entire-body for XML and multipart bodies
description: Carved out of i4fa at its close (advisor audit 2026-09-12), per 33t's close-reason statement: XML/multipart insertion points keep the entire-body fallback until bcheck models them (single-parser policy). Implementing real XML/multipart-aware insertion points removes a blunt fallback that makes XML/multipart attacks noisier than Burp's.
close_reason: Fixed in c5d70cc. bcheck now models XML and multipart bodies (multipartBodyPoints: part content + name/filename attributes; xmlPoints: text nodes and attribute values named by element path, recognised by shape as well as Content-Type), with three new codings (XML entity-escape, MIME quoted-string, raw for part content) and a refusal mechanism for containers with no escape that carries into nested points and is checked on the rebuilt value. Intruder adopts every container through one accessor (BodyWindow + ContainerCode) and one escape definition (WireValue), retiring escapeJSON/escapeNested. Declines unchanged for non-UTF-8, plain text and unreadable multipart framing. Verified: 8 new intruder + 14 new/rewritten bcheck tests; multipart Apply re-parsed with mime/multipart (payload verbatim in the attacked part, siblings untouched), XML Apply re-parsed with encoding/xml (payload decoded); 4 mutations all caught (content refusal disabled, sibling index dropped, XML window as JSON, nested refusal not propagated); scanner runtime coverage re-run on the final code: 160 distinct catalog rows demonstrated across 163 endpoints, 0 missed (pin holds); safe-twin suite all PASS including /safe/xml/parse and /safe/xml/expand; e2e-go.sh 24/24; go build ./... , go vet and gofmt clean. Rust reference declines both containers, so the divergence is recorded in gaps.md; the attack-side reporting gap it exposes is filed as 194b.

title: scanner: only 18 of Burp's 78 scan-config keys are honoured (3 more report unapplied)
description: Carved out of oco4 at its close (advisor audit 2026-09-12): t2s landed 18 of the 78 scan-config keys Burp exposes, and 3 further keys are accepted but report unapplied. Decide the target key set for parity, then implement the remainder. Evidence trail: t2s's close reason records the 18/78 accounting.
close_reason: Fixed in 82c3612 and 9dd4cb7. Accounting: every key Burp's 29 shipped configurations set under scanner/* (55 distinct, transcribed from /root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/BuiltInConfigs) now has a row in builtInConfigKeys — 25 honoured (up from 18) and 30 reported as not-applied with a per-key reason, pinned by Test_burps_shipped_scanner_keys_all_have_a_row (25/30) and Test_a_reported_key_is_named_by_both_spellings. The six transcribed presets are now faithful for every honoured key (three select point classes, two set the percentage).
