comments.author: AuditProxy
comments.text:
AuditProxy, Proxy-screen parity audit 2026-08-27 — this issue's premise is false at HEAD, and its grep method is why.

The preview it asks for EXISTS: pages/matchreplace.tsx:399-452 is a "Draft test" card with side-by-side editors — "Sample input" (:433-443) and "Transformed output" (:444-450) — plus a changed/no-change badge at :408 and a "Test draft" button at :427 that applies the draft rules server-side via useTestMatchReplace (:77). That is an original-vs-auto-modified preview.

The body's verification reads: "grep preview|original message|auto-modified in matchreplace.tsx returns no matches." Correct, and misleading — the feature is labelled "Sample input" / "Transformed output" / "Draft test". This is the label-grep failure, not an absence: the capability was searched for by Burp's wording rather than by what it does.

Suggest closing as FALSE, or re-scoping to the one thing that genuinely differs: the test panel is per-RULE-SET (it runs the whole draft against one sample), whereas Burp previews per rule. If that per-rule distinction is what is wanted, the title should say so, because as written the issue invites someone to build a second preview beside the one that already ships.

Not to be confused with burpsy-react-ui-c05, which I filed for a different claim: history does not RETAIN original bytes for real captured traffic, so a rule's effect on live traffic cannot be reviewed after the fact. That one is outstanding.

title: wshistory: no filter surface at all — not just Bambda
description:
RE-TITLED, because the original framing named the one thing that was already decided against and understated the actual gap.

The Bambda half is NOT a gap: burpsy has its own typed query DSL and 8sa closed the Bambda question in burpsy's favour on the grounds that a second filter language would give two ways to say the same thing and stop the query box being the single statement of what is filtered. Filing 'no Bambda filter' invites someone to build the thing that decision refused.

THE REAL GAP, verified: wshistory.tsx contains ZERO matches for 'filter'. Not a DSL box, not a toolbar select, not a search field — nothing. History gained per-column filters composing into the DSL in 5ffe51b and the WS page got none of it, so an operator with a busy WebSocket connection has no way to narrow the frame list at all. That is worse than missing Bambda and is the thing to fix.

## Shape of the work

The DSL is the wrong tool as it stands: internal/query's fields are host/method/path/mime/status/body/length/duration/header/extension/params/highlight/comment — all HTTP-shaped. A frame has a direction, an opcode, a payload and a connection, and none of those are expressible. So this is either:

1. a plain toolbar filter over the frame list (direction, opcode, payload substring), which is small and honest; or
2. new DSL fields for frames, which means deciding what a Queryable is for a frame — the crawler's frontierRow precedent says an adapter that cannot answer a field must report absent rather than guess, and a frame cannot answer  or  at all.

Prefer (1) first. It is the operator-facing gap, and (2) is a grammar decision that should not be made to serve one page.
acceptance_criteria: The WebSocket history frame list can be narrowed by direction, opcode and payload substring; an empty result is distinguishable from an empty connection; the Bambda framing is not reintroduced.
close_reason: WebSocket history frame list narrows by direction, opcode and payload substring — server-side on /api/ws/history (new direction/opcode/payload params; payload read through WsPayload per candidate because the bytes are not on the row; unknown direction/opcode refused 400 rather than ignored, matching the exchange param's rule). UI gains the toolbar (direction, opcode, debounced substring, clear-when-set) and the empty state distinguishes 'no frames match the filters' from 'no frames on this connection' from 'nothing captured yet'. Query key carries all three axes so cache entries cannot cross views. Bambda framing not reintroduced, per 8sa. Tests: TestWsHistoryFiltersByDirectionOpcodeAndPayload, TestWsHistoryRefusesUnknownFilterValues. Committed b4ad874.

title: scope: rule arms are literal globs/prefixes, not per-component regex; IP ranges unsupported
description: Audit gap #37/#38 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). scope.tsx has no advanced scope-rule builder (protocol/host/port/file/param include-exclude expressions) and no 'save to scope library' action. Verified absent: grep advanced|library|save to in scope.tsx returns no matches.
close_reason: Fixed in 0f9bf53. Scope rule arms are no longer literal-only: 'regex:' compiles anchored (\A(?:…)\z) for host and path components, 'range:' accepts CIDR or a bare address (IPv6 included), both opt-in inside the existing Pattern/PathPrefix strings so they survive persist's pattern+path_prefix round trip, the config bundle and the remove/replace identity paths without a new column. Fail closed: an uninterpretable rule matches nothing and a scope holding one contains nothing and is not 'worth considering' (Contains and MayContainHost both refuse) — skipping the broken rule is fail-open exactly when it is an exclude; Scope.Validate/Explain name the offender and the endpoints refuse it with 400. Host bits refused rather than masked; names never resolved (a DNS-dependent scope verdict is one an attacker with a resolver can move); empty expressions refused rather than compiled to match-all. NewScopeRule records a fault instead of panicking (it is on persist's restore path) and Scope.Add compiles both arms at the door, so a restored regex path arm behaves as the stored one did — the restore chain (persist.Restore → scope.Add) was read to confirm it. UI: Host match / Path match selectors in the add form and edit dialog, arm-labelled columns, and Burp's simple mode as component state over the existing paste parser (never on the wire). Verified: 31 Go + 20 TS slice tests, plus an independent 23-assertion harness by the main agent (existing glob/prefix semantics unchanged, both new arms at their edges, IPv6 and bare-address cases, fail-closed agreement between Contains and MayContainHost, offender named, arm rebuilt from Pattern+PathPrefix alone still compiling); gofmt/go vet/go test ./internal/core, web scope+config+capture suite, tsc and bun test src/lib all clean.

comments.author: AuditDashTarget
comments.text:
Independent re-verification at HEAD (655a777), AuditDashTarget Dashboard/Target audit 2026-08-27.
**Part of this issue's premise is now wrong, and the accurate gap is narrower than stated.**

The description says scope.tsx "has no advanced scope-rule builder (protocol/host/port/file/param
include-exclude expressions)". Those arms DO exist: `pages/scope.tsx:163-194` has fields for Rule kind
(Include/Exclude), Host pattern, Port, Path prefix and Protocol, and the table renders all five
(`:98-130`). The wire carries them too (`:54-61`). As written, this issue would be closed by work that
has already shipped.

The absence grep quoted — "grep advanced|library|save to in scope.tsx returns no matches" — is true but
does not support the stated claim; it only shows the words are absent, not the capability. This is the
grep-hit-counting failure mode: the labels differ, the arms are there.

What is actually missing, verified in `internal/core/scope.go`:

1. **Rule arms are literal, not regex.** `NewScopeRule` compiles the host pattern as a glob — `*` and
   `?` translated, everything else `regexp.QuoteMeta`'d (`:55-63`) — and the path is
   `strings.HasPrefix(path, *r.PathPrefix)` at `:101`, a literal prefix. Burp specifies a **regular
   expression per URL component**: `map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zg5d`, *"Specify a regular expression to
   match each URL component, or leave blank to match any item."*
2. **No IP ranges.** Same Burp class: `Host or IP range:`, `Enter regex, IP range or leave blank`.
   `ScopeRule.Matches` (`:83-89`) only regex-matches the host string.
3. **No simple/advanced mode.** Burp ships both — `burp.Zry2`: `enable advanced scope control` /
   `disable advanced scope control` — where simple mode is a flat list of URL prefixes
   (`prefix for in-scope URLs`). burpsy is permanently in a middle state: more than prefixes, less
   than regex. The mode a Burp user meets first has no equivalent.

Suggest rewriting the title and body to "scope rule arms are literal globs and prefixes, not regex, and
IP ranges are unsupported", which is closable on evidence. The save-to-library half is a separate claim
and I have not verified it.

Three smaller scope gaps outside this issue's premise are filed separately, one claim each:
burpsy-react-ui-k5l (a rule cannot be edited), plus the disable-a-rule and Paste-URL/load-from-file
issues.

title: ui: Site map second-view switch (URL vs crawl-paths) and passive-scan controls absent
description: Audit gap #35/#36 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). sitemap.tsx has no read-only/items/queued/processed indicators and no view switch. NOTE: crawl-paths VIEW (#16) and passive-scan branch controls (#17) were already filed as burpsy-react-ui-tix/p09 and closed. This issue tracks only the remaining sitemap read-only indicator + items/queued/processed counters, which are still absent (grep read.only indicator|items|queued in sitemap.tsx returns only the exchange inspector's readOnlyNote, no tree-level indicator).
close_reason: INVALID — its own title asserts what now exists. sitemap.tsx has the URL/Crawl-paths view switch (565c6c7, tix) and the 'Passive scan branch' control (655a777, p09), both in the page header. The body acknowledges this and narrows to 'read-only indicator + items/queued/processed counters', but a tracker is read by title, and a title claiming an absent feature that shipped an hour earlier will be acted on. The narrowed remainder does not survive either: the header already carries three badges — nodes, exchanges, and 'in flight' when non-zero — which are Burp's items/queued/processed under different names, and the grep behind the claim ('read.only indicator|items|queued') tested for Burp's vocabulary rather than for the capability. 'Read-only site map' is a Burp state burpsy has no equivalent of: nothing here makes the tree read-only, so there is no state to indicate. title: ui: Dashboard pause/resume and listener-status controls absent
description: Audit gap #32/#33 (PlumOtter parity audit 2026-08-27). Dashboard.tsx has a live task-progress bar (line 117) but no pause/resume control for a running task and no listener up/down status indicator. Burp's dashboard exposes both. Verified absent: grep for pause|resume|listener status|telemetry in dashboard.tsx returns no matches.
close_reason: Suite-wide pause/resume: dash.Registry gains a paused atomic gate + GateCheck(ctx) (50ms tick, cancellation senior — pause+cancel stops cleanly); tasks already inside one unit finish it, which is the contract, not a limitation. POST /api/tasks/pause|resume with {paused, running} — the running count is the honest part of the reply on an empty dashboard. Sequencer capture takes the gate at its existing between-sends placement. Dashboard: 'Pause all tasks' / 'Resume tasks' button + 'Task execution is paused' warning bar; paused rides the dashboard poll (dashboardResp.Paused). Tests: TestTheSuiteWidePauseRoundTripsThroughTheAPI (gate is state, survives a task finishing, idempotent), TestPausingWithNothingRunningReportsZero, TestGateCheckYieldsToCancellation. Verified live: pause flips button + warning bar + toast 'Tasks paused (0 running)', API reads paused:true; resume clears all. Commits caaca7f (backend), 2868d3b (UI).

comments.author: AuditDashTarget
comments.text:
Independent re-verification at HEAD (655a777), AuditDashTarget Dashboard/Target audit 2026-08-27.
Confirming the pause/resume half and adding evidence that argues this is a capability gap rather
than P3 polish.

Server-side, not just UI: `internal/web/server.go:819` registers
`s.mux.HandleFunc("/api/tasks/", s.handleTaskCancel)` as the ONLY task-mutation route, and
`internal/web/api_tasks_cancel.go:25` parses only the `/cancel` suffix. So pause/resume is absent from
the wire too — this is not a control missing from an existing capability, it is the capability.

Burp side, for the record: `dashboardPauseAllTasksButton`, `dashboardResumeAllTasksButton`
("Pause all tasks" / "Resume task processing"), `dashboardTasksPausedWarningBar`
("Task execution is paused") and per-task `taskListEntryResumeButton` — `map_root.tsv` classes
`burp.Zr_o` and `burp.Zr__`. Note Burp has both a suite-wide pause and a per-task one.

Suggest re-pricing to P2: an operator running a long crawl who needs to do manual testing through the
proxy has only "cancel and lose the crawl" available.

One scope correction to the description: it says "no pause/resume control ... and no listener up/down
status indicator", which bundles two claims. The pause/resume half is confirmed. I did not audit the
listener indicator (Proxy is not my screen set), so that half is still unverified here — worth
splitting so the issue can be closed on evidence.

The remainder of Burp's `taskListEntryOptionsMenu` — rename, delete task, scan again, settings, show

title: ui: whitespace reformat of 5 files hides the substance of the ContextMenu change
description:
The uncommitted ContextMenu work re-indents five whole files from 2-space to 1-space, which buries
the substance and has already caused one outage-class corruption.

## Measurement

    git diff --stat      -> 2247 insertions, 2180 deletions
    git diff -w --stat   ->  124 insertions,   83 deletions

Files: `intercept.tsx`, `matchreplace.tsx`, `organizer.tsx`, `scope.tsx`, `session.tsx`.

So ~96% of the diff is whitespace. The three real defects filed alongside this issue
(burpsy-react-ui-3g5, -e64, -aih) all live in that remaining 4%, and none of them is findable by
reading the diff as presented.

## It has already broken a file

Earlier the same reformatting pass left `intercept.tsx` non-parsing: re-indented wholesale, a
`SplitPane` prop dropped, `TS1003` at line 609, 593 open braces against 565 closes on a 656-line
file. It was restored from HEAD. The current pass parses (`npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0), which is luck
rather than a property of the process.

## The gate that misses it

`bun run build` **succeeded** on the corrupted copy — esbuild strips types without checking them. Any
workflow that treats a green `bun run build` as verification will ship a file that cannot compile.
`npx tsc --noEmit` is the only gate that catches this and belongs in whatever runs before a UI commit.

## Ask

1. Land reformatting as its own commit, separate from behaviour, or not at all.
2. If the 1-space indentation is intentional as a house style, apply it once across the tree in a
   single mechanical commit that touches nothing else, and pin it in a formatter config so it stops
   arriving as a side effect of feature work.
3. Add `npx tsc --noEmit` ahead of `bun run build` in the UI pre-commit path.
acceptance_criteria: Reformatting is separated from behavioural change; tsc --noEmit runs before bun run build in the UI commit path.
close_reason: Done in ecfe2bd, by not landing the reformat at all. The behavioural change was reapplied onto HEAD's 2-space formatting rather than committed on top of the 2-space-to-1-space reindentation: git diff --stat and git diff -w --stat on intercept.tsx are now IDENTICAL at 63 lines, which is the measurable form of what this issue asked for. The other five files (scope, matchreplace, session, advisories, dashboard) had already been reverted to HEAD by their author. Worth recording as the reason this mattered rather than as a style preference: the fixContent_length regression was one character in the middle of six hundred reformatted lines, and that is why it survived a review request that claimed tsc was clean. Item 3 of the issue — running tsc before bun run build — is not enforced by a hook and remains a process matter; noted here rather than claimed.

title: crawl: MaxDuration is only checked between visits — up to four GraphQL guess probes can be sent after the time limit
description:
Follow-up from PR #341 (tyso).

## Evidence
The crawl's MaxDuration is checked between visits only; the GraphQL endpoint-guess step sends up to four probes within one visit, so they can go out after the limit has passed.

## Consequence
A time-boxed crawl can overrun its limit and send requests the operator expected not to be sent.
close_reason: MERGED via integrator (c93a3ab5). Crawler records its Run start; BOTH GraphQL send paths answer to MaxDuration: guessGraphQL checks per probe (up to four requests used to go out past the limit) and introspect checks before its POST. Refusals record the existing SkipGraphQLIntrospection with a time-limit detail - no new skip variant. Red-then-green through crawler.Run vs httptest targets, including an Elapsed>=MaxDuration assertion against vacuous pass. Crawler suite green on the merged tree.

title: sender: the HTTP/1 keep-alive pool is not flushed when upstream-proxy rules or client certificates change — for up to 5s a send can reuse a connection dialled under the old route or identity
description:
Found in review of PR #315 (rj3h.2, ry5n keep-alive).

## Evidence
- The raw-send keep-alive pool is flushed on every client rebuild and idles connections out after 5s, but changing upstream-proxy rules or client certificates does not flush it.

## Consequence
For up to 5s after such a change, a send can reuse a pooled connection dialled through the old upstream proxy or authenticated with the old client certificate.

## Previous close claim
Done in W3 wave: keep-alive pool drops stale-route/stale-cert connections - routeState fingerprint (resolved upstream rule + sha256 of client cert leaf), idleConns stamped at put, take() closes mismatches; route-flip-back cannot resurrect. Red evidence: old-route reuse + cert-bind pre-fix. Merged, pool green.

## Reopened: W3 finding at ce9668d5 (source-only, no tests run, not confirmed exploitable)
- keepalive.go:47-60 reads the live Policy/ClientCerts.
- sender.go:1196 and 1391 stamp the route/cert after the exchange; the re-put at 1212 preserves the stamp.
- So a config change during the first exchange can label a connection dialled under old settings as current, defeating take's live comparison at 1076-1077.
- The pre-dial route variable also has a TOCTOU. The exact dial-consumed identity is the boundary.
- The decompressor allocation-limit concern is separate and not part of this bead.

title: collaborator: identity persistence relies on SIGINT making interactsh-client write its session file — on Windows os.Interrupt cannot be sent, so NewClient fails while -collaborator-state-dir is on
description:
Found in review of PR #309 (odvj, d657 client identity survives restarts).

## Evidence
- The session file is written by interactsh-client (-sf) when it receives SIGINT; burpsy stops the subprocess with os.Interrupt to trigger that.
- On Windows, os.Process.Signal(os.Interrupt) is not supported, so the session is never written and NewClient fails whenever -collaborator-state-dir is set.

## Consequence
On Windows the persistence flag breaks Collaborator outright rather than degrading to a fresh identity.
close_reason: Done in W3 wave: collaborator identity persistence degrades honestly on platforms that cannot signal SIGINT (Windows) - fresh per-process identity, Resumed() false, log still written; signal-capable platforms keep save-and-resume incl. hard refusal. Platform-degradation test added. Merged, oob green.

title: Platform decisions: mapped and declined
description:
USER STORY
As an operator comparing burpsy with Burp, I want every Burp capability family to have a stated answer in burpsy, even when the answer is "no, and here is why". That covers licensing, updates, account sign-in, Burp AI, Enterprise/CI, BApp sharing, Infiltrator and shared Organizer collections. Then I can tell "absent by decision" from "not yet noticed" when I scope an engagement or justify the tool to a client. The parity map should have no silent holes.

---

Burp capability families that need a recorded decision, not code. Infiltrator (azbh); licensing, updates, account sign-in and Enterprise (9g5y); shared Organizer collections (rzqc). Each child closes when gaps.md carries the decline with its Burp evidence and reason, or when a design bead replaces it.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-azbh, burpsy-react-ui-9g5y, burpsy-react-ui-rzqc (3).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none. All three children are open, none in progress.

**Phase 1 — Platform families: licensing, updates, account, AI, Enterprise, BApp sharing (closes 9g5y)**

Files: `burpsy-go/gaps.md` (new section, appended at the end).

Design: one sub-entry per family.
- **Licensing:** the `license*` controls in `/root/burp-re/out/ui_report/setname_inventory.tsx`.
- **Update channel and early adopter:** `AutoUpdateDefaults.json`, `desktop/settings/suite/**`. Cross-reference fyua rather than restating it.
- **Performance feedback.**
- **Burp Suite account sign-in and Burp AI credits:** `desktop/burp-at`, plus the three AI hotkey rows.
- **Enterprise/CI:** the "Enterprise-only feature" literal, already a ROADMAP.md row; link it.
- **BApp-account sharing.**

The shared reason: burpsy is open source and has no vendor backend, licence, account or credit meter. Each entry's re-open condition is "a self-hosted equivalent is designed", where one makes sense, for example AI through the operator-supplied LLM endpoint tracked in bead ei0v.

Tests: a grep that the section names 9g5y and every family; a read-through.

**Phase 2 — Infiltrator (closes azbh)**

Files: `burpsy-go/gaps.md`.

Design:
- **Burp evidence:** `desktop/tools/infiltrator.html` ("patches the application bytecode…"), tree build 51467.
- **burpsy evidence:** `grep -ri infiltrator burpsy-go/internal` returns nothing, as of the PR's HEAD.
- **Reasons:**
  - It needs an agent deployed into the target's JVM or .NET runtime. burpsy has no JVM and no bytecode tooling (ROADMAP: "Loading Burp extensions — no JVM").
  - Its findings flow through a Collaborator server burpsy does not host (ROADMAP: "Hosting a Collaborator server").
  - Instrumenting a client's runtime is outside what a black-box proxy engagement normally authorises.
- **Re-open:** a Collaborator server, plus an operator-supplied agent contract.

Tests: grep for azbh; a read-through.

**Phase 3 — Shared Organizer collections (closes rzqc)**

Files: `burpsy-go/gaps.md`. Optionally, one new bead filed for a file-based collection export/import; that would be a bd create, done by whoever executes this, not by this plan.

Design:
- **Decision: decline.** Burp's Share, Unshare, Copy link and the "Cannot modify a shared collection" state all ride on PortSwigger account sharing.
- burpsy is a single-operator local process. Its console is deliberately loopback-only behind the same-origin gate (`internal/web/api_sameorigin.go`), so a multi-operator share would first need console authentication — a different and much larger design.
- The honest near-term substitute is a file export/import of a collection; today Organizer exports CSV only (`pages/organizer.tsx` ~652). That gets its own bead, cited in the entry.

Tests: grep for rzqc; a read-through.

Risks / open decisions:
- **gaps.md is a Rust-to-Go parity ledger** by its own title, and this section records Burp-to-burpsy platform declines. Recommendation: label the section explicitly as Burp-parity declines so readers don't mistake it for a Rust gap. Alternatively, add a one-line pointer in ROADMAP.md's "Deliberately out of scope" table so the Discover limits panel (`lib/reference.ts`) can surface it. That is optional and would touch UI.
- **Pre-existing duplication.** The repeated sections in gaps.md are a defect in their own right. Recommend filing a separate bead to de-duplicate them, not doing it in this PR.
- **rzqc.** The user may prefer a multi-operator design bead over a decline. The plan defaults to declining.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: none

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- **ga7i/n2un** points Help → License and Check for updates at the 9g5y decline, so 9g5y should land first or in the same window.
- **ga7i/2czi** declines three Burp AI hotkey rows by citing the Burp AI entry this epic writes.
- **rj3h** has no dependency on this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- **One new section, appended once.** `burpsy-go/gaps.md` gains a single appended section, "Platform decisions: mapped and declined (2026-10, burpsy-react-ui-4ep5)". The file already duplicates Decline 5, Decline 6 and the reflected-XSS header section (around lines 1394–1547), so nothing new goes inside that region.
- **Every declined family is covered.** Each family named by 9g5y, azbh and rzqc has its own entry, giving:
  - the Burp evidence: doc path, decompiled identifier, and the build it came from, per SOURCE-OF-TRUTH §1 (tree 2026.7.1 / build 51467 versus installed 2026.7.3 / build 52685)
  - the burpsy evidence as of the PR's HEAD
  - the reason
  - the re-open condition
- **Burp AI is named.** It appears explicitly, including the three AI hotkey rows in `Preferences/UserDefaults.json` (`explain_this`, `send_to_burp_at`, `open_burp_at`), so that ga7i/2czi can cite the decline.
- **Existing declines are referenced, not restated.** fyua (Suite settings: Performance, Startup tuning, Updates, Early adopter) and the ROADMAP.md "Deliberately out of scope" rows (Enterprise/CI, loading Burp extensions, hosting a Collaborator server) are linked.
- **rzqc ends with a decision.** Either a decline, or a replacement design bead whose id is cited in the entry.
- **The prose holds up.** No claim in the new section is stronger than its evidence: every "absent" is backed by a dated grep or code read, never by a grep miss alone.
- **Gate is green on the PR.** This is a docs-only change: the GitHub gate on the epic PR, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` unchanged, and `bun run check` green if the Discover limits rows (`lib/reference.ts`) are touched.
- **Read back and checked.** The rendered gaps.md section is read through once, and each bead id is grep-confirmed present before its child is closed.
close_reason: Closed 2026-10-08 on the originating machine: All three children closed; PR #307 merged (33d7d0a).

title: AI and agent workflows
description:
USER STORY
As a pentester, I want to highlight a header, cookie or script in Repeater and ask the configured LLM to explain it, and to send one finding to a bounded "explore" pass that proposes follow-up probes, sends only the ones I approve, and summarises what they showed as advice. As an operator running a supervised agent, I want to split a goal into sub-tasks with their own approvals, attach items as resources, stop in-flight calls, and rename or archive tasks — with every request the AI causes going through burpsy's scope check and confirmation gate.

---

PREREQUISITE: burpsy-react-ui-x40l, the supervised agent loop, which is open and outside this batch. 51li (sub-tasks) and h83q (task lifecycle) are written as extensions of x40l and cannot start before it. Explainer (hiq7) and Explore Issue (2z3c) can start independently on the existing LLM endpoint that ei0v uses.

Children: burpsy-react-ui-51li, burpsy-react-ui-h83q, burpsy-react-ui-hiq7, burpsy-react-ui-2z3c (4).

DO NOT CLOSE this epic while any child is open — bd close has no open-children guard.

Source: Burp-parity capability map 2026-10-07 (children carry label burp-parity-2026-10-07; epics carry burp-parity-epic).
design:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (one PR per epic; phases are review checkpoints)

Already done or claimed: none — all 4 children open. Prerequisite x40l (supervised agent loop) is open and outside this batch. Context: ei0v (LLM triage endpoint) is closed.

Phase 1 — Shared LLM client and Explainer (closes hiq7)
  Files: new internal/llm/; internal/scanner/triage.go (uses internal/llm); new internal/web/api_ai_explain.go; route_manifest.go (/api/ai/explain POST riskEgress); ui pages/repeater.tsx, ui/inspector.tsx, lib/data.ts.
  Design: input {message_id | raw, selection {offset, length} | text, question?}; the prompt is the selection plus a bounded context window; the response carries the model, prompt size and redactions; the UI action is disabled with the two-gate reason when the endpoint is not configured.
  Tests: llm/llm_test.go against a fake endpoint (key header, errors, size cap); web/ai_explain_test.go (redaction; unconfigured → 503 naming what is missing; marshalled JSON); scanner/triage_test.go unchanged and green.

Phase 2 — Explore Issue, bounded (closes 2z3c)
  Files: new internal/web/api_ai_explore.go; route_manifest.go (/api/ai/explore/plan POST riskEgress, /api/ai/explore/run POST riskAttack); internal/scanner (an advice note type beside TriageNote); internal/toollog (attribution for AI-originated probes); ui pages/scanner.tsx / advisories.tsx.
  Design: the LLM proposes up to 10 probes as reqedit ops against the finding's base request; the plan shows each dry-run request; run takes the plan as its body so the e0yq digest covers exactly what was shown; after the run the LLM summarises and the note links the probe message ids. No loop — a multi-round version becomes an x40l preset later.
  Tests: web/ai_explore_test.go (plan sends nothing to the target — httptest hit count 0; run without token → 428; drifted plan → 428; out-of-scope probe refused and counted; the note never changes Severity or Confidence; marshalled JSON).

Phase 3 — Sub-tasks (closes 51li) — BLOCKED on x40l
  Files: x40l's agent-run package and routes (not yet in the tree); ui agent panel.
  Design: a parent run spawns child runs with their own step queues and approval state; a waiting child shows "needs human intervention"; children inherit, and cannot widen, the parent's scope and policy.
  Tests: a child's approval does not approve the parent or a sibling; parent cancel cascades.

Phase 4 — Task lifecycle (closes h83q) — BLOCKED on x40l
  Files: the x40l run store, its routes, the agent panel.
  Design: attach Proxy, Target or Issue items as resources (by id, read through riskRead routes); Stop interrupts in-flight calls (context cancel plus /api/tasks/{id}/cancel, reusing 2jrr wdza); rename, archive, restore persist; per-turn dedup by SHA-256 over (session, turn, tool, args).
  Tests: Stop cancels a pending send (the target sees the connection close); a duplicate call in one turn returns the first result; archive and restore survive a restart.

Risks / open decisions:
- Explore Issue sends attack traffic a model decided. Building it before x40l risks a second, unsupervised loop; holding every run at a call-bound confirm and a single round is what keeps it supervised. Confirm this reading of "can start independently".
- Explainer and Explore send engagement bytes (possibly tokens) to a third-party endpoint: confirm riskEgress rather than riskCredential, and redaction on by default.
- Phase 2 depends on 2jrr vuxy (reqedit) and e0yq (digest-bound tokens); without them it needs an interim plan-hash check.

QUESTION FOR THE USER: 51li and h83q cannot start until x40l lands, so "one PR per epic" cannot hold unless x40l joins this PR. Options: (a) pull x40l into riw8's PR (large); (b) hold the whole riw8 PR until x40l merges; (c) allow two PRs — hiq7 + 2z3c now, 51li + h83q after x40l.

CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCIES
- Phase 1 extracts internal/llm, which wiwh xpuh (ai.prompt) also needs — whichever merges first owns it.
- 2z3c depends on 2jrr vuxy (reqedit ops and dry-run) and e0yq (call-bound confirm with preview).
- h83q's Stop reuses 2jrr wdza's cancel and notification path; 51li's per-child approval should sit on 2jrr 2jig's policy floor.
- x40l should reuse 2jrr Phase 1's grouped, typed tool mapping rather than a second mapping, as x40l's own text asks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Explainer and Explore Issue use the operator-configured endpoint through a shared internal/llm client extracted from scanner/triage.go; the ei0v two-gate rule (configured AND enabled) refuses with the missing piece named, and the key is never echoed.
- /api/ai/explain is riskEgress (the /api/collaborator/payload precedent for egress that is not to the target). Credential-bearing headers outside the selection are redacted by default; the response JSON lists what was redacted (redacted [] when nothing was).
- Explore Issue is two routes — plan (riskEgress, LLM only, sends nothing to the target) and run (riskAttack, gated). The run's token is bound to the exact plan digest; a drifted plan → 428. Every probe goes through AuthorisedSender, appears in the tool log and is linked from the note. The note sits beside the finding and never moves Severity or Confidence (pinned by a test, as ei0v does).
- Explore Issue is a single round — one plan, one approved batch, one summary; a test asserts no second plan is requested automatically.
- 51li and h83q land only on top of x40l's run object: each sub-task keeps its own approval state; Stop cancels in-flight HTTP calls; rename, archive and restore persist; a re-issued identical call in one turn is deduplicated by a (task, turn, tool, args) digest — tested through the x40l HTTP routes.
- Integration tests through the HTTP routes against a fake OpenAI-compatible httptest server and an httptest target; marshalled JSON asserted for explain, plan, run and note shapes.
- Every new route has a manifest entry and risk class; the confirmation-worthy test list, gated-routes.ts, route-risk.ts and MCP tool tests are updated.
- Live drive against the combined rebuild: Explain a selected cookie in Repeater in the browser console; run an explore plan → confirm → run on a seeded finding; call the same routes over a real MCP stdio session (plan ungated; run → 428 → confirm → run).
- Gate green: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.2 go fmt ./..., build, vet, go test ./... (triage tests unchanged and green), UI tsc + bun run check, ../e2e-go.sh, GitHub gate on the epic PR.
notes: Split approved by the user on 2026-10-07: this epic ships as 2 PRs, one per sub-epic — burpsy-react-ui-riw8.1 = AI assist: Explainer and Explore Issue (PR 1 of 2); burpsy-react-ui-riw8.2 = Agent workflows: sub-tasks and task lifecycle (PR 2 of 2). The general multi-step-auth mechanism: capture a value (a JWT/bearer token, a CSRF token) from one response and inject it into the headers/body of later requests across tools, beyond what a single session rule's macro+extraction already threads. Build on session.Extraction (regex + JSONPath lift) and the {{name}} interpolation the macro engine already has; the open question is the surface — a project-level extraction+injection set that applies outside a login macro, vs. extending the session rule's actions. Acceptance: a token extracted from a login response is injected into a subsequent Repeater/scanner request without the operator pasting it.

title: scanner/editor: name protobuf fields via gRPC server reflection when no .proto is loaded
description: Follow-up to burpsy-react-ui-3pco (.proto naming landed in 8b62526). When the operator has no .proto, ask the target's grpc.reflection.v1(alpha).ServerReflection service for the file descriptors of the called service and feed them to the same Annotate path. Needs: a reflection client over the authorised sender (HTTP/2 + gRPC framing), a FileDescriptorProto -> grpcproto.Schema adapter, and a scope/egress decision (it sends traffic to the target, so it is at least riskEgress and must respect scope). Acceptance: on a target exposing reflection, a captured gRPC call's Protobuf tab can 'Fetch schema from server' and then names fields exactly as a loaded .proto would; refused (with reason) for out-of-scope targets.
close_reason: Merged e5f5da59 (+ regen 0ee7feb8, corpus fix). POST /api/protobuf/reflect-decode (riskEgress): per-request opt-in reflect{target,service,tls}; AuthoriseRequest on the reflection RPC path pre-dial (same gate as Repeater); 5s timeout; no jar credentials ever; FetchServiceDescriptors BFS + SchemaFromFiles + shared decode path; schema_source:reflection + schema_files provenance in the response (target-claimed names never read as operator-pasted); failure = named error + schemaless tree. Pins: happy-path names+provenance+exactly-one-dial (bufconn), out-of-scope 403 zero dials, invalid request zero dials, fetch-failure honesty. Console affordance is mup0 (W2); route sits in uiRouteMissingSurface until then. Integrator gates: grpcproto green, full web suite 100.2s green on merged tree.

title: scanner/editor: resolve protobuf field names and types from a .proto or gRPC reflection
description: Second follow-up to burpsy-react-ui-3x2g (schemaless decode landed). When a .proto is supplied or a gRPC server reflection (grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection) response is available, resolve the field numbers the schemaless view shows into field names and declared types, so the Protobuf tab reads 'user_id: 150' rather than '#1 varint 150'. Build on internal/grpcproto (the wire walk) + a .proto parser or a reflection client. Acceptance: with a .proto loaded, the editor labels fields by name; without one, it falls back to the numbers-and-wire-types view that already ships.
close_reason: Implemented in 8b62526. .proto parsing (proto2/3: messages, enums, oneofs, maps, nested scope resolution, service rpc signatures) + Annotate (names, declared types, enum names; corrects schemaless len-field guesses without changing encoded bytes — every test re-encodes). gRPC call path resolves request/response message types automatically. Covered across the full surface: schema shared in the store for every HttpEditor, per-direction message choice; 9 panes that dropped body bytes now pass body_base64 (bun guard scans every HttpEditor; negative control vs HEAD flags the 9); response panes pass requestPath; Repeater response_body_base64; intercept raw_body_base64 + byte-exact raw_base64 forward. Also fixed: unedited intercept forwards no longer resend mangled text for binary bodies; editable surfaces only take a plain-wire body (no Content-Encoding/chunked). title: scanner: passive check flags a response reflecting a normalized form of an input (server-normalization tell)
description: Optional half of burpsy-react-ui-d617 (the normalize payload processor shipped). A passive/active check that flags a response reflecting a NORMALIZED form of an input different from what was sent — evidence the server normalizes after validating, the tell for the Unicode-normalization bypass class. Reuse internal/intruder/normalize.go's forms: send/observe a known marker, and if the reflection is its NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD/fullwidth-collapsed form rather than the literal, raise a finding. Likely an active check (needs to send a crafted marker) rather than purely passive.
notes: ATTEMPTED and reverted (not shipped). Design: fold a fullwidth probe into the existing 'Suspicious input transformation (reflected)' check (checks_final.go) — every ASCII printable has a fullwidth twin in U+FF01..U+FF5E that NFKC/NFKD collapse to ASCII, so a fullwidth marker reflected in ASCII proves the server normalizes after parsing (the ASCII-only probe the check already sends cannot see this: NFKC(ascii)=ascii). Unit tests passed (fullwidth->ASCII reflection flagged; verbatim/no-reflection not). BLOCKER: the integration test TestTheScannerDetectsWhatTheTargetDeclaresItIsVulnerableTo regressed — the SECOND probe this check now sends to a stored-write endpoint (/st/note?text=) pollutes the stored state so 'Cross-site scripting (stored)' confirmation on /st/notes fails (clean HEAD: 0 missed; with the probe: 1 missed). Sharing one harness (no 2nd baseline) did NOT fix it — the regression is the extra PROBE interfering, not baseline traffic. The runtime target tolerates the existing 1 probe/point but not 2 on stored endpoints. NEXT: either detect normalization from the EXISTING single probe (send the one probe as fullwidth and detect both general-transformation and normalization from it — risk: changing the ASCII probe may shift the big test's other transformation detections; needs validation against runtime_coverage_test), or skip the fullwidth pass on insertion points that write stored state. Must map to Burp catalog issue 'Suspicious input transformation (reflected)' (TypeIndex present; native registry requires one descriptor per catalog issue, so ENHANCE that check, do not add a second). Reusable: toFullwidth(s) maps ASCII printable -> +0xFEE0.

title: storage: the backup lacks Burp's interval schedule and delete-on-shutdown lifecycle
description:
## Claim

burpsy's backup is a real and well-argued implementation — VACUUM INTO rather than a file copy, retention pruning scoped to its own filename pattern, a warning when written beside the live database. What it lacks is Burp's *interval schedule* as a first-class setting and the delete-on-clean-shutdown lifecycle.

## Burp-side evidence (build 51467)

L4 `Zrgw.java:40-64` panel construction; `:137-186` the five controls — "Automatically back up the project every [N] minutes", "Include in-scope items only", "Show progress dialog during backups", "Delete backup file on clean shutdown of Burp", and the `" [disk projects only]"` suffix; `:79` the `user_options.misc.automatic_project_backup` preference; `Zrpa.java:56-82` the progress dialog.

## burpsy-side evidence

`internal/web/api_backup.go:52-62` `backupParams{Dir, Retention}` — two fields, no interval; `registerScheduleKinds` mentioned in `api_backup_test.go:289-292` (a scheduled backup kind exists), so the interval is reachable only as a generic task, not as a backup setting; nothing prunes on shutdown; nothing narrows to in-scope rows.

## Classification

PARTIAL.

## What an operator cannot do

Cannot state "back this up every 15 minutes and keep the last 7" as a configuration (it must be re-created as a scheduled task), and cannot have a throwaway backup auto-deleted at clean shutdown.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `backup` settings section carrying the interval and the delete-on-shutdown switch, both persisted, with the interval validated (0 = off) and refused rather than clamped.
2. The in-scope-only narrowing is **declined with a reason** in the UI: the snapshot is a `VACUUM INTO` of one SQLite file and a scope filter would mean a second, differently-shaped export — a different feature, not a switch.

## Priority

P4.
close_reason: Implemented in 60bb1ed. Automatic-backup interval as a first-class setting (PUT /api/backup/config reconciles one managed 'Automatic backup' schedule of the existing backup kind; 0=off; interval validated+refused not clamped) + delete-on-clean-shutdown (persisted in backup.config; CloseProject sweeps backupFilePattern files in the configured dir before Close, clean-shutdown only, scoped so operator files are untouched). In-scope-only narrowing declined with reason in UI (AC2). Backend+UI+persist+route manifest+gated-routes. Verified: gofmt, go build, go test ./internal/web (incl new api_backup_config_test.go: negative-interval-refused, reconcile create/update/remove, round-trip, 503 without -db, shutdown-sweep-deletes-only-own), tsc, bun check (884), build. NOT exercised live (sandbox SIGURG) — in-process httptest + unit coverage.

title: ui: the message editor has no font-name control — Burp's http_message_display.font_name has no counterpart
description:
## Claim

Burp persists two font knobs for the message editor: a family and a size, plus a smoothing toggle. burpsy has the size (`editorFont`, `store.ts:440`) and the UI scale, but the family is fixed by the stylesheet.

## Burp-side evidence (build 51467)

## burpsy-side evidence

`settings.tsx:1475-1478` "Editor font size" only; `store.ts:440` `editorFont: EditorFont` is a size union.

## Classification

STILL_MISSING (small).

## What an operator cannot do

Cannot set a monospace family that reads HTTP bytes well on their machine — the single most-read surface in the tool.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An `editor_font_family` preference (a select of the families the stylesheet can express, plus a monospace default) that feeds the editor's CodeMirror theme and the `--editor-font-family` custom property, persisted like the other browser-side appearance preferences.

No stale parity doc (no font_name reference in Go/docs). All green: tsc, bun check (868), build; editor-font.test.ts covers the helper + store->property->theme wire.

title: theme: a JSON theme import that fills burpsy's existing tokens — not the 240-slot L&F indirection
description:
## Claim

Burp's theme is a data format (`ThemeFactory.loadCustom` parses a JSON theme, inherits from a built-in default, and a custom L&F becomes selectable). burpsy's theme choice is three hard-coded values. The uncovered part is narrower than "the theme engine": Burp lets an operator **load a theme file**, and burpsy has no equivalent of that one affordance.

## Burp-side evidence (build 51467, out-of-jdt_src layer)

`out/theme/burp/theme/ThemeFactory.java:14-40` (`loadCustom`, `getDarkProperty`, `inheritFrom(built-in defaults)`) and `:42-51` (`loadBuiltIn`); `out/theme/resources/DarkTheme.json:129-139` 10 palette families; `THEMES.md:99-127` the swatch→palette→slot indirection; `BurpLaf.properties` 779 keys. L4 `Zcwd.java:42-47` `user_options.display.user_interface.look_and_feel` is the persisted selector.

## burpsy-side evidence

`settings.tsx:60-64` `THEMES = [system, light, dark]`; `styles.css:103-135` fixed `--editor-*`; `platform-gaps-2026-09-26.md:111-114` records that adopting Burp's indirection layer is a *declared design decision* (and it is right: Burp's editor hexes would regress contrast); `gen-tokens.mjs:6-8` makes Penpot canonical.

## Classification

STILL_MISSING, and **partly a declared design decision** — the token *values* are settled. The uncovered affordance is the theme-file load, scoped to what burpsy's tokens already have.

## What an operator cannot do

Cannot give a colleague a named look, and cannot adopt a house palette without a source edit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A JSON theme import that reads the subset burpsy's tokens already have (the `ui.text`/`ui.background`/`ui.editor.message` families), fills only tokens the file names, and leaves the rest at the Penpot defaults.
2. A preview-and-revert control and a stated refusal for a file naming a slot burpsy has no token for.
3. Explicitly **not** the 240-slot indirection and **not** the group/highlight/status families (those belong to `axm9`).

## Priority

P4.
close_reason: Implemented in 916f7de + preview/guard follow-up 6a4eed1. JSON theme import scoped to the ui.text/ui.background/ui.editor.message token families: parseThemeFile fills only named slots, refuses unknown slots (naming them) and non-colour values; applied as inline --token overrides on <html> with unnamed slots cleared (revert restores Penpot defaults). True preview via non-persisted themePreview (a bad palette is escaped by reload); Keep persists; Revert clears. Corrupt-persisted-theme crash guarded. Explicitly NOT the 240-slot indirection or group/status/highlight families (axm9); editor syntax colours stated as not-yet-themeable. Verified: tsc, bun check (879), build; theme-import.test.ts (fill/refusal/colour-validation/corrupt-guard/persist-structure). Browser-side only (no server config export carries appearance prefs); off by default so a11y suite unaffected. NOT exercised live (sandbox SIGURG-kills a running burpsy) — verification is unit + structural tests.

title: intruder: denial-of-service mode is declined — a send-and-do-not-read attack cannot be run
description:
## Claim

Burp's "Use denial-of-service mode (no results)" sends each request and deliberately does not read the response. burpsy refuses to implement it and says so in the UI; there is no wire field and no engine path.

## Burp-side evidence (build 51467)

`Zru3.java:25-31` — `this.ZP.setText("Use denial-of-service mode (no results)")` in the attack's Other-settings tab, alongside the five settings burpsy does implement at `:32-50`.

## burpsy-side evidence

`ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx:2826-2838` renders a field-hint saying it is not implemented, and `internal/intruder/connection.go:17-19` repeats the reason. `grep` for dos / no_results across `internal/web/api_tools.go` and `internal/intruder` returns nothing — there is no field to refuse.

## Classification

CONFIRMED, and DELIBERATE — a stated decline, not a silent gap. Filed as a parity increment only.

## What an operator cannot do

The flow-control/consistency attack (a parameter that makes the server hang, a race on a lock, a cache-poisoning sequence) is unrunnable from burpsy. The operator must script it by hand outside the tool.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `dos_mode` wire field on `intruderRunReq`.
2. A send that can leave without reading, plumbed through the same authorised sender.
3. **EVERY attempt-recording path must carry "no response was read" rather than a zero status/length/reflected** — this is the real work, and the reason the current decline is correct.
4. A report test proving a DoS-mode run records zero-length and no-response rather than 0.
5. No UI affordance ships before (3) lands.

## Priority

P4 (explicitly declined, correctly).
close_reason: Resolved as a documented decline (no code change). DoS mode (send-and-do-not-read, for flow-control/consistency/DoS attacks) is deliberately not implemented in burpsy and is stated as such in the UI (intruder.tsx:2891-2898) and the engine (connection.go; refused by wire-field absence). The bead's own classification is 'CONFIRMED and DELIBERATE — a stated decline, not a silent gap.' It is also outside what I will build: implementing a denial-of-service attack mode is refused by policy. The acceptance criteria describe what a full implementation would require (notably AC3: every attempt-recording path carrying 'no response read' rather than a zero status/length) and correctly note why the decline stands. Closing as won't-implement; the stated decline is the intended resolution.

title: decoder: Smart decode is deliberately declined and Burp's transform set is UNKNOWN — record both so neither is re-filed
description:
## Claim

This bead is deliberately NOT a parity claim. Two things are unresolved and one is declined.

## (a) UNRESOLVED: Burp's decoder transform list

`Zear.java:12-26` carries the display names but its static initialiser was removed by the ZKM-strip pass, so the NAMES ARE NOT RECOVERABLE from this tree (build 51467). `Zryp.java:63-103` proves three SEPARATE lists exist — `Zear.ZY` (encode), `Zear.Zg` (decode), `Zear.Zx` (hash) — but not their members. burpsy has ten layers (`codec.go:54`) plus ascii and rot13 (`api_toolkit.go:1906-1915`) plus four hashes (`:1964-1982`). Whether Burp has transforms burpsy lacks is UNKNOWN, not absent. **Anyone grepping jdt_src for transform display names will get zero hits and wrongly conclude Burp has fewer transforms than it does.**

## (b) DECLINED: Smart decode

`Zryp.java:485-486` ("Smart decode" / tooltip "Try to decode automatically"). burpsy removed the guess-alphabet control and `api_toolkit.go:1781-1785` records that removal as correct, because the control was decorative — it accepted input, returned 200 and changed nothing.

## Classification

(a) UNKNOWN per the project's evidence rule 1. (b) a deliberate decline that should be recorded so it is not re-filed.

## Acceptance criteria

Either recover `Zear`'s members by running the decompiled class under a ZKM-aware harness (the `lambda$…` synthetic-name route, or a runtime FeatureTracer over the live jar), or record the transform list as UNKNOWN in `gaps.md` with the exact reason. Do not file any specific transform as missing without that evidence.

## Priority

P4.
close_reason: gaps.md now records both halves: Decline 6b notes smart decode is deliberately declined (the decorative guess-alphabet control was removed), and the transform-list gap is recorded as UNKNOWN because Zear's static initialiser was stripped from the decompiled tree. No specific transform is filed as missing.

title: scanner: cannot test an MCP server as a target — enumerate and probe its tools/resources/prompts (scope decision first)
description:
## Claim

burpsy cannot test an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server as a target. As AI agents adopt MCP, the servers they connect to become an attack surface — over-broad tools, injectable prompts/resources, tools that reach internal services — and ZAP added first-class MCP-target scanning in 2026. burpsy has no notion of MCP as a target.

## Scope question (decide before building)

This is forward-looking and outside classic web-app parity. It is filed at P4 so the priority reflects that. Whoever picks it up should first confirm MCP-target testing is in burpsy's intended scope; if it is not, close as out-of-scope rather than build it. Filed because it is novel, on-theme, and low-risk to record now.

## Evidence

burpsy:
- No MCP-target capability: burpsy treats MCP only as a shape for its OWN API (crates/web MCP-02, route_manifest.go riskClass). There is no scanner scope, check, or client that connects OUT to a third-party MCP server and probes it. (Distinct from burpsy-react-ui-q31t, which exposes burpsy over MCP; this is the inverse — burpsy as the client attacking a server.)

External precedent: ZAP (2026) can "scan MCP servers as a first-class target," performing the MCP handshake, enumerating every tool, resource, and prompt the server exposes, and sending a representative request to each (zaproxy.org updates, cybersecuritynews). This is the reference behaviour.

## Fix direction

An MCP client scanner scope that, given an MCP server endpoint (stdio or HTTP/SSE):
1. Performs the MCP handshake and enumerates tools, resources, and prompts.
2. Sends a representative call to each tool and records the result.
3. Runs checks for the MCP-specific classes: tools that reach internal/SSRF-reachable hosts, prompt/resource injection, over-broad or unauthenticated tool exposure, and tool descriptions that smuggle instructions.
4. Reports findings in the existing catalogue with a new MCP category.

Reuse burpsy's own MCP knowledge: the risk-class vocabulary it already applies to its own routes (route_manifest.go) is a ready model for classifying a target server's tools.

## Why it matters

MCP servers are becoming core infrastructure for AI-driven systems and are currently under-tested. Being able to point burpsy at one and enumerate and probe its surface would put burpsy alongside ZAP on a surface that barely existed a year ago — if it is in scope.
design:
APPROACH DECIDED (user, 2026-09-27): ship MCP-target scanning as an OPT-IN toggle that installs and runs an external scanner on demand, rather than reimplementing natively. This preserves burpsy's pure-Go / no-external-binary default — the dependency exists only when the operator opts in.

Design:
- A Settings toggle 'MCP target scanning' (default OFF). Enabling it clearly states that burpsy will download and run third-party code.
- Default engine: tamish560/mcprobe (MIT, single static Go binary, zero deps, no Python, no API key). 'Install' = fetch the pinned release binary, verify a checksum, cache it; 'run' = exec it against the target MCP endpoint and parse its SARIF/JSON into the existing finding catalogue. Easiest possible install-and-run because it is one binary.
- Advanced engines (optional, later): invariantlabs-ai/mcp-scan or cisco-ai-defense/mcp-scanner (Apache-2.0, Python + LLM key). Only if the operator supplies the runtime and key; keep them behind the same toggle, invoked as subprocesses, never bundled.
- Safety: MCP-target scanning both executes an external binary AND sends probes to a target, so gate a run behind the existing riskAttack confirm (route_manifest riskClass) in addition to the toggle, and confirm the target is in scope. Record which engine and version produced each finding (provenance) so a result is reproducible.
- Pin the engine version and checksum; surface the version in the UI. Do not auto-update silently.

This supersedes the earlier 'reference-and-reimplement in Go' recommendation in the notes: that remains a fallback if a bundled default (no download) is later wanted, and mcprobe's MIT license still permits porting its enumeration/deterministic checks into Go at that point.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in toggle (default OFF): enabling it downloads and checksum-verifies the pinned mcprobe binary; with the toggle on and the target confirmed in scope (riskAttack confirm), a run execs the engine against the MCP endpoint, ingests its SARIF/JSON into the catalogue with engine name+version recorded, and produces at least one finding on a known-poisoned test server. Toggle off = no external binary present or run.
notes:
2026-10-06: not implemented this session. The bead itself says to confirm MCP-target testing is in burpsy's intended scope BEFORE building, and close as out-of-scope if not. That scope call belongs to the project owner, not an implementing agent. Left open pending that decision; recommendation on request.
SCOPE DECISION 2026-10-07: user confirmed MCP-target scanning IS in burpsy's scope. Extensive online research dispatched (threat catalogue, protocol/transports/auth, existing scanners, standards mapping). Uncommitted WIP exists in internal/mcpscan + web/api_mcpscan.go (builds, tests pass, not wired to routes).
2026-10-09: a native scanner port exists on branch beads/f-mcpscan (cdd8230b), held as reference per the user's decision of 2026-10-09; wflj follows the Sept 27 opt-in mcprobe design.

title: agent: no supervised agent loop over the existing risk/confirm gate — task, per-step approval, transcript
description:
## Claim

burpsy has the two hard pieces of a supervised agent runner — an LLM triage path and a per-route risk/confirm gate — but no operator-facing loop that ties them together: a task you hand it, a visible sequence of proposed steps, per-step approval for anything that sends attack traffic, and a recorded transcript you can stand behind. This is the model the whole field adopted in 2026 (Burp AT, Caido AI skill, ZAP MCP), and it is a natural build-on, not a from-scratch feature. Larger and more speculative than the other beads; filed at lower priority.

## Evidence

burpsy:
- LLM triage exists: internal/scanner/triage.go, internal/web/api_triage.go, internal/web/api_capture.go (the DOM dynamic-tier "Confirm" verdict).
- The enforcement primitive exists: internal/web/route_manifest.go `riskClass` (riskRead vs riskAttack) and the MCP-02 confirm gate (crates/web/src/lib.rs).
- What is missing: no task/step/approval loop. `grep -rniE 'approval'` over internal/web returns nothing; there is no agent-run record, step queue, or approval UI.

External precedent: Burp AT's stated design is "Agents propose. Burp enforces. You decide," with scope, tool access, and approval rules "in the tooling layer, architecturally separate from the model," and "every request and decision is recorded" so a finding is reproducible (portswigger.net/blog/introducing-burp-at, 2026.7). ZAP's MCP add-on and Caido's AI skill are the same shape. This is the industry-standard safety model, and burpsy already implements its core (risk + confirm).

## Fix direction

An agent-run object and a panel:
1. A task the operator states in natural language, scoped to targets already in burpsy's scope.
2. The agent proposes steps; each step maps to an existing API route and inherits that route's `riskClass`.
3. riskRead steps may auto-run; every riskAttack step waits on the existing confirm, surfaced as an approve/deny in the panel — the enforcement is the route manifest's, never the model's word.
4. Every proposed step, decision, and resulting request/response is appended to a transcript tied to the run, so a finding it produces is reproducible.

Depends on nothing, but is most useful after the MCP server bead (which exposes the same routes to a model over a standard transport) lands, and should reuse that tool mapping rather than a second one.

## Why it matters

burpsy already paid for the expensive, dangerous part — deciding per route what an unattended model may do and where a human must sign off. Without the loop, that safety model only guards the human-driven UI. With it, burpsy can run supervised agent work under its own scope and approval enforcement, matching what operators now expect from every proxy in this class, without trusting a prompt to stay in bounds.
acceptance_criteria: An agent run takes a scoped task, proposes steps each mapped to an API route with its riskClass, auto-runs riskRead steps, holds every riskAttack step at the existing confirm as an approve/deny, and records every step and request/response to a run transcript.
notes: 2026-10-06: not implemented this session. A supervised agent runner (task -> proposed steps -> per-step approval gated on the existing riskClass -> recorded transcript) is a multi-file subsystem the bead itself flags as 'larger and more speculative', and it is most useful after the MCP server bead lands so it can reuse that tool mapping. Not a single-session build to a real standard; left open.

title: theme: burpsy cannot express Burp's group/status/issue colour families, and the message editor has no cookie tokens
description:
## Claim
Two related gaps from the theme inventory. (a) Burp's 15 group colours, 9 annotation highlights, 5 task statuses and 5 issue severities are named, themeable families; burpsy has three semantic status roles (`--good/--warn/--bad`) and maps severity to a tone inside TSX. (b) Burp colours cookies in the message editor (`DarkTheme.json:280-281`, `cookieName`/`cookieValue`); burpsy has `--editor-url-param-name/value` and no cookie token at all.

## Evidence
- Burp: `out/theme/resources/BurpLaf.properties:917-965` (groups/highlights), `:1068-1076` (status/issue); `DarkTheme.json:141-240,359-371` (resolved values), `:280-281` (cookies).
- burpsy: `ui/src/tokens/semantic.css:55-57,82-84` (three status roles); `ui/src/styles.css:77-100,124-151` (editor syntax tokens, no cookie pair); `ui/src/pages/issues*.tsx` maps severity->tone in TSX.

## Fix direction
Compose a `severity-*` scale in `semantic.css` from the existing red/orange/yellow/blue primitives and consume it in the Issues table; add the two cookie tokens and colour cookie spans in the editor (the cookie spans already exist in `lib/message.ts`). Do NOT adopt Burp's editor syntax hexes — burpsy's are Darcula values deliberately lifted past WCAG AA with the contrast measurements recorded in-file — and do NOT import Burp's three-tier palette indirection over the Penpot pipeline `scripts/gen-tokens.mjs` declares canonical.

## Why it matters
Severity and status are what an operator reads at a glance in a triage table; a colour hard-coded per component cannot be themed and drifts from the rest of the console. The cookie tokens are the single genuinely additive item the 779-key inventory turned up.
notes: EVIDENCE 2026-09-27: Burp's colour families are now code-recoverable — out/theme/resources/BurpLaf.properties carries Colors.ui.groups.0..14 (15), Colors.ui.highlight.0..8 (9), Colors.ui.status.*, Colors.ui.issue.*; DarkTheme.json:129-313 carries the full palette + the 44-key ui.editor.message family; THEMES.md documents the swatch->palette->slot indirection. Also corrected the same pass: styles.css's dark block is NOT Darcula (0 darcula hits in the tree; Burp's dark editor palette is DarkTheme.json:264-313) — the comment now says so.
close_reason: Implemented in c0c7268, per the bead's fix direction. (a) One --severity-* scale (aliases of semantic status roles, hand-authored per semantic.css's rule for pure aliases) consumed through lib/severity.ts by all four surfaces that had their own switch (scanner, advisories, site map, dashboard) plus the tree severity dots; themeable via a new ui.issue family in the JSON theme import; guard test flags a reintroduced local mapping (negative control: flags all 4 at HEAD). (b) --editor-cookie-name/value in both themes (reusing already AA-measured colours) and editor decoration of Cookie pairs / Set-Cookie's cookie. title: scope: no scope-change notification — a plugin or subscriber can never be told the scope moved
description:
## Claim
Burp pushes a `ScopeChangeHandler` callback when scope changes. burpsy re-reads the scope on every request (correct, and documented as deliberate) but exposes no notification, so nothing can subscribe.

## Evidence
- Burp: `out/burp/api/montoya/scope/ScopeChangeHandler.java:20-26`; `ScopeChange.java` (an empty marker interface, i.e. the callback carries no payload).
- burpsy: `internal/web/server.go:797-811` — the suite-scope predicate is a closure reading live state per request, with the reason recorded in the comment.

## Fix direction
One `OnChange(func())` on `core.Scope`, invoked by `Add`/`RemoveScoped`/`ReplaceScoped`/`Clear`. Self-contained in `internal/core/scope.go`; the event stream and any extension subscriber can then react.

## Why it matters
Anything that caches a scope decision (an extension, a crawler frontier, the live-audit sweep) either re-reads forever or goes stale, with no third option.
notes: ADJACENT EVIDENCE 2026-09-27: Burp's own subscription mechanism is the Montoya Scan_change_handler family (L1 /root/burp-re/out/burp/api/montoya/scope/ — ScopeChangeListener / ScopeChange) plus the internal Zr-series; build 51467. The burpsy-side acceptance shape: an event on the live stream (the existing dash.EventBus) carrying old/new scope, consumed like EventScopeChanged already is by the Settings page.
close_reason: Landed in aff297b. Scope.OnChange(handler) registers a scope-change subscriber and returns an unregister function; removal is by registration id so two registrations of the same function are independent. Fires from Add, Remove, RemoveScoped, SetRuleEnabled, ReplaceScoped and Clear, always AFTER the write lock is released - every mutator used defer-unlock, so a notification inside the critical section deadlocks as soon as a handler calls Contains(), which is the obvious thing for a subscriber to do. Handlers are panic-contained: the edit is already applied and must not be lost to third-party code. A callback rather than the existing dash.EventBus, because a bus subscriber is HTTP-shaped while an extension is a child process whose host need not be serving a console. notify vs notifyUnconditional is load-bearing: three mutations change meaning while leaving the rule count identical (toggle, in-place edit, clear-of-empty), and a count-difference filter would drop exactly the events a stale subscriber needs. 10 tests, 3 mutations killed, including the write-lock one which deadlocks and is caught by a timeout whose stack names SetRuleEnabled. NOT included: publishing to dash.EventBus for the console surface, which the bead's own note proposes and which belongs with the caller that wants a console to reflect the change; internal/web is a peer's working set.

title: suite: no REST-API settings page — burpsy IS a JSON API with nothing describing or gating it
description:
## Claim
Burp's REST API is a 12-key settings page (enabled, address, port, keys, listen mode, callback base URI, insecure mode, debug, update server, shutdown-on-heartbeat-failure). burpsy serves roughly 200 routes and no surface describes them, classifies them, or gates them.

## Evidence

## Fix direction

## Why it matters
An operator cannot see what their console exposes to the network, and the classification that would answer the question already exists inside a test file.

Read-only Settings > REST API section renders the full route inventory (~150 routes) grouped by the server's risk class, each with the manifest's own definition, confirm-gated classes marked (derived from the gate table), plus the -web bind address with loopback-vs-network note. No backend. Verified: tsc, bun check (885), build.

title: ui: the status bar is outside any landmark, which the WCAG-tagged a11y check cannot see
description:
Found by the live pass (./ui-live.sh + burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md) on a clean load of #intercept, light theme:

  axe, unrestricted rule set -> region(moderate): .statusbar\n\n'region' is an axe best-practice rule, not a WCAG 2.0/2.1 A or AA rule, so it is NOT in the tag set the a11y spec (and the live pass) assert on — TAGS = wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa. Both report zero violations on the same page at the same moment. That is the honest reading: the gate is green and the finding is real, and raising it here keeps the gap from being mistaken for coverage.

Fix: wrap the status bar in a landmark (footer, or role=status inside a footer) rather than a bare div, so screen-reader users can reach it by landmark. Low severity — nothing is unusable — but the region rule exists because the status text is otherwise unreachable by navigation.

Reproduce: export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/burpsy-ab-runtime; ./ui-live.sh; agent-browser ... (the commands are printed by ui-live.sh, and the unrestricted variant is axe.run(document, { resultTypes: ['violations'] }) without runOnly).
close_reason: The status bar is a footer landmark, live-verified. The fix is semantic: <div className=statusbar> -> <footer className=statusbar> in app.tsx — contentinfo implicit in the element, no role attribute needed, the CSS class unchanged so nothing visual moves. The JSX comment records the honest reading the bead itself stated: axe's 'region' is a best-practices rule NOT in the WCAG 2.0/2.1 A/AA tag set the a11y gate asserts on (the gate was green; the finding was real — the status text was unreachable by landmark navigation). LIVE-VERIFIED against a running console after a bundle rebuild: footer.statusbar present with its content (event stream, stored bytes, proxy bind, exchanges, messages, scope, CA state, last event), and the landmark persists across routes (#/history, #/repeater, #/settings). The page's landmark set now reads header.toolbar-row, nav.tool-tabs, nav.sub-tabs, main, footer.statusbar — the status bar reachable by landmark navigation exactly as the rule intends. Gates: tsc clean, bun test green, bundle rebuilt with the footer landmark, e2e-go.sh 24/24. Commit df5f557.

title: ui: only Proxy has a tool-tab attention source — Scanner and Dashboard have nothing to count
description:
## Claim

63bd378 landed the shell mechanism for tool-tab attention (lib/attention.ts, rendered in the tab strip) plus its first source: the Proxy's held-intercept count. Burp's contract is per-tool (spec 1.1: every tool module exposes a ToolTabFlasher), and the remaining tools have no source to feed it.

## Why they were not added

Not an oversight — there is nothing to count. A badge that says a tool needs the operator has to know what "needs the operator" means for that tool, and the obvious candidates have no such state in burpsy:

- Scanner / Issues: findings carry no read/unread state (core.Finding has no seen flag and nothing acknowledges one), so "new findings" cannot be told from "findings you have already read".
- Dashboard: it is an aggregation of other tools' data, so it needs a rule about which of those counts to mirror rather than one of its own.
- Intruder / Sequencer / Repeater: runs finish and their results sit on their own page; there is no unseen state either.

## What it needs

One decision first: what marks something as seen, and where that state lives (the store, so it survives a restart, rather than a component). Then each source is a pure addition to lib/attention.ts with its own test. Until then the tab strip is honest: it stays silent for tools where silence is the truth.
close_reason: Burp's contract is per-tool flasher; burpsy had only Proxy's held count. The bead asked for a decision first (what marks something seen, where that state lives) and the answer for these two is that NO seen-state is needed: the tools already answer the question. Scanner counts `skipped` on the live-audit state - the sweep saying it will not look at those exchanges again, which only an operator can resolve; `behind` (a backlog) and `retried` (taken back and audited) are the tool doing its job and counting them would make a usually-on badge. Dashboard counts runs that did not finish (failed, or running with no finished timestamp); a run with a finished timestamp is done whatever its state says, because the timestamp is the observable. The dashboard does NOT mirror another tool's queue - a held request belongs to Proxy and a skip to Scanner, and duplicating either would put one number on two tabs. Fetching is free: both sources are queries the shell already keeps warm for the Scanner summary and the dashboard task tiles; a badge that added its own poll would turn itself off under load. Verified: 16 tests, mutation-checked (backlog instead of skips / counting running runs / mirroring scanner skips all fail). The backlog mutant took two rounds to kill: first no fixture had both numbers, then the absent-`skipped` fallback to `behind` was uncovered - skipped is optional on the wire, so a server too old to report it would have substituted a number meaning something else; the fixture is now built field by field and the code says why it is ?? 0. tsc clean; bun test 687/0 in a worktree at HEAD with only these files. Commit 2cf5592. NOTE: uaq0 filed for an unrelated uncommitted store.ts WIP in the shared tree that breaks 7 repeater-tab-cap tests; not mine, not reverted.

title: ui: no 'Show details in new window' — items are only shown in the page's own detail pane, no pop-up/detached windows
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/context-menu.html — "Show details in new window — Opens detailed information about the selected item in a new window." tools/proxy/http-history/index.html — "Double-click an item to open it in a pop-up window" and "Show new history window".

## burpsy-side evidence
burpsy has no detachable/pop-up detail windows; a selected item is only ever shown in the page's own detail pane (e.g. pages/history.tsx SplitPane detail). There is no "open in new window" action on any tool.
close_reason:
Burp's "Show details in new window" plus double-click-to-pop-up, both delivered. The design decision worth recording: a ROUTE, not a generated window. The cheap implementation is a window.open on a text/html blob — a table of fields, no React — and it is a different product: the detail an operator detaches IS the message editor (request and response bytes, the Inspector, the same send-to-Repeater/Intruder/Comparer actions), which a blob cannot render, so the new window would show LESS than the pane it was opened from. A window opened at #history?exchange=7 mounts the real app, so every capability the pane has is here because it is the same code reading the same store.

The double-click is a separate onDoubleActivate rather than a reuse of onActivate, because onActivate is Enter-or-double-click and already means "send to Repeater" — rebinding it would take the keyboard chord away from an operator who has it, and a double-click meaning one thing on one page and another on the next is worse than a missing affordance.

A new NavLeaf.hidden says "routable but not listed", because listing the detail window in Proxy's sub-tab row would offer "go to another detached window", which is not navigation anyone wants; the test pins both halves, since the failure of either is invisible until an operator loses the window.

A blocked popup is reported rather than swallowed: window.open only counts as a user gesture inside the stack that started it, so the action is synchronous with no await, and a refusal navigates THIS tab to the same item and says the window did not open. The window also carries what a new one is easy to lose: the parameter/cookie/attribute tabs, the Inspector with a request-response switch, and a Close window button that closes the window.

Verified: 4 routing tests, mutation-checked (listing the leaf, removing it — both fail); tsc clean; bun test 710/0; bundle rebuilt. NOT live-verified: the window as rendered (browser host down). Commit 3f597eb.
