title: session: cannot validate only after a set number of requests (no validation interval)
description:
## Burp-side evidence
settings/sessions/session-handling-rules.html — Check session is valid: "Optionally, you can configure Burp to validate the session after a set number of requests. This helps you to avoid making unnecessary requests in cases where the application rarely invalidates your session."

## burpsy-side evidence
The session rule (pages/session.tsx, SessionRuleFull) has no "validate every N requests" throttle; validity is checked per the recovery flow with no interval control. There is no field for it in the rule editor.
close_reason: Burp's validate_every_num_requests, recovered as the same literal class that carries issue_current_request / match_indicates / stop_if_valid (burp.Zcfs in map_root.tsv), landed as a validate_every field on the check_validity action. Zero = every request (the pre-field behaviour, so every existing rule is unaffected); a negative interval is refused at configuration time rather than read as always/never, because 'validate never' is a rule that silently stopped protecting the session. The count is per RULE and advanced once per REQUEST, not per check: the tests caught the per-call version, where a rule's two checks disagreed about which request was due (on request 1 one skipped and the other ran). A skipped check walks the valid branch and records why - a rule that never checked cannot claim the session is alive, and taking the invalid branch would fire the recovery actions the interval exists to avoid. The counter is not persisted: it is a running cost decision, and restoring it would make a rule's behaviour depend on when the process last stopped; a restart is the safe direction. Editor: one field on the check-validity card, blank = every request, sent only once it parses to a positive integer so a half-typed '-' is never sent as 0. Verified: 6 Go tests, mutation-checked (removing the skip, per-call increment, and skipped-takes-invalid each fail them); go vet/gofmt/build clean; internal/session + internal/web green; tsc clean; bun test 676/0. NOT live-verified: the editor's rendered control (browser host down this session). Commit 9296c42.

title: intruder: attack settings absent — Set Connection: close header, denial-of-service mode, and store-full-payloads toggle are unavailable
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/intruder/configure-attack/settings.html — attack settings include "Set Connection header" (add/update Connection: close), "Use denial-of-service mode" (issue request then close the TCP connection without processing the response), and "Store full payloads" (retain full payload values to allow modifying grep or resending at runtime).

## burpsy-side evidence
internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx has only Grep match/extract on its Settings tab (intruder.tsx:1431-1485) and Max requests / concurrency / rps on the pool tab. None of Set Connection header, denial-of-service mode, or a store-full-payloads toggle exist in the UI or the /api/intruder/run body (intruder.tsx:759-807).
close_reason: Two of three landed, the third declined with the reason on screen (this bead's 2026-09-16 PARTIAL comment scoped it that way). The engine implemented both in 29a7ee3 with no way for a request to set either; this adds the wire (`set_connection_close` / `store_full_payloads` as *bool, so absent = 'not asked for' = the off-state body every existing client already posts), attaches them in handleIntruderRun, persists them in the saved-attack configuration, and adds the two checkboxes. Set Connection is byte-exact by span in the engine (an existing CONNECTION:   keep-alive becomes CONNECTION:   close, not a normalised header) and applied after the splice so insertion-point offsets do not move. Store full payloads adds one slice header plus a 16-byte string header per payload per row (~28KB at the default 500-row limit, two positions) - the payload SETS are materialised either way and the bytes are shared, not copied. Denial-of-service mode is NOT implemented and the Settings tab says so: Burp sends the request and deliberately does not read the response, which needs a fire-and-forget send AND every attempt-recording path (status, length, reflection, report buckets) to carry 'no response was read' instead of a zero - otherwise the report would count a request it never saw an answer to. A checkbox quietly reporting an empty response as a zero-length 0 is the exact lie this project treats as worse than the gap. Verified: 3 Go tests (a real target observes Connection: close; an attack that never mentions it does not get it; store_full_payloads is accepted not refused), mutation-checked including the absent-pointer-as-true inversion; 2 config-file tests pin the round trip and the off defaults. go test ./internal/web/ ./internal/intruder/ green, gofmt clean, tsc clean, bun test 706/0, bundle rebuilt. NOT live-verified: the checkboxes as rendered (browser host down). Commit e8aa241.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text: PARTIAL — 2 of 3, landed in 29a7ee3, NOT closing. Set-Connection-header and Store-full-payloads are implemented in the engine. Denial-of-service mode is explicitly NOT implemented and the commit says so rather than leaving it to be discovered. Set Connection is byte-exact by span (an existing 'CONNECTION:   keep-alive' has only its VALUE rewritten, becoming 'CONNECTION:   close', not a normalised 'Connection: close'), and a template whose header terminator is malformed is refused unchanged. Remaining: denial-of-service mode — Burp sends the request and deliberately does not read the response, so the honest implementation must also ensure the report never counts an unread response as received. Not started; reopen scope is that one setting.

title: history: Time is one total duration — no start/end response-timer (TTFB vs complete) split
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/proxy/http-history/index.html — two distinct timing columns: "Start response timer - the time in ms from when the request was sent until the first byte of the response is received" and "End response timer - the time ... until the complete response was received."

## burpsy-side evidence
pages/history.tsx:737-742 renders a single "Time" column from duration_ms; Exchange (lib/types.ts) has only duration_ms. There is no time-to-first-byte vs time-to-complete distinction, so a slow-body response reads the same as a slow-to-respond one.
close_reason: Fixed in ce11b60. The bead's honest first question — is the first byte measured at all? — was no, so it is now MEASURED rather than synthesised: ReadResponseHeadTimed takes the instant inside the read at the wire, and the untimed ReadResponseHead became a wrapper over the same parser so the two cannot drift. TTFB is a core.ExchangeDuration, so (Measured, Us) keeps 'nobody timed this' separable from 'this was instant'; only producers that own the response read populate it (the HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 relays), while Repeater, Intruder, the crawler and pre-existing rows leave it Unmeasured. The wire carries ttfb_ms as a POINTER — null, never 0 — because 0 would claim an instantaneous first byte for every exchange nobody timed; the column renders an em dash. The proxy's parity guard forced this to be a DECISION rather than an omission: core.Exchange's field rules refused to pass until TTFB was classified, and it is ruleMayDiffer with the reasoning recorded (the crawler fetches through a client that hands back a finished response and genuinely cannot state a first-byte instant; forcing ruleIdentical would make one producer lie). Verified live through the proxy against two origins built to defeat the old single column, both ~1s total: /slow-head ttfb_ms=1002 duration_ms=1002 (origin took ~1s to START answering) vs /slow-body ttfb_ms=2 duration_ms=1003 (answered at once, BODY took ~1s). One total cannot tell those apart; the pair does. Unit test asserts the MARSHALLED JSON, because that is where the distinction lives (nil *uint64 -> null vs uint64 -> 0). gofmt/build/vet clean; go test across core/httputil/scanner/proxy/web green; tsc + bun test clean.

title: decoder: transforms apply to the whole input only — no per-selection transform and no colour-coding of the applied encoding
description:
## Burp-side evidence
tools/decoder.html: "The transformation applies to the whole data set. To apply the transformation to only a portion of the data, select the relevant section before you choose an operation." and "The data is color-coded to indicate the type of encoding or decoding that is applied."

## burpsy-side evidence
burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/decoder.tsx:646-659 the pipeline mutates `{ input, steps }` — the entire input string is transformed by each step; there is no way to select a substring and transform only that portion. Output is rendered as plain text/hex (decoder.tsx:600 `<div className="prose tool-output">`) with no per-byte colour-coding of which encoding was applied; only a "detected" layer-chain badge row (decoder.tsx:566-574) is shown.
close_reason: Fixed in 6e59efa. Burp's Decoder applies a transform to a SELECTED span and colour-codes the output by the encoding applied; burpsy transformed the whole input only and rendered flat text. A selection now feeds only that span through the pipeline with the surrounding text held aside and rendered unchanged around each step's output; with nothing selected the whole input is transformed exactly as before, so the new behaviour is opt-in by selecting — Burp's rule too. The selection is read at run time with EditorView.findFromDOM because src/ui/editor.tsx is owned by another slice and exposes no onSelectionChange; that read is the seam that becomes the prop when editor.tsx's owner adds one, and it is noted at the call site rather than left to be rediscovered. editor.tsx was NOT edited. The colour is tied to the transform that actually ran, not decoration. VERIFIED LIVE in a real browser: the page states the contract ('Select a span in the input to transform only that part; with nothing selected the whole input is transformed'); whole-input path hello world -> hello%20world (Encode · url, 13 B); the colour is real styling, not an empty class — .enc-span computed background color(srgb 0 0.568627 1 / 0.04), border-bottom rgb(0,145,255) 2px against body rgb(187,187,187). STATED LIMIT, not glossed: the per-SELECTION path itself was NOT driven live. A selection set programmatically never reaches CodeMirror's state — it painted zero .cm-selectionBackground nodes and the DOM range collapsed — so an automated background tab can only exercise the no-selection branch, which it did correctly. The span logic is covered by 13 unit tests across decoder-span.ts and decoder-colours.ts instead, and the owed foreground-browser check is filed as its own issue. tsc clean; bun test 572 pass.

title: repeater: tab strip has no scrolling/wrapped view toggle, no drag-reorder, and individual (ungrouped) tabs cannot be colored
description:
Three small tab-strip affordances Burp's Repeater has and burpsy's does not. Grouped here because
each alone is cosmetic; together they are the difference between a strip that scales to the dozens
of tabs a real engagement accumulates and one that does not.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/repeater/managing-tabs.html`:

> **Switch tab view** - Use the tab view toggle in the top-right corner to choose from two different
> views: **Scrolling view** - a single, scrollable row ... [or a] drop-down list of open tabs ...
> **Wrapped view** - wrap tabs onto multiple rows.

`groups.html`: "Select a group color. The group's tabs are highlighted with this color on the tab
bar." Burp also lets tabs be dragged to reorder and dragged between groups.

## burpsy-side evidence (`internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx`)

1. **No scrolling/wrapped view toggle.** `ungrouped.map(renderTabTrigger)` renders one flat
   `tabs-list` row; with many tabs it overflows with no scroll affordance and no overflow dropdown.
2. **No drag to reorder / drag into a group.** Order is fixed to `state.repeaterTabs`; moving a tab
   into a group is menu-only (`setRepeaterTabGroup`). There is no `draggable`/`onDrag*` anywhere in
   the page or a `moveRepeaterTab` reorder action in `store.ts`.
3. **Individual tabs cannot be colored.** Color lives on the *group* (`group.color`, the colored
   border); an ungrouped tab has no color. Burp colors per group too, but exposes it as a tab-bar
   highlight; a single ungrouped tab still cannot be marked.

## Not in scope of this issue

Per-tab *settings* (Burp's blue settings icon + "Restore global default") are already at parity:
the Config trigger shows an override count `Config (N)` and offers "Reset overrides"
(`SendOptionsPanel`). Rename (double-click) and duplicate are also present.
close_reason: Three tab-strip affordances. (1) Scrolling/wrapped toggle: Burp's scrolling view is one scrollable row plus a dropdown of open tabs, so forty tabs cost one row of height and two clicks to reach the thirty-ninth; scrolling is the default for the same reason Burp defaults to it (a wrapped strip eats height on a page whose editor needs it) and wrapping is one button away. (2) Drag to reorder, with two decisions in lib/repeater-tabs.ts because they are the ones an operator cannot debug by looking: the target index is computed AFTER the removal, so 'drag the first of three to the end' does not land one short (clamping against the ORIGINAL length is exactly that off-by-one), and a drop landing on a row in another group is REFUSED rather than reinterpreted - crossing a boundary means 'move it into that group', a different gesture, and a drag that silently re-files a request under a gesture aimed at position is the worst kind of accident. (3) Per-tab colour, which is the gap the bead names: Burp colours a GROUP, so an ungrouped tab had no way to be marked at all and an operator pointing at the one request to attack next could not colour a whole group to say so. A tab's own colour wins over its group's, and the palette is the SAME one row highlights use so 'red' cannot mean two colours. Every rule is a pure function over a tab list, which is the only reason an off-by-one in a reorder is catchable without a browser. Verified: 16 tests, mutation-checked (clamp against original length, ignore group boundary, group colour wins, drop ungrouped from dropdown - all fail). tsc clean; bun test 703/0 in a worktree at HEAD with only this feature's files. NOT live-verified: drag/toggle/colour as rendered (browser host down). NOTE store.ts also carries an unrelated UNCOMMITTED openRepeaterTab change already in the shared tree (broken per uaq0), landed not reverted. Commit c1ef251.

title: ui: no 'Save items' — selected exchanges cannot be exported as request/response pairs, only the request alone
description:
## Claim
"Copy request to file" saves the request only. Burp's "Save items" saves the selected request/response pairs together in a structured format, which is what an operator hands to a colleague or attaches to a report.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Save items** — *"Saves the selected items in the specified format"*. Listed separately from **Copy to file** — *"Enables you to select a file and copy the contents of the current message to that file"* — so Burp has both, and they are different actions.

## burpsy-side evidence
- burpsy has the Copy-to-file half only: `lib/actions.ts:808` `{ id: "to-file", label: "Copy request to file", ... }` -> `lib/actions.ts:685-698` `copyRequestToFile`, which fetches `exchange.request` alone (`fetchRaw(exchange.request)`, `:687`) and downloads it as `.txt`. The response is never included.
- Absence grep: `grep -rli 'Save item' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- Report export exists but is a different object: `app.tsx:437-443` exports findings reports (HTML/JSON/SARIF), not selected exchanges.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency.

## What an operator cannot do
Export one or more selected exchanges, request and response together, as a single artefact. Today: download the request, then separately copy the response bytes out of the editor.
acceptance_criteria: The row menu offers saving the selected exchange(s) with both request and response in one file in a documented format.
close_reason: Implemented in a1c8ada. 'Save request and response' in the shared copy group: one labelled file (REQUEST + RESPONSE sections), missing response saves labelled rather than refusing. Verified live by intercepting the download blob: 678 bytes with real request/response bytes under their markers, confirming toast.

title: ui: no 'Add to site map' action — the site map is populated only by observed traffic
description:
## Claim
There is no "Add to site map" action. Burp lets you push a selected item onto the site map; in burpsy the site map is populated only by observed proxy traffic and crawls.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Add to site map** — *"Adds the selected items to the project scope"* [sic — the table's description column; the option name and its effect are the site map].

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Add to site map' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The shared row menu's organise and scope groups (`lib/actions.ts:811-827`) offer Add to Organizer, Filter history by host, Open URL in browser, Add host to scope, Audit exchange, and two crawl scopes — no site-map insert.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency.

## What an operator cannot do
Put a URL they know about onto the site map without sending traffic to it. Note this interacts with the documented append-only store property (`lib/reference.ts:349-351`: *"the site map adds and never removes. A host on the map was observed at some point — that is not evidence it is reachable now."*) — an operator-inserted node would break that invariant's current meaning.

## Decision needed
Whether an operator-added node is acceptable at all given the disclosure above. If yes, it needs to be distinguishable from an observed node on the map, or the disclosure needs rewording. Worth answering before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on whether operator-inserted site-map nodes are allowed; if allowed, the row menu offers 'Add to site map' and inserted nodes are visually distinguishable from observed ones.
close_reason: Decision recorded on the bead (allowed, kept SEPARATE from the observed tree and marked), because the map's disclosed property is 'a host on the map was observed at some point' and an operator-added node makes that false if folded in; refusing would leave the gap. internal/sitemap gains an `inserted` map BESIDE `hosts` - mechanically necessary as well as honest, because Sync rebuilds the observed tree wholesale from the traffic store and would erase anything written into it (pinned: insert, Sync with an empty store, node still there, observed tree still empty). The API says which of two things happened: already_seen + reason for a path that was observed, a recorded insert otherwise; a repeated insert keeps the first timestamp; a host with no port is refused (app.test:0 is not an authority). The tree keeps its shape - missing ancestors are synthesised and marked inserted too; a first version grafted through a returned slice and reported child_count 3 while rendering no children, so the graft is through a pointer and parent counts are recomputed from what was actually grafted. Visible: dashed underline plus an 'added by you' marker with a title saying no traffic was observed there, because its counts are all zero precisely because nothing was requested and a zero that reads as a clean observation is the lie the separation prevents. Verified: 5 sitemap + 3 API tests, mutation-checked across both halves (Sync erasing inserts, insert-of-observed recording anyway, port guard dropped, already_seen hardcoded false, node never marked inserted - all fail). go vet/gofmt/build clean; internal/sitemap + internal/web green incl. route-manifest and verb guards; tsc clean; bun test 676/0. NOT live-verified: the row-menu action and the rendered marker (browser host down). Commit 5733282.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text: DECISION 2026-09-24 (Main): allowed, kept SEPARATE from the observed tree and labelled. The alternative — refusing — leaves the operator unable to record a URL they know about, which is the whole capability; and folding inserts into the observed tree would make reference.ts's disclosure ("a host on the map was observed at some point") false, which is the defect this project treats as worse. So an inserted node lives in its own store, survives Sync's rebuild (which only walks exchanges), and is drawn with its own marker and an 'added by you' label: the map then answers two questions truthfully — what was observed, and what you recorded. A node that is both observed and inserted shows the observation (the stronger fact) and says so.

title: ui: no 'Copy links' action to extract URLs from a selected response
description:
## Claim
There is no "Copy links" action. Burp parses the selected items for links and copies them, which is the standard way to harvest URLs out of a response for a wordlist or a crawl seed set.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Copy links** — *"Parses the selected items for links and copies them to the clipboard"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Copy links' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The copy group in the shared row menu is `lib/actions.ts:802-810`: Copy URL, Copy as curl, Copy exchange id, Copy request to file. No links extraction.
- burpsy does parse links elsewhere — the crawler has a frontier — so the capability exists server-side but is not offered as a clipboard action on a response.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP, low frequency but cheap.

## What an operator cannot do
Pull every link out of a captured response in one action, to feed a content-discovery run or a manual review list.
acceptance_criteria: The row and editor menus offer 'Copy links', which extracts the links from the selected response body and copies them one per line.
close_reason: Implemented in 0415420. 'Copy links' in the shared row-menu copy group (all tools). extractLinks harvests quoted attrs + bare absolute URLs + CSS url(), deduped, order-preserving, as-found; javascript:/mailto:/data:/fragments/trailing punctuation excluded (5 unit tests). Verified live: real page harvest toasted 'Copied 3 links from #0'.

title: docs: the command-palette note says Burp has no default binding — Burp's own docs say Ctrl+K, which burpsy already matches
description:
## Claim
Two documents state that Burp's command palette has no default hotkey, or that it is Ctrl+Shift+P. Burp's own shipped documentation says the default is Ctrl+K — which is exactly what burpsy binds, so a correct parity claim is being recorded as a divergence.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/command-palette.html` (Burp 2026.7.1 bundled docs, `/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/`):
> *"**If** you have already assigned the `Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K` hotkey to another command, the command palette isn't assigned a default hotkey. Set one manually in **Settings > User interface > Hotkeys**."*

Ctrl+K is the default; the no-default case is the conditional fallback when the operator has already taken that chord.

## burpsy-side evidence (the two wrong statements)
1. `lib/shortcuts.ts:82` — `{ id: "nav.palette", ..., defaultChord: "mod+k", ..., note: "Burp ships its palette with no default binding at all" }`. The binding is right; the note is wrong, and it is rendered to operators beside the row (`app.tsx:58`, `pages/settings.tsx:1266`).
2. `/root/burp-re/BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` section 3.2 and section 5.2 both give the palette trigger as `Ctrl + Shift + P` / `Cmd + Shift + P`. The spec is wrong here and the bundled docs supersede it.

## Classification
Documentation defect. No code change to the binding — `mod+k` is exact parity.

## What an operator cannot do
Nothing is broken; the cost is that a reader of the shortcut table is told burpsy invented a binding Burp does not have, when in fact it matches. The spec being wrong also matters for anyone else auditing against section 5.2.
acceptance_criteria: lib/shortcuts.ts's nav.palette note records that mod+K matches Burp's documented default, and the spec's Ctrl+Shift+P claim in sections 3.2 and 5.2 is corrected or annotated as superseded by tools/command-palette.html.
close_reason: Fixed in b012797: the nav.palette note in shortcuts.ts:82 claimed 'Burp ships its palette with no default binding at all' — false; Burp's documented default is Ctrl+K, which burpsy already binds (defaultChord: mod+k, unchanged). The note now reads 'Burp's documented default is also Ctrl+K, so this matches Burp exactly'. One-line change; bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect.

title: Sharded CI flakes: x5u/jku listener port race; cold Chrome start per shard
description: Since #350 split the gate into shards, master (f2eadd3e) and #351 went red on three different tests. (1) scanner jwtHostedCheck closed its jku/x5u listener after forging and re-listened on the same port; another listener in the process could take the port in between, the re-listen failed and the row reported nothing (master scanner-rest: 'JWT arbitrary x5u header supported did not fire against its vulnerable twin'). title: domexec: chromedp's 20s DevTools-URL timeout overrides the browser start bound
description: domexec.NewBrowser bounds startup with Options.Timeout (default 30s) but never passes it to chromedp's ExecAllocator, whose WSURLReadTimeout defaults to 20s and fires first. A Chrome that takes 20-30s to print its DevTools URL (a loaded CI runner, under -race) fails with 'websocket url timeout reached' inside the intended bound, and any caller setting Timeout above 20s is silently capped at 20s. Seen on PR #351 race-web-0: TestARecordedTOTPLoginReplaysAndAuthenticatesACrawlThroughTheRoutes failed at 20.07s. Fix: chromedp.WSURLReadTimeout(timeout) in the exec allocator options.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #353 (db8900423944): ci: fix the flakes sharding exposed (x5u/jku port race, cold Chrome per shard)

title: Connection pool liveness probe misses a closed peer under load
description: sender.alive() sets a 1ms read deadline then peeks. Go's poller refuses a read whose deadline has already passed without calling the socket, so when the goroutine is descheduled >1ms between SetReadDeadline and Peek (any loaded machine, e.g. an Intruder attack) the probe reports a timeout - the 'healthy' answer - for a socket whose FIN already arrived. A POST is then sent on the dead connection and fails with EOF (not retried, being non-idempotent). Seen as TestAnIdleConnectionTheServerClosedIsNotUsed failing in a round-4 T2 run; reproduced 1/300 with CPUs saturated. Fix: non-blocking MSG_PEEK on the socket first (unix), deadline probe as fallback; deterministic regression test with a conn whose deadlines are always past.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #351 (39aace49e429): Round 4: WS attach/clone, API definition fetch, call-bound confirmations, NTLM over the sender, pool probe fix

title: Cap CPU and RAM per local heavy test run (scripts/capped-run.sh)
description: User decision 2026-10-09: local heavy runs (whole-package go test, race, Chrome drives) run under a hard CPU and memory budget so concurrent agents on one machine cannot starve each other. scripts/capped-run.sh: own cgroup (v1/v2) with memory limit and CPU quota (default half the machine each), GOMAXPROCS / go -p / GOMEMLIMIT matched, N slots (/tmp/burpsy-heavy.<n>.lock) replacing the single heavy lock, clear message when the memory cap killed the run, graceful fallback without cgroups. Docs: DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #352 (a6a5bd34fb83): process: cap CPU and RAM per heavy local test run (scripts/capped-run.sh)

title: CI scripts: list_tests swallows build failures; Buildkite curl|bash without pipefail

(1) scripts/ci-shard.sh list_tests: errexit is off inside command substitution, so a package that fails to build (e.g. disk full) yields an empty list and require_test reports 'no longer exists' / race shards 'selected no tests' - misleading. Fix: out=$(go test -list ...) || return 1 and names=$(list_tests ...) || exit 1 at call sites (or shopt -s inherit_errexit); correct the 'Fails if listing fails' comment. (2) .buildkite/Dockerfile: curl https://bun.sh/install | bash runs under /bin/sh without pipefail; a failed download leaves a dangling bun symlink. Fix: SHELL ["/bin/bash","-o","pipefail","-c"].

title: Decode Brotli and zstd response bodies with the already-linked decoders
description: httputil.DecodeBody handles gzip/deflate only; its comment says br/zstd "mean adding a dependency", and gaps.md (of0z) lists "no Brotli decoder in this build". andybalholm/brotli and klauspost/compress/zstd are already compiled in (via gitleaks). Make them direct deps and decode br/zstd everywhere bodies are decoded (proxy history, Repeater, scanner). Add size bounds like the existing decoders. Doc §1.
close_reason: Brotli and zstd response decoding shipped. httputil.DecodeBody gains br (andybalholm/brotli) and zstd (klauspost/compress) cases; both promoted to direct deps. Unpackable and the proxy unpack path include them; errors are wrapped with the encoding name ("br:", "zstd:"); the MaxDecodedBody cap applies to the decoded output. Red-then-green: fixed known-answer vectors, corrupt-input and bomb tests in internal/httputil; positive proxy rule-reach tests for br and zstd mirroring the gzip pin (options_unpack_test.go); repeater gains TestUnpackDecodesBrotli and TestUnpackNamesAnEncodingItCannotDecode now pins the chain shape ("gzip, br") as the one still-undecodable form. Honesty sweep: "cannot decode" copy updated in options.go, api_scanner_coverage.go, api_types.go, readable.go, gaps.md, proxysettings.tsx, scannerlaunch.tsx, data.proxyoptions.ts. Suites: internal/httputil, internal/proxy, internal/web (minus environmental TestDiscovery*, needs ffuf), and the scanner short suite all green; go build ./... clean.

title: Decode Huffman-coded HPACK strings with x/net/http2/hpack
description: internal/http2/hpack.go returns HpackHuffmanNotImplemented (lines 25, 211, 369), so most real HTTP/2 header blocks cannot be shown in the raw H2 view (gaps.md 54-60). golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.HuffmanDecode is already linked (sender/h2fields.go uses that package). Keep the hand-written raw layer for malformed-frame work; use the library only for Huffman decoding. Doc §1.
close_reason: Done: the Huffman seam is closed. decodeHpackString decodes H=1 string literals through golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.HuffmanDecodeToString (already linked via sender/h2fields.go); the hand-written layer keeps every bounds/framing check, and malformed Huffman is refused by name as the new HpackHuffmanInvalid (same enum slot as the old HpackHuffmanNotImplemented, so ordinals hold). Tests: RFC 7541 C.4.1 and C.6.1 vectors decode (www.example.com, no-cache), malformed 0x00 0x00 refused at the string's length-octet offset, and the bounds-before-Huffman ordering pin kept. Deliberate divergence from the Rust port, which keeps its seam - documented in the module docs and gaps.md. internal/http2 + internal/sender suites green, go build ./... green.

title: TLS leaf cert cache is unbounded and key generation is serialised behind one lock
description: proxy.TlsEngine caches per-host leaves in an unbounded sync.Map certPool and generates the RSA key inside a single e.mu.Lock, so first visits to different hosts wait on each other. Use hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 (already linked) with a size bound, and per-host singleflight (golang.org/x/sync/singleflight) for generation. Consider ECDSA P-256 leaves (much faster) where clients accept them. Doc §1.
close_reason: TLS leaf caches bounded and minting parallelised. certPool and the self-signed pool are now hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 LRU caches capped at leafCacheBound=4096 (eviction costs only a re-mint); both promoted from sync.Map. CA-signed minting moved behind per-host golang.org/x/sync/singleflight under e.mu.RLock: first visits to different hosts mint in parallel instead of queueing behind one Lock around RSA keygen, while concurrent misses for one host still share a single mint. ImportCA/RegenerateCA swaps take the write Lock, which waits for in-flight mints, and the cache purge (now Purge under poolMu) cannot race a mint add because adds happen inside the RLock. Self-signed minting keeps its separate cache (4trc) and no longer touches e.mu at all. Red-then-green: TestTheLeafCacheIsBounded and TestTheSelfSignedCacheIsBounded pin the LRU bound and eviction order (bound shrunk to 16 in-test; the old sync.Map stored all 24), TestConcurrentMissesForOneHostMintOneLeaf pins the single-mint identity; ca_import_test.go cache assertions updated via a cachedLeafCount helper. Verified: full internal/proxy suite green, -race green (24.8s), scanner short suite green (338s), go build ./... clean. ECDSA P-256 leaves not adopted: RSA-2048 leaves remain for maximal client compatibility; noted as a possible follow-up.

title: Replace hand-rolled evicting stores with golang-lru/v2
description: evictLocked-style bounded stores exist in sender/h2sessions.go, dash/tasks.go, dash/events.go, scanner/audit_items.go, servercerts and the netauth/prompt LRU. hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 is already linked. Consolidate where the semantics match. Doc §1.
close_reason: MERGED via integrator (0920436d+c1a23b7e): W3 servercerts/netauth seen-caches moved to golang-lru/v2 bounded caches, hand-rolled eviction dropped. CORRECTED contract: eviction identity is bounded by lock ordering, not by distinct LastSeen timestamps. Gate: CI run 40221203392 green at exact SHA 0920436dd5ff19cfeb286c2fbbbaa2b340610897 (all jobs): https://github.com/Chaim12345/burpsy/actions/runs/40221203392. title: SQL injection: close the detection gaps against sqlmap-class coverage

The owner approved going beyond Burp-recovered payloads. sqlmap is GPLv2 and its licence treats reading its data files (and arguably parsing its output) as creating a derived work, so burpsy writes its own payloads/signatures and runs sqlmap only as an external tool. See docs/DETECTION-GAPS-2026-10-10.md. UPDATE 2026-10-10: licence decided — burpsy is GPL-3.0-or-later; reusing sqlmap's GPL-2+ payload/boundary/error data and parsing its output is allowed (keep notices).

title: SQLi: time-delay probes for MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle, SQLite, DB2 with statistical confirmation
description: Only PostgreSQL (pg_sleep) and SQL Server (WAITFOR DELAY) are sent today. Add burpsy-authored probes: MySQL SLEEP()/BENCHMARK() (and IF(cond,SLEEP(n),0) inside quoted/numeric contexts), Oracle DBMS_PIPE.RECEIVE_MESSAGE and a heavy-query fallback when DBMS_PIPE is not granted, SQLite heavy randomblob/hex queries, DB2 heavy queries. Confirm with at least three delays (e.g. 0, d, 2d) and require the response time to track the requested delay linearly, plus a repeat, to resist network jitter. Respect the existing method gates (Time delays + dialect). Lift the "Burp-recovered only" note in sqli_techniques.go for these dialects. Negative control: a target that sleeps on every request must not be reported.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (47e5ff59ad91): time-based blind SQLi for MySQL, Oracle, SQLite, DB2, H2, HSQLDB with two delay values, ratio tracking, repeat, zero-delay and foreign-dialect controls; constant-pace twin stays clean. MySQL/Oracle/DB2 exercised only against simulations.

title: SQLi: expand DBMS error signatures and report the identified DBMS

Write burpsy's own regex bank (not sqlmap's GPL errors.xml) covering MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle (ORA-xxxxx), SQLite, DB2 (SQLSTATE/SQLCODE), Sybase, Informix, H2, HSQLDB, Derby, ClickHouse, CockroachDB, Snowflake, plus driver/ORM errors: PDO, JDBC, ODBC, Hibernate/HQL, Sequelize, ActiveRecord, Django, SQLAlchemy, EF Core. Each signature names its DBMS, and the finding reports the DBMS so time/OOB probes can be narrowed. Keep the existing baseline-differs rule (an error in the baseline is not evidence). UPDATE 2026-10-10: burpsy is now GPL-3.0-or-later, so sqlmap's xml/errors.xml (GPL-2+) may be imported directly as the base of the bank (keep its notice, record the sqlmap version), extended with burpsy's own driver/ORM signatures.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (f2b59667f312): sqlmap's errors.xml (187 regexes, 31 engines) embedded as a second bank naming the DBMS, with shell/script-engine attribution. Burpsy's own ORM/driver signatures (Hibernate, Sequelize, SQLAlchemy, EF Core, ActiveRecord, Django) remain: v0ei.9.

title: SQLi: out-of-band (DNS/HTTP) detection through the OOB channel

TO PROGRAM / dblink. A DNS interaction tied to the probe's canary is a certain finding even when the response shows nothing. Gate under the OOB/Collaborator setting.

title: SQLi: robust boolean-based detection (similarity ratio, more condition shapes and contexts)

Require true==original and false!=original, repeated, before reporting.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (f2b59667f312): boolean SQLi with learned dynamic regions, reflection subtraction, similarity ratio, fresh-operand second pair, LIKE and nested-paren shapes, opt-in OR shapes. ORDER BY/CASE WHEN, IN() and arithmetic condition shapes remain: v0ei.11.

title: Race conditions as an opt-in scan check (single-packet attack)

Opt-in, capped check: send N identical requests to limit-overrun candidates (coupon, OTP, transfer) in one packet; report divergent success counts. State-changing, so off by default. Source: portswigger.net/research/smashing-the-state-machine.
close_reason: Done across W3 (sender side) + W1 design: AuthorisedSender.SendSynchronizedGroup with all-or-nothing scope pre-flight, atomic PaceN on intruder.RateLimiter (MaxGroupPace=64, refuses with 'cannot admit'), pool.ContextPacer.PaceN, sender.GroupPacer optional interface (per-send-only declines, never staggers), SendFailurePacing distinct kind, Sent per dispatched member, barrier mirrors api_repeater_group.go; latent sync_send.go barrier deadlock fixed. N=4 race win vs check-then-set endpoint proven. Scanner-side check lands with W1's 0vzb.8 follow-through. Merged, sender/intruder/pool green.

title: Reference-tool parity: validate each scanner class against its industry-standard tool
description: For every vulnerability class, name an industry-standard reference tool (sqlmap for SQLi, etc.) and use it as the comparison and validation oracle for burpsy's detection: same targets, same endpoints, compare what each finds (misses = burpsy gaps to file; burpsy-only hits = verify or false positive). Children: the shared harness (.1) and one bead per class. Reference tools run as external processes (licences: GPL tools fine now that burpsy is GPL-3.0-or-later). Verify each tool is still maintained when its bead starts. See docs/REFERENCE-PARITY-2026-10-10.md.

title: Parity harness: run burpsy and a reference tool on the same targets and diff the findings
description: One harness all class beads use. Targets: burpsy's own vulnapp (internal/vulnapp, already declares what each endpoint is vulnerable to) plus containerised public suites — OWASP Benchmark (21k labelled cases, half true / half false), WAVSEP (reinforced), DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, and per-class labs where noted. For each class: run the reference tool with a pinned version and fixed options, normalise its findings to (endpoint, parameter, class, technique), run burpsy's scan with the same scope, and report per class: both found, reference-only (burpsy miss -> file a bead), burpsy-only (verify: true positive or false positive), plus precision/recall against the suite's ground truth. Output JSON + a markdown table; run nightly (not per PR) under scripts/capped-run.sh; store results so trends are visible. Reference tools pinned and hash-checked like ci-install-tools.sh.

close_reason: MERGED via integrator (847cb58e). Param-mining parity class (Arjun 2.2.7 publisher-checksum pin, x8 self-measured pin) registered with exit-code hardening (exit_code.txt written, nonzero+empty raises; raise path independently exercised by pre-reviewer via mock). Python suites reproduced: 39 tests RUN 3 PASS 3. CAVEATS recorded: (a) numbers (burpsy 4/4, Arjun 2/4, x8 0) are worker-run evidence pending clean re-run + CI nightly - no raw artifacts committed; (b) x8 pin hash is SELF-MEASURED - the release publishes no checksums, so equality-to-recorded-bytes is enforced but the initial binary is unauthenticated, weaker provenance than crlfuzz's publisher checksum; (c) collector accepts unstable/budget/stopped states as reports without saving the terminal reason - not auditable from burpsy.json alone. Silent-failure loopholes (stdout banner, stale JSON, stamp-path bypass, cosmetic wrong-dir message) appended to pbharden.

Python suites reproduced by pre-reviewer and integrator: 37 tests RUN 3 PASS 3. CAVEAT recorded: parity numbers (burpsy 3/3 CORS vs Corsy 2/3, 3/3 CRLF vs crlfuzz path-only) are worker-run evidence, not integrator-verified - durable verification is the CI nightly parity job. Hardening follow-up filed as pbharden (live-collector binding, loud reference/config failure, URL/method binding, pinned pip deps). crlfp stays open pending CI nightly reproduction of the corrected numbers.

title: OS command / code-injection checks fire on non-matching endpoints (30 FPs on VulnerableApp)
description: Full-profile VulnerableApp run: 'OS command injection' raised on 35 cases, only 5 are command injection; the rest are file upload (8), persistent XSS (6), XXE (7, 4 SECURE), LDAP, cache poisoning, error SQLi. Python/Perl/PHP/Ruby code injection (12 each) and SSTI (7) also fire on unrelated endpoints. Find which confirmation (timing? reflection?) passes on these and tighten it. Raw data: va-raw.jsonl from the run (see docs/VULNERABLEAPP-BASELINE-2026-10-10.md).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (abf79f815c43): computed, twice-confirmed proofs for OS command, code and template injection; VulnerableApp off-target OS command 31 -> 0, code/SSTI/EL rows to 0.

title: Active-scan sender ignores network tls.verify=false
description: PUT /api/network/settings {tls:{verify:false}} turns verification off on the proxy leg only; the active scanner's sender keeps verifying, so targets with self-signed/expired certs (OWASP Benchmark v1.2 on :8443, cert expired 2015) cannot be audited. Fix: one TLS setting consulted by proxy and scanner sender. Acceptance: audit of an https exchange to an expired-cert lab target runs when verify=false and refuses when true.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (3f23fbe2dfff), PR #362 (0cce9f781a21): tls.verify reaches the sender's raw and typed dial paths; a saved document without tls keeps verification on. Test pins both directions on a self-signed target.

title: Query/form payload encoder sends raw " < > so Tomcat 400s every XSS probe
description: percentEscapeOpts (internal/bcheck/insertion.go) escapes only & = + ; # %, controls and high bytes. Payloads with " < > go raw in the query string; Tomcat 8.5 and Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat reject them with 400 before the app runs. Repro: GET /VulnerableApp/XSSWithHtmlTagInjection/LEVEL_1?value="><svg/onload=1> -> 400; percent-encoded -> 200 and reflected. Result: reflected/persistent XSS 0/14 on VulnerableApp. Burp encodes these. Fix: escape request-line-illegal bytes (RFC 3986 non-query chars) in default mode; keep Raw semantics for decoding variants. Acceptance: VulnerableApp XSS cases detected; test asserting the wire bytes.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (c465f213144c), PR #362 (2bb26aa6d298): request-line-illegal bytes escaped in the default policy (Raw stays byte-exact), wire bytes pinned by tests. VulnerableApp XSS stayed 0/14 because those endpoints are DOM-only (text/plain + innerHTML); that harness work is j1mk.38.

title: Benchmark-in-CI: VulnerableApp parity run as a nightly scored job
description: Turn the scratch harness (seed through proxy, POST /api/audit/{id}, score by exchange+CWE, strict filter for blanket issue types) into scripts/bench/ in the repo, run VulnerableApp nightly, keep the per-type table as a tracked baseline and fail on regressions. Covers j1mk.1 for VulnerableApp; OWASP Benchmark v1.2 joins once the scanner TLS bug is fixed.

title: Default scanner config leaves cmd/LDAP/XPath/path/XXE/redirect checks off
description: Default server config dispatches 58 checks; CheckActiveInjection, CheckExtendedActive and CheckReflectionProbes default false, so OS command, LDAP, XPath, file path, XXE and open-redirect checks never run. VulnerableApp: default 4.8% vs full 12.9% (strict). Decide whether these belong on by default (Burp's default audit runs them) or the UI must make the choice obvious.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #362 (ce50631bed84): default audit runs the non-destructive active families (CheckActiveInjection, CheckXXE, CheckReflectionProbes on), pinned by TestDefaultAuditPolicy.

title: Error-based SQLi misses VulnerableApp levels 3-4; open redirect misses levels 6-7
description: Full profile: ErrorBasedSQLi 2/4 (L3, L4 missed), Http3xx open redirect 7/9 (L6, L7 missed). Investigate the filters those levels apply and add the bypass variants. Compare with sqlmap (j1mk.2) and OpenRedireX (j1mk.16).
close_reason: MERGED via integrator (3f6971d2). _NoRedirect replaces the default redirect handler for all redirect codes (verified in code); all 3 callers use side-effect capture only; regression test binds pre/post (base RemoteDisconnected, tip passes); WHATWG parser probes (at-sign, backslash, encoded slash, dotdot) all keep the app origin; VulnerableApp 2.1.0 source confirms the fixed-authority-then-slash structure. CONSERVATIVE FINDING WORDING (adopted verbatim): no cross-origin redirect demonstrated under WHATWG parsing; the app-provided backslash payload remains a same-origin path in the tested parser - no legacy-IE semantics asserted (unverified). Live scores are worker-run evidence with reports delivered: SQLi strict TP4/FN0 (100%), open-redirect strict TP8/FN1/TN1/FP0 (80%). Parity-harness semantic change noted: seeds now capture the initial exchange only (no caller depends otherwise). OPEN: the 'L7' reference does not resolve anywhere in-repo (grep-clean) - W9 to point me at the ledger line it names; the disposition itself (verified-not-exploitable under the tested parser) is ruled.

VulnerableApp PathTraversal levels 1-12 (filter bypasses: encoded, double-encoded, ..;/, null-byte, prefix-required) all missed. Compare with dotdotpwn (j1mk.10). Acceptance: >= 8/12 levels, SECURE level stays clean.

title: DOM engine attached (-dom) breaks POST login/OTP audits: 2 checks send-failed, ~50 units abandoned

description: Phase 2 of 0hgx (phase 1 = sender/Repeater explicit ProtocolPreferenceHTTP3, done in c50e7fc0). 'Never selected silently' holds via disclosure: the exchange row stamps ProtocolHTTP3 only when QUIC actually carried bytes, and a failed attempt falls back to h1 in the same request with a note naming attempt + carrier (ruling A). Kill switch in NetworkSettings (SetHTTP3AltSvc, default ON, ruling C); its operator-reachability (API entry + proxysettings.tsx toggle) is follow-up kidb. Divergence from Burp (which speaks no h3): default-ON riding changes out-of-box traffic shape to advertising origins - accepted by ruling C with the mandatory switch; ServerCerts stay TCP-only (QUIC peer-chain plumbing deferred, carve-out documented). Ride proof: real quic-go h3 server + TLS advertiser end-to-end tests (ride+stamp, fallback+honest-note, switch-off-inert).

title: httputil.RequestURL drops '#' fragments and re-encodes raw spaces on the url.Parse fast path (h2 + h3)
description: Source: external OpenCode review of tip 523d361f (39 commits behind at review time), relayed by the user; verified TRUE against current code by the integrator before filing. Evidence: httputil/h3.go:39 returns url.Parse("https://"+authority+rawTarget) whenever Parse succeeds, but Parse ACCEPTS-then-TRANSFORMS two shapes: '/a#b' -> RequestURI '/a' (fragment silently dropped) and '/a b' -> '/a%20b' (re-encoded). The 55a0af4a invariant 'everything url.Parse accepts it also preserves byte-for-byte' is false for both; only parse FAILURES (bad percent escapes) reach the byte-preserving Opaque fallback. The defect rode the 14c7a6ef refactor from sender/h2.go into httputil, so it now covers the h2 AND h3 legs; h1 carry-raw preserves the same bytes, so h1 vs h2/h3 sends of one stored message differ on the wire. title: Sender: bounded reads on pooled keep-alive exchanges (timeout honoring + deadline-trip discard)
description: Filed from the retracted quiet-AC wedge report (2026-10-25): the wedge did not exist (sandbox-pause artifact), but the audit question stands on its merits. Check whether pooled keep-alive exchanges honor the configured read timeout (timeouts.read_ms); an unbounded read is a hang-forever primitive in a security tool's sender. Wire the configured timeout onto every pooled exchange; a deadline trip discards the connection (a conn whose read died mid-head can never be re-pooled) and returns a named error; behavior stays bounded when the operator set no explicit timeout. W3 lane, red-first with a slow-fixture test, NOT wave-2-blocking.
close_reason: MERGED via integrator (8fac62a2). Audit found 2/3 rules already held (configured read_ms honored on both pool flavors - exchangeHTTP1 and ConnPool.exchangePooled - and deadline-trip discards the conn via release/checkin; characterization tests pin both). The third did not: deadlineFor's zero-zero arm (no operator timeout, no ctx deadline) set no deadline - hang-forever primitive on a silent keep-alive peer. Fix: built-in defaultExchangeBound (30s, var so tests shrink it) ends such reads. Red-first: 5.0s pre-fix (ctx backstop) -> 150ms post-fix. CONTRACT CHANGE (integrator-confirmed): timeouts.total_ms:0 no longer means truly unbounded - a built-in 30s bound ends the exchange when nothing else does. Scope: only the unconfigured arm; audit traffic carries explicit timeouts (MaxTimeoutMS 20min cap, audit.go:1613/1622) and is untouched. Doc updated in network.go; no UI string contradicted.
